offroad.name: Trophy Mountain Forest Service Road
offroad.distance: about 11 km of gravel logging road (the Bear Creek road) branching off Clearwater Valley Road near Spahats Creek Park, up to the Trophy Mountain meadows trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Rough with loose rock, potholes and washboard, but BC Parks describes it as manageable for most cars — the truck is comfortably over-equipped
offroad.season: BORDERLINE. Wells Gray forest service roads are not plowed in winter and the Trophy meadows sit high enough to take snow early. The stop arrives 26 Sep 2027 — the alpine flower show is long over and the first snow of the season is plausible at that elevation. Check the BC Parks Wells Gray trail-and-road status report before driving up.
offroad.note: Replaced a vague entry with the concrete road behind it. The other half of the original phrase, Clearwater Valley Road itself, is paved for the first 42 km to the Helmcken Falls turnoff and graded gravel after — that is a scenic drive, not an offroad route, and belongs in the scenic-drives box. Trophy Mountain is the road that genuinely wants the truck.

clearwater.dogs_source_quote: Dogs and other pets are welcome in Wells Gray Park, but they must be kept under control.
clearwater.dogs_source_note: DRIFT, and it cuts both ways. Our card says simply "allowed on leash" and credits Parks Canada, which has no jurisdiction — Wells Gray is a BC provincial park. BC Parks' actual rule is zoned: leashed in the frontcountry (within 1 km of a highway or park road) and dogs MAY be off leash in the backcountry. So our card is stricter than the authority in the backcountry and, because it does not mention them, silent on the beach and park-building exclusions ("Pets are not allowed in beach areas or most park buildings.") where the authority is stricter than us.

grand-canyon.dogs: SPLIT BY THE RIM. NPS: "Leashed pets are allowed on trails above the rim" on the South Rim, and "Pets are not permitted below the rim (on inner canyon trails)." So the Rim Trail is open to the dog and every descent is not.

Rim Trail — strings together a dozen vie.entity: Rim Trail, Grand Canyon South Rim

trails.name: Rim Trail
trails.was: Rim Trail, Yavapai Point to Mather Point. — prose entry
trails.note_source: The dog-legal walk here: NPS allows leashed pets on trails ABOVE the rim. No single listing matched the Yavapai-to-Mather section cleanly.

grand-canyon.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are allowed on trails above the rim, Mather Campground, Desert View Campground, Trailer Village, and throughout developed areas.

offroad.name: Forest Road 302 to Grandview Lookout Tower (Coconino Rim Road / FR 310)
offroad.distance: about 16.9 miles from the Tusayan Ranger District — FR 302 for approximately 15 miles, then FR 310 for approximately 1.4 miles. From inside the park it is about 18 miles: US-64 east, then "Coconino Rim Road/Forest Road 310 and follow for approximately 1.3 miles"
offroad.difficulty: NOT PUBLISHED. Kaibab National Forest gives the route and the mileages and says nothing about surface, high clearance or 4WD — recorded as unknown rather than guessed.
offroad.season: No gate date published. About 7,000 ft on the Coconino Rim and the stop arrives 12 Mar 2028, so late-season snow and spring mud are both live. The Forest publishes no winter status for these roads.
offroad.note: The straightforward version of the Grandview country: graded forest road from Tusayan out to the 1936 Grandview Lookout Tower, with a paved return into the park on SR 64 if the dirt turns bad. FR 310 leaves Desert View Drive within minutes of the park boundary. This is the answer to "where can the truck go off pavement at the South Rim" — because inside Grand Canyon National Park it cannot; the park has no unpaved road open to visitor driving on this rim, and Tuweep's rough roads are on the far side of the canyon, a five-hour drive, not a day trip.
offroad.source: USFS Kaibab National Forest — Vishnu Trail #125 (driving directions)

offroad.name: Grandview Loop — Forest Roads 302, 310, 2718 and 2719
offroad.distance: 30.4-mile loop — FR 302 for 14.3 miles east from Tusayan, FR 310 (Coconino Rim Road) for 2.1, FR 2718 for 1.5, FR 2719 for 6, then FR 302 for 6.5 back
offroad.difficulty: "A high-clearance vehicle is required for forest roads 2718 and 2719, and four-wheel-drive is recommended." FR 302 and 310 are ordinary graded forest road.
offroad.season: No published gate. This is Kaibab NF at about 7,000 ft on the Coconino Rim and the stop arrives 12 Mar 2028 — late-season snow and spring mud are both live possibilities on FR 2718/2719. The paved bail-out is stated on the source: passenger cars can enter the park and return on SR 64 instead.
offroad.note: This is the answer to "where can the truck actually go off pavement at the South Rim", because inside the park it cannot. Kaibab National Forest wraps the park's south boundary and FR 310 (Coconino Rim Road) leaves Desert View Drive within minutes of the park line, running to the 1936 Grandview Lookout Tower. Recorded from Arizona Highways — the Kaibab NF pages found do not describe this route.

zion.dogs: PROHIBITED except one trail. NPS: "The only trail that allows pets is the Pa'rus Trail, which begins at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center." Not on any other trail, in wilderness, on the shuttle buses, or in buildings. Keep the dog out of the Virgin River — harmful cyanobacteria.
zion.dogs_exception: Pa'rus Trail only — flat, paved, from the Zion Canyon Visitor Center.

Emerald Pools Trail.entity: Historical buildings and structures of Zion National Park

trails.name: Angels Landing Trail
trails.was: Angels Landing / Grotto Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: Permit required by lottery for the chains section. Dogs prohibited — Pa'rus is the only dog trail in Zion.

trails.name: The Watchman Trail
trails.was: Watchman Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: The Zion Narrows Riverside Walk
trails.was: The Narrows — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: The maintained paved walk at the end of the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive. The full Narrows route continues up the river beyond its end — that is the drysuit-and-flash-flood one, and is not this listing.

trails.name: Pa'rus Trail
trails.cruise_reason: Paved end to end (NPS: 93.6% asphalt, 6.4% hard wood decking), 2.6% typical grade, bicycles explicitly permitted by the authority, wheelchair accessible, no walk-your-bike section and no puncture-hazard reports. The one place on this trip where the bike, the dog carrier and a legal dog trail are the same 3.5 miles.
trails.note: THE ONLY TRAIL IN ZION THAT PERMITS PETS. NPS: "The only trail that allows pets is the Pa'rus Trail, which begins at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center." Leash 6 ft or shorter. Two things that matter on the 15 Mar 2028 arrival: it starts at the Visitor Center, where you can park, so it does NOT need the shuttle — and dogs are barred from the shuttle anyway, which is the only way up Zion Canyon in March. Keep the dog out of the Virgin River (harmful cyanobacteria). The unpaved connector spur to the Human History Museum is NOT approved for pets or bikes — stay on the paved trail.
trails.note_source: NPS Zion pet regulations and NPS 'Hike Pa'rus Trail' (nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-pa-rus-trail.htm), fetched: length 3.5 mi (5.6 km) total / 1.6 mi one way, gain 151.7 ft, 30-120 minutes, typical grade 2.6%, max 11.4%, hiking/bicycles/wheelchairs/pets all Yes, "Pets must be restrained on a leash no longer than 6 feet." Difficulty 'Easy' is Visit Utah's published grade (visitutah.com Pa'rus Trail: "Difficulty: Easy 3.5 miles out-and-back"); NPS publishes grade percentages rather than a word. Review count 7,978 from the AllTrails result title; no star surfaced in any snippet.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike Pa'rus Trail
other_links.note: Authority. Publishes the length, grade, surface and the pets-Yes permitted-use table.

other_links.label: TrailLink — Pa'rus Trail
other_links.note: Rail-trail database listing; gives it as 1.6 mi from Watchman Campground to Floor of the Valley Road.

trails.name: Emerald Pools Trails (Lower, Middle and Upper)
trails.distance: NPS publishes each segment one-way from the Emerald Pools Trailhead by Zion Lodge: Lower 0.6 mi (1.0 km), Middle 0.9 mi (1.4 km), Upper 0.3 mi (0.4 km) beyond the junction. NPS does not publish a single figure for walking all three; a Lower-Middle-Upper round trip from the Lodge is commonly reported as about 3 mi.
trails.time: 1-2 hours per NPS for each of the three segments; allow a half day to link all three and return via the Kayenta Trail
trails.difficulty: Lower is EASY — 96.2% hard concrete, typical grade 7.1%, and NPS files it under 'Easy Hikes'. Middle and Upper are MODERATE — NPS: 'The initial ascent is quite steep'; Middle has a typical grade of 10.3% and a maximum of 38.1%, Upper a maximum of 37% with staircases stepping up to 30 in.
trails.elevation_gain: Lower 131 ft (40 m); Middle 333 ft (101 m); Upper 76 ft (23 m) — each figure is NPS's own measured gain for that segment
trails.reviews_note: Count read from the AllTrails result title as displayed. No star rating was visible in any result read for this listing.
trails.dogs_source: NPS trail pages for Lower, Middle and Upper Emerald Pools all state PETS ALLOWED: No.

alltrails.name: Emerald Pools Trail
alltrails.note: AllTrails indexes the three NPS segments as one route starting from Zion Lodge.

trails.season: NPS lists SEASON: Year Round for all three segments. Mid-March is the best time for it: the waterfalls over the Lower Pool alcove are ephemeral and run on snowmelt, so a March visit is one of the few times of year they are actually falling. Do not enter the water — the pools are the wildlife water source and swimming is prohibited.
trails.note: The missing middle of Zion Canyon. Walk out from Zion Lodge to the Lower Pool and its dripping alcove, climb to Middle for the canyon view, add the short Upper spur to the base of the wall, and come back down the Kayenta Trail to the Grotto for a loop rather than a there-and-back. It is the half-day that sits naturally between an Angels Landing morning and a Riverside Walk afternoon.

trails.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
trails.distance: 1 mi (1.6 km) round trip — 0.5 mi (0.8 km) one way (NPS)
trails.time: 1-2 hours (NPS duration); most people are back in about an hour
trails.difficulty: Moderate — NPS: 'a moderate, 1 mi (1.6 km) trail on the East Side of Zion', beginning with sandstone steps and a metal handrail over rocky terrain above a slot canyon. Long drop-offs, mostly fenced. Typical grade 7.6%, maximum 50.4%; overhanging rock with as little as 4 ft of vertical clearance in places.
trails.reviews_note: Count read from the AllTrails result title as displayed. No star rating was visible.
trails.dogs_source: NPS Canyon Overlook page: PETS ALLOWED: No.
trails.season: NPS lists SEASON: Year Round. In March the slickrock can hold ice in the shaded slot section early in the day; it is an afternoon trail at this date. Best light is late afternoon, looking down the canyon at the Towers of the Virgin.
trails.note: By far the best view for the effort in the park, and the only trail on this card that is not in Zion Canyon proper. Take the TRUCK, not the coach: the trailhead sits immediately east of the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel, and oversized vehicles need a paid escort and one-way traffic control through it — the coach has no business on that road. NPS warns parking is extremely limited and that you must turn right to enter or exit the lot; be prepared to make more than one attempt, which six nights comfortably allows.

offroad.name: Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway
offroad.distance: 9.25 miles
offroad.difficulty: BLM publishes no surface grade or vehicle requirement for it — an absence worth knowing, since the byway designation makes it sound easier than the warning below implies
offroad.season: BLM: "This route often becomes impassable during heavy rain and periods of inclement winter weather." The stop is 15-21 Mar 2028 — late enough that winter weather is unlikely but spring rain is not. No gate; the surface is the gate.
offroad.note: The stop's own road. It runs between Rockville and Apple Valley, just south of Zion and a couple of miles from the Virgin base, climbing to the mesa top under Smithsonian Butte with the Zion cliffs behind. "No services are available along the Byway." The Grafton ghost town road branches off the Rockville end.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway

offroad.name: Gooseberry Mesa Road
offroad.difficulty: not published as a driving grade. BLM's mesa map is written for mountain bikers — "Slickrock portions of trail are marked with white dots" — and it is the authority on which routes are open to vehicles, so read it before driving anything beyond the main mesa road
offroad.season: No gate published. Same wet-weather caveat as Smithsonian Butte; the mesa clay is the problem.
offroad.note: The mesa immediately south of Smithsonian Butte, reached off the byway, with a rim view straight into Zion. Included with a caution: the published material here is bike material, and BLM's map — not a trail database — decides which routes a vehicle may use.

zion.dogs_source_quote: The only trail that allows pets is the Pa'rus Trail, which begins at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center.
zion.dogs_source_note: Exclusion wording on the page is "Pets are not permitted on any other trails, wilderness areas, on shuttle buses, or in public buildings in Zion." Cyanobacteria advice confirmed: "Keep dogs out of the water and on a leash while in Zion."
zion.dates_checked: 15-21 Mar 2028, 6 nights, based at Virgin, UT.
zion.trails_note: Four trails for six nights, and the existing four were well chosen — Angels Landing, Watchman, Pa'rus and the Riverside Walk are the right spine. Two obvious gaps: the Emerald Pools, which is the classic mid-canyon half-day and the connector everyone actually walks, and Canyon Overlook, which is the whole east side of the park and the single best view-per-mile hike Zion has. Both are added; the card is then at six for six nights and needs nothing else. Two dates facts that bear on trails already on the card: Angels Landing needs a PERMIT by lottery for the chained section past Scout Lookout (recreation.gov, seasonal and day-before lotteries) — six nights gives several day-before entries, which is the realistic route in; and the bottom-up Narrows beyond the end of the Riverside Walk is routinely closed in mid-March when Virgin River flow exceeds 150 cfs on spring runoff, so the Riverside Walk should be planned as the walk in its own right rather than as the approach to the Narrows.
zion.dogs_stop_level: Zion permits pets on the Pa'rus Trail and nowhere else. NPS's own trail listings answer PETS ALLOWED: Yes for Pa'rus and No for every other trail in the park, including both trails added below. Pa'rus is already on the card and is the dog's entire Zion.

olympic.dogs: PROHIBITED on all trails except a named few: Peabody Creek Trail, Rialto Beach to Ellen Creek, the Kalaloch beaches between the Hoh and Quinault Reservations, Madison Falls Trail, Spruce Railroad Trail, and July Creek Loop. Leash 6 ft.
olympic.note: Spruce Railroad Trail is both the dog-legal trail here AND a former rail grade — the shape that has produced the only confirmed gravel cruises on this trip. Worth a surface check.

not_a_trail.problem: A road-status link, not a trail. Belongs with the stop notes.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sol Duc Road to Sol Duc Hot Springs
scenicDrives_patch.note: Turns south off US-101 west of Lake Crescent, about 40 minutes from Port Angeles, and runs up the Sol Duc valley to the hot springs resort and the Sol Duc Falls trailhead at road's end.
scenicDrives_patch.season: OPEN, JUST. The road is open year-round as far as Sol Duc Falls, but the upper section is seasonal and closes in winter storms; the hot springs resort runs roughly 20–25 March to the LAST WEEKEND IN OCTOBER. Arrive 19 Oct 2027 — the resort is open, with about a week to spare. Recorded road & weather line: 360-565-3131.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS Olympic Sol Duc valley page; NPS current road conditions

trails.name: Peabody Creek Trail
trails.note: PET-LEGAL, and the closest one to camp — it starts at the Olympic National Park Visitor Center in Port Angeles. NPS names it first in the short list of trails where leashed pets are allowed; leash 6 ft. Follows Peabody Creek through a wooded ravine. This is the dog's default walk on a Port Angeles base.
trails.note_source: NPS Olympic pets page (nps.gov/olym/planyourvisit/pets.htm), fetched: pets allowed on "Peabody Creek Trail (Olympic National Park Visitor Center in Port Angeles)", Rialto Beach parking lot to Ellen Creek, the beaches between the Hoh and Quinault Reservations, Madison Falls Trail, Spruce Railroad Trail and July Creek Loop Trail; "Pets must be restrained on a leash no longer than 6 feet." Stats from Washington Trails Association (wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/peabody-creek-trail), fetched: "5.6 miles, roundtrip", 800 ft gain, highest point 1,100 ft, difficulty "Moderate", "Dogs allowed on leash". WTA's own description says the trail follows the creek "for 2.8 miles" one way, which is the same figure halved. Review count 842 from the AllTrails result title; no star and no AllTrails distance surfaced in any snippet.

other_links.label: WTA — Peabody Creek Trail
other_links.note: Length, gain, high point, difficulty, and its own confirmation that dogs are allowed on leash.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Olympic
other_links.note: The rule. The complete list of pet-legal trails in the park.

trails.name: Madison Falls Trail
trails.note: PET-LEGAL, named in the NPS list, leash 6 ft. Paved and gently sloping from the parking area to a 60 ft waterfall, at the Elwha entrance — a five-minute walk rather than an outing, but it is one of only six places in Olympic the dog may legally stand on a trail.
trails.note_source: NPS Olympic pets page names "Madison Falls Trail (Elwha)". AllTrails result snippet, verbatim: "Madison Falls Trail is an out-and-back trail that covers 0.2 mi, with an elevation gain of 49 ft. It takes about 0.5-1 hr to complete", 3,379 reviews from the result title; no star surfaced. NPS 'See Madison Falls' describes "a 0.1-mile, paved, gently sloping trail" — that is the one-way figure against AllTrails' 0.2 mi out-and-back. Difficulty 'Easy' is Komoot's published grade for the same trail ("Madison Falls Trail is an easy hike"); neither NPS nor the AllTrails snippet published a difficulty word.

other_links.label: NPS — See Madison Falls
other_links.note: Authority: "Continue beyond the parking lot on a 0.1-mile, paved, gently sloping trail leading to Madison Falls."

other_links.label: Komoot — Madison Falls Trail

trails.name: Spruce Railroad Trail
trails.cruise_reason: A 1918 railroad grade, now paved end to end as a section of the Olympic Discovery Trail, with both original tunnels (McFee and Daley-Rankin) restored and reopened by 2020. NPS states plainly that bicycles AND pets are permitted. Rail grade means no walk-your-bike section; paved means no puncture hazard. This is the single best gravel-cruise-with-the-dog candidate on the whole west coast run.
trails.note: PET-LEGAL AND BIKE-LEGAL — NPS: "As a continuation of the Olympic Discovery Trail, bicycles and pets are permitted on this trail." Named in the park pet rule; leash 6 ft. Hugs the north shore of Lake Crescent for 4 miles on the old railroad grade. The card already carries "Devils Punchbowl via Spruce Railroad Trail" (2.4 mi) — that is the popular short out-and-back to the punchbowl bridge off the east end. This entry is the full trail, which is the one the bike and the dog carrier want.
trails.note_source: NPS Olympic pets page names "Spruce Railroad Trail (North shore of Lake Crescent)". NPS trailhead pages (nps.gov/places/000/spruce-railroad-trailhead-east.htm and .../spruce-railroad-trailhead-camp-david-jr-road.htm), verbatim: "Accessed from either the East Beach Road or Camp David Junior Road, the Spruce Railroad Trail hugs the shore of Lake Crescent for 4 miles (6.4 km) along an old railroad route. As a continuation of the Olympic Discovery Trail, bicycles and pets are permitted on this trail." Paving and tunnel restoration from olympicdiscoverytrail.org ("the incredible McFee tunnel was opened in 2017. In 2020 the Daley-Rankin tunnel was restored, and the trail between the tunnels was completed") and the Olympic Discovery Trail's own notice ("The Spruce Railroad Trail is paved and 4 miles long one way"). Review count 1,932 from the AllTrails result title; no star, distance or difficulty surfaced in any snippet.
trails.url_note: Both AllTrails hits for this trail carried a locale segment — /en/trail/... and /en-gb/trail/... . Only the locale segment was removed to match the form every other url in this db uses; the slug itself is the one the search returned and was not assembled from the trail's name. AllTrails titles the listing "Spruce Railroad Trail: Lake Crescent".

other_links.label: NPS — Spruce Railroad Trailhead (East)
other_links.note: Authority: 4 miles along the old railroad route; bicycles and pets permitted.

other_links.label: Olympic Discovery Trail — the ODT
other_links.note: The tunnel restorations and the completion of the paved section between them.

trails.name: July Creek Loop Trail
trails.note: PET-LEGAL, named in the NPS list, leash 6 ft. On the north shore of Lake Quinault, branching from the July Creek Picnic Area trail. NO PUBLISHED LENGTH — NPS names the trail and describes it only as "A loop branching from the July Creek Picnic Area trail", and it appears in no trail database. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Worth knowing before driving: Lake Quinault is the far south-west corner of the park, roughly two hours each way from a Port Angeles base, so this is a whole day, not an evening walk.
trails.note_source: NPS Olympic pets page names "July Creek Loop Trail (North shore of Lake Quinault)"; NPS day-hiking page lists it. NPS place page (nps.gov/places/000/july-creek-loop-trail-trailhead.htm), fetched, carries only the one-line description and no length, surface or difficulty. Three separate searches found no AllTrails, WTA, Komoot or TrailLink listing under this name. Length, difficulty and time are unknown and are left blank deliberately.

other_links.label: NPS — July Creek Loop Trail Trailhead
other_links.note: The only page the authority publishes for it. No length given.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Olympic
other_links.note: The rule that makes it legal.

trails.call: Olympic NP Wilderness Information Center, 360-565-3100 — ask the length of the July Creek Loop. No authority publishes it, and it is one of only six pet-legal trails in the park.

offroad.name: Obstruction Point Road
offroad.distance: 7.8 miles from Hurricane Ridge
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "Gravel, narrow, winding mountain road". Trailers are not recommended on it.
offroad.season: RIGHT AT THE EDGE OF THE STOP DATES. NPS publishes status rather than dates and gives no closing date; a local conditions aggregator describes it as open July-October only, weather permitting. The stop is 19-25 Oct 2027 at around 6,000 ft on the Olympic crest — this road can be shut by the first real snow of the season, and that snow routinely falls in October. Phone the recorded road line, (360) 565-3131, updated daily, before driving up.
offroad.note: The highest road in Olympic National Park and the only unpaved one that goes anywhere. It runs the ridge from Hurricane Ridge out to the Obstruction Point trailhead with the Bailey Range across the valley. If it is open during this stay it is the single best drive of the stop; if it is shut, Hurricane Ridge Road (17 miles, paved) still gets most of the view.
offroad.source: NPS Olympic NP — Current Road Conditions

offroad.name: Deer Park Road
offroad.distance: 18 miles total, of which NPS says "The last nine miles are gravel"
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "narrow, windy mountain road with numerous blind corners", and the gravel section is "not suitable for RVs or trailers"
offroad.season: SAME RISK AS OBSTRUCTION POINT. NPS: "From late fall until late spring when snow melts, the road is closed." No date is published. The stop is 19-25 Oct 2027, which is the ragged front edge of 'late fall' at 5,400 ft.
offroad.note: The eastern equivalent of Obstruction Point, climbing from near Sequim to the Deer Park campground and the Blue Mountain summit. Steeper and narrower than Obstruction Point and with a longer gravel section. The two are connected on foot by a ridge trail but not by road.
offroad.source: NPS Olympic NP — Deer Park Area Brochure

olympic.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not permitted - on any trails not listed above, in public buildings, on interpretive walks, or in the wilderness.
olympic.dogs_source_note: All six permitted routes on our card are confirmed verbatim on the page. Leash rule reads "Pets must be restrained on a leash no longer than 6 feet."

yosemite.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails "even if carried" — NPS states there are no exceptions for carried pets. Allowed on a few paved paths: Bridalveil Fall, Lower Yosemite Fall, the paved Cook's Meadow path, the paved road to Mirror Lake, Wawona Meadow Loop, and some Wawona/Hodgdon fire roads.

trails.name: Lower Yosemite Fall Trail
trails.was: Lower Yosemite Fall Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Paved and one of the few Yosemite trails where DOGS ARE PERMITTED. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.
trails.note: PET-LEGAL — NPS: "Leashed pets and strollers are allowed." Paved loop with exhibits; the eastern half, 0.6 mi one way from the Yosemite Falls shuttle stop to the viewing area, is wheelchair accessible. Already on the card without figures; these are the authority's own. Still no AllTrails trail listing — AllTrails has only a point-of-interest page for Lower Yosemite Fall, not a listing for this trail, so no url is claimed.

other_links.label: NPS — Lower Yosemite Fall Trail
other_links.note: Authority. Distance, gain, difficulty, time and the pet sentence.

trails.name: Valley Loop Trail
trails.was: Valley Loop Trail — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.

trails.name: Bridalveil Fall Trail
trails.note: PET-LEGAL — NPS states on the trail's own page: "Leashed pets are allowed on this trail." Paved, part of it wheelchair accessible, at the west end of Yosemite Valley on the Wawona Road junction, which is the side of the valley the Hwy 140 base arrives from. Leash six feet or shorter. One of only a handful of paved paths in Yosemite the dog may use; NPS is explicit that pets are barred from trails "even if carried", with no exception for carried pets.
trails.note_source: NPS Yosemite pets page (nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/pets.htm), fetched: leashed pets permitted on the "Bridalveil Fall trail", "Lower Yosemite Fall trail", the "paved trail through Cook's Meadow (including boardwalks)", the "paved road to Mirror Lake (but not the unpaved trail around Mirror Lake)" and the "Wawona Meadow Loop"; "pets must be restrained on a leash not more than six feet long or otherwise physically restrained". NPS Bridalveil Fall Trail page (nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/bridalveilfalltrail.htm), fetched: "Distance: 0.5 mi (0.8 km) round trip", "Elevation gain: Approximately 80 ft (24 m)", "Difficulty: Easy", "Time: 20 minutes", paved, "Leashed pets are allowed on this trail." Review count 2,107 from the AllTrails result title; no star surfaced.

other_links.label: NPS — Bridalveil Fall Trail
other_links.note: Authority. Distance, gain, difficulty, time and the pet sentence.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Yosemite
other_links.note: The complete list of paths in Yosemite where leashed pets are allowed.

trails.name: Wawona Meadow Loop
trails.season: CHECK BEFORE DRIVING — Wawona is at the far south of the park and the 19 Dec 2027 arrival is mid-winter
trails.note: PET-LEGAL — named in the NPS pet rule; leash six feet or shorter. An old dirt road circling the meadow behind the Wawona Hotel, and the longest legal dog walk in Yosemite by a wide margin: the other pet-legal paths are all under a mile. The catch is where it is. Wawona is about 27 miles south of the valley on the Wawona Road, well over an hour from a Midpines/Hwy 140 base, and the arrival is 19 December — check Yosemite's road-conditions line for the Wawona Road before committing the day. No closure is asserted here; the season is a reason to check, not a finding.
trails.note_source: NPS Yosemite pets page (fetched) names "Wawona Meadow Loop" among the paths where leashed pets are allowed. AllTrails result snippet, verbatim: "Wawona Meadow Loop Trail is a loop trail that covers 3.7 mi, with an elevation gain of 249 ft. It takes about 1-1.5 hr to complete", 1,699 reviews from the result title; no star and no difficulty word surfaced. Third-party guides describe it as easy/flat (yosemite.com "relatively easy", yosemite.travel "a flat, easy walk on an old dirt road") and give the loop as ~3.5 mi, but no authority or trail database published a difficulty grade, so none is recorded.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Yosemite
other_links.note: The rule that makes it legal, and the only authority page that names it.

offroad.name: Merced River Road (Briceburg, the old Yosemite Valley Railroad grade)
offroad.distance: 4.5 mi to Railroad Flat; 7 mi to the North Fork primitive camp
offroad.difficulty: Unpaved. BLM: "It is NOT recommended for trailers over 18 feet or large RV's to cross over the suspension bridge."
offroad.season: OPEN — and it is the only one. BLM publishes no seasonal closure. Briceburg sits at low elevation on Highway 140, twelve miles north-east of Mariposa, so this is the one driveable dirt road within reach of this stop that is not behind a snow gate on 19–23 Dec 2027.
offroad.note: Follows the old Yosemite Valley Railroad grade downstream along the Wild & Scenic Merced from the Briceburg suspension bridge. Distances from the visitor center: McCabe Flat 2.3 mi, Willow Placer 3.6 mi, Railroad Flat 4.5 mi, with the North Fork primitive camp 2.5 miles beyond Railroad Flat. BLM Mother Lode Field Office. The Merced River Trail continues downstream from the road end but has rock and mud slide damage. This is on the Hwy 140 corridor the stop already sits on, which is what makes it work.
offroad.source: BLM Merced River Recreation Management Area

offroad.name: Yosemite winter road status — what is open, and why none of it is dirt
offroad.season: NPS Winter Road Closures lists as open all year: "Wawona Road (Highway 41), El Portal Road (Highway 140), Big Oak Flat Road (Highway 120 from the west), and Hetch Hetchy Road". Closed across 19–23 Dec 2027: Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road, both "usually from sometime in November through late May or early June" (the first five miles of Glacier Point Road open mid-December to March for Badger Pass only), and Mariposa Grove Road, which closes "on or about November 30" and reopens no earlier than 15 April. Tire chains may be required on any of them.
offroad.note: Recorded as the answer to the question rather than as a route: every Yosemite road NPS lists as open in winter is paved, and its winter road page names no unpaved public road as open. Hetch Hetchy Road is a genuine dead-end backcountry drive with a gate and daylight-only hours, but it is pavement. There is no legal off-pavement driving inside Yosemite for this stop — the Briceburg road above is the substitute.
offroad.source: NPS Yosemite National Park — Winter Road Closures

yosemite.dogs_source_quote: On trails, including the trail to Vernal Fall, even if carried (however, pets are allowed on the Wawona Meadow Loop)
yosemite.dogs_source_note: DRIFT (small, in our favour to fix): our card says pets are allowed on "the paved road to Mirror Lake" — the page is explicit that this is "the paved road to Mirror Lake (but not the unpaved trail around Mirror Lake)". The page also names two paved paths our card lists (Bridalveil Fall trail, Lower Yosemite Fall trail, "paved trail through Cook's Meadow (including boardwalks)") plus "Chowchilla Mountain Road, and Four Mile and Eleven Mile fire roads", "Carlon Road from the trailhead to Hodgdon Meadow (but not to Carlon Falls)", and "Old Big Oak Flat Road from Hodgdon Meadow to Tuolumne Grove parking lot".

great-basin.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails and in the backcountry, with exactly two exceptions: the Lexington Arch Trail and the trail between Baker and the Great Basin Visitor Center. Leashed pets are otherwise allowed only in campgrounds, in front of the visitor centers, and ALONG ROADS — which is what makes the March visit work: with Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive gated at Upper Lehman Creek, walking up the closed road is walking a road, and NPS's own spring page lists it as "Hike along the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive past the closure (Dog friendly!)". Not permitted in Lehman Caves or at evening programs.
great-basin.dogs_exception: Lexington Arch Trail and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail only.

Dark sky stargazing.entity: Great Basin NP is a certified dark-sky park, but this is the Salida Hot Springs trap: the Great Basin National Park article's full 10k of text contains no occurrence of 'dark sky', 'stargazing' or 'astronomy'. Linking the park would be a working link to an article that does not document the thing.

trails.name: Bristlecone Pine and Glacier Trail
trails.was: Bristlecone Pine / Alpine Lakes Loop — two separate routes in one entry
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail.
trails.season: Above the winter gate — the Scenic Drive is closed to vehicles at Upper Lehman Creek Dec through Mar, and NPS says the Bristlecone Trailhead at the top opens ~May, around Memorial Day. On 21-24 Mar the drive itself is a 20-mile round-trip ski or snowshoe with 2,500 ft of gain before this trail's first step; NPS lists the Glacier/Bristlecone/Alpine Lake cirque area as a 5-mile Intermediate-to-Expert winter route on top of that, and says do not attempt it without significant backcountry winter experience and equipment.

trails.name: Alpine Lakes, Bristlecone, and Glacier Loop
trails.season: Above the winter gate — the Scenic Drive is closed to vehicles at Upper Lehman Creek Dec through Mar, and NPS says the Bristlecone Trailhead at the top opens ~May, around Memorial Day, after a typical winter. On 21-24 Mar this is a 20-mile round-trip ski or snowshoe with 2,500 ft of gain just to reach the trailhead, and NPS states it is "not recommended to hike these trails unless you have significant backcountry and winter experience and equipment". North-facing slopes hold significant snowpack and ice well past the road opening.

trails.name: Mountain View Nature Trail
trails.season: Open on 21-24 Mar — it starts at the Rhodes Cabin beside the Lehman Caves Visitor Center at 6,825 ft, below every closure in the park, and the visitor center is open year round.
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail. NPS ranger tip: "a common route for those wanting to get on dirt who may not be able to go the distances of Great Basin's more involved trails." Interpretive; a trail guide is loaned at the front desk. Passes the original Lehman Cave entrance.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike the Mountain View Nature Trail

trails.name: Lexington Arch Trail
trails.season: Reachable on 21-24 Mar — trailhead is 7,050 ft and BLM's Lexington Creek Road is not gated, unlike every park road. The catch is spring: NPS says washouts and running water are common, and the road is currently severely washed out with parking about a mile short of the trailhead, so budget an extra two miles on foot.
trails.note_source: THE ONE THAT MATTERS FOR THE DOG. NPS: "Lexington Arch is the one and only trail within Great Basin National Park that permits pets" — six-foot leash. A six-storey limestone arch, rare among western arches which are almost all sandstone. Reached from Utah SH-21 south of Garrison, not from Baker's side of the range. A burn took out much of the shade along the old roadbed. NPS asks visitors to carry vehicle recovery gear.

trails.name: Pole Canyon Trail
trails.season: NPS lists it as "year round", and at a 6,880 ft trailhead it is the lowest of the park's real hikes — but it hangs off Baker Creek Road, which closes intermittently through winter and spring, and NPS warns of "a short snowshoe from the Baker Creek pit toilet to the trailhead". The NPS spring page suggests hiking "the first ½ mile of Pole Canyon" when snow is deep, which is the realistic version on 21 Mar.
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail. Trailhead is off Baker Creek Road about 1.5 miles in, near Grey Cliffs Campground; the trail crosses Baker Creek then climbs under aspen and conifer with views out over Snake Valley. NPS also lists a Pole Canyon/Timber Creek loop of 7.5 miles round trip as a novice-to-intermediate ski and snowshoe route in winter.

trails.name: Lehman Creek Trail
trails.season: The only route on this card that starts exactly AT the closure rather than behind it — the trailhead is Upper Lehman Creek Campground, three miles up the Scenic Drive at 7,750 ft, which is where the gate sits. NPS: "During winter, this is the best route to snowshoe or crosscountry ski to reach the upper trails when the Scenic Drive is closed." On 21-24 Mar expect snow within the first mile; NPS's own spring advice is to walk "the first mile of the Lehman Creek Trail or until the snow deepens". The full 8-mile round trip to the Wheeler Peak parking lot is graded Advanced to Expert in winter conditions.
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail. NPS grades the trail itself Moderate/Strenuous; AllTrails calls it challenging and gives an average of 4 h 1 min. In winter, park at the pullout across from the campground rather than at the summer trailhead. AllTrails gives 10.6 km against the NPS figure of 6.4 mi / 10.3 km; the NPS figure is the authority's.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike the Lehman Creek Trail

trails.name: Timber Creek Trail
trails.season: Behind a closure on 21-24 Mar in most years. The trailhead is at the END of Baker Creek Road at 8,020 ft, and NPS says that road "is gravel and can close intermittently in the winter and spring" — so this is either a drive-up or a long walk-in depending on the day, and NPS tells spring visitors to bring snowshoes. NPS lists a Pole Canyon/Timber Creek loop, 7.5 mi round trip, as a novice-to-intermediate winter ski and snowshoe route from lower down.
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail. Steep climb through pine forest opening onto large meadows. The AllTrails listing is the longer user-assembled South Fork Baker Creek and Timber Creek loop, which contains the official NPS Timber Creek Trail rather than matching it — the 5.1 mi and 1,610 ft figures above are the NPS ones.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike the Timber Creek Trail

trails.name: Osceola Ditch Trail to Mill Creek
trails.distance: ~2 mi round trip to Mill Creek; 9.2 mi round trip for the full ditch trail
trails.season: CORRECTION TO THE OBVIOUS ASSUMPTION: this is not a drive-up spring hike. Both of its trailheads are behind winter closures. The main one is 4.5 miles up the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive at 8,400 ft — a mile and a half ABOVE the Upper Lehman Creek gate at mile 3 — and the western one is on Strawberry Creek Road, which NPS closes at the park boundary for the winter. On 21-24 Mar it is a ski or snowshoe of roughly three miles each way from the gate before the trail even starts. Park roads generally open ~May, around Memorial Day.
trails.note_source: Dogs prohibited — Great Basin permits them only on Lexington Arch and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail. NPS calls the full trail "a relatively flat 9.2-mile round trip trail that leads to the Strawberry Creek area of the park"; the short version goes "roughly one mile in to Mill Creek and then return". Mill Creek holds a remnant population of native Bonneville cutthroat trout. The ditch is the 1889 hand-dug 18-mile flume that carried Lehman Creek water to the Osceola mines — the same story as the Osceola townsite road in the offroad box, from the receiving end. Pieces of the original wooden flume survive along it. AllTrails also carries a separate shorter Osceola Ditch Interpretive Trail listing (242 reviews) covering the same ground; only one is listed here.

offroad.name: Lexington Creek Road (Lexington Arch access)
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "4WD is recommended on this road, and high clearance is absolutely necessary."
offroad.season: The one 4x4 road here that is not gated on 21 Mar. BLM manages it, and NPS notes the park "may not close the road even if conditions are hazardous" — so it stays driveable-in-principle year round, but late March is exactly when it is worst: NPS says "washouts and running water are common" in spring, and "travel with caution after heavy rain" because wet conditions can render it impassable.
offroad.note: Leaves Utah SH-21 south of Garrison, signed near Pruess Lake, and runs almost entirely on gravel and dirt to a trailhead at 7,050 ft. NPS road conditions currently rate it severely washed out with parking required about a mile short of the trailhead — assume the last mile is walked. Carry vehicle recovery gear; NPS asks for it by name on this road. A burn has taken out most of the shade along the old roadbed. This is also the approach to the only trail in Great Basin that permits dogs.

offroad.name: Sacramento Pass two-track and NF 453, BLM Sacramento Pass Recreation Area
offroad.distance: 15 mi network; the first 4.5 mi of the OHV route are passable in a full-size 4x4
offroad.difficulty: Nevada Trail Finder: "steep switchbacks and loose rock"; "the first 4.5 miles are passable in a Full size 4x4", after which "trail width grows limited"
offroad.season: Low end is the most likely thing to be driveable on 21 Mar of anything on this card apart from Lexington Creek Road — the trailhead sits on US-50 at Sacramento Pass, 7,154 ft, on a highway kept clear year round, reached by "a well-maintained gravel road" off the highway. But the two-track climbs south straight into the Snake Range and holds snow and mud into spring at those elevations; treat the upper switchbacks as unverified rather than open.
offroad.note: 15 miles west of the Utah line and about 15 miles from Baker on US-50 — the shortest offroad day of the stop. Two things to get right: BLM's three signed trail loops here (6.5 miles total) are CLOSED to motorized use, so the driving is on the designated two-track roads and NF 453 only; and OHV use is not permitted once you cross into the National Park boundary. There is free BLM camping and an equestrian trailhead at the pass. No agency publishes an elevation profile for the road itself.
offroad.source: https://www.nvtrailfinder.com/trails/trail/sacramento-pass-recreation-area — motorized detail; https://www.blm.gov/visit/sacramento-pass-recreation-area — managing agency, loop mileage and the closed-to-motorized rule; pass elevation 7,154 ft per AARoads and Pass Bagger

offroad.name: Blue Mass Scenic Area approach, Kern Mountains
offroad.season: Valley-floor dirt for most of its length, so it is a dry-weather road rather than a snow question. BLM puts the scenic area itself at 7,000 ft. In late March the approach is driveable when dry and impassable clay when it is not; nothing published gives a closure date because there is no gate.
offroad.note: BLM: "Scenic wonderland of streams and springs, old cabins, granite cliffs and pinnacles and lush vegetation" — spires and rounded outcrops of bluish-grey granite in the Kern Mountains near the Utah line, between Mt Moriah and the Deep Creek Mountains. This is the long day of the stop, not a half-day: one published route runs 18 miles northwest from Baker on US 6-50 to Eight Mile Ranch Road and then a long way north on dirt. No agency page gives a mileage, a road number or a vehicle requirement, so treat the routing as unverified and check it against the BLM Kern Mountains surface-management map before committing.
offroad.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/blue-mass-scenic-area for the area and its 7,000 ft elevation; routing from newdescents.com/locations/blue-mass-scenic-area, which is not an agency source

offroad.name: Baker Creek Road
offroad.difficulty: Gravel, no published clearance requirement
offroad.season: Gated somewhere below the top from first snow through Mar; NPS says park roads generally open ~May, around Memorial Day, and that this one specifically "can close intermittently in the winter and spring". Where the gate sits on any given day in late March is a phone call, not a lookup — the NPS spring page tells visitors to "Hike past the closure on Baker Creek Road to the trails beyond".
offroad.note: Leaves NV-488 near the Lehman Caves Visitor Center and climbs to the Baker Creek Trailhead at 8,020 ft at its end. This is the access for Pole Canyon, Grey Cliffs and Timber Creek, so whether it is open decides three trails on this card. NPS lists it as gravel and closed in winter. Even when the gate is up, the Pole Canyon trailhead can need "a short snowshoe from the Baker Creek pit toilet".

offroad.name: Snake Creek Road
offroad.difficulty: Dirt, no published clearance requirement
offroad.season: Gated at the park boundary Nov through Mar; park-wide, NPS says most roads open ~May, around Memorial Day, and this one reopens earlier "when conditions allow in the spring" with no date ever published. Assume shut on 21 Mar and treat an open gate as a bonus.
offroad.note: The park's south-side dirt road, running west from the Snake Valley floor into the range. NPS posts it and Strawberry Creek Road together each autumn: "Snake Creek Road and Strawberry Creek Road are now closed for the winter season at the park boundary. They will reopen when conditions allow in the spring." No mileage or elevation profile is published by the park.
offroad.source: https://www.nps.gov/grba/planyourvisit/conditions.htm; closure wording from the park's own seasonal road-closure notice

offroad.name: Strawberry Creek Road
offroad.difficulty: Dirt, no published clearance requirement
offroad.season: Gated at the park boundary Nov through Mar; park-wide, NPS says most roads open ~May, around Memorial Day, and this one reopens "when conditions allow in the spring" with no date published. Assume shut on 21 Mar.
offroad.note: North-side dirt road into the Strawberry Creek drainage, and the western trailhead for the Osceola Ditch trail — which is why its closure matters twice on this card. Closed in the same seasonal notice as Snake Creek Road. No published mileage or elevation.

offroad.name: Osceola townsite and mining district road
offroad.difficulty: Unpaved; "a high-clearance vehicle is wise" — no agency has published a grade or a vehicle requirement
offroad.season: Unverified for 21 Mar, and recorded as unverified deliberately. The road is not gated by anyone, but Osceola is a west-slope Snake Range mining district rather than valley floor, and no source found publishes the townsite elevation, the road number or a mileage — so there is no basis for calling it open or shut. Sun-exposed and south-facing for much of the climb, which argues for driveable in a normal late March, but that is inference, not a source.
offroad.note: Nevada's biggest placer gold camp, worked from 1872 and largely gone: a cemetery, a crumbling brick storefront and the diggings. Reached by unpaved road off US-50 about three miles west of the park, in White Pine County. The Osceola Ditch — the 18-mile hand-dug 1889 flume that fed these mines from Lehman Creek — is the same story from the other end, and its trail is on the trails box. Carry water and a full tank; nothing out here is signed. Worth a call to the BLM Bristlecone Field Office for current road condition before driving it, since no page publishes one.
offroad.source: unitedstatesghosttowns.com and osceolagoldinc.com/history/osceola-ghost-town/ — no BLM or Forest Service page for this road was found

offroad.name: Mount Washington Road
offroad.difficulty: Totally unpaved; high clearance and 4WD essential; "extremely rough" with steep switchbacks that need three-point turns
offroad.season: Shut, and not marginally. The summit is 11,459 ft — one of the highest roads in Nevada — and it is deep in snow in March; its eastern approach runs from Pole Canyon and Snake Creek, both of which are behind their own winter gates. Recorded because knowing it is out is worth as much as knowing it is in: this road opens ~Jul in most years, not spring.
offroad.note: Built in 1948 up the west side of the South Snake Range to the Mount Washington bristlecone grove, a genuinely remote corner of the park with an experienced-driver-only reputation. It is the alternative bristlecone grove to the one behind the Wheeler Peak gate, and on this stop's dates neither is reachable. This is a July-or-later route on some future trip, not a March one.
offroad.source: dangerousroads.org 7192 for the 11,459 ft summit and the 4WD requirement; desertsurvivor.blogspot.com for the road-surface reports. No NPS page publishes a mileage or an opening date for it.

great-basin.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets can only be exercised in the campgrounds, in front of the visitor centers, and along roads.

black-canyon-gunnison.dogs: PROHIBITED on all hiking trails, inner canyon routes, in the wilderness and on ski trails — with TWO exceptions, not one. NPS: "Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail." Also allowed in picnic areas, campgrounds, parking lots, on paths to overlooks and along roads open to vehicles. The North Rim is across the canyon via Crawford and is not a realistic day from the South Rim campground, so Rim Rock is the practical one. NOTE ON THE SUMMER FAWN CLOSURE: that comes from Colorado Trail Explorer, the state trail register, which gives the dog-permitted window as 11 Aug - 31 May. NPS publishes no such closure and no dates at all — worth the call before counting on either reading. The 8 Apr 2028 arrival is inside COTREX's permitted window either way.
black-canyon-gunnison.dogs_exception: Rim Rock Trail only, and not in summer — deer with fawns.

trails.name: Rim Rock Trail
trails.official_length: 0.8 mi (Colorado Trail Explorer, manager: Black Canyon of the Gunnison NP); 0.9 mi (Hiking Project)
trails.season: DOG-LEGAL ON THESE DATES — dogs are permitted on this trail 11 Aug-31 May and barred 1 Jun-10 Aug; the 8-10 Apr 2028 stay is inside the permitted window
trails.note: THE ONLY TRAIL ON THE SOUTH RIM THE DOG MAY WALK, and on this stop's dates it is walkable. NPS: "Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail", leash six feet (1.8 m) maximum; pets are prohibited on all other hiking trails, inner canyon routes, in the wilderness and on snowshoe/cross-country ski trails. Three things decide whether this actually works on 8-10 April, and all three come out yes. (1) The summer dog closure does not bite — dogs are shut out 1 Jun-10 Aug, which is nowhere near these dates. (2) The road reaches it. The South Rim Road is usually open to vehicles only from late April, but NPS states that in winter it is open as far as Gunnison Point at the visitor center, and this trail runs between the visitor center and the South Rim Campground — i.e. entirely inside the stretch that stays open. Warner Point and the rest of the rim drive are the part that is still shut in early April, and the dog could not use those anyway. (3) It is open after the 2025 South Rim Fire — but it burned. NPS current conditions, verbatim: "Open. Trail is dry. Trail passes through heavily burned area; beware of uneven surfaces and blowing ash." Take water and expect ash on a windy day; a dog through burned ground comes back filthy. Rocky, with stairs and steep unfenced drop-offs to the canyon — six-foot leash, not a flexi. The other named exception, the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail, is on the far side of the canyon: a long drive round via Crawford on a road that is itself seasonal, and not a realistic outing from a Montrose base for two nights.
trails.note_source: NPS Black Canyon pets page (nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/pets2.htm), fetched, verbatim: "Leashed pets are permitted in picnic areas, campgrounds, and parking lots, on paths to overlooks, and along roads currently open to vehicles"; "Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail"; "Leashes must be a maximum of six feet (1.8 m) in length"; "Pets are prohibited on all other hiking trails, inner canyon routes, within the wilderness, or on snowshoe/cross country skiing trails." Seasonal dog window from Colorado Trail Explorer's Rim Rock record (trails.colorado.gov/trails/rim-rock-6042), fetched, which names Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park as manager and publishes "Dogs 08/11-05/31", total length 0.8 mi, elevation 8,152-8,357 ft, delta 205 ft, dirt surface, hiking and snowshoeing permitted, bikes/horses/motor vehicles prohibited. Distance, gain and difficulty from Hiking Project (hikingproject.com/trail/7014561/rim-rock-nature-trail), fetched: 0.9 mi, 195 ft gain / 6 ft loss, high 8,343 ft, low 8,154 ft, Easy/Intermediate, "begins at the South Rim Visitor Center's southeast parking area" and "passes the Uplands Trail at around 0.75 miles before ending at the Campground Loop C". Road season from NPS operating hours (nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/hours.htm), fetched, verbatim: "The South Rim Road is usually open to vehicles from late-April to mid-November. In winter, the South Rim Road is open to Gunnison Point at the visitor center." Fire condition from NPS current conditions (nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm), fetched, last updated 5/29/2026. Review count 813 from the AllTrails result title; no star for this trail surfaced in any snippet — the 4.6 (1,099) figure that AllTrails publishes on its Black Canyon park page belongs to the composite "Oak Flat, Uplands, and Rim Rock Nature Trail Loop", which is a different listing and is not recorded here.
trails.name_note: NPS calls it the "Rim Rock Trail"; AllTrails, Hiking Project and Colorado Trail Explorer all title the same trail "Rim Rock Nature Trail". Same trail, same endpoints. The authority's name is used as the entry name.
trails.stats_note: The published figure is point-to-point, visitor center to South Rim Campground Loop C. Walked as an out-and-back from either end it is roughly double that. Colorado Trail Explorer's odd "Dogs 08/11-05/31 0.6mi" field appears to describe the dog-permitted mileage of the 0.8 mi record; no authority explains the discrepancy and none is asserted here.

Add one question to it: is the Rim Rock Trail open and is the dog closure still 11 Aug-31 May? Gunnison Point / Visitor Center overlook.entity: South Rim overlooks at the visitor center. No article. The Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park full text never names Gunnison Point; its one 'visitor center' mention is Curecanti NRA's, a different place.

black-canyon-gunnison.dogs_note: The dog is NOT stranded at Black Canyon on 8-10 Apr 2028. The Rim Rock Trail is inside the summer-closure-free window, inside the stretch of South Rim Road that stays open before the late-April opening, and open (though burned) after the 2025 fire. It is 0.9 mi and it is the whole of it — everything else on this card is closed to pets.

offroad.name: North Rim Road
offroad.distance: NPS publishes no length, only that "The last 7 miles of the park access road and the entire North Rim Drive road are unpaved gravel"
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS; no vehicle requirement or length limit published
offroad.season: LIKELY CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. NPS: "The North Rim is closed to vehicles in the winter and early spring" and "In winter and early spring, these roads are unplowed and the North Rim is closed to vehicles." The stop is 8-10 Apr 2028 — squarely in what NPS calls early spring. No exact opening date is published, which makes this a phone call rather than a plan.
offroad.note: The quiet rim. Gravel the whole way in, five overlooks reachable by car, and a fraction of the South Rim's traffic. Reached from CO-92: "turn west on Black Canyon Road approximately 3 miles south of Crawford" — which from a South Rim base is a long way round the canyon, roughly two hours. If it is open on these dates it is the best thing at this stop; if it is gated, the stop has essentially no unpaved driving.
offroad.source: NPS Black Canyon of the Gunnison — North Rim

offroad.name: East Portal Road
offroad.difficulty: paved, but a "winding, steep road down the canyon" at a 16% grade with tight curves; vehicles longer than 22 feet are prohibited
offroad.season: Closes seasonally for winter; the stop's 8-10 Apr 2028 dates sit near the reopening, and there is a further complication — the road was closed after the July 2025 South Rim Fire because of unstable slopes. Check https://www.nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm before counting on it.
offroad.note: Not dirt, so it is only half an offroad entry — but it is the only way to drive to the river inside the park, it drops 2,000 ft in a couple of miles, and the 22 ft limit makes it a truck-only trip in exactly the way the dirt roads are. Included for that reason, flagged for what it is.
offroad.source: NPS Black Canyon of the Gunnison — East Portal

black-canyon-gunnison.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail.
black-canyon-gunnison.dogs_source_note: DRIFT — TWO PROBLEMS. (1) Our card says there is ONE exception, the Rim Rock Trail. The page names TWO: "Leashed pets are only permitted on the Rim Rock Trail and on the North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail." (2) Our card says the Rim Rock exception "is itself closed to dogs in summer because of deer defending fawns" — the current page carries NO seasonal closure, no mention of deer or fawns, and no summer restriction of any kind. That claim is unsupported by the authority as of this check and should be re-verified or dropped. Note also the page lives at /pets2.htm; /pets.htm returns 404.

dog_trails_noted.North Rim Chasm View Nature Trail: Dog-legal and deliberately not added: it is on the NORTH rim, reached via Crawford, and is not a realistic day from the South Rim campground where the coach sits. Rim Rock is the practical exception and is on the card.
dog_trails_noted.Rim Chasm View Nature Trail: Same trail as the entry above; the rule's wording clips the leading 'North'.

joshua-tree.dogs: PROHIBITED on hiking trails and in the backcountry. Two paved exceptions — Oasis of Mara and Keys View — plus anywhere a vehicle can go, within 100 ft of roads, parking or campgrounds.

Geology Tour Road (truck).entity: The backcountry road in Joshua Tree. No article, and the Joshua Tree National Park full text never names it -- its two 'Geology' hits are a section heading and a cited book title.

joshua-tree.dogs_note: NPS: "pets are not allowed on hiking trails, in the backcountry, or in park buildings"; leashed pets may go no further than 100 ft from roads, picnic areas and campgrounds. The ONLY named exceptions are the paved Oasis of Mara and Keys View trails. Every other trail on this card is a walk the dog does not get.

trails.name: Hidden Valley
trails.note: Rock-enclosed valley loop, the classic first walk of the park. Distance, time and difficulty are NPS figures.

trails.name: Barker Dam
trails.note: Flat loop past the cattlemen's dam and a petroglyph panel; water behind the dam is seasonal and often absent.

trails.name: Cholla Cactus Garden
trails.note: AllTrails warns the segments of "jumping" cholla break off onto people and animals — stay on the boardwalk-width path, closed-toe shoes. Best at first light.

trails.name: Ryan Mountain
trails.distance: 3 mi out and back (NPS); AllTrails logs 2.9 mi
trails.season: AllTrails gives the good window as October–May; the 3–8 Jan stay is inside it.
trails.note: The one hard trail kept on this card, and it earns it on 11,474 reviews — the highest-reviewed trail in the park. Steady stair-stepped climb to the best 360° in Joshua Tree. Already named in the stop's activities.

trails.name: Oasis of Mara
trails.note: ONE OF ONLY TWO DOG-LEGAL WALKS IN THE PARK. Flat paved loop at park HQ in Twentynine Palms — NPS names it explicitly in the pet policy, and AllTrails calls it "the only officially designated dog-friendly trail in Joshua Tree". Leash 6 ft or shorter. Wheelchair and stroller passable.

trails.name: Keys View
trails.note: THE OTHER DOG-LEGAL WALK. NPS pet policy names "Oasis of Mara and Keys View trails" as the paved exceptions. Paved rim path over the Coachella Valley and the San Andreas fault; 5,185 ft, so it is cold and windy in January. Distance, time and difficulty are NPS; no AllTrails listing surfaced in search, so it carries no trail link.

trails.name: Skull Rock
trails.note: Figures are NPS. The named rock is a roadside stop; the trail is the loop behind it through the boulder field. No AllTrails URL surfaced in search — search returned only third-party guides — so no trail link rather than a constructed one.

offroad.name: Geology Tour Road
offroad.distance: 5.4 miles down to the loop, then a 6-mile one-way loop
offroad.difficulty: NPS requires high clearance and four-wheel drive; "mostly downhill but bumpy and sandy"
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published; the stop's 3-8 Jan 2028 dates are peak season for it.
offroad.note: The one to do first and the easiest genuine backcountry road in the park. Downhill on the way in, which means the sand is worked on the way out. Numbered interpretive stops the whole way.
offroad.source: NPS Joshua Tree NP — Backcountry Roads

offroad.name: Queen Valley Road network (with Big Horn Pass Road and O'Dell Road)
offroad.distance: 13.4 miles of interconnected road
offroad.difficulty: NPS lists it as suitable for two-wheel-drive vehicles — the only backcountry road in the park that is
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published.
offroad.note: A grid of easy graded roads through the densest Joshua tree stands in the park, between Hidden Valley and the Desert Queen Mine. The low-effort option on a day when nobody wants a technical drive.
offroad.source: NPS Joshua Tree NP — Backcountry Roads

offroad.name: Berdoo Canyon Road
offroad.distance: 11.5 miles
offroad.difficulty: high clearance and 4WD; NPS describes deep sand, sharp bedrock and rough boulders, and warns that pinch points "may deny full-size trucks"
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published.
offroad.note: Read the pinch-point warning before committing — this is the one road in the park NPS specifically says a full-size truck may not fit through, and it drops out of the park into Coachella Valley rather than looping back. It leaves the bottom of Geology Tour Road, so it is the natural extension of that day, not a separate one.
offroad.source: NPS Joshua Tree NP — Backcountry Roads

offroad.name: Covington Flat Roads
offroad.distance: 3.8 miles one-way to Eureka Peak, plus about 6.5 miles more of connecting road
offroad.difficulty: high clearance and 4WD; steep near the end
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published. Highest corner of the park, so the first place to hold snow after a winter storm.
offroad.note: The far west end of the park, reached from Yucca Valley rather than from Twentynine Palms — a longer drive out but it holds the largest Joshua trees in the park and the Eureka Peak view over Coachella Valley. Out-and-back, unlike the others.
offroad.source: NPS Joshua Tree NP — Backcountry Roads

NPS's pet page names Devil's Golf Course Road among the short list of places leashed pets are permitted, and this listing is that road out to the salt pinnacles. trails.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes Trail
trails.note: Open dune field near Stovepipe Wells with no fixed path - walk out as far as suits and turn round. Low winter sun is what makes it, which is exactly what the 28 Dec - 1 Jan window gives.
trails.note_source: NPS names 'Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes beyond the parking lot' among the places pets may not go.

trails.name: Natural Bridge Canyon Trail
trails.note: Gravel canyon walk to a natural rock span, off Badwater Road. Short enough to pair with Badwater and Artists Drive in a single outing.

trails.name: Artists Palette
trails.note: The short scramble up into the mineral-stained hills at the Artists Drive pullout. Twelve minutes for the best colour in the park, and best in late afternoon.

trails.name: Zabriskie Point
trails.note: The paved ramp to the overlook - eight minutes, and the classic badlands view. NPS names the Zabriskie Point paved trail specifically among the places closed to pets, so this is a walk taken without the dog even though it is a car park away.

offroad.name: Titus Canyon Road
offroad.distance: 27 miles, one way westbound, entered from Nevada Highway 374 about two miles east of the park boundary; the last 3 miles at the west end are two-way
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. High-clearance two-wheel drive recommended; 4WD may be needed after storms. Rough, steep and narrow, with the canyon narrows the tightest section. Allow 2–3 hours
offroad.season: RE-VERIFY BEFORE COUNTING ON IT. NPS scheduled a full closure of Titus Canyon Road from 1 October 2026 through at least 30 April 2027 for repairs, after an earlier repair-and-reopen cycle. The stop arrives 28 Dec 2027, eight months past the earliest stated reopening — so on the face of it there is no conflict, but 'at least' is doing real work in that sentence and this road has a recent history of extended closures. Beyond that, NPS says it is often closed for snow, mud or washouts, and December storms are exactly the cause.
offroad.note: Winter is the right season for it — summer travel is not advised and the canyon floods flash. One-way means committing: once past the entrance there is no turning back for 24 miles, the road is infrequently patrolled and there is no cell service. If the through route is closed, the two-way western three miles into the narrows is still driveable in a standard-clearance vehicle and is the best part of the canyon anyway.

not_a_route.problem: A status check, not a route. Nothing to link. Death Valley's road-status page is worth carrying on the stop, but as a note, not as a list item pretending to be a drive.

not_a_trail.problem: Not a trail — a 27-mile ONE-WAY backcountry driving route, east to west, starting from NV-374 two miles east of the park boundary; only the last 3 miles at the west end are two-way. NPS calls it the most popular back-country road in the park and requires two-wheel-drive high clearance as a minimum, with 4WD needed after weather. It belongs in offroad (or scenic drives), not the trails box. 2–3 hours to drive.
not_a_trail.season: SEASONAL — VERIFY BEFORE THE STOP. NPS scheduled a FULL CLOSURE of Titus Canyon Road from 1 October 2026 through at least 30 April 2027 for repairs. Arrive 28 Dec 2027 is after that published window, but the road is also routinely closed by snow, mud and washouts and is prone to flash flooding — never enter with rain threatening. Check park road status on the day.
not_a_trail.note_source: NPS Death Valley Titus Canyon page; Pahrump Valley Times and 8NewsNow reopening/closure reporting

Permitted in campgrounds, turnouts, picnic areas and on roads — and in the surrounding Bridger-Teton National Forest, which is the workaround here.

sequoia-kings-canyon.dogs: PROHIBITED on ALL trails, explicitly including the paved ones — NPS names the General Sherman Tree Trail, Big Trees Trail and Grant Tree Trail. Pets are allowed only in parking lots, on paved roads, in campgrounds and picnic areas. Every one of this stop's five trails is closed to the dog, including the Christmas ones.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Moro Rock/Crescent Meadow Road spur off Generals Highway
scenicDrives_patch.note: The spur from Giant Forest Museum past Tunnel Log to Moro Rock and Crescent Meadow. Even in summer NPS prohibits single vehicles over 22 ft and ANY vehicle towing — so this was never a coach road, and it is a truck day with the pickup unhitched. In summer it is shuttle-only at weekends and holidays.
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASONAL CONFLICT ON A HARD-ANCHORED STOP. The Moro Rock/Crescent Meadow Road CLOSES TO VEHICLES as soon as snow accumulates and is not plowed, typically staying shut until around Memorial Day weekend. Arrive 23 Dec 2027 — the Christmas anchor cannot move, so plan on the road being closed to driving. It becomes a marked winter trail for walking, snowshoeing and cross-country skiing from Giant Forest Museum, which is the realistic version of this outing. The Moro Rock stairway is also closed when snow and ice make the exposed granite steps unsafe. Generals Highway between Ash Mountain and Giant Forest is the winter access road and is usually open but closes in storms.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS SEKI vehicle length limits page; NPS 'Crescent Meadow Road winter trail'; SEKI winter trip planners

offroad.name: South Fork Road
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "High clearance vehicles recommended"
offroad.season: OPEN — and it is the only unpaved road in either park that is not seasonally closed across 23–27 Dec 2027. NPS says it is "typically open year-round", with the caveat that it becomes slippery during rain or snow.
offroad.note: Unpaved beyond the park entrance, running from Three Rivers up the South Fork of the Kaweah to South Fork Campground. NPS's road-conditions page currently carries an active alert that it is accessible but not all the way to the original trailhead parking. Its length is not published.
offroad.source: NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Parks

offroad.name: Mineral King Road
offroad.distance: 30 mi from Three Rivers, a 1 hour 30 minute drive
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "extremely narrow, steep, winding, and unpaved in some areas"
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES — shut, with no negotiating it. NPS: "generally open from the Wednesday before Memorial Day to the last Wednesday in October", then it "closes at the park boundary to general vehicle traffic for the winter season". 23–27 Dec 2027 is deep inside the closure.
offroad.note: The classic Sequoia backcountry drive and the reason people come to Three Rivers with a capable vehicle; it simply does not exist as an option in December. Kept on the card flagged rather than deleted, so the reason is visible. NPS adds that RVs and trailers are not advised and not permitted in the area's campgrounds — irrelevant here since it would be the truck, but it is the published restriction.
offroad.source: NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Parks

offroad.name: Sequoia NF / Giant Sequoia NM — Western Divide and Kern River winter road closure order
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. The 2025–26 order, Forest Order No. 0513-25-12, ran 4 December 2025 through 15 June 2026 and closed 76 named Forest Roads to "any type of motorized wheeled vehicle". An equivalent order is issued every year and starts late November or early December — the 2024–25 order ran 23 Nov 2024 – 15 Jun 2025 — so the whole Western Divide network south of the park should be assumed gated across 23–27 Dec 2027.
offroad.note: The only exemptions are a Forest Service permit FS-7700-48, officials on duty, and tracked over-snow vehicles where there is at least twelve inches of snow on the road. Roads named in the order include Dennison Peak 19S05, Mountain Home North 20S87, the Balch Park area roads, Quaking Aspen 21S61 and Dome Rock 21S69. Recorded so the December answer is on the card: the forest roads behind Three Rivers are shut, and the Kings Canyon Scenic Byway to Cedar Grove is separately closed from mid-November to late April.
offroad.source: USFS Sequoia National Forest — Forest Order 0513-25-12
