Ring the Wilderness Information Center or the Methow Valley Ranger District on (509) 996-4000 before taking the dog up Maple Pass. (2) WA-20 over Washington and Rainy Passes is a seasonal highway that WSDOT closes for the winter — normally well after these dates, but the whole card except Goat Peak depends on it.

Skate Creek Road scenic drive (FR 52).entity: Skate Creek Road (FR 52), Gifford Pinchot NF

trails.name: Packwood Lake Trail
trails.was: Packwood Lake Trailhead — a trailhead
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.

trails.name: Snowgrass Flats and Goat Lake Loop
trails.was: Snowgrass Flat Trail — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: Seven listed routes reach Snowgrass Flat; this is the classic loop. A 12.4 mi day in the Goat Rocks — arrival is 9-16 Oct, when the high country can already be under snow.

trails.name: Naches Peak Loop Trail
trails.season: June through October per AllTrails, so the 9-16 Oct stay is at the very end of the window. The real constraint is SR 410 over Chinook Pass, which WSDOT closes for the winter once the snow comes - check it is still open before driving round.
trails.note: PARTIAL DOG ACCESS, AND THE ONLY DOG ACCESS AT MOUNT RAINIER. NPS prohibits pets on ALL Mount Rainier trails with one exception, the Pacific Crest Trail - and the eastern half of this loop IS the PCT. NPS states dogs 'are NOT allowed on the non-PCT sections of the Naches Peak Loop Trail within the park', so the dog can walk the PCT half from Chinook Pass and must turn back rather than complete the circuit. The most-reviewed trail on this card by a wide margin.
trails.note_source: NPS Mount Rainier pets page, fetched: 'Pets are prohibited on ALL Mount Rainier National Park trails and wilderness areas'; 'Dogs on a leash no longer than 6 feet are permitted on the Pacific Crest Trail'; and the explicit Naches Peak Loop carve-out quoted above.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets at Mount Rainier
other_links.note: Authority. The PCT is the single exception to a park-wide trail ban.

other_links.label: NPS — Naches Peak Loop Trail
other_links.note: Park page for the loop, showing which half lies outside the park boundary on the PCT.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails files this listing under 'near Goose Prairie, Washington' rather than Packwood; it is the Tipsoo Lake / Chinook Pass loop on Rainier's eastern boundary, about an hour from Packwood by road.

trails.name: Silver Falls Loop
trails.season: Ohanapecosh is low - around 2,000 ft - so this is one of the few Rainier trails still reliably open in the second week of October.
trails.note: NO DOG, AND THE CARD MUST SAY SO. AllTrails' own summary of this listing calls it 'a dog-friendly trail' and says reviewers mention hiking it with dogs. That is wrong and it is the dangerous direction of wrong: the trail is inside Mount Rainier National Park, where NPS prohibits pets on every trail without exception but the PCT. The walk itself is the Ohanapecosh River loop to Silver Falls, eleven miles from Packwood and the closest good hike to the stop.
trails.note_source: NPS Mount Rainier pets page, fetched: 'Pets are prohibited on ALL Mount Rainier National Park trails and wilderness areas.' Distance 'all in just three miles' is Washington Trails Association's figure, not AllTrails' - AllTrails' own mileage did not surface in the snippet.

other_links.label: Washington Trails Association — Silver Falls Loop
other_links.note: Source of the three-mile figure and the description of the Ohanapecosh River section.

trails.name: Ohanapecosh and Stafford Falls Trail
trails.note: The longer river walk out of the same Ohanapecosh corner of the park, past Stafford Falls. Low, forested and shoulder-season-proof. Pets prohibited, as everywhere in the park off the PCT.
trails.note_source: NPS Mount Rainier pets page, fetched, as above.
trails.stats_note: This listing surfaced on the plp.alltrails.com mirror; the path is copied verbatim from that result and only the host normalised to www.

trails.name: Dry Creek Trail
trails.season: March through November per AllTrails - a longer window than anything inside the park, which is the point of it.
trails.note: Gifford Pinchot National Forest, not the park - which is what makes it dog-legal. Graded Challenging, but on a seven-night stay it is the long walk the dog can actually come on.
trails.note_source: Gifford Pinchot NF, already recorded on this stop: dogs must be 'on a six-foot leash at all times when in developed recreation areas and on interpretive trails'; 'There are no leash requirements for most of the forest.' Individual trailheads can post their own rule, so check the trailhead sign.

offroad.name: Skate Creek Road (FR 52)
offroad.distance: 23 miles east–west between Packwood and Ashford, joining Hwy 12 to Hwy 706
offroad.difficulty: not published as an offroad grade. Nominally paved, but low-maintenance for years — slumps, potholes and broken edges rather than technical terrain
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, BUT CLOSE TO THE EDGE. Gifford Pinchot gates FR 52 in winter once snow gets too deep to drive safely, roughly November through April. The stop arrives 9 Oct 2027 — open, with about three to four weeks of margin before the usual gating.
offroad.note: This is the back way to the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier and cuts a long detour off the highway route. Being paved it sits on the line between scenic drive and offroad; it is kept here because the surface condition makes it a truck road in practice, and Trails Offroad carries it as a scout route (https://www.trailsoffroad.com/US/washington/scout-routes/670-fs-52-skate-creek). It has been closed outright by landslide in the recent past — check status with Gifford Pinchot rather than assuming it is through.

not_a_route.problem: A thing to check, not a route. There is nothing to link and nothing to drive — it belongs as a note on the stop, or as a reminder attached to the routes it affects.

not_a_route.entry: Snowgrass Flats day hike, Goat Rocks Wilderness
not_a_route.problem: A hike, and one inside designated wilderness where motor vehicles are prohibited outright. Belongs in the trails box. The offroad-relevant part is the forest road to the Berry Patch trailhead, which is a separate entry if it is wanted.

packwood.authority: USDA Forest Service — Gifford Pinchot National Forest
packwood.dogs: Gifford Pinchot NF: dogs must be "on a six-foot leash at all times when in developed recreation areas and on interpretive trails". "There are no leash requirements for most of the forest", though the forest recommends a leash for safety, and "Dogs are NOT allowed to chase game animals."
packwood.dogs_exception: Individual trailheads can carry their own leash requirement — the forest posts it on the trailhead page, so check the specific trail before assuming the off-leash default.

official_links.label: Dogs in the National Forest — Gifford Pinchot NF (USFS)

packwood.stats_note: 'Packwood Lake Trail and Pipeline Road Loop' (7.8 mi, moderately challenging, 4.7 from 213) surfaced and was deliberately NOT added: it is the same lake by a second route and would read as a duplicate of the Packwood Lake Trail already on the card.
packwood.dogs_source_quote: National Forest guidelines require that dogs be on a six-foot leash at all times when in developed recreation areas (means an area which has been improved for recreation) and on interpretive trails.
packwood.dogs_source_note: Minor drift: the page now carries a parenthetical definition our card omits — "(means an area which has been improved for recreation)". The other two quotes are exact: "There are no leash requirements for most of the forest." and "Dogs are NOT allowed to chase game animals."

Johnston Ridge Observatory / SR-504 — cu.entity: Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument

Ape Cave lava tube.entity: Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument

Hummocks Trail.entity: Hummocks Trail, Mount St. Helens NVM

trails.name: Ape Cave Trail
trails.was: Ape Cave — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: Trail No. 239 inside the lava tube — the longest continuous lava tube in the continental US at 2.5 miles, and a National Recreation Trail taking 170,000 visitors a year. Timed-entry permits apply in season.

trails.name: Hummocks Trail
trails.was: Hummocks Trailhead — a trailhead
trails.note_source: Interpretive loop through the debris-avalanche landscape of the 18 May 1980 eruption.

trails.name: Sediment Dam Loop
trails.note: Loop at the Toutle River sediment retention structure - the engineering answer to the 1980 lahar, and a short walk at low elevation that works in the third week of October.

trails.name: Mt St Helens Forest Learning Trail
trails.note: Short interpretive loop off SR 504 at the Forest Learning Center, well below the road closure and well below the snow. Forty minutes, and it explains the blast zone better than the drive does.

alltrails.name: Mt St Helens Forest Learning Trail

trails.name: Goat Marsh Lake via Toutle Trail
trails.note: The long option on the mountain's quiet south-west side, out to Goat Marsh Lake through old growth the blast never touched. Nine miles, so a whole day out of a three-night stop - but it is the only substantial moderate walk here that does not depend on the SR 504 corridor.

alltrails.name: Goat Marsh Lake via Toutle Trail

silver-lake.authority: USDA Forest Service — Gifford Pinchot National Forest / Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument
silver-lake.dogs: Gifford Pinchot NF: dogs must be "on a six-foot leash at all times when in developed recreation areas and on interpretive trails"; "There are no leash requirements for most of the forest", and "Dogs are NOT allowed to chase game animals." Pets are listed among the items prohibited inside Ape Cave, and the site advises "Please leave your pets safely at home."
silver-lake.dogs_exception: The lava tube is closed to pets and there is nowhere safe to leave a dog while you are underground — Ape Cave is a day out without the dog, or not at all. The monument order also bars pets at the Johnston Ridge Observatory building, amphitheatre, plaza deck and Eruption Trail; leashed dogs are exempted everywhere else in that area.

official_links.label: Dogs in the National Forest — Gifford Pinchot NF (USFS)
Mount St. Helens Volcanic Monument Restrictions (USFS)

silver-lake.stats_note: Ape Cave, already on this card, is closed to pets and there is nowhere to leave a dog while you are underground - that is recorded on the stop already and none of the three above changes it. All three are dog-legal in principle under Gifford Pinchot's general rule, but the monument order carries its own restrictions around the Johnston Ridge facilities, so `dogs` is left absent rather than asserted.

offroad.name: Forest Road 81
offroad.difficulty: USFS: "While mostly paved, be prepared for several miles of gravel (between Forest Road 830 and 8123) and a road that is sometimes very rough." Trailers are not advised over Red Rock Pass.
offroad.season: No calendar gate published for FR 81 itself. Gifford Pinchot's forest-wide statement applies: "Most forest roads are not plowed in winter and some roads may be impassable for cars without high clearance and four-wheel drive or chains." The stop is 16-19 Oct 2027 — normally still open, but this is the south flank of a Cascade volcano and an early storm decides it.
offroad.note: The south-side approach to Mount St Helens from Cougar, past Kalama Horse Camp and Red Rock Pass to FR 830 and Climber's Bivouac. Closest real gravel to the Silver Lake base, roughly an hour round the mountain's west side.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 81

offroad.name: Forest Road 83 to Lava Canyon
offroad.difficulty: USFS: "Paved, but rough in places"
offroad.season: OPEN ON THESE DATES, with the gate close behind. USFS: "Forest Road 83 is closed and gated at Marble Mountain Sno-Park Dec. 1 - March 31 for winter recreation." The stop is 16-19 Oct 2027, six weeks ahead of the gate.
offroad.note: The other south-side road, and the one that reaches the good stuff: Ape Cave via spur 8303, June Lake, the Lahar Viewpoint, and the Ape Canyon and Lava Canyon trailheads. Paved rather than dirt, so it earns its place here on the gate and the roughness rather than the surface.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 83

offroad.name: Forest Road 99 to Windy Ridge
offroad.distance: 16 miles
offroad.difficulty: USFS calls it narrow with rough surfaces and "not appropriate for trailers"; "repairs and gravel stretches are common". A trailer drop point exists at Wakepish Sno-Park.
offroad.season: OPEN, but only just. USFS gives the season as "July 1st - Nov 30th" and the stop is 16-19 Oct 2027 — inside it, with about six weeks to spare. Snow can shut it early; Gifford Pinchot's seasonal-closures alert page is where the gate status is posted.
offroad.note: Ten interpretive stops ending at Windy Ridge, looking straight into the crater across Spirit Lake — the best view of the 1980 blast zone that exists from a road. The catch is the approach: FR 99 is reached from Randle via FR 25, on the far side of the mountain from Silver Lake, so this is a full day of driving, not an afternoon. The Silver Lake base's own road, SR 504 to Johnston Ridge, is paved and is a different trip.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 99

silver-lake.dogs_source_quote: There are no leash requirements for most of the forest.
silver-lake.dogs_source_note: DRIFT — the Ape Cave half of our card merges two separate statements. Both are real and both are on https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/giffordpinchot/recreation/ape-cave-interpretive-site, but they are different rules: "Pets" is the first item in the list introduced by "In order to protect the fragile cave environment, the following are prohibited inside Ape Cave:", whereas "Please leave your pets safely at home." belongs to a hot-car warning — "Please be advised the inside of cars get very hot during summer months. Please leave your pets safely at home." Our card reads the second as part of the cave prohibition; it is advice about leaving a dog in the vehicle while you tour the cave, which is the practical problem at this stop.

trails.name: Hall of Mosses Trail
trails.was: Hoh Rainforest Visitor Center / Hall of Mosses — a visitor centre and a trail in one entry

trails.name: Sol Duc Falls Trail
trails.was: Sol Duc Falls Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Rialto Beach to Hole-in-the-Wall
trails.was: Rialto Beach — no url
trails.note_source: No formal trail — you walk the beach itself to Split Rock and Hole-in-the-Wall. Tide-dependent, and this is one of the six Olympic trails where DOGS ARE PERMITTED (Rialto to Ellen Creek).

trails.name: July Creek Loop Trail
trails.season: Reachable in late October — US 101 and the Lake Quinault North Shore Road are low-elevation and open year-round; the 25-29 Oct 2027 stay carries no seasonal block, only the drive
trails.note: PET-LEGAL, named in the NPS list, leash 6 ft. On the north shore of Lake Quinault, branching from the July Creek Picnic Area trail. NO PUBLISHED LENGTH — NPS names the trail and describes it only as "A loop branching from the July Creek Picnic Area trail", and it appears in no trail database. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed; this is the same recorded absence the olympic stop already carries for the same trail, and nothing here contradicts it. Worth knowing before driving: from Forks it is about 68 miles / 1 hour 20 minutes each way south on US 101, plus the run in along the North Shore Road — a half day, not an evening walk. The nearer dog-legal ground from a Forks base, named in the same NPS rule, is the Kalaloch stretch of beach between the Hoh and Quinault Reservations, which is on the way south and needs no detour.
trails.note_source: NPS Olympic pets page (nps.gov/olym/planyourvisit/pets.htm) names "July Creek Loop Trail (North shore of Lake Quinault)" among the permitted trails and states "Pets are not permitted on any trails not listed above", leash no longer than 6 feet — this stop's own `dogs` field already quotes it. NPS place page (nps.gov/places/000/july-creek-loop-trail-trailhead.htm), fetched: carries only "A loop branching from the July Creek Picnic Area trail" and no length, surface or difficulty. NPS day-hiking page lists the trail by the same name. A further search under the exact name returned only the NPS day-hiking page and two third-party dog-travel guides, none of which publishes a length — no AllTrails, WTA, Komoot or TrailLink listing exists. Length, difficulty and time are unknown and are left blank deliberately. Forks-to-Quinault driving distance is not published by any authority; three independent route calculators agree at 68 miles / 1 h 16-23 min (trippy.com, distancesfrom.com, fromto.travel), which is why it is given as a rounded figure rather than a precise one.

other_links.label: NPS — July Creek Loop Trail Trailhead
other_links.note: The only page the authority publishes for it. No length given.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Olympic
other_links.note: The rule that makes it legal, and the closing sentence that shuts every trail it does not name.

trails.call: Olympic NP Wilderness Information Center, 360-565-3100 — ask the length of the July Creek Loop. No authority publishes it, and it is one of only six pet-legal trails in the park. Already logged against the olympic stop; the same call answers both.

forks.authority: National Park Service — Olympic National Park
forks.dogs: Olympic names its pet-friendly routes and closes the rest: "Pets are not permitted on any trails not listed above." The listed trails are Peabody Creek, Madison Falls, Spruce Railroad and July Creek Loop; the listed beaches are "Rialto Beach parking lot to Ellen Creek (1/2 mile)" and the Kalaloch beaches between the Hoh and Quinault Reservations. Leash no longer than 6 feet.
forks.dogs_exception: Rialto is half open: leashed pets may walk from the parking lot to Ellen Creek, about half a mile. Hole-in-the-Wall is a further mile north, past the closure. Hall of Mosses and Sol Duc Falls are closed outright. The nearest pet-legal trail is the Spruce Railroad on Lake Crescent.

scenicDrives_patch.name: La Push Road (SR-110) to Third Beach and La Push
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: La Push Road (SR-110) out to Third Beach/La Push
scenicDrives_patch.note: SR-110 leaves US-101 1.5 mi north of Forks and runs 14 mi west along the Quileute and Sol Duc rivers to La Push. Third Beach parking is on the left at about mile 13; the beach itself is a 1.5 mi walk in through hemlock and spruce to Strawberry Bay. Mora Road branches off it and runs about 5 mi to Rialto Beach.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No seasonal gate — but VERIFY THE MORA BRANCH. In 2026 the park closed Mora Road past Mora Campground to the Rialto Beach parking area from mid-July for storm-damage repairs, expected back 15 Oct 2026. That is a 2026 project, not a 2027 one, and should be clear well before the 25 Oct 2027 arrival; confirm rather than assume. Expect rain in any month — this coast takes over 100 in a year.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS Visiting Mora and Rialto Beach; 2026 Mora Road closure reporting

forks.dogs_note: Forks and olympic are two bases on the same park and share the same six pet-legal trails. This entry is deliberately identical to the one on the olympic card, down to the missing length, so the two do not disagree at a trailhead. What differs is the drive: from Port Angeles July Creek is roughly two hours, from Forks about 68 miles / 1 h 20.

offroad.name: Lake Quinault Loop — North Shore Road and South Shore Road
offroad.distance: 31 miles round the lake and the lower Quinault River — that figure is from local sources, not from NPS, which describes it only as "a scenic loop drive"
offroad.difficulty: not published by NPS or the Forest Service. Part-gravel; the north shore is Olympic National Park, most of the south shore is Olympic National Forest.
offroad.season: No published gate — this is low, wet rainforest rather than high country. The risk on 25-29 Oct 2027 dates is washout, not snow: Olympic National Forest warns "Forest roads are prone to flooding and washouts. Never attempt to cross a road washout as you could easily get trapped."
offroad.note: Honest framing: this is the only named, published unpaved driving loop found within reach of Forks, and it is about an hour and a half south. Olympic National Forest's Pacific Ranger District has a large road network — a third-party tally puts it at 261.5 miles of motorized routes — but the Forest publishes no named backcountry driving route for it, only maintenance levels ("Level 2 roads require a high clearance vehicle") and a Motor Vehicle Use Map. Nothing was invented to fill the gap. Note also that the Olympic coast beaches are National Park and closed to vehicles — the beach driving on this leg is at Long Beach, not here.
offroad.source: NPS Olympic NP — Visiting Quinault (mileage from quinaultrainforest.com)

forks.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not permitted - on any trails not listed above, in public buildings, on interpretive walks, or in the wilderness.
forks.dogs_source_note: DRIFT (truncation, ours not theirs): our card quotes the closing sentence as "Pets are not permitted on any trails not listed above." The page's actual sentence continues "...in public buildings, on interpretive walks, or in the wilderness." Everything else on the card checks out verbatim, including "Rialto Beach parking lot to Ellen Creek (1/2 mile)" and the 6 ft leash.

trails.name: Discovery Trail
trails.was: Discovery Trail (Long Beach trailhead) — a trailhead
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.

trails.name: Coastal Forest Loop Trail
trails.season: AllTrails gives March through October; the 29 Oct - 2 Nov stay catches the last days of it, and this is forest rather than exposed headland, so it is the sheltered option if the razor-clam week turns wet.
trails.note: Old-growth spruce loop inside Cape Disappointment State Park, a mile from the Discovery Trail already on the card.
trails.note_source: Washington State Parks lists Cape Disappointment State Park's rule as 'Dogs Allowed on Leash'.

other_links.label: Washington State Parks — Cape Disappointment
other_links.note: Managing authority; source of the leashed-dogs rule.

trails.name: Lighthouse Keepers Trail
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Thirteen minutes out to the lighthouse keepers' quarters above the Columbia bar - the short evening walk on a clam-dig day, and the highest-rated trail in the park.
trails.note_source: Washington State Parks: Cape Disappointment State Park, 'Dogs Allowed on Leash'.

trails.name: Black Lake
trails.season: January through October per AllTrails - the stay is right at the edge, and the note that matters is that this is a lake loop that gets soft in wet weather.
trails.note: Freshwater lake loop behind Ilwaco. The flat inland alternative when the surf is too much.

trails.name: Benson Beach Trail
trails.note: Short link from the Cape Disappointment campground out onto Benson Beach - the walk from the door if the coach ends up in that park rather than in town.
trails.note_source: Washington State Parks: Cape Disappointment State Park, 'Dogs Allowed on Leash'.

long-beach.dogs: The Discovery Trail runs into Cape Disappointment State Park, and Washington State Parks lists the park's rule as dogs allowed on leash; the City of Long Beach publishes nothing extra for its half of the trail.
long-beach.stats_note: Greenhead Slough Trail (1.1 mi, easy, 10 reviews) also surfaced near Ilwaco and was left off: its AllTrails listing states dogs are not allowed, and it adds nothing the four above do not.

offroad.name: Long Beach Peninsula beach driving — Bolstad Avenue to Oysterville Gap Road
offroad.distance: 13.5 miles, the longest open-all-year section on the peninsula
offroad.difficulty: not graded. Washington State Parks: "stay on hard-packed sand" to avoid damage or getting stuck; ATVs and UTVs are prohibited outright, street-legal vehicles are not.
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, AND THE TIMING IS FAVOURABLE. The peninsula's seasonal bans run 15 April to the day after Labor Day; the stop is 29 Oct - 2 Nov 2027, well outside them. Better still, the two closures that apply the rest of the year are lifted "during any recreational razor clam season" — which is exactly what this stop is anchored to. On these dates the whole peninsula opens up: the 2.7 miles north of Oysterville Gap Road, the 1.4 miles between Bolstad and Seaview Gap Road, the 4 miles at Leadbetter Point / Willapa NWR and the 2.5 miles at the North Jetty and Benson Beach all become legally driveable during a dig.
offroad.note: Washington beaches are legal highways and this is the real off-pavement answer at this stop — not a forest road but 13.5 miles of hard sand you can drive at 25 mph with the ocean on one side. Pedestrians always have right of way, and razor-clam diggers will be everywhere on these dates, which is the point. Do not park on the beach approaches. The state parks map is the authority on which section is which; the governing rules are WAC 352-37.
offroad.source: Washington State Parks — Beach Driving Rules, Long Beach Peninsula Area (map) and Seashore Conservation Area rules

cannon-beach.authority: Oregon State Parks — Ecola State Park
cannon-beach.dogs: Ecola State Park, asked whether pets are allowed: "Yes. Pets must be on a leash not more than six feet long, and kept under physical control at all times." Statewide, pets are allowed in all Oregon state parks except Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP and named trails at Silver Falls.
cannon-beach.dogs_exception: Snowy-plover beach closures (15 Mar–15 Sep) can shut a beach to pets even on a leash; this stop is outside that window.

offroad.name: Ocean shore, Peter Iredale Road to the Gearhart beach ramp
offroad.season: Open to motor vehicles "at any time" — the only dated Clatsop County restriction is a 12:01 p.m.–midnight closure from 1 May through 15 Sep, which does not touch 2–6 Nov 2027. No conflict.
offroad.note: Hard sand beach driving between the Peter Iredale Road approach in Fort Stevens State Park and the beach ramp at Gearhart. Everything south of the Gearhart ramp to the Tillamook County line — all of Gearhart, Seaside and Cannon Beach itself — is closed to vehicles year-round except vehicles towing dory boats between Sunset Drive and Warren Way, with access from Warren Way only.
offroad.source: Oregon Parks & Recreation Dept — OAR 736-024-0005 (rule text via oregon.public.law)

offroad.name: Ocean shore, Columbia River south jetty to Peter Iredale Road
offroad.season: Closed to vehicles between 12:01 p.m. and midnight from 1 May through 15 Sep only. On 2–6 Nov 2027 the segment carries no time restriction.
offroad.note: The northern half of the Fort Stevens beach, running up to the Columbia south jetty. The same rule sets a Clatsop County beach speed limit (OAR 736-024-0010); the Director of State Parks can issue special permits for otherwise restricted areas.
offroad.source: Oregon Parks & Recreation Dept — OAR 736-024-0005 (rule text via oregon.public.law)

offroad.name: Nicolai Mountain OHV Area, Clatsop State Forest
offroad.season: ODF publishes no seasonal gate date for Nicolai Mountain on its motorized-trails page. Unverified for 2–6 Nov 2027.
offroad.note: ODF describes it as carrying "four-wheel drive trails" and says side-by-side riders will enjoy "the bulk of the trail network in the Nicolai Mountain OHV Area". ODF does NOT publish whether a full-size street-legal 4x4 pickup may use the trails, nor a trail mileage, nor a difficulty grade — one call settles all three. Area contact Reid Brown, 503-536-3879. It sits inland near Clatskanie, a long way east of Cannon Beach.

cannon-beach.dogs_source_quote: Yes. Pets must be on a leash not more than six feet long, and kept under physical control at all times.
cannon-beach.dogs_source_note: Confirmed as the Ecola State Park profile page, and the sentence is verbatim as our card has it. The statewide exception list (Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP, Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls) is confirmed separately at https://stateparks.oregon.gov/index.cfm?do=v.page&id=79.

Catherine Creek Loop.entity: The Catherine Creek recreation area in the Columbia River Gorge NSA, Klickitat County, WA. No article: 'Catherine Creek' on Wikipedia is a 32-mile creek in NORTHEASTERN OREGON (Grande Ronde valley) and is a different watercourse entirely — rejected on identity. The Columbia River Gorge article's raw text never mentions Catherine Creek.

trails.name: Wahclella Falls Trail
trails.was: Wahclella Falls Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Dog Mountain Trail
trails.was: Dog Mountain Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: Permit required on spring weekends for the wildflower season; the stop is late October, outside that.

trails.name: Catherine Creek Arch Loop
trails.season: OPEN, BUT OFF ITS BEST. Low-elevation Gorge oak grassland, walkable year-round. The reason people come is the wildflowers, which peak mid-April through May. Arrive 6 Nov 2027 — bare oak, brown grass, big Gorge views, no flowers.
trails.note: 'Catherine Creek' as written was the recreation area, not a route — it holds several trails. This is the signature one, past a waterfall and up through rocks and oaks to the natural arch. No fee or permit. Dogs allowed on leash; BIKES ARE NOT. Heavy poison oak — long trousers. The paved 1 mi Universal Access Loop is the flat alternative on the other side of Old Highway 8.
trails.note_source: USFS Columbia River Gorge NSA Catherine Creek page; Friends of the Columbia Gorge; AllTrails indexed snippet

other_links.label: Catherine Creek Universal Access Trail (1 mi paved, 236 reviews)

trails.name: The Labyrinth to Coyote Wall Loop
trails.note: The nearest serious walk to camp - the trailhead is minutes east of White Salmon on WA-14 - and the most striking thing in this half of the Gorge: a curving basalt wall above the river, reached through the Labyrinth's oak groves, seasonal waterfalls and rock outcrops. WTA calls it a year-round hike, which is exactly what a 6-11 November stay needs. Open oak and grassland means the views work in flat winter light, unlike the forest hikes further west.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'The Labyrinth to Coyote Wall Loop is a loop trail that covers 6.8 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,453 ft. It takes about 3.5-4 hr to complete', and 'considered a moderate hike'. Cross-checks: Oregon Hikers 7.3 mi / 1,790 ft / moderate / all year; Trailforks 7 mi / 1,547 ft; Komoot 6.3 mi / 1,381 ft / moderate. WTA: 'This year-round hike offers great views of the Columbia River Gorge along with enchanting stands of oak, cascading waterfalls, dramatic basalt outcroppings, and profuse wildflowers in the spring.'
trails.stats_note: No review count was returned for this specific listing in any search read this pass. The neighbouring 'Coyote Wall Loop' listing shows 4.7 from 3,636 reviews on the AllTrails Columbia River Gorge NSA page, which is the area's popularity signal but is a different route and is not recorded as this trail's rating.

other_links.label: WTA - Coyote Wall / The Labyrinth Loop
other_links.note: Washington Trails Association. The year-round note comes from here.

trails.dogs_note: Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area, USFS. No published pet rule was read this pass.

trails.name: Cape Horn Loop Trail
trails.note: The Washington-side counterpart to the Oregon waterfall hikes already on the card, and better in November than most of them: a loop that climbs to a viewpoint about 1,200 ft above the Columbia, drops to the river through lava-rock fields and basalt towers, and passes Cape Horn Falls on the way. About 45 min west of camp on WA-14. Reviewers warn of rocky sections and blackberry thorns - long sleeves and long trousers.
trails.season: The lower half of this loop carries a spring closure for peregrine falcon nesting, commonly published as 1 Feb to 15 Jul. NOT VERIFIED against a Forest Service page this pass, and it does not affect a 6-11 November stay either way - noted so a future date change does not walk into it.
trails.note_source: AllTrails Cape Horn point-of-interest page: 'the best place to hike near Cape Horn is Cape Horn Loop Trail, which has a 4.6 star rating from 4,572 reviews. This trail is 6.7 mi long with an elevation gain of 1,338 ft.' Trail page titles showed 4,533 and 4,578. Route description and the thorn warning from the AllTrails trail page and WTA. A shorter point-to-point listing, Cape Horn Trail: East to West, is moderate, 3.8 mi, 928 ft, 2-2.5 hr, about 1,550 reviews.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 4,533, 4,572 (with the 4.6 star) and 4,578. Ordering signal only.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Cape Horn Trail: East to West (shorter version)
other_links.note: 3.8 mi point to point, 928 ft, 2-2.5 hr, moderate. The half-day option.

trails.name: Latourell Falls Loop
trails.note: The most-reviewed walk within reach of this stop by a wide margin, and short. Latourell is the third tallest waterfall in the Gorge, a 249 ft plume straight off a wall of columnar basalt with the yellow lichen that makes it recognisable, and the loop takes in the upper falls too. Guy W. Talbot State Park on the Oregon side of the river, at the west end of the Historic Columbia River Highway. Early November is high water and the loop is open all year.
trails.note_source: AllTrails Latourell Falls point-of-interest page: 'the best place to hike near Latourell Falls is Latourell Falls Loop, which has a 4.8 star rating from 11,712 reviews. This trail is 2.2 mi long with an elevation gain of 606 ft.' Trail page title showed 11,757 and describes it as 'a moderately difficult trek through Guy W. Talbot State Park to Upper Latourell Falls'. Hikespeak gives 2.3 mi / 475 ft; Oregon Tails 2.3 mi.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Latourell Falls and Upper Latourell Falls are within Guy Talbot State Park, managed by Oregon State Parks. No permits are required. Dogs must be on a leash.
trails.dogs_note: Friends of the Columbia Gorge, quoting the managing authority (Oregon State Parks) and matching OPRD's statewide six-foot leash rule. No permit needed, which is worth knowing next to Dog Mountain.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 11,712 (with the 4.8 star) and 11,757. A separate short listing, 'Latourell Falls', is a different 0.5 km viewpoint walk with about 1,650 reviews - not this one.

white-salmon.authority: USDA Forest Service — Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area
white-salmon.dogs: Catherine Creek trailhead: "Dogs on leash in Catherine Creek planning area year round. Dogs on leash in Coyote/Burdoin planning areas December 1st through June 30th." Leash requirements in the Gorge are set site by site rather than area-wide.
white-salmon.dogs_exception: The Gorge publishes its dog rule per recreation site, not per forest, so silence on Dog Mountain and Wahclella here means unresearched, not permitted. Dog Mountain also needs a timed-entry permit on spring weekends.

official_links.label: Catherine Creek Trailhead — Columbia River Gorge NSA (USFS)

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

white-salmon.dogs_source_quote: Do not cross the fencing near the natural arch, as the area is closed to protect sensitive resources. Bikes are prohibited on this trail. Horses prohibited on this trail. Dogs must be on leash year round.

offroad.name: Forest Road 66 along the Big Lava Bed
offroad.difficulty: not published by the Forest — no length, surface or vehicle requirement is given for FR 66, only the route and a posted speed limit of "35 mph or less as signed"
offroad.season: Status listed as Site Open, with no gate date published. Gifford Pinchot's forest-wide warning governs: "Most forest roads are not plowed in winter and some roads may be impassable for cars without high clearance and four-wheel drive or chains." The stop is 6-11 Nov 2027, the start of that window rather than the middle of it.
offroad.note: USFS: the road "Starts at the Town of Willard and heads north ending at the intersection with Forest Road 60" and "follows the Big Lava Bed" — a 20-square-mile, 8,200-year-old lava flow with no road across it, only around it. Little Huckleberry trailhead and South Prairie are on it. Closest forest road network to the White Salmon base.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 66

offroad.name: Forest Road 24
offroad.difficulty: not published — the Forest gives endpoints and access points for this road and nothing else
offroad.season: Status listed as Site Open; no gate date published. Same forest-wide winter caveat.
offroad.note: USFS: it "starts at the end of Hwy 141 west of Trout Lake at the Forest Service Boundary and ends at the junction with the 8851 Road north of Big Mosquito Lake." The Ice Cave and Natural Bridges area and Peterson Prairie are in this corner. Recorded with its blanks left blank — Gifford Pinchot publishes no length, surface or vehicle requirement for it, and the Mt Adams Ranger District, (509) 395-3402, is the only source that will know.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 24

offroad.name: Forest Road 88
offroad.difficulty: not published by the Forest
offroad.season: Status listed as Site Open; no gate date published. Climbs toward Mount Adams, so it is the most snow-exposed of these three in early November.
offroad.note: USFS: it "Starts at Hwy 141 west of Trout Lake and heads north", passing Trout Lake Creek Campground, the Sleeping Beauty trailhead, Flattop Sno-Park, the Basket Tree interpretive site and a Pacific Crest Trail access. The Sno-Park on it is the tell — this road is a winter recreation route from roughly December, which means it is a driving route only at the front end of this stay.
offroad.source: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF — Forest Road 88

white-salmon._review: Three trails for five nights, and one of them - Dog Mountain - is a 7-mile 2,800 ft climb whose whole point is the May wildflower display; in November it is a wet slog with no flowers and no permit requirement. What the card lacked was the year-round Gorge walking that is on the doorstep. The Coyote Wall complex is four miles east of White Salmon and was not listed at all.

trails.name: Ramona Falls Trail
trails.was: Ramona Falls — no url
trails.note_source: Seasonal footbridge over the Sandy River is removed in winter — the stop is 6-9 Nov, so check before going.

trails.name: Mirror Lake Loop
trails.was: Mirror Lake Trail #664 — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: The most popular trail in Oregon by review count. About 2 miles to the lake; continues to Tom, Dick and Harry Mountain.

trails.name: Old Salmon River Trail
trails.season: Open year-round - and at roughly 1,500 ft this is the one that is genuinely true for. Mirror Lake, already on this card, sits above 4,000 ft and can be under snow by 11-15 Nov.
trails.note: Old-growth river trail along the Salmon a few minutes from Welches - moss, big Douglas fir, the river the whole way, and flat. The single best fit on this card for the stop's dates, and the highest-rated trail found at any of these 21 stops.

trails.name: Cascade Streamwatch Trail
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Barrier-free interpretive loop at the Wildwood Recreation Site with an underwater window onto a salmon stream. Fifteen minutes, paved, and open in the wet.

trails.name: Wetlands Boardwalk Trail
trails.season: March through October per AllTrails; the 11-15 Nov stay is outside it. Boardwalk over wetland, so the window is about water level and standing water rather than closure - worth a look at conditions rather than a drive out on faith.
trails.note: The second loop at Wildwood Recreation Site, on boardwalk across the wetland. Pairs with Cascade Streamwatch into one short outing.

trails.name: Feather Trail
trails.note: Quiet three-mile option near Welches for a day that wants more than the interpretive loops but not a mountain.
trails.stats_note: Surfaced on the plp.alltrails.com mirror; slug copied verbatim, host normalised to www.

welches.authority: USDA Forest Service — Mt. Hood National Forest
welches.dogs: Mt. Hood NF: "Make sure pets are kept on leashes no longer than 6 feet in designated recreation areas."

official_links.label: Safety and Outdoor Ethics — Mt. Hood NF (USFS)

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

welches.stats_note: Mid-November is the constraint that shaped this list. High Rock (1.1 mi, 4.7 from 49) is a superb short trail and was left off the front of the card because its window is June through October and it sits near 4,900 ft; Salmon Butte, Bonanza and Lake Lenore are all challenging AND all May-or-June starts. Everything above is under 2,000 ft.

offroad.name: Lolo Pass Road (FR 18 / FR 1800)
offroad.difficulty: not graded. Mt Hood NF says the Zigzag-side FR 1800 is "NOT maintained for winter travel" and that FR 18 on the Hood River side gets "a lot of snow" and is "very treacherous"
offroad.season: OPEN ON THESE DATES BUT ON BORROWED TIME. No fixed gate is published for this road, unlike most of the others in the district. The stop is 11-15 Nov 2027; Mt Hood NF's general rule is that seasonal closures run "December 1 through March 31", so the whole network shuts about two weeks after departure — and an early-November snowfall on the pass can make the point moot sooner.
offroad.note: The crossing from Zigzag over Lolo Pass to Hood River, round the northwest side of Mount Hood — the classic Mt Hood back road and the one that starts closest to the Welches base. Ramona Falls and the PCT are off it.
offroad.source: USFS Mt. Hood National Forest — National Forest Roads

offroad.name: Barlow Road (FR 3530)
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's road list
offroad.season: OPEN ON THESE DATES, CLOSES SHORTLY AFTER. Mt Hood NF: "Seasonally closed December 1 to April 1." The stop is 11-15 Nov 2027 — about sixteen days of margin.
offroad.note: The original Oregon Trail wagon route around the south side of Mount Hood, the alternative to rafting the Columbia. Driving it is the point rather than the terrain. Appears on both the Barlow and Hood River district lists with the same dates.
offroad.source: USFS Mt. Hood National Forest — National Forest Roads

offroad.name: Bennett Pass Road (FR 3550)
offroad.difficulty: not graded, but the restriction says a lot: Mt Hood NF closes it "to vehicles over 50 inches wide" seasonally, which is a snowmobile-and-quad rule — a full-size pickup is excluded once that is in force
offroad.season: OPEN ON THESE DATES. The 50-inch restriction runs "December 1 to April 1"; the stop is 11-15 Nov 2027, ahead of it. From 1 December this road is not driveable in the truck at all.
offroad.note: The high road southeast of Mount Hood off OR-35 near Mount Hood Meadows, running the ridge toward Gunsight and Badger Lake. The most interesting driving of this stop and the one with the tightest window.
offroad.source: USFS Mt. Hood National Forest — National Forest Roads

offroad.name: Last Chance Mountain Road (FR 1828)
offroad.difficulty: not graded; Mt Hood NF describes it as "Typically impassable during winter months" without giving a date
offroad.season: UNCERTAIN ON THESE DATES. No gate date published — the Forest simply says winter makes it impassable, and 11-15 Nov 2027 is the boundary. Treat as go-and-see rather than planned.
offroad.note: Zigzag Ranger District, climbing above the Salmon River country south of Welches. Listed with its uncertainty stated rather than dropped, because it is the nearest road of its kind to camp and 'we do not know' is the honest status.
offroad.source: USFS Mt. Hood National Forest — National Forest Roads

welches.dogs_source_quote: Make sure pets are kept on leashes no longer than 6 feet in designated recreation areas.
welches.dogs_source_note: DRIFT — the second half of our card is not on the page. "every year dogs run off and are permanently lost in the forest" could not be found on this page or any other Mt. Hood NF page. The page's actual supporting sentence is "Pets can spook horses or other pack animals, impact others' camping experiences, and more." The leash sentence itself is verbatim.

Crater Lake day trip (rim road closed —.entity: Crater Lake National Park, 139 km south of Bend. Recorded WITH its limits rather than left off the card. The stop arrives 15 Nov 2027 and NPS closes the North Entrance Road and both West and East Rim Drive on 1 November "or earlier if snowfall is significant" — so the rim road system is already shut. What stays open is Munson Valley Road, which NPS keeps open year round, and OR-62, plowed daily. That reaches Rim Village and the lake view. It is a half-day of driving each way in the truck for a lake you look at rather than drive around, and once there is snow on the rim routes the dog cannot come — NPS prohibits pets on them.

trails.name: Misery Ridge and River Trail
trails.reviews: (10,693) — star rating not published in the indexed snippet
trails.needs: star rating
trails.season: Open year-round. Arrive 15 Nov 2027 — cold and clear is the good version; the Misery Trail is loose gravel and steps with no shade, and ice on the steps is the November hazard.
trails.note: 'Smith Rock State Park' as written was a park, not a route — replaced by the park's signature loop, up Misery Ridge and back along the Crooked River. Terrebonne, 26 mi north of Bend. Day-use parking 2026: $10 Oregon resident, $12 non-resident. The shorter, flat River Trail alone is the easy alternative if the ridge is out.
trails.note_source: smithrock.com; Oregon State Parks fee schedule as reported; AllTrails indexed snippets

other_links.label: Misery Ridge Trail alone (2.5 mi, 1,154 ft, 1,653 reviews)

trails.name: Todd Lake Loop
trails.season: SEASONAL CONFLICT — LIKELY GATED SHUT. Todd Lake sits about 2.5 mi west of Mount Bachelor, INSIDE the winter closure of the Cascade Lakes Highway. Deschutes County gates the highway between Dutchman Flat and Deschutes Bridge every winter, typically between late October and mid-November — recent published dates are 12, 15, 19 and 21 November. Arrive 15 Nov 2027 sits exactly on that range. The highway does not reopen until mid-May or early June. Assume no vehicle access and check Deschutes County road closures (541-388-6581) before planning a day around it.
trails.note: Easy level loop around an alpine lake with Broken Top and Mount Bachelor above it. If the gate is shut it becomes a snowshoe from the Mt Bachelor Nordic Center.
trails.note_source: Deschutes County road closure notices; USFS Deschutes Todd Lake Day Use Area; AllTrails indexed snippet

other_links.label: USFS — Todd Lake Day Use Area/Trailhead

trails.name: Shevlin Loop Trail
trails.note: Bend's own park loop along Tumalo Creek - the reliable mid-November walk once Cascade Lakes Highway is shut and Todd Lake, already on this card, is unreachable.

trails.name: Tumalo Falls and Double Falls
trails.season: Winter access is the whole question. Tumalo Falls Road (FR 4603) is not plowed to the falls and the snow gate position in mid-November has to be confirmed with Deschutes National Forest before driving out; if it is down, the falls become a walk or ski in from the gate rather than a 2-mile stroll.
trails.note: AllTrails' own summary of this listing describes it as a dog-friendly waterfall hike, which is crowd data, not the Forest Service - treat the dog answer as unconfirmed until Deschutes NF is asked.

trails.name: Pilot Butte
trails.note: Cinder cone inside the city limits with a summit road as well as trails - the most-reviewed walk in Bend and snow-free most of the winter. Oregon State Parks describes it as an urban park with more than seven miles of trails and two ways to the 480-foot summit.

other_links.label: Oregon State Parks — Pilot Butte State Scenic Viewpoint
other_links.note: Managing authority. 'Hike up and around on one of three trails.'

trails.name: Deschutes River Trail: Old Mill Reach
trails.note: Flat riverside loop through the Old Mill District, paved and packed in sections. The zero-effort option straight from town on a short November afternoon.

alltrails.name: Deschutes River Trail: Old Mill Reach

bend.authority: Oregon State Parks (Smith Rock SP) and USDA Forest Service — Deschutes National Forest (Todd Lake)
bend.dogs: Oregon State Parks: "Your pet needs to be physically restrained, meaning you must have them on a leash no longer than six feet"; pets are permitted in every state park except Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP and the Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls — Smith Rock is not on that list. Deschutes NF: "Over 95% of the Deschutes National Forest trails are open to dogs off-leash in the summer", but leashes are required on the Three Sisters Wilderness trails "including Todd Lake and Crater Ditch trails" from July 15 to September 15, and at all trailheads and developed recreation sites year-round.
bend.dogs_exception: Deschutes NF closes a few places to dogs entirely: the Bend Municipal Watershed year-round, the Beach and Sunset View day-use areas at Elk Lake, and Scout Lake day-use. Smith Rock rangers enforce the leash law strictly and ask everyone to stay on trail.

official_links.label: Smith Rock State Park (Oregon State Parks)

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.
Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

offroad.name: Paulina Peak Road (FR 2100-500)
offroad.distance: 4.1 miles
offroad.difficulty: USFS: a "steep and dusty road" that is "quite rough and narrow in some places", limited to "Vehicles less than 23' in length (passenger cars, pick-ups and vans)"
offroad.season: PROBABLY CLOSED ON ARRIVAL. USFS: the site "is often inaccessible and closed due to snow until early July and will close in late October/early November depending on snow conditions." The stop arrives 15 Nov 2027, after that window. The access road makes it worse: Deschutes County and the Forest Service close Paulina Lake Road and Cascade Lakes Highway for winter — in 2025 that was 8 a.m. on Nov 18, with reopening "typically... before Memorial Day". On a comparable calendar the gate would drop on the fourth day of a six-night stay.
offroad.note: The 7,984 ft rim of the Newberry caldera, looking down on Paulina and East lakes and out to the whole Cascade crest — the best short drive near Bend when it is open. Recorded with the conflict stated because the dates are genuinely marginal: it might be driveable on arrival and it will not be on departure.
offroad.source: USFS Deschutes NF — Paulina Peak Observation Site; closure date from Deschutes County Road Department

offroad.name: Millican Valley OHV Trail System
offroad.distance: 255 miles of designated routes
offroad.difficulty: not graded. BLM permits "Class I, II, and III off-highway vehicles (OHVs)" but does not define the classes on this page and does not say whether a full-size street-legal pickup qualifies — that needs the Prineville field office before driving out, not after.
offroad.season: THE ONE THAT WORKS AT THESE DATES. BLM: "Millican Plateau is open year round. North Millican and South Millican have seasonal closures" — no dates given for those. Low sagebrush country east of Bend at around 4,000 ft, so it is clear when the Cascades are not.
offroad.note: Reached from Bend via Alfalfa Market Road, or from George Millican Road. "No fees - Oregon State ATV Permit Required", and spark arrestors are required year-round. The honest caveat is the vehicle class: this is signed as an OHV system and the published material is written for quads and dirt bikes, so confirm a full-size truck is legal on the routes intended before committing a day to it.
offroad.source: BLM Oregon — Millican Valley OHV Trail System

offroad.name: Christmas Valley Back Country Byway
offroad.distance: 93 miles
offroad.difficulty: BLM publishes no surface breakdown or vehicle requirement for the byway as a whole, noting only that some areas are "Accessible by foot or 4WD vehicle"
offroad.season: No gate published, and that is the point of listing it — this is high desert at around 4,300 ft southeast of Bend, well below and east of the Cascade crest, so it is driveable on the stop's 15-21 Nov 2027 dates when Paulina Peak and Cascade Lakes Highway are shut. Short days in late November are the real limit on a 93-mile loop.
offroad.note: The long way round Lake County's volcanic country from the Black Hills Interpretive Site — sand dunes, the remains of an eroded volcano, the Lost Forest. Crack-in-the-Ground is off it, reached by "Crack-in-the-Ground Road for about 7 miles" of gravel. Roughly 90 minutes southeast of Bend before the loop even starts, so it is a whole day. BLM's own advice: "Check weather and road conditions ahead of time" and carry area-specific maps, water, fuel and emergency equipment — there are no services on it.
offroad.source: BLM Oregon — Christmas Valley Back Country Byway

bend.dogs_source_quote: Your pet needs to be physically restrained, meaning you must have them on a leash no longer than six feet.
bend.dogs_source_note: Two authorities. Oregon State Parks half is clean — the three exceptions are Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP and the Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls, and Smith Rock is genuinely not among them. Deschutes NF half verified at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/deschutes/safety-ethics/dog-restrictions: "Over 95% of the Deschutes National Forest trails are open to dogs off-leash in the summer and there are 1,200 miles of summer trails on the forest." is verbatim. TWO DRIFTS THERE: (1) our card says the Three Sisters leash rule covers those trails "including Todd Lake and Crater Ditch trails", implying an open list — the page gives a CLOSED list of six: Green Lakes, Moraine Lakes, South Sister, Soda Creek, Todd Lake and Crater Ditch, 15 Jul to 15 Sep. (2) our card's "at all trailheads and developed recreation sites year-round" is only partly right: the central dog-restrictions page states "All campgrounds and day-use areas require dogs to be on-leash unless they are exiting or entering the water", and it is the individual Deschutes recreation-site pages (e.g. Benham Falls East/West, Meadow Day Use) that carry "Dogs must be on leash at all trailheads throughout the year". Also omitted from our card: a year-round ban — "Dogs or any domestic animal are not allowed on national forest lands within the Bend Municipal Watershed at any time" — dogs banned at Beach & Sunset View (Elk Lake) and Scout Lake day-use areas, and the Deschutes River Trail leash season being 15 May to 15 Sep, not the wilderness dates.

Historic Bayfront & sea lion docks.entity: Yaquina Bay bayfront; California sea lions

Devil's Punchbowl State Natural Area.entity: Devils Punch Bowl State Natural Area

trails.name: Yaquina Head Lighthouse and Cobble Beach Loop
trails.was_name: Cobble Beach / Quarry Cove tide pools
trails.season: TIDE-DEPENDENT, not seasonal. The tidepools are only there at low tide — check the tide chart against the day. Arrive 21 Nov 2027. Harbor seals haul out on the near-shore rocks off both Cobble Beach and Quarry Cove, best seen when the tide is out.
trails.note: BLM's Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area, 5 mi north of Newport; entrance fee. A long stairway drops from the observation deck to a beach of smooth black basalt cobbles laid down by Columbia River lava 14 million years ago. DOGS: permitted on the trails and walkways EXCEPT near the lighthouse and IN THE COBBLE BEACH TIDE POOLS. The other tidepool access named in the original entry is the paved, wheelchair-accessible Quarry Cove Trail (1.2 mi, 206 ft — the longest trail in the ONA); no individual AllTrails URL for it was returned by search, so none is recorded.
trails.note_source: BLM Yaquina Head ONA pages; AllTrails indexed snippet

other_links.label: BLM — Yaquina Head learn and explore

trails.name: Nye Beach to Agate Beach
trails.season: AllTrails gives the best window as March through May, so a 21-27 Nov stay is well outside it - which for a beach walk means wind, rain and short daylight rather than closure. Walkable, but check the tide before setting out; it is a sand route.
trails.note: The long beach walk north out of Newport, from Nye Beach up to Agate Beach under the Yaquina Head headland. Five miles of flat sand, and the biggest single walk this stop has.

trails.name: Beverly Beach State Park Campground
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Loop through the creek-side forest at Beverly Beach, seven miles north of town, with a tunnel under 101 to the sand. The sheltered option on a November storm day.

trails.name: Hatfield Marine Science Center Estuary Trail
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Flat estuary path on the south side of Yaquina Bay by the science centre - birds, mud, and a walk that takes twenty minutes when the weather gives you twenty minutes.

alltrails.name: Hatfield Marine Science Center Estuary Trail

trails.name: Saint Perpetua and Giant Spruce Trail
trails.note: Cape Perpetua is the highest point you can drive or walk to on the Oregon coast and the best viewpoint on it, and this route takes both halves of it from the visitor centre: up the Saint Perpetua switchbacks to the shelter and the 70-mile view, then down Cape Creek to a Sitka spruce more than 500 years old. About 25 miles south of camp, past Yachats. The Giant Spruce half alone is a separate AllTrails listing with 610 reviews, flat and easy, if the climb is more than the day wants.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Saint Perpetua and Giant Spruce Trail is considered a moderate hike that covers 4.4 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,007 ft. It takes about 2.5-3 hr to complete.' Count 503 from the trail page title. USFS Siuslaw National Forest for the Giant Spruce Trail #1365 description - 'From the Cape Perpetua Visitor Center hike through the lush forest to a more than 500 year-old Sitka spruce tree.'
trails.stats_note: No star rating appeared alongside the count in any snippet read; the 503 is a raw count. The Giant Spruce Trail listing on its own showed 610 reviews.

other_links.label: USFS Siuslaw NF - Giant Spruce Trail #1365
other_links.note: The authority for the lower half of this route.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Giant Spruce Trail (short version)
other_links.note: 610 reviews. Reviewers: 'Flat and easy to walk with almost no elevation gain', out-and-back with an optional loop through the campground.

trails.dogs_note: Siuslaw National Forest. No published pet rule was read for this trail this pass - do not assume either way.

trails.name: North Loop and Drift Creek Falls #1378 Loop
trails.note: The best-known hike within an hour of Newport and not on the card: a 100 ft suspension bridge slung across the canyon directly in front of a 75 ft waterfall, in the Siuslaw National Forest east of Lincoln City. The straight out-and-back to the falls is about 3 mi with 420-540 ft of gain; the #1378 loop adds the north leg. Well maintained, mostly shaded, and late November is high water.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'North Loop and Drift Creek Falls #1378 Loop is considered a moderate hike that covers 3.7 mi, with an elevation gain of 597 ft. It takes about 1.5-2 hr to complete.' Out-and-back figures from waterfallhikes.com (3.2 mi, ~540 ft, moderate) and Trailspotting (3 mi, easy, 420-490 ft) - community tier and they disagree, which is why the AllTrails loop figures are the ones recorded.
trails.stats_note: No review count or star was returned for either Drift Creek listing in any search read this pass, including a targeted 'star rating from' query. Genuinely absent, not omitted.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Drift Creek Falls (point of interest)
other_links.note: AllTrails indexes two trails reaching the falls.

trails.dogs_note: Multiple trail guides describe it as dog friendly; no Siuslaw National Forest page stating the rule was read this pass, so it is left unset.

trails.name: Mike Miller Educational Trail
trails.note: A mile of old-growth Sitka spruce a mile south of Newport in South Beach, on bridges and boardwalk with numbered interpretive posts and observation decks. Lincoln County's, not the state's. This is the walk for the days the November weather makes the beach pointless - it is short, sheltered, and takes 45-60 minutes.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Mike Miller Educational Trail is considered a moderate hike that covers 0.9 mi, with an elevation gain of 141 ft.' Count 256 from the trail page title; a second snapshot showed 239 and a third 257. Lincoln County: 'The Mike Miller loop is ~1 mile, and is a perfect hike to experience the beauty of native coastal vegetation along with native wildlife.' Discover Newport gives 45-60 minutes.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 239, 256, 257. No star rating appeared with any of them.

other_links.label: Lincoln County - Mike Miller Park
other_links.note: The managing authority. Also describes the Wilder Trail connection to Newport's Wilder Twin Park.

newport.authority: Bureau of Land Management — Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area
newport.dogs: BLM: "Pets may accompany visitors on trails and walkways except near the lighthouse and in the Cobble Beach tide pools", and "must remain on a 6-foot leash at all times". Therapy animals and pets are not allowed inside buildings.
newport.dogs_exception: The tide pools themselves are the one thing at Yaquina Head the dog cannot do — that and the ground near the lighthouse. The rest of the headland's trails and walkways are open on a 6 ft leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Otter Crest Loop
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: Otter Crest Loop, a short paved detour off Hwy 101 near Depoe Bay with pullouts at Cape Foulweather and Devil's Punchbowl — check current status, as landslide repairs have periodically restricted the loop.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Short paved detour off US-101 between Depoe Bay and Otter Rock. Otter Crest State Scenic Viewpoint sits 500 ft above the Pacific on Cape Foulweather, named by Cook in 1778, with the 1937 Cape Foulweather gift shop (on the National Register) and a view down to Devil's Punchbowl. Whale watching, and brown pelicans and eagles working the updrafts.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No seasonal gate, but the road's history is the caveat the original entry was pointing at: two landslides in the 1990s destroyed part of the roadway — one dropped a van down the slope — and the stretch was foot-traffic-only behind a concrete barrier for years before reopening in the early 2000s as a ONE-WAY lane with a bike lane. Arrive 21 Nov 2027; confirm current status, storm season is exactly when this road has trouble.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Oregon Parks and Recreation Department park profile; beachconnection.net Otter Crest Loop history

not_a_trail.entry: Cobble Beach / Quarry Cove tide pools
not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.
A campground, not a trail. AllTrails indexes the campground itself; the walks there are the beach and the Spencer Creek loop.

newport.dogs_source_quote: Pets may accompany visitors on trails and walkways except near the lighthouse and in the Cobble Beach tide pools.
newport.stats_note: 'Yaquina Head Lighthouse Trail' (0.9 mi, easy, 19 min) also surfaced and was deliberately left out as a near-duplicate of the Yaquina Head Lighthouse and Cobble Beach Loop already on the card. BLM's rule at Yaquina Head, already recorded on this stop, is worth repeating: 'Pets may accompany visitors on trails and walkways except near the lighthouse and in the Cobble Beach tide pools.'

offroad.name: Oregon Dunes NRA — South Jetty beach, Florence
offroad.difficulty: Beach open to OHV, 25 mph maximum
offroad.season: SPLITS THE STAY. The Forest Service OHV map states "BEACH OPEN TO STREET LEGAL VEHICLES Oct. 1 – April 30, Sunrise to sunset weekdays only" and "BEACH CLOSED TO ALL VEHICLES: May 1 – September 30, All weekends & holidays". The stay runs Sun 21 – Sat 27 Nov 2027, so it is driveable Mon 22 through Fri 26 only; Sunday the 21st and Saturday the 27th are out. Thanksgiving falls on Thu 25 Nov 2027 and the map attaches its "holidays" wording to the summer closure line, not this one — worth confirming with the Siuslaw NF before planning that day around it.
offroad.note: Riding curfew for Siltcoos to South Jetty is 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; all staging areas open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; 93 dB sound limit. The beach south of Siltcoos is marked "CLOSED TO OHV YEAR-ROUND". Roughly 50 miles south of Newport.
offroad.source: USFS Siuslaw National Forest — OHV Riding at the Oregon Dunes NRA map

offroad.name: Sand Lake Recreation Area
offroad.season: Campgrounds "open year round". The only dated restriction the Forest Service publishes is a camping-reservation or vehicle-ticket requirement over the Fourth of July holiday. No winter closure published — no conflict with 21–27 Nov 2027.
offroad.note: "1,076 acres of open sand dunes, surrounded by forests and adjacent to the Pacific Ocean". A fee is required at all campgrounds, the day-use lot and the open sand, and Oregon administers the OHV permit. The Forest Service page does not state which vehicle classes may ride or whether a full-size street-legal 4x4 is permitted on the open sand — that is unresolved. Roughly 55 miles north of Newport, near Pacific City.

offroad.name: Ocean shore, Tillamook County open segments (Sand Lake and Cape Kiwanda)
offroad.season: The three open segments carry no dated restriction. The rule's one dated provision covers the stretch south of Oswald West State Park to the Nehalem Bay State Park north boundary, 1 Oct – 30 Apr, 7 a.m. to noon — read the rule text before relying on that one, the wording is easy to invert.
offroad.note: Three segments are open to motor vehicles year-round: the Boy Scout property south boundary to the Galloway Road beach access (the Sand Lake / Tierra del Mar stretch), the Cape Kiwanda State Park north boundary to the base of the headland, and Pacific Avenue at Pacific City to Porter Point. The rest of the county's ocean shore is closed. Pairs naturally with a Sand Lake day. Note there is NO legal beach driving at Newport itself — Lincoln County's ocean shore is closed to motor vehicles from the Tillamook line to the Lane line under OAR 736-024-0025.
offroad.source: Oregon Parks & Recreation Dept — OAR 736-024-0015 (rule text via oregon.public.law)

offroad.name: Marys Peak Road
offroad.season: Siuslaw NF: "Most forest roads are not maintained for winter travel and do not receive snow removal. This includes the road to Marys Peak." No gate date is published, so this is a conditions call on the day rather than a closure — late November can be either.
offroad.note: Highest point in the Oregon Coast Range, east of Newport off Highway 34. The Forest Service pages do not publish the road's number, length or surface, so those are recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Siuslaw NF also lists Cascade Head Road (FSR 1861) as closed to motor vehicle traffic.
offroad.source: USFS Siuslaw National Forest — Current Conditions

newport._review: Four entries for six nights, one of which ('Beverly Beach State Park Campground') is a campground and not a trail at all, and the rest all within ten minutes of camp on the same stretch of sand. What was missing was every day-trip walk: Newport sits between Cape Perpetua to the south and the Drift Creek suspension bridge to the north, and neither was on the card.

Cape Blanco Historic Heritage Site (Hugh.entity: Cape Blanco and the Hughes House

trails.name: Cape Blanco Loop
trails.was: Cape Blanco Loop Trailhead — a trailhead
trails.note_source: Several Cape Blanco listings exist — Beach Loop, Coastal Trail, North Shore, Lighthouse and two horse trails. The Beach Loop is the one the card describes.

trails.name: Coquille Point Trail
trails.note: Paved loop out onto the headland above Face Rock, looking down on the Oregon Islands NWR sea stacks, with stairs to the beach. Five minutes from town and short enough to take in any gap between the late-November storms.

trails.name: Bullards Beach
trails.note: The short walk out to the Coquille River Lighthouse at the river mouth, inside Bullards Beach State Park. Flat sand and jetty, and the one that works when the wind is up.

trails.name: Bullards Beach and North Loop Trail
trails.note: The longer beach-and-dune circuit out of the same state park - the half-day version of the lighthouse walk.

alltrails.name: Bullards Beach and North Loop Trail

trails.stats_note: The longer of two Bullards listings — it takes in the North Loop Trail as well as the beach. "Bullards Beach" above is the beach walk on its own. Two AllTrails listings, one containing the other, kept as both per §2 rather than merged.

trails.name: Lost Lake Trail
trails.note: Inland forest walk for a day when the headlands are unwalkable - the rain option rather than the view option.

trails.name: Sunset Bay to Cape Arago
trails.note: The best-known walk on Oregon's south coast and absent from the card. It links three state parks along the cliff edge - Sunset Bay, Shore Acres, Cape Arago - on the old Cape Arago Pack Trail, ending above Simpson Reef where the sea lion and elephant seal haul-out is loudest in winter. About 45 min north of camp. It can be cut short at Shore Acres and walked back, which is what most people do.
trails.season: Shore Acres runs its Holiday Lights display from late November through New Year, floodlit gardens on the cliff, and the 27 Nov - 3 Dec stay is inside it. Cape Arago's south cove trail closes 1 Mar - 30 Jun for the seal pupping season, which does not touch these dates.
trails.note_source: AllTrails Cape Arago point-of-interest page: 'the best place to hike near Cape Arago is Sunset Bay to Cape Arago, which has a 4.7 star rating from 892 reviews. This trail is 12.7 km long with an elevation gain of 205 m.' The trail page title showed 959 reviews. Route description and the shorter Shore Acres turnaround from Coos Trails (coostrails.org), which puts the full walk at about 8.5 mi with the shortcuts.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be kept on a leash and under the physical control of the handler at all times. The leash may not exceed six feet in length. The handler is responsible for removal of all animal waste from park property, including hiking trails.
trails.dogs_note: The park's own trail map card, so this is the rule for the Sunset Bay / Shore Acres / Cape Arago trail system the walk uses. Six-foot leash, waste carried out, trails included.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 892 (with the 4.7 star, on the POI page) and 959 (trail page title). Ordering signal only.

other_links.label: Coos Trails - Sunset Bay, Shore Acres and Cape Arago trails
other_links.note: Local trail group's description of the pack trail and where it can be picked up. Recommends starting at the south end from the Cape Arago group picnic area for the fullest version.

trails.name: Golden and Silver Falls
trails.note: Two of the tallest waterfalls in the Oregon Coast Range - Silver at 259 ft and Golden at 254 ft - on a short easy walk, and the card had no forest walk at all. Golden and Silver Falls State Natural Area is 24 miles inland from Highway 101 up a narrow road from Allegany; the drive is the hard part, not the trail. The short version is a bridge crossing to Golden Falls and a 10-15 minute walk to Silver; the full three-trail system is 3.0 mi with about 570 ft of gain, or 5.8 mi / 840 ft if the upper viewpoint trails are added.
trails.season: Late November is the right time to be there rather than the wrong one - these falls are Coast Range creeks, at their most powerful in winter and spring and thin by late summer.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Golden and Silver Falls is considered an easy hike that covers 1.2 mi, with an elevation gain of 180 ft. It takes about 0.5-1 hr to complete.' Star and count from the AllTrails park page for the natural area: 4.7 star rating from 593 reviews. Falls heights from Oregon Hikers field guide. Longer trail-system figures from Trail Scholar (3.0 mi / 570 ft) and Oregon Hiking (4 mi / 370 ft to both bases, 5.8 mi / 840 ft for all trails) - community tier, and they disagree with each other, so the AllTrails figure is the one recorded above.
trails.dogs_source_quote: He can run free in a fenced off-leash area or hike with you on 12 miles of dog-friendly trails
trails.dogs_note: Oregon Parks and Recreation Department's statewide pet page: leashed dogs are welcome on state park trails. This is a State Natural Area under OPRD, and AllTrails reviewers describe it as a trail dog owners specifically seek out.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 470, 593, 612 and 626 across four indexed snapshots, with 4.6 and 4.7 both appearing. 4.7 (593) is a star-and-count pair read together. Ordering signal only.

bandon.authority: Oregon State Parks — Cape Blanco State Park
bandon.dogs: Oregon State Parks: pets are allowed in all parks except Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP and named trails at Silver Falls — Cape Blanco is not among them. "Your pet needs to be physically restrained, meaning you must have them on a leash no longer than six feet."
bandon.dogs_exception: One seasonal trap on this coast: "Pets and service animals are not permitted on some beaches or at certain times of the year (even on a leash) to protect wildlife, such as western snowy plovers" — the plover closures run 15 Mar to 15 Sep. This stop falls outside that window, but check the posted signs at the beach access.

offroad.name: Oregon Dunes NRA — Spinreel to Horsfall, open sand riding and beach
offroad.difficulty: Open riding on sand; beach 25 mph maximum
offroad.season: OPEN FOR THE WHOLE STAY. The Forest Service OHV map states "BEACH OPEN TO OHV: Oct. 1 – April 30" and "BEACH CLOSED TO ALL VEHICLES May 1 – Sept. 30" for the Horsfall/Bull Run end — so 27 Nov – 3 Dec 2027 is inside the open season. Snowy plover beach restrictions run 15 Mar – 15 Sep, also clear. Riding curfew Horsfall to Spinreel is 6 a.m. to midnight; staging areas 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
offroad.note: The northern part of this beach panel is marked "BEACH CLOSED TO OHV YEAR-ROUND" — the open beach section is at the Horsfall / Bull Run end, reached from Horsfall Beach Road. 93 dB sound limit. Bull Run OHV Staging Area has paved parking and quick beach access via the Bull Run OHV Trail. About 25 miles north of Bandon via Coos Bay.
offroad.source: USFS Siuslaw National Forest — OHV Riding at the Oregon Dunes NRA map

offroad.name: Ten Mile OHV Trail (Spinreel)
offroad.distance: 2.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: Loose sand; the Forest Service lists it open to all off-road vehicle classes
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published for the trail itself. It ends at the beach, and the beach it reaches is under the 1 Oct – 30 Apr OHV season, which covers the stay.
offroad.note: USFS: "The Ten Mile OHV Trail is 2.8 miles long and is loose sand. It begins at Spinreel OHV Staging Area and ends at the beach." The Oregon Dunes NRA south unit is a 31,500-acre portion of the Siuslaw National Forest. Whether a full-size street-legal 4x4 counts as an admitted class on the sand trails is not stated on this page.
offroad.source: USFS Siuslaw National Forest — Oregon Dunes NRA South

offroad.name: Ocean shore, Five Mile Point to Bullards Beach State Park
offroad.season: Open, with no dated restriction. The only seasonal Coos County closure is the stretch 500 feet north of the Horsfall Beach access south to the Dunes NRA boundary, 1 May – 30 Sep. No conflict with 27 Nov – 3 Dec 2027.
offroad.note: The beach immediately north of the Coquille River — the Whiskey Run / Seven Devils stretch — is open to motor vehicles year-round. Bandon's own town beaches are NOT: the rule closes the shore from the northerly beach access at Bullards Beach State Park south to north of China Creek. A second open stretch runs from north of China Creek south to about a mile north of the Twomile Creek mouth, which is the New River end of Bandon State Natural Area.
offroad.source: Oregon Parks & Recreation Dept — OAR 736-024-0040 (rule text via oregon.public.law)

offroad.name: Umpqua Dunes, Winchester Bay
offroad.season: Umpqua Dunes is the one Oregon Dunes riding area listed "Open 24-hours"; the gate at the Umpqua Beach staging areas is "Closed 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.". No seasonal closure — open on 27 Nov – 3 Dec 2027.
offroad.note: Sand riding only. The map marks the Umpqua beach itself "BEACH CLOSED TO OHV YEAR-ROUND", so this is dunes, not beach driving, and the southern end of the panel is "CLOSED TO MOTORIZED USE". Staged from Umpqua Beach #2 and #3 parking areas. Roughly 55 miles north of Bandon — the furthest of the three dune areas.
offroad.source: USFS Siuslaw National Forest — OHV Riding at the Oregon Dunes NRA map

bandon.dogs_source_quote: Your pet needs to be physically restrained, meaning you must have them on a leash no longer than six feet.
bandon.dogs_source_note: The three statewide exceptions are confirmed on this page — Dabney State Recreation Area, Shore Acres State Park, and the Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls. Cape Blanco is not among them, so the card's inference holds.
bandon._review: The existing box holds five entries but only four distinct walks: 'Bullards Beach' and 'Bullards Beach and North Loop Trail' are the same state park beach walk under two names. Worth folding into one before the next pass. Six nights, so two additions bring the box to six distinct walks - and both are the day trips the card was missing: everything on it was within ten minutes of camp.

trails.name: Grove of Titans
trails.dogs_note: Redwood National and State Parks — 'No Pets on Park Trails'. Same authority and same rule as the three trails already on this card.
trails.season: AllTrails' own description says the trail is especially beautiful in the shoulder seasons and that parking is limited in peak season — a 3-10 Dec arrival is the opposite of the parking problem. The access is Howland Hill Road, which is narrow and unpaved: truck only, and check it after rain.
trails.note: The highest-rated trail anywhere near this stop and it was not on the card. Completed in summer 2022 as an elevated boardwalk with a suspension bridge, built to keep feet off the root systems of some of the largest redwoods by volume in the world; the Mill Creek Trail was rerouted through the grove in 2021 to make it work. Distance and time are not published in the AllTrails result and are not guessed here — the 1.8-mile figure is a third-party measurement and reviewers describe just over a mile each way and roughly two hours if you linger. The NPS page is the authority to read before going.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title read in browser (7,248 Reviews, 4.9/5); NPS Grove of Titans Trail page for the 2022 construction and access; HappyWanders for the 1.8-mile round-trip figure; Redwood Hikes for the 2021 Mill Creek reroute
