trails.name: Fern Falls via Boy Scout Tree Trail
trails.dogs_note: Redwood National and State Parks — 'No Pets on Park Trails'.
trails.season: No seasonal window is published; the trail is a low-elevation redwood valley walk and is a December trail as much as a July one. It will be wet — Fern Falls is the point, and December is when it runs hardest. Access is Howland Hill Road, unpaved and narrow: truck only.
trails.note: The big redwood walk of Jedediah Smith and the one serious hike this stop was missing — 5.5 miles and a thousand feet through old growth to a fern-hung waterfall. Reviewers describe it as family-friendly despite the distance. Same road as the Grove of Titans, so the two make one very good day or two easy ones.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title read in browser (5,026 Reviews, 4.8/5) and its stat line for distance, gain, time and difficulty; Hiiker corroborates the length at 8.3 km and the grade as medium

trails.name: Crescent Beach Loop Walk
trails.dogs_note: CAREFULLY QUALIFIED. NPS bars pets from every trail in Redwood NSP but permits them on a leash of 6 ft or less 'in developed campgrounds, on beaches, in picnic areas, and on roads'. Crescent Beach is a beach, so the sand is open to the dog — this is the one place at this stop where that is true. The adjacent Coastal Trail: Crescent Beach Section Loop is explicitly closed to dogs, so if the loop leaves the sand the dog does not go with it. Read the NPS pets page and the signs at the lot, and keep to the beach.
trails.season: Open year-round. December on this coast means storms and king tides; check the tide before walking out, because the beach is the walk.
trails.note: A mile on the sand, eighteen minutes, five minutes from town — the walk you can do every day of a seven-night December stay when the weather has closed everything else, and the only one the dog is allowed on. It is on the card because of the dog, not because it is the best trail here.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser; NPS Redwood National and State Parks pets page for the beach exception, already this stop's dogs_source

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Redwood National and State Parks

offroad.name: Davison Road to Gold Bluffs Beach and Fern Canyon
offroad.was_name: Fern Canyon (Prairie Creek Redwoods, via Davison Road)
offroad.distance: unpaved road running west off US-101 to Gold Bluffs Beach and on to the Fern Canyon trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded dirt with a creek crossing near the beach end — the restriction that bites is size, not terrain
offroad.season: NO PERMIT CONFLICT — the opposite. Permits are required for the Gold Bluffs Beach day-use area including the Fern Canyon trailhead only from 15 May to 15 September. The stop arrives 3 Dec 2027, outside the permit season, so no reservation is needed. The trade is weather: December is storm season on this coast and Davison Road has been closed outright for storm damage before. Check status with Redwood National and State Parks before driving out.
offroad.note: The size limit is the whole story for this rig: maximum single vehicle length 24 ft, maximum width 8 ft, and no trailers of any kind on Davison Road. The truck goes; the coach never could, and could not turn around if it tried. Renamed to the road, since the road is the constraint and the canyon is the destination. Expect to wade in December — the seasonal footbridges in the canyon are a summer installation.

crescent-city.authority: National Park Service / California State Parks — Redwood National and State Parks
crescent-city.dogs: "No Pets on Park Trails" — pets on leashes up to 6 feet are allowed only in "developed campgrounds, on beaches, in picnic areas, and on roads", and are excluded from ranger-led activities.
crescent-city.dogs_exception: Fern Canyon, Stout Grove and Damnation Creek are all closed to the dog — you may park at the Fern Canyon and Stout Grove lots but not walk the trails. What is open: Crescent Beach, Gold Bluffs Beach, Freshwater Beach, the Klamath River and Redwood Creek overlooks, and two gravel roads under big trees — Cal Barrel Road (Prairie Creek) and Walker Road (Jedediah Smith).

official_links.label: Pets — Redwood National and State Parks (NPS)

scenicDrives_patch.name: Howland Hill Road through Jedediah Smith Redwoods
scenicDrives_patch.note: Hard-packed gravel former stage road, roughly 6 mi of old-growth redwood, about an hour end to end, with the Stout Grove trailhead on it. RVs, trucks and vehicles with trailers are TOO WIDE — the NPS says so outright, and the wider park restricts motorhomes to 25 ft and trailers to 21 ft. This is the towed pickup, unhitched, or it is nothing.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate, but the surface varies with season and with how recently it was graded; it can be soft or rutted after rain, which on this coast is most of the winter. Arrive 3 Dec 2027 — expect wet, and check with the park.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS Redwood 'Drive Howland Hill Road'

crescent-city.dogs_source_quote: Your pet must be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet (1.8 meters).
crescent-city.dogs_source_note: "No Pets on Park Trails" is confirmed as a heading on the page, and "Pets are not allowed during ranger-led activities" is confirmed. Our card's list of where pets ARE allowed is broader on the page than "developed campgrounds, on beaches, in picnic areas, and on roads" — it names specific campgrounds (Elk Prairie, Gold Bluffs Beach, Mill Creek, Jedediah Smith), specific beaches (Freshwater, Gold Bluffs, Crescent Beach) and specific gravel roads (Cal Barrel Road, Walker Road), so the general phrasing on our card is safe but less precise than the source.
crescent-city._review: 7 nights, arrive 3 Dec 2027. Three trails for a week in the redwoods, and the two highest-rated walks in the whole Crescent City index were both missing — Grove of Titans at 4.9 from 7,248 and Fern Falls via Boy Scout Tree at 4.8 from 5,026, both of which outrank two of the three that were on the card. Also missing: anywhere at all the dog can go. Redwood NSP bars pets from every trail and permits them on beaches, so the third addition is a beach. Three added, giving six for seven December nights.
crescent-city._also_considered: Tolowa Loop Trail (4.5 mi, moderate, 44 reviews) and Yontocket Trail (2.5 mi, easy, 4.3 from 33) in Tolowa Dunes State Park north of town both show dogs permitted on AllTrails, which would make them the dog answer if true — but California State Parks publishes no readable pet rule for Tolowa Dunes and AllTrails is not a source for this field on this trip. Left off rather than recorded on a guess. If someone rings Redwood NSP or CA State Parks, this is worth asking about: two dog-legal trails would change this stop considerably.

trails.was: Jug Handle State Natural Reserve — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: The ecological staircase — five marine terraces, each about 100,000 years older than the last.

trails.name: Headlands Trail
trails.note: THE ONLY TRAIL IN RUSSIAN GULCH STATE PARK THE DOG MAY WALK. California State Parks: pets "are allowed at the picnic area, beach, in the campground, and on paved park roads and the Headlands Trail. Except for service animals, dogs are not allowed on any other trails in the park." Leash no longer than six feet. Short bluff loop west of Highway 1 out to the Devil's Punch Bowl, a 100 ft wide, 60 ft deep collapsed sea cave, with the Russian Gulch bridge in view. Both walks already on this card — the Ecological Staircase and the Russian Gulch waterfall loop — cross to the inland, dog-free side of Highway 1, so this is the dog's walk at this stop.
trails.note_source: California State Parks Russian Gulch SP pet rule, already quoted in this stop's `dogs` field in links_db. AllTrails result snippets, verbatim: "Try this 0.5-mile loop trail near Mendocino, California. Generally considered an easy route, it takes an average of 9 min to complete" and "Headlands Trail (Devil's Punchbowl) is a loop trail that covers 0.5 mi, with an elevation gain of 16 ft. It takes about 0.5-1 hr to complete." Star and count from AllTrails' own Blowhole point-of-interest page, verbatim: "the best place to hike near Blowhole is Headlands Trail (Devil's Punchbowl), which has a 4.7 star rating from 590 reviews." AllTrails files the listing under Russian Gulch State Park, which confirms it is the same trail the state park rule names. Komoot corroborates: "Hike the easy 0.5-mile Headlands Trail in Russian Gulch State Park for ocean views, sea arches, and the Devil's Punchbowl."
trails.stats_note: AllTrails publishes two times for this trail — an average of 9 min and a 0.5-1 hr band. The 0.5-1 hr band is recorded because that is the figure on the listing card; 9 minutes is the recorded moving average and does not include standing at the punchbowl.

other_links.label: Komoot — Headlands Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the 0.5 mi easy loop in Russian Gulch State Park to the Devil's Punchbowl.

trails.name: Laguna Point Boardwalk Loop
trails.note: MacKerricher's seal-watching boardwalk, three miles north of town and the most-walked thing in the park. Raised boardwalk out to viewing platforms over the harbour seal haul-out, wheelchair accessible, and mid-December is grey whale migration season off this stretch of coast. Flat, short, and the obvious first walk of the stop.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Laguna Point Boardwalk Loop is considered an easy hike that covers 1.4 mi, with an elevation gain of 59 ft'; a second snapshot gave 2.3 km length, 18 m gain, 0.5-1 hr estimated time, circular. Star and count from the AllTrails MacKerricher park page: 'the most popular is Laguna Point Boardwalk Loop with an average 4.7 star rating from 643 community reviews.'
trails.dogs_note: UNRESOLVED, and it matters here. MacKerricher is one of the few California state parks that allows leashed dogs on beaches and trails, and the Haul Road is explicitly included - but one secondary source states dogs are barred from Glass Beach Trail, Virgin Creek Beach and the Seal Rookery, and Laguna Point IS the seal rookery viewing station. No parks.ca.gov page was found this pass that states the rule either way. Do not assume the dog can come on this one; the park office is 707-964-9112. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

trails.name: Point Cabrillo Light Station Coastal Trail
trails.note: A loop across coastal prairie and bluff to the restored 1909 light station, with a working third-order Fresnel lens you can stand next to. Thirty acres of light station inside about 270 acres of undeveloped headland, halfway between Fort Bragg and Mendocino. Easy, level, and the single best whale-watching stand of the stop in mid-December.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Point Cabrillo Light Station Coastal Trail is a loop trail that covers 2 mi, with an elevation gain of 147 ft. It takes about 0.5-1 hr to complete.' Star and count from the AllTrails park page: 4.6 star rating from 647 reviews; the trail page title showed 686. Komoot rates the same route easy at 2.0 mi / 72 ft / about 51 min. Park description and acreages from pointcabrillo.org.
trails.dogs_source_quote: The State Historic Park is open from sunrise to sunset daily. The main floor of the Lighthouse is dog-friendly.
trails.dogs_note: The light station's own site, operating the park under California State Parks. If the dog is welcome inside the lighthouse the headland trail is not in question - but the quote is about the building, so treat the trail as leashed-and-welcome rather than formally published.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 647 (with the 4.6 star) and 686. Difficulty is Komoot's; AllTrails' own grade was not in any snippet read.

other_links.label: Point Cabrillo Light Station (operator)
other_links.note: Hours, the Fresnel lens, and the extent of the park. Lighthouse main floor open 11am-4pm year-round.

trails.name: MacKerricher Haul Road Trail
trails.distance: 4.5 mi one way (paved section); 8.2 mi as the Pudding Creek to Glass Beach round trip
trails.time: about 3 hr 20 min for the 8.2 mi version
trails.difficulty: Moderate (Komoot, for the full 8.2 mi; the paved section is flat)
trails.cruise_reason: This is the gravel-cruise entry the whole Mendocino stop was missing. It is a former Union Lumber Company logging railbed - paved, multi-use, and Komoot measures the grades at under 5%, which is rail-grade by definition. It starts at the Pudding Creek Trestle, a 515 ft railroad bridge converted to foot and bike use in 2007, in walking distance of the north end of town. THE LIMIT: north of Virgin Creek the sand takes over - Komoot reports sections that are 'sandy and rough, especially near Virgin Creek where shifting sand occurs', and beyond the paved road it stops being a cruise. Ride the paved southern half and turn round.
trails.note: The everyday walk-and-ride of this stop, and the reason to be camped here rather than anywhere else on the Mendocino coast: flat, paved, coastal, and dog-legal, which almost nothing else in a California state park is.
trails.note_source: TrailLink lists the MacKerricher Haul Road Trail at 4.5 mi. Komoot's guide to the park: 'The most popular hiking route is Pudding Creek Beach & Glass Beach via the MacKerricher Haul Road - Mackerricher State Park, an 8.2 miles (13.1 km) trail that takes 3 hours 21 minutes to complete. This moderate route...' and, for surface: 'The main MacKerricher Haul Road is a paved multi-use trail, generally flat with slopes less than 5%. However, some sections can be sandy and rough, especially near Virgin Creek where shifting sand occurs.' Trestle history from DogTrekker's Haul Road entry.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Hours: Sunrise to 10 pm. Haul Road trail: 6 am-10 pm. Dogs: On leash
trails.dogs_note: Access California's park record, reviewed June 2025, naming the Haul Road specifically and its own separate hours. Corroborated by MacKerricher's Tripadvisor park Q&A - 'dogs are allowed on leash and on designated trails, the boardwalks and the old Haul Road which runs from the north end of Fort Bragg at Pudding Creek, through MacKerricher, and north.' No parks.ca.gov page carrying the rule in text was found this pass, so this is one tier below where it should be; the same phone call that settles Laguna Point settles this.

other_links.label: TrailLink - MacKerricher Haul Road Trail
other_links.note: Length 4.5 mi. Only one TrailLink review, so there is no usable rating for this entry.

other_links.label: Komoot - Pudding Creek Beach and Glass Beach via the MacKerricher Haul Road

other_links.label: Mendocino Land Trust - MacKerricher Coastal Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the route runs from Glass Beach north to the Inglenook Fen-Ten Mile Dunes Natural Preserve.

fort-bragg.authority: California State Parks — Jug Handle State Natural Reserve and Russian Gulch State Park
fort-bragg.dogs: Jug Handle SNR: "Dogs allowed on beach and headland trails west of Highway 1. Dogs not allowed on Staircase Trail or areas east of Highway 1." Russian Gulch SP: "Dogs not allowed on Fern Canyon Trail or trails east of Highway 1" — "Pets must be on a leash no longer than six feet. They are allowed at the picnic area, beach, in the campground, and on paved park roads and the Headlands Trail. Except for service animals, dogs are not allowed on any other trails in the park."
fort-bragg.dogs_exception: Both card walks cross to the inland, dog-free side of Highway 1 — the Ecological Staircase and the Fern Canyon route to the waterfall. West of the highway the dog is welcome on a 6 ft leash: Jug Handle's beach and headland trails, and Russian Gulch's Headlands Trail, beach and paved roads.

Russian Gulch State Park (California State Parks)

offroad.name: Jackson Demonstration State Forest winter-open roads — Road 200, 250, 350, 500, 700, 810, 900
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES, PARTLY. CAL FIRE's Public Notice — Seasonal Road & Campground Closure closes all JDSF campgrounds and seasonal roads for the wet season, effective 1 October in the notice read here (signed 18 Sep 2025), reopening "in the spring". 10–16 Dec 2027 is squarely inside that closure, so only the exception roads below will be driveable — and CAL FIRE says even those "may be closed periodically without further notice depending on road and/or weather conditions or timing of forest management activities".
offroad.note: The roads that generally stay open through winter are: Road 200; Road 250 (up to Road 1000 only); Road 350 (access to Camp 1 Day Use Area); Road 500; Road 700 (to Mendocino Woodlands State Park); Road 810; Road 900 (only to Road 810/920). Two hard rules on the same notice: "It is always unlawful to operate unlicensed vehicles (including off-road vehicles with or without green stickers) on State Forest roads" and "Off-road travel with motorized vehicles is not permitted on the State Forest" — a licensed truck on these numbered roads is the only legal shape this takes. Closed roads stay open to hiking, biking and horseback. JDSF office 707-964-5674; the forest starts on the eastern edge of Fort Bragg. No mileages are published in the notice.
offroad.source: CAL FIRE — Jackson Demonstration State Forest

offroad.name: Usal Beach road, Sinkyone Wilderness State Park
offroad.distance: approximately 6 mi north from Highway 1
offroad.difficulty: California State Parks: "unpaved, steep, narrow road"
offroad.season: State Parks publishes no gate dates, but warns in capitals: "ROADS MAY BE IMPASSABLE IN WET WEATHER." 10–16 Dec is mid wet season on the Mendocino coast, so this is a conditions call on the morning, not a plan — and there is no cell signal and nowhere to turn around once committed.
offroad.note: Access to the south end of the Lost Coast. State Parks gives the turn as mile marker 90.88 on Highway 1, "Approximately one hour north of Ft Bragg", then north about 6 miles. "RV'S & TRAILERS NOT RECOMMENDED." Note that the State Parks page does not use the names "Usal Road" or "County Road 431" — those names are not sourced from the authority, only the route description is. The park's north end (Needle Rock) is reached from Briceland Road / Mendocino County Road 435 out of Redway, last 3.5 miles unpaved, steep and narrow — roughly a three-hour drive from Fort Bragg, not a day trip.
offroad.source: California State Parks — Sinkyone Wilderness State Park

fort-bragg.dogs_source_quote: Yes: Dogs allowed on beach and headland trails west of Highway 1. Dogs not allowed on Staircase Trail or areas east of Highway 1.
fort-bragg.dogs_source_note: Jug Handle SNR quote is verbatim. Russian Gulch SP verified separately at https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=432 and there our card DRIFTS by omission: the live field leads with a permission we drop — "Yes: Dogs allowed in campground, beach, and trails west of Highway 1. Dogs not allowed on Fern Canyon Trail or trails east of Highway 1." The longer rule is verbatim as we have it, and adds one sentence we omit that matters with a dog in the coach: "At night, pets must be in a tent or vehicle."
fort-bragg._review: Three trails for six nights, and all three were bluff-and-forest walks of the same kind. What was missing: the seal-watching boardwalk, the lighthouse headland, and the one route that is both dog-legal and rideable. Fern Canyon at Van Damme State Park was considered and deliberately left off - it is widely reported to ban dogs, and Russian Gulch Waterfall Loop already on the card is the same fern-canyon-to-waterfall walk.

trails.name: Marina State Beach
trails.season: Open year-round - which for a three-night stop over 16-19 Dec is the whole point.

trails.name: Garrison Loop
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Fort Ord National Monument loop, same BLM ground as the Badger Hills trail already on the card - and BLM's rule there is leashed everywhere, with marked off-leash segments nearby. The dog day out at this stop, because Point Lobos is closed to dogs entirely.

trails.name: Jerry Smith Cooridor
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Flat corridor path on the Marina side - short, level, and the one to use when the December weather is against a longer day. Listed under AllTrails' own spelling, which misspells 'Corridor'.

trails.name: Marina Dunes
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Dune preserve walk immediately north of the state beach. NO DOG: California State Parks' rule for Fort Ord Dunes State Park is that dogs are allowed on the north/south recreation trail but 'are not allowed on spur trails to the beach OR on the beach due to endangered bird species and sensitive habitat areas', and the AllTrails listing for this dune route likewise states dogs are not allowed.
trails.note_source: California State Parks, Fort Ord Dunes State Park page, fetched, quoted above.

other_links.label: California State Parks — Fort Ord Dunes SP
other_links.note: Authority for the dune/beach dog restriction.

not_a_route.problem: A whole BLM monument, and a non-motorized one. BLM restricts use to non-motorized travel on authorized trails only — 86+ miles of them, for hiking, biking and horses; non-street-legal vehicles are never allowed, and going off the marked trails runs into unexploded-ordnance areas. There is no 4x4 route here at all. It belongs in trails or biking, not offroad. https://www.blm.gov/programs/national-conservation-lands/california/fort-ord/know-before-you-go

marina.authority: California State Parks (Point Lobos SNR) and Bureau of Land Management (Fort Ord National Monument) — two authorities, opposite answers
marina.dogs: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve: "No Dogs" — "Dogs are not allowed anywhere within the reserve and cannot be left inside parked vehicles." Fort Ord National Monument: "Dogs and stock must be on a leash/lead rope that is no more than six feet long", leashed in parking lots, at trailheads and along driveways; BLM's 2019 supplementary rules also designate marked off-leash segments and bar dogs from the Inland Range Planning Unit.
marina.dogs_exception: Point Lobos will not even let the dog stay in the parked car, so it is a day out that needs the dog left at camp. Fort Ord is the opposite — leashed everywhere, with marked off-leash segments on Guidotti, Skyline and Oilwell Roads near Badger Hills.

official_links.label: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve (California State Parks)
Fort Ord National Monument — Know Before You Go (BLM)
Final Supplementary Rules for Fort Ord National Monument (Federal Register)

marina.stats_note: Point Lobos, already on this card, bars dogs from the entire reserve and will not even let one wait in a parked car - California State Parks, quoted: 'Dogs are not allowed anywhere within the reserve and cannot be left inside parked vehicles.' Garrison Loop is the substitute day out on a Point Lobos day.

offroad.name: Old Coast Road
offroad.difficulty: "severe switchbacks, blind curves and few pullouts or places to turn around"; a high-clearance all-wheel or four-wheel drive vehicle is recommended
offroad.season: No published gate dates. The source says the dirt road "may be impassable and closed during wet weather", and 16–19 Dec is inside the wet season, so it is a conditions call. No Monterey County, Caltrans or State Parks page for this road could be found — the seasonal status is genuinely unpublished rather than merely unfound. Worth a call to Monterey County Public Works before driving it.
offroad.note: Leaves Highway 1 at Bixby Bridge and rejoins it near Andrew Molera State Park — the inland original alignment of the coast road. "When passable, the drive takes about one hour." Declared a public road by Monterey County in 1855; most land either side is now private, so there is nowhere to stop. Tiered community deliberately: no authority publishes this road, which is itself the finding.
offroad.source: Wikipedia — no official county or state page located

offroad.name: Nacimiento-Fergusson Road (Forest Road 22S01)
offroad.season: UNRESOLVED, AND WORTH RE-CHECKING. No seasonal gate is published. The status history is the problem: a Forest Service release of 5 June 2024 reported the road "remains closed to motorized vehicles until late summer" for storm repairs, while a forest order effective 5 Sep 2025 through 5 Sep 2027 restricts roadside camping along it, which reads as a road that was open when the order was written. Re-check before the 16–19 Dec 2027 stay — Monterey Ranger District 831-385-5434.
offroad.note: The only road crossing the Santa Lucia Range between Big Sur and the Salinas Valley. The forest order covers the road "from its intersection with State Highway 1 then east for 12 miles" and bans camping within 300 feet of it. The Forest Service pages do not publish the road's surface or full length, so neither is recorded here.

offroad.name: Central Coast Ridge Road (Cone Peak Road)
offroad.season: CLOSED, and not seasonally. Los Padres National Forest lists Central Coast Ridge Road, aka Cone Peak Road, under roads with long-term closure to vehicular traffic. That is open-ended, not a winter gate — assume shut on 16–19 Dec 2027 unless the forest says otherwise.
offroad.note: The ridge road running north off Nacimiento-Fergusson Road toward Cone Peak. Recorded here so it is not researched again from scratch: the answer is no, and it has been no for years. Length and surface are not published. Note also that Fort Ord National Monument, the obvious BLM land next to this stop, is not a driving option at all — BLM states "Use is non-motorized on authorized trails only" (https://www.blm.gov/programs/national-conservation-lands/california/fort-ord/know-before-you-go).
offroad.source: USFS Los Padres National Forest — Current Conditions

marina.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are not allowed anywhere within the reserve and cannot be left inside parked vehicles.
marina.dogs_source_note: Point Lobos confirmed verbatim, including the "No Dogs" field. Fort Ord National Monument verified separately at https://www.blm.gov/programs/national-conservation-lands/california/fort-ord-national-monument, which carries our quoted string verbatim in context: "All animals must be on a leash and under the owner/handler's physical control within developed recreation sites at all times: Dogs and stock must be on a leash/lead rope that is no more than six feet long and is held or otherwise attached to the owner/handler while in parking lots, at trailheads, along driveways, or anywhere else that signing indicates that pets must be leashed." NOT SOURCED: the rest of our Fort Ord sentence — the 2019 supplementary rules designating marked off-leash segments, and the ban on dogs in the Inland Range Planning Unit — is on neither that page nor blm.gov/visit/fort-ord-national-monument (which carries no pet text at all). The BLM dog flyer PDF linked from the programs page 404s at its published address. Treat the off-leash-segment and Inland Range clauses as unverified.

Red Rock Canyon NCA Scenic Drive.entity: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

links.label: Wikipedia — Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

Calico Tanks Trail (Red Rock Canyon).entity: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

links.label: Wikipedia — Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area

trails.name: Calico Tanks Trail
trails.was: Calico Tanks / Fire Wave / White Domes — three trails in one entry, and duplicated in two more

trails.name: Fire Wave, White Domes and Seven Wonders Loop
trails.note_source: Valley of Fire. AllTrails marks this combined loop CLOSED — check Nevada State Parks before planning it. The White Domes Trail listing above is the open alternative.
trails.was: Fire Wave Trail — renamed to the listing's own title

trails.name: White Domes Trail
trails.note_source: Valley of Fire State Park. Nevada State Parks calls this trail "White Domes Loop" — the card carries AllTrails' title, so expect the park's own signage and closure notices to use the other name.
trails.was: White Domes Loop — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.season: Nevada State Parks uses the card's exact name — "White Domes Loop" appears verbatim on the Valley of Fire park page's closure list — so the name is right; AllTrails indexes it as "White Domes Trail", hence match: contains. Review count 3,427 from the AllTrails search result; AllTrails currently flags the listing [CLOSED], which reflects the park's seasonal closure and not a permanent one. SEASON, and it is good news: the park closes this trail annually May 15 - September 30 along with Fire Wave, Seven Wonders Loop, Pastel Canyon/Pink Canyon, Pinnacles Loop, Prospect Trail, Arrowhead Trail, Natural Arch Trail and Charlie's Spring, because of "a history of frequent medical calls, search and rescue missions, and fatalities during this time of year". The stop arrives 1 Jan 2028, well inside the open window. Nevada State Parks publishes no distance or difficulty for it and directs visitors to the visitor centre or the park brochure, so neither is recorded here — community listings put it around 1.1-1.25 miles but no authority confirms that.

not_a_trail.problem: Duplicate of the Calico Tanks Trail entry, which carries the listing.

not_a_trail.entry: Fire Wave and White Domes trails (Valley of Fire).
not_a_trail.problem: Duplicate — both are separate entries now.
Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

vegas-area.authority: Bureau of Land Management (Red Rock Canyon NCA) and Nevada State Parks (Valley of Fire SP)
vegas-area.dogs: Red Rock Canyon NCA: pets are welcome on all trails — "The only places in Red Rock Canyon you can go but your pet can't are the visitor center and associated outdoor exhibits (for the protection of our tortoises)." "Pets should be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet (2 m)." Valley of Fire SP: "Pets are welcome, but they must be kept on a leash of not more than six feet in length"; "Pets are not allowed in the Visitor Center."
vegas-area.dogs_exception: Both authorities allow dogs on trail. The constraint here is heat, not law — slickrock and sand, and no shade on the Fire Wave or Calico Tanks.

official_links.label: Red Rock Canyon NCA — Planning Your Visit (BLM)
Valley of Fire State Park (Nevada State Parks)

offroad.name: Rocky Gap Road
offroad.distance: 8.9 miles
offroad.difficulty: 4WD required. The eastern 1.7 miles are described as "reasonable for any 4WD vehicle"; the western section is "more washed out" and "under normal conditions, driving the entire road is suitable only for skilled drivers"
offroad.season: No published gate. Winter storms wash it out further; the surface is the variable, not the calendar.
offroad.note: Willow Springs Picnic Area in Red Rock Canyon NCA over to Lovell Canyon Road in the Spring Mountains NRA — BLM land at one end, Forest Service at the other. The short out-and-back to the east is the sane version; the full crossing is a commitment with no easy turnaround in the middle. Difficulty and mileage are from birdandhike.com, a long-running local reference, not from BLM — BLM's own Red Rock pages do not describe this road.

offroad.name: Mormon Well Road
offroad.distance: 47 miles (76 km) to the connection with US-93
offroad.difficulty: FWS: "A high-clearance vehicle, and four-wheel drive (4WD) is suggested."
offroad.season: No calendar closure, but FWS warns "The full route may be closed due to hazardous conditions" — check before setting out.
offroad.note: Corn Creek up through Desert Pass and out to US-93, across Desert National Wildlife Refuge — the largest refuge outside Alaska. Joshua tree to pinyon-juniper as it climbs. Quiet in a way Red Rock never is.
offroad.source: US Fish & Wildlife Service — Desert NWR Auto Tour

offroad.name: Alamo Road
offroad.distance: over 70 miles (113 km)
offroad.difficulty: FWS: "A high-clearance vehicle, and four-wheel drive (4WD) is suggested."
offroad.season: No calendar closure. FWS notes the Dry Lake portion is "often impassable and closed due to hazardous conditions".
offroad.note: The long one — over 70 miles of rugged backcountry across the refuge, part of the 150+ miles the refuge maintains. Too much for a 2-night stop unless it is the whole day; Mormon Well is the better pick at these dates.
offroad.source: US Fish & Wildlife Service — Desert NWR Auto Tour

vegas-area.dogs_source_quote: The only places in Red Rock Canyon you can go but your pet can't are the visitor center and associated outdoor exhibits (for the protection of our tortoises).
vegas-area.dogs_source_note: Both authorities verified, both verbatim. Red Rock's leash sentence is fuller than ours: "Pets should be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet (2 m) to minimize conflicts with other people, other pets, and native wildlife." Valley of Fire SP confirmed at https://parks.nv.gov/parks/valley-of-fire — "Pets are welcome, but they must be kept on a leash of not more than six feet in length." and "Pets are not allowed in the Visitor Center." Red Rock also warns that rattlesnake bites can be fatal to pets and that pets may not be left unattended in vehicles or tied outside.

Fish Creek Wash & Sandstone Canyon (truc.entity: The truck route up Fish Creek Wash into Sandstone Canyon, inside Anza-Borrego Desert SP. Neither has its own article. The park article's geology section does document this drainage in its own text -- the Fish Creek Badlands, and the oyster and pecten coquina forming the 'Elephant Knees' along Fish Creek, which is the landmark this drive passes. Sandstone Canyon is not named in it.

scenicDrives_patch.name: S-22 Borrego–Salton Seaway (Erosion Road), with the Font's Point spur
scenicDrives_patch.note: TWO DIFFERENT ROADS, and the original entry ran them together. S-22 is the PAVED highway east out of Borrego Springs, nicknamed Erosion Road for the weathered country it crosses — a 21-mile driving tour through the Borrego Badlands with viewpoints, climbing into the Santa Rosa foothills at the east end. Font's Point is the famous overlook, and it is reached by a separate 4-MILE SANDY WASH off S-22: soft, rutted, high-clearance 4WD only, and a standard vehicle will not make it. Pavement in the coach's world, sand in the truck's.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Desert season is roughly October to April; the badlands are unusable in summer heat. Arrive 8 Jan 2028 — ideal. The wash is the hazard, not the calendar: it softens further after rain and this is flash-flood country.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Visit California Borrego Badlands/Font's Point; DesertUSA Anza-Borrego badlands region; americansouthwest.net

borrego-springs.dogs_note: California State Parks for Anza-Borrego: "Dogs allowed in the campgrounds, on designated park roads, and the Visitor Center/Campground Trail." That is the whole permission — this is NOT a dog-permissive stop, despite being a state park. Leash under 6 ft, and dogs may not be left outside at night.

trails.name: Borrego Palm Canyon Trail
trails.distance: 3 mi round trip (State Parks); 3.25 mi as a loop with the alternate return
trails.season: The stream through the canyon is seasonal and heaviest in early spring; expect it low or dry in the 8–14 Jan window.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. Distance from parks.ca.gov, time and gain from Hikespeak; neither the authority nor the indexed snippet published a difficulty grade, so none is recorded. Trailhead is at the Borrego Palm Canyon campground — walkable from camp. Hikespeak: "Dogs and bikes are allowed in the campground but not on the hiking trails".

trails.name: The Slot
trails.distance: 1–2.2 mi depending on whether the wash loop is closed
trails.season: FLASH FLOOD: do not enter with rain or thunderstorms anywhere in the area. Access is Buttes Pass Road, 2 miles of gravel described as suitable for standard vehicles — this one does NOT need the truck, unlike most of the Borrego washes.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. Distance/time/difficulty/gain from Earth Trekkers; the state park charges to park at The Slot as well as at the visitor centre and the campgrounds.

trails.name: Maidenhair Falls via Hellhole Canyon Trail
trails.season: The 20 ft fall is seasonal — Hikespeak says early spring or after rain. In a dry January expect the palms and the canyon, not the waterfall.
trails.note: Distance, time and gain from Hikespeak; no review count surfaced in the indexed snippet and neither source published a difficulty grade. The state park charges to park at Hellhole Canyon. Hikespeak: "dogs are likely not allowed on Hellhole Canyon Trail", consistent with the park's own rule.

trails.name: Pictograph Trail
trails.season: TRUCK: AllTrails states the road to the trailhead is sandy and 4-wheel drive is recommended. Blair Valley access, not a coach or a 2WD errand.
trails.note: Kumeyaay painted boulders, then an overlook down Smugglers Canyon. Never touch the pigment. Distance and gain from Hikespeak; the indexed snippet published no time or grade.

trails.name: Marshal South Home / Ghost Mountain
trails.season: AllTrails gives the good window as October–May; the 8–14 Jan stay is inside it. Same Blair Valley dirt access as the Pictograph Trail.
trails.note: Short steep climb to the adobe ruins of the South family's 16-year desert homestead. Thinly reviewed at 26 — the count is real, the confidence in the 26 is not the same as in The Slot's 3,714. AllTrails states dogs are not allowed.

trails.name: Wind Caves Trail
trails.season: TRUCK: high-clearance strongly recommended for the rough rocky dirt road in. This is off Fish Creek Wash, the route the stop already plans to drive.
trails.note: Wind-pocketed sandstone above Fish Creek — pairs with the Fish Creek Wash and Sandstone Canyon drive already in the stop's activities, so it costs no extra day. Stats from Hikespeak, which also states dogs are not allowed. Appears on AllTrails only inside a longer combined route (West Butte / Wind Caves / Slot loop), so no standalone listing is linked.

trails.name: Visitor Center / Campground Trail
trails.note: THE ONLY DOG-LEGAL TRAIL IN ANZA-BORREGO. California State Parks names it by name as the single trail dogs may use, alongside the campgrounds and the paved park roads. No published length, time or grade could be sourced and no trail database lists it — recorded as an absence rather than guessed. Worth a call to the visitor centre (760-767-4205) to confirm the length before planning round it.

trails.name: Calcite Mine Trail and the Narrows
trails.season: TRUCK: the route follows an old 4x4 mining road and Hikespeak warns of occasional vehicle traffic on it.
trails.note: Slot narrows plus the WWII optical-calcite workings above S-22. Stats from Hikespeak, which also states dogs are not allowed. No AllTrails listing surfaced in search, so no trail link.

offroad.name: Font's Point Wash
offroad.difficulty: State Parks grades it "4WD only" and rates the surface "poor" — deep sand with S-curves the road-conditions page calls difficult
offroad.season: No gate. Anza-Borrego's washes are a cool-season activity and the stop's 8-14 Jan 2028 dates are the middle of the good window. The hazard is rain, not date: the whole wash system changes after a storm, which is why State Parks re-publishes this page rather than a fixed list.
offroad.note: The classic Borrego Badlands run out to the Font's Point overlook above the Borrego Sink. Sand the whole way — momentum matters more than clearance. Check the road-conditions page the morning you go; State Parks grades every named route on it and updates as conditions change.
offroad.source: California State Parks — Anza-Borrego Desert SP Road Conditions

offroad.name: Fish Creek to Sandstone Canyon
offroad.difficulty: State Parks lists Sandstone Canyon as "2WD acceptable" but condition "poor", with narrow sections; the Fish Creek approach to the Wind Caves trail is graded "4WD only, poor"
offroad.season: No published gate. Same rain caveat as the other washes.
offroad.note: Up Fish Creek Wash from Split Mountain into Sandstone Canyon — the narrowest walls in the park, a slot you drive rather than walk. Note the split verdict: the canyon itself is the easy part, the wash getting there is the 4WD part. North Fork Fish Creek is listed CLOSED at Mollusk Wash.
offroad.source: California State Parks — Anza-Borrego Desert SP Road Conditions

offroad.name: Buttes Pass Road to The Slot and Hawk Canyon
offroad.difficulty: "2WD acceptable, good condition" to The Slot; "4WD only, good condition" to Hawk Canyon, with deep sand near the entrance
offroad.season: No published gate.
offroad.note: The gentlest of the four and the one to do first — a graded run off CA-78 to the top of The Slot, with the Hawk Canyon spur as the optional sandy bit. This is the route that works when the badlands washes are freshly cut up.
offroad.source: California State Parks — Anza-Borrego Desert SP Road Conditions

offroad.name: Arroyo Tapiado and Arroyo Seco del Diablo
offroad.difficulty: "4WD only, poor condition" — and State Parks flags it "one-way only"
offroad.season: No published gate. Mud-cave country; do not enter after rain.
offroad.note: The mud caves. State Parks marks this pair as one-way travel, so it is committed once started — down Tapiado and out Diablo, not there-and-back. Furthest of the four from Borrego Springs, down at the Bow Willow end of S2.
offroad.source: California State Parks — Anza-Borrego Desert SP Road Conditions

Betty's Kitchen National Recreation Trai.entity: National recreation trail on the lower Colorado near Yuma. No article. Checked both plausible parents: Imperial Dam and Mittry Lake mention neither Betty's Kitchen nor any trail.

Rest and reset before the service days.entity: A rest day, not a place. No entity to link.

trails.name: Betty's Kitchen National Recreation Trail
trails.was: Betty's Kitchen National Recreation Trail — no url
trails.note_source: A short interpretive loop on the Colorado below Imperial Dam. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

trails.name: Painted Desert Trail, Imperial NWR
trails.was: Painted Desert Trail, Imperial NWR — no url
trails.note_source: US Fish & Wildlife: a 1.3 mi loop from a trailhead about 3 miles north of the visitor centre via Red Cloud Mine Road, through 30,000-year-old volcanic ash formations. Official page verified: fws.gov/refuge/imperial/visit-us/trails

trails.name: Horse Tanks
trails.season: AllTrails gives January through March - the 14-18 Jan stay is at the very start of the best window for it.
trails.note: Kofa NWR desert wash walk to natural rock tanks. The one real half-day hike within driving range of the LTVA, and January is exactly when the desert is worth walking.

trails.name: Meers Point Trail
trails.note: Imperial National Wildlife Refuge's own short trail on the Colorado, and the refuge allows pets on a leash. Pairs with the Painted Desert Trail already on the card without a second long drive.
trails.note_source: US Fish & Wildlife Service, Imperial NWR trails page, fetched: Meers Point Trail, 0.8 miles, Moderate. The same table lists Painted Desert Trail at 1.3 miles, Desert Garden Trail and Pupfish Pond Trail.

other_links.label: USFWS — Imperial NWR trails
other_links.note: Managing authority. Publishes the trail list with lengths and difficulty.

trails.name: Long Telegraph Pass Loop
trails.season: Listed as open year-round; in January that is genuinely true rather than a formality.
trails.note: Gila Mountains climb south-east of Yuma. Graded Challenging, and kept on the card only because 167 reviews at 4.5 is a strong enough signal to be worth the drive on a cool day - not a walk to start at midday even in January.

trails.name: Laguna Mountains-Yuma Trail
trails.note: The long desert loop in the Lagunas, closest of these to the LTVA. Ten miles with no shade - a whole-day-or-nothing option, listed so the card shows the full range rather than only short walks.

offroad.name: Indian Pass Road
offroad.distance: runs north-east from Ogilby Road (County S-34) toward Picacho State Recreation Area, along the south side of the Indian Pass Wilderness
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded desert road with sandy wash sections; the far end toward Picacho is rougher
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT — this is the right season for it. The hazard in this corner of the Colorado Desert is summer heat, not winter closure; nothing gates the road. The stop arrives 14 Jan 2028, which is prime desert-driving weather.
offroad.note: The Indian Pass Wilderness lies along the north side of the road, and vehicles are prohibited inside wilderness — stay on the designated route, which is the road itself. No BLM page exists for the road on its own; the wilderness page is the land manager's coverage of the area and is the honest link. Dispersed camping is widespread along it. Carry water and recovery gear: this is remote, sandy and effectively unpatrolled.

not_a_route.entry: Tumco (Hedges) ghost town, off Ogilby Road
not_a_route.problem: A destination, not a route. Tumco is reached by a short dirt track off Ogilby Road onto BLM Route 668, roughly 8 miles north of the I-8 exit — a few minutes of easy driving, not a 4x4 route. It should move to the points-of-interest box, where the mine history (Hedges, peak ~3,200 residents 1893–1899, renamed Tumco in 1910, abandoned 1911) and the BLM interpretive signage at the parking area are the content. Keeping it in offroad implies a drive that is not there.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Imperial Dam and Laguna Dam river road
scenicDrives_patch.note: The BLM river country north of Yuma on the California side — Imperial Dam, Senator Wash reservoir and dam, Squaw Lake, and the run down to Laguna Dam with Mittry Lake Wildlife Area between the two dams. Access from I-8 via S-24 north about 22 mi, then Senator Wash Road. There is a check-in station at Senator Wash.
scenicDrives_patch.season: LTVA permit season runs 15 SEPTEMBER to 15 APRIL — that is when this area exists as a destination and when the winter-visitor population is here. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — peak of the season, so expect the LTVA busy. Permits: $180 long-term (the full seven months) or $40 for any 14 consecutive days.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Imperial Dam LTVA page; Visit Yuma river access map

other_links.label: Yuma river access points and map

scenicDrives_patch.name: Ogilby Road and the Cargo Muchacho mining district
scenicDrives_patch.note: Exit I-8 about 15 mi west of Yuma at Ogilby Road and run north roughly 8 mi; Tumco is signed by BLM. Gold town founded as Hedges, at least 500 people in the 1890s, abandoned 1905, renamed Tumco in 1910 after The United Mines Company. Now BLM land in the Cargo Muchacho Mountains with interpretive signage and a designated parking area. No entry fee. THE TOWNSITE IS CLOSED TO DRIVING — foot travel only past the parking area.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; year-round, but this is open desert with no shade and summer is genuinely dangerous. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — the right season for it.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Tumco Historic Mine page; Imperial Valley Press feature; mindat district records

imperial-dam.dogs: Imperial National Wildlife Refuge allows pets on leash, which covers the Painted Desert Trail; BLM's Betty's Kitchen page addresses only service dogs, so a pet dog there is unstated.
imperial-dam.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be on a leash, unless being actively used for lawful hunting purposes.
imperial-dam.stats_note: Several strong Yuma-area AllTrails listings are OHV routes rather than trails - McPherson Pass OHV Trail and Route of Butterfield Stage OHV Trail both surfaced and both were left out of this box; they belong in offroad if anywhere.

Castle Dome Mines Museum, on the way out.entity: Castle Dome City (Castle Dome Landing), AZ

Coach service — book Tue 18 to Fri 21.entity: A booking window for RV service, not a place.

Mobile techs, solar and lithium.entity: A category of service to arrange, not an entity.

Tyres and alignment.entity: A service task, not an entity.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-95 north toward Castle Dome and Kofa
scenicDrives_patch.note: US-95 runs north from Yuma between the Yuma Desert and the Kofa refuge, which begins about 40 mi out on the east side of the highway and covers 665,000 acres. Six entrance roads lead east off the highway — Crystal Hill, Palm Canyon, King Valley, Castle Dome among them; the southernmost, about 40 mi north of Yuma, goes to the southern Castle Dome Mountains. Palm Canyon Road is at MILEPOST 85, then 7 mi of dirt east to the trailhead — Arizona's only native palms, fewer than a hundred left, plus desert bighorn. The refuge was established in 1939 for the bighorn.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate. Best season is the cool half of the year; the entrance roads are unmaintained dirt and washboard, and washouts after storms are the constraint. Arrive 18 Jan 2028 — ideal.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: USFWS Kofa NWR visit page; Arizona Highways; Wilderness.net Kofa Wilderness

yuma-az.dogs_note: No managing-authority pet rule was found for the Gila Mountains (BLM) or the Yuma East Wetlands. AllTrails' crowd flag says leashed dogs are welcome on Long Telegraph Pass Loop and Bettys Kitchen, but that is not the authority, so no dogs value is recorded. This is the safe state, not a finding.

trails.name: East Wetlands Interpretive Trail
trails.note: Flat interpretive loop through the 400-acre restored wetland below the Territorial Prison, with a side trail connecting to the prison itself — which is already in the stop's activities. Cottonwood, willow, mesquite and cattail; the best birding within walking distance of town. The indexed snippet described the trail but published no distance, grade or time.

trails.name: Bettys Kitchen Interpretive Trail
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Short shaded birding loop on the Colorado backwater north of town, off the Mittry Lake road. A twenty-minute stop, not a day — good for the gaps while the coach is in the shop.

trails.name: Mittry Lake Trail
trails.note: Leaves the Mittry Lake Wildlife Area parking and runs south through low hills. AllTrails' snippet warns it is almost entirely exposed to the sun — fine in January, not in the shoulder seasons. Boat launches at the trailhead.

trails.name: Telegraph Pass Trail
trails.note: The most-reviewed trail anywhere near Yuma by a wide margin. Gila Mountains east of town, off the I-8 north frontage road. AllTrails' snippet is unusually blunt: the path is not well marked, download the offline map, the ground is loose and rocky, and there is a steep paved section near the top. NOT the same Telegraph Pass as the South Mountain one in Phoenix — the Yuma listing is the one whose summary views Yuma and Wellton.

trails.name: Long Telegraph Pass Loop
trails.season: Open year-round; the 18–22 Jan window is the only sane season for it.
trails.note: The full loop version of the pass, quiet by AllTrails' own account. Kept below the easy/moderate band because it is graded challenging and carries only 167 reviews.

offroad.name: Muggins Mountain Wilderness access roads
offroad.distance: the wilderness sits about 25 miles east of Yuma; BLM publishes no mileage for the approach roads themselves
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "Access by high-clearance and/or four-wheel drive vehicles is recommended."
offroad.season: No published closure. Winter is the season for it — the stop's 18-22 Jan 2028 dates are right.
offroad.note: The nearest genuine backcountry driving to a stop that exists for service and hookups. Roads lead to the wilderness boundary only; inside a designated wilderness no vehicle may go, so this is drive-to-the-edge-and-walk.

offroad.name: Imperial Sand Dunes Recreation Area — Gecko Road and Osborne Overlook
offroad.difficulty: not graded. The graded corridor roads are ordinary driving; the open dunes are not — soft sand riding is for sand-prepared vehicles, and BLM's rules page is the authority on where a street-legal vehicle may go
offroad.season: Year-round, but the dunes are a winter destination and busiest on holiday weekends.
offroad.note: About 20-25 miles west of Yuma across the California line. Worth the drive as a look rather than a drive-the-dunes day: "A permit is required for all primary street legal vehicles" in the fee areas, and Osborne Overlook is the place to stand and watch. Read https://www.blm.gov/visit/imperial-sand-dunes/rules-and-regulations before going — the permit and vehicle rules are specific.

Astronomy night.entity: A generic activity, not a named entity. The Kofa National Wildlife Refuge article has no astronomy or dark-sky content either.

kofa-nwr.dogs_note: US Fish & Wildlife Service for Kofa NWR: "Pets are permitted if they are confined or on a leash. Dogs may only be off-leash when they are participating in quail and cottontail hunting." That is a refuge-wide permission with no trail exceptions published — so this is a stop where the dog walks everything on the card. Rare on this leg.
kofa-nwr.box_note: Kofa is deliberately short, and that is the finding rather than a gap. Komoot's refuge guide states that most hiking here is "unmaintained social trails requiring good route-finding skills"; AllTrails indexes 14 routes for a 665,000-acre refuge. Palm Canyon is the one built, signed trail. The rest of the stay is the Kofa Queen Canyon and Castle Dome driving already in the activities.

trails.name: Palm Canyon Trail
trails.distance: 0.45 mi (USFWS); described elsewhere as a half-mile
trails.difficulty: Moderately easy (American Trails); Komoot calls it short but strenuous
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities and the reason the stop exists. Steady rocky incline to the sign below the side canyon holding Arizona's only native California fan palms — the palms are up and to the left of the sign, and AllTrails warns the sign is NOT the way to continue on the trail. Best light on the palms is around midday; they are in shade otherwise. Two authorities give slightly different lengths and grades, both recorded rather than averaged.

trails.name: Signal Peak Trail
trails.note: The high point of the Kofa Mountains at 4,877 ft. AllTrails describes it as a desert summit climb through rugged terrain in a remote corner of the state; no distance, grade or time surfaced in the indexed snippet, and the refuge publishes nothing. Treat as a full committing day and settle the figures before setting out.

trails.name: Big Eye Mine
trails.note: Remote route into the Castle Dome Mountains ending at the preserved Big Eye Mine — the same range as the Castle Dome City ghost town already in the activities. AZOffroad rates the approach 5.5/10 as a 4x4 route, so this is a truck day with a walk at the end rather than a trailhead you drive to. Twenty reviews: real, but thin.

trails.name: Horse Tanks
trails.note: The half-day walk this stop was missing. Runoff off the Kofa's rock faces has scoured swimming-pool-sized tinajas into the bedrock and they hold water through the dry months - which in a desert refuge established for bighorn sheep is exactly where the sheep are. Reached off King Road on an unnamed track; sources describe it as passable to most high-clearance vehicles with a few dicey washes, so it is a truck day, not a coach day. AllTrails notes you are unlikely to meet many other people.
trails.season: Late January is the good half of the year here. Kofa in summer is unwalkable; 22-27 Jan is close to ideal.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Explore this 6.3-mile out-and-back trail near Yuma, Arizona. Generally considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 2 h 8 min to complete... it's unlikely you'll encounter many other people while exploring.' Star and count from the AllTrails Horse Tanks point-of-interest page: 4.2 star rating from 64 reviews, 6.3 mi, 324 ft. Tinaja description from Trails Offroad's Horse Tanks route page; access-road condition from a first-hand van account (davidelmore.com).
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted if they are confined or on a leash.
trails.dogs_note: US Fish and Wildlife Service, refuge-wide. Off-leash only for quail and cottontail hunting dogs. Same rule applies to every trail at this stop.
trails.stats_note: A second, much thinner listing exists - 'Horse Tanks Hike', 16 reviews - describing the same primitive route. The 64-review listing is the one recorded.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Horse Tanks Hike (second listing)
other_links.note: 16 reviews. 'Winding through the rugged Kofa National Wildlife Refuge... a primitive path... toward natural rock basins, or tanks.'

trails.name: Crystal Hill
trails.note: The short walk of the stop, and the only one on the card with a reason to look at the ground rather than the horizon: Crystal Hill is a designated rock-collection area inside the refuge where surface quartz crystals may legally be picked up. It sits about 5.6 miles east of AZ-95 down a washboard gravel road, roughly eleven miles south of Quartzsite, in a 14-day dispersed camping area - so it doubles as a scouting run for a boondocking spot.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Head out on this 1.3-mile out-and-back trail near Quartzsite, Arizona. Generally considered a moderately challenging route, it takes an average of 47 min to complete', 84 reviews from the page title. Access and collection rules from Roadtrippers ('It is a 14 day BLM camping area where you can also collect surface minerals', 5.6 miles from AZ 95) and The Dyrt (eleven miles south of Quartzsite along Highway 95, 5.7 miles of washboard gravel, USFWS land).
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted if they are confined or on a leash.
trails.stats_note: No star rating and no elevation gain appeared in any snippet read for this listing - only the raw count of 84. Recorded as absent.

offroad.name: Palm Canyon Road
offroad.distance: about 7 miles of unpaved road from US 95 — the first 3 graded and wide to the refuge boundary, the remaining 4 narrower but smoother
offroad.difficulty: Not graded by FWS. The refuge says only that "Most refuge roads are not maintained. Many are passable only by four-wheel drive vehicles. Some roads may be passable by two-wheel drive, high clearance vehicles." Palm Canyon is the maintained exception.
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published. The stop's 22-27 Jan 2028 dates are prime desert season; the hazard here is a washed-out road after rain, and FWS asks you to phone (928) 928-6873 for current conditions.
offroad.note: The one road at Kofa that does not need a 4x4, and the one everybody drives — it ends at the trailhead below the only native palms in Arizona. Mileage is from americansouthwest.net, not from FWS; FWS publishes no length for it.
offroad.source: US Fish & Wildlife Service — Kofa NWR Visit Us (mileage from americansouthwest.net)

offroad.name: King Road
offroad.difficulty: described as an easy drive; no official grade published
offroad.season: No published closure. Refuge roads are unmaintained and change with weather.
offroad.note: The main western entrance to the refuge off US 95, running east into King Valley between the Kofa and Castle Dome ranges. FWS confirms the refuge has this road network and marks junctions with numbered markers, but publishes no description of individual roads — this entry's characterisation is from Trails Offroad, not the refuge.
offroad.source: Trails Offroad — Kofa Wildlife Refuge region page

offroad.name: Castle Dome Mine Road
offroad.distance: pavement ends at 1.8 miles; roughly 8 miles in from Castle Dome Road, then about 12 miles down to the King Valley Road junction
offroad.difficulty: not published on a free listing — Trails Offroad and onX both paywall their difficulty scales
offroad.season: No published closure.
offroad.note: The southern approach, from US 95 north of Yuma past the Castle Dome Mine Museum and up into the Castle Dome Mountains. Mileages here are from onX and a trip report, not from FWS. The refuge rule that governs all of this: "Vehicles and bicycles are limited to designated roads which can be identified by numbered markers at junctions. Off-road driving is prohibited."
offroad.source: onX Offroad (rule quoted from US Fish & Wildlife Service — Kofa NWR)

scenicDrives_patch.name: Martinez Lake Road and Red Cloud Mine Road into Imperial NWR
scenicDrives_patch.distance: US-95 between mileposts 46 and 47, then about 10 miles west on Martinez Lake Road, then north on Red Cloud Mine Road and three miles of brown signs to the visitor center
scenicDrives_patch.season: Visitor center open November 1 - March 31 only, Friday-Sunday 10:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m. The 22-27 Jan stay is inside that window, and Sat 22 and Sun 23 Jan are the two staffed days that fall in it. Refuge lands, roads and trails are open dawn to dusk daily year-round.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Fish and Wildlife's own visit page. The mile figures come from the refuge's Locations page: "From Yuma/Quartzite: Take Highway 95 (north from Yuma or south from Quartzite) and turn west onto Martinez Lake Road located between mile markers 46 and 47." Camp is on Palm Canyon Road further north on the same highway, so this is a straight run south on US-95 and back. At the end: an observation platform by the headquarters, and two gravel walking trails off the road - Painted Desert Trail 1.3 miles and Meers Point Trail 0.8 miles. FWS publishes no signed auto-tour loop for Imperial, only these access roads and trailheads, which is why no loop mileage is recorded here. Headquarters office Mon-Thu 8:00-4:30, Fri 8:00-3:30.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Goose Loop Auto Tour, Cibola NWR
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 3-mile drive at 25 mph
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset. The refuge's own leaflet: "Winter viewing of geese, cranes, and ducks is particularly good along this drive" - a late-January stay is the middle of it.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Figures are from the Service's own Goose Loop Auto Tour leaflet (PDF, Jan 2025), not from a travel site. Two things off that leaflet worth carrying: "Please stay in your vehicle except to walk the Nature Trail and use the restroom", and "Pets not allowed out of your vehicle on the loop or the Nature Trail" - which decides how the dog's day works. The loop runs the edge of the refuge alfalfa and corn fields past marked burrowing-owl burrows; there is a 1-mile Nature Trail loop to a wildlife observation deck over a 40-acre pond, with a photography blind nearby, and Cibola Lake Overlook is a further 11 miles on. This is the longest of the three - north to Quartzsite, west toward Blythe, then south - so it is a whole day, not an afternoon.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Avenue 7E to Mittry Lake and Betty's Kitchen
scenicDrives_patch.distance: AZ-95 east 7 miles from Yuma, then north on Avenue 7E 9.5 miles to the end of the pavement, then about half a mile unpaved to the lake; Betty's Kitchen is signed off the same avenue about 9 miles north, past Laguna Dam
scenicDrives_patch.note: Two BLM pages, both read. Mittry Lake Wildlife Area is about 3,000 acres with a three-lane boat launch; BLM lists mule deer, javelina, bobcat and desert bighorn alongside the birds. Betty's Kitchen sits between Mittry Lake, Laguna Dam and the Colorado River and carries a 0.5-mile interpretive trail, a National Recreation Trail since 1993, with about ten parking spaces on dirt, two picnic tables and a fishing pier - no grills, no fire pits, day use only. BLM says the site is "best visited during the spring, winter, and fall", which puts a January visit in the good half of the year. Yuma Field Office 928-317-3200 for road condition.

kofa-nwr._review: Three entries for five nights in a refuge where AllTrails indexes fourteen trails. Palm Canyon is a 0.9 mi walk, Big Eye Mine is reached down a 15-mile offroad track, and Signal Peak is a full mountain - so the middle of the range was empty. Both additions are refuge-wide pet-legal, which at this stop is every trail.

trails.name: Hutch's Pool via West Fork Sabino Trail FS #24
trails.was: Sabino Canyon Recreation Area — a recreation area, not a trail
trails.note_source: Sabino Canyon's best-rated route. No direct listing url surfaced; the area page is on the box heading.

trails.name: Desert Discovery Nature Trail
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL, AND THIS STOP NEEDED ONE. Saguaro West, paved half-mile interpretive loop. It matters because the only trail previously on this card, Hutch's Pool, starts inside the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area - the single place in the whole Coronado National Forest where dogs are banned outright. Ten nights in Tucson with an animal aboard needed a legal walk on the card.
trails.note_source: NPS Saguaro pets page, fetched. West District (Tucson Mountain): Desert Discovery Trail, 0.5 mile paved loop; Bajada Loop Drive; Golden Gate Road. East District (Rincon Mountain): Mica View Trail, 0.7 miles; Mica View dirt road, 1.5 miles; Desert Ecology Trail, 1/4 mile paved; Cactus Forest Loop Road. 'Pets prohibited on all other trails.' Leash 6 ft.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets at Saguaro
other_links.note: Authority; names every dog-legal trail and road in both districts, with lengths.

trails.name: Mica View Trail
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL. Saguaro East, off the Cactus Forest Loop Road - flat desert-floor walking through dense saguaro forest, and it joins the 1.5-mile Mica View dirt road, which is also open to dogs. February is the right month to be doing it.
trails.note_source: NPS Saguaro pets page, fetched - see the Desert Discovery entry for the full list.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets at Saguaro
other_links.note: Authority; names Mica View Trail (0.7 miles) and the Mica View dirt road (1.5 miles).

trails.name: Desert Ecology Trail
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL. Quarter-mile paved loop on the Cactus Forest Loop Road in Saguaro East, about how desert plants find water. Wheelchair-flat, and the shortest legal leg-stretch with the dog anywhere in the park.
trails.note_source: NPS Saguaro pets page, fetched - see the Desert Discovery entry.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets at Saguaro
other_links.note: Authority; names the Desert Ecology Trail (1/4 mile paved).

trails.name: Dripping Spring via the Sutherland Trail
trails.season: November through April per AllTrails - a 4-14 Feb stay sits in the middle of the best window it has.
trails.note: Catalina State Park, north of the city: four easy miles up a wash to a seasonal spring, with the Santa Catalina front range above. The best-fitting real hike found for this stop's dates.

alltrails.name: Dripping Spring via the Sutherland Trail

trails.name: Sentinel Peak Road Loop
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: 'A Mountain' - the loop up Sentinel Peak right beside downtown, with the whole city laid out below. Under two miles, paved road for most of it, and the most-reviewed easy walk in Tucson.

tucson.authority: USDA Forest Service — Coronado National Forest
tucson.dogs: Coronado NF: "Dogs are allowed anywhere in the forest except the Pusch Ridge Wilderness Big Horn Sheep closure area and the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area." The forest notes the bighorn closure "is only a portion of the Pusch Ridge Wilderness".
tucson.dogs_exception: The one trail on this card starts inside the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area, which is the single place in the whole forest where dogs are banned — trails, tram road, picnic areas, shuttle and all. Everywhere else in the Coronado is open; this stop needs a different trailhead if the dog is coming.

official_links.label: Hiking and Camping with Dogs — Coronado NF (USFS)

not_a_route.problem: Not a drive — SABINO CANYON HAS BEEN CLOSED TO PRIVATE VEHICLES SINCE 1978. The 7.4 mi road up the canyon is served by the Sabino Canyon Crawler shuttle, and is otherwise walked, ridden on horseback or cycled. Road cycling on it is further restricted to before 9am and after 5pm because of the trams. It cannot be a truck day-trip; it is a shuttle ride, a walk or an early-morning bike. Move it out of scenicDrives — as a bike outing it is a strong one: paved, no traffic, stroller- and wheelchair-usable.
not_a_route.season: Open year-round. Arrive 4 Feb 2028 — the good season in the Catalinas.
not_a_route.note_source: USFS Coronado Sabino Canyon Recreation Area; americansouthwest.net; RPC shuttle operator

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sabino Canyon Road
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 3.8 miles of paved road through the canyon
scenicDrives_patch.note: NOT DRIVABLE, in any vehicle. Coronado National Forest, the managing authority: "The canyon itself has been closed to private vehicles since 1978. However, you can still visit Sabino Canyon in an emission-free, open-air Sabino Canyon Crawler or Bear Canyon shuttle." The only motorised traffic on the 3.8-mile road is the Sabino Canyon and Bear Canyon shuttles and agency vehicles. This belongs on the card as a shuttle-and-walk outing, not as a scenic drive — the truck goes no further than the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area lot at 5700 N. Sabino Canyon Road. Recreation area page: fs.usda.gov/r03/coronado/recreation/groups/sabino-canyon-recreation-area. February arrival is peak season for it, so expect the lot to fill.

tucson.stats_note: The three NPS trails carry no AllTrails link because none was searched for this pass - `unlisted` here is 'not searched', not 'not listed'. Their distances and their dog status come straight from the National Park Service, which is the better tier for both.

offroad.name: Redington Road #371
offroad.distance: approximately 12 miles to the community of Redington; Coronado NF budgets about three hours round trip from Tucson
offroad.difficulty: not published by Coronado NF — the page gives no surface or vehicle requirement, which is itself worth knowing before setting out
offroad.season: No gate published. High point about 4,500 ft, so snow is not usually the issue; the road washboards badly and grading is intermittent.
offroad.note: Straight off the end of Tanque Verde Road at the edge of town, over the pass between the Santa Catalinas and the Rincons. The most convenient dirt from a Tucson base by a wide margin, and the closest thing to an after-lunch option. Lower Tanque Verde Falls trail is on it.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Redington Road #371 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Charouleau Gap Road #736
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF: "This scenic route is for 4-wheel drive vehicles only. The road up and over Samaniego Ridge is rough and rocky and requires good ground clearance as well as excellent traction."
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists it as available year-round. High point about 5,400 ft.
offroad.note: The serious one — a historic route between Oracle and Tucson over Samaniego Ridge, and the Forest is unusually blunt about the surface. No published mileage. Starts near Lago del Oro on the Oro Valley side, so it is closer to the Catalina State Park end of this cluster than to central Tucson.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Charouleau Gap Road #736 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Control Road #38 (Old Mt Lemmon Road)
offroad.difficulty: "This rough, winding road that snakes up the northeastern slopes of the Santa Catalinas" — Coronado NF publishes no vehicle requirement
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. Coronado NF: "Seasonal gate closure is in effect yearly from December 15th to February 28th." The stop runs 4-14 Feb 2028, entirely inside the closure. Enforced under 36 CFR 261.13, so it is a gate and a citation, not a suggestion.
offroad.note: The back way up Mt Lemmon from Oracle, climbing to about 8,000 ft — the first major access route ever built to the top. Shut for the whole of this stay and the whole of the Catalina State Park stay that follows. It reopens 29 Feb 2028 (2028 is a leap year), which is after both. Santa Catalina Ranger District, (520) 749-8700, if a late-February reopening is worth asking about.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Control Road #38 Scenic Drive

tucson.dogs_source_quote: Yes, dogs are allowed anywhere in the forest except the Pusch Ridge Wilderness Big Horn Sheep closure area and the Sabino Canyon Recreation Area.
tucson.dogs_source_note: Our card drops the leading "Yes," (the page is an FAQ answer) — otherwise verbatim. The qualifier is confirmed on the same page: "The Pusch Ridge Wilderness Big Horn Sheep closure area is only a portion of the Pusch Ridge Wilderness."

Charouleau Gap (truck).entity: 4x4 route over the Santa Catalina foothills. No article, and the Catalina State Park full text never mentions it.

catalina-state-park.dogs_note: Arizona State Parks for Catalina: "Dogs are welcome on all park trails and in the washes but must be kept on a leash with a maximum length of 6 ft/1.8 m at all times." That permission STOPS at the Coronado National Forest boundary — the park's own trail pages state "Dogs and bicycles are not allowed" on the Romero Canyon Trail beyond the Forest Service gate, on the wilderness section of the Sutherland Trail, and on the Trail Link, all of which enter the Pusch Ridge Wilderness bighorn closure. So the dog walks the park freely and stops at the gate.

trails.name: Canyon Loop Trail
trails.difficulty: Moderate (Arizona State Parks); AllTrails calls it easy and 80% of reviewers agree
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities and the obvious first walk — it starts at the main trailhead car park, a few minutes from the campground. Both grades are recorded because the authority and the trail database disagree; the authority is not overruled.

trails.name: Birding Trail
trails.distance: 1.0 mi (Arizona State Parks); AllTrails logs the loop at 1.2 mi
trails.difficulty: Moderate (Arizona State Parks); AllTrails calls it easy
trails.note: Horses are not allowed, per the park. Branches right off the Romero Pools / Canyon Loop start and drops straight into the shadiest, greenest ground in the park — the best cool-hour walk of the stay.

trails.name: Romero Ruins Interpretive Trail
trails.note: Horses and bicycles are not allowed, per the park. A 1,200-year-old Hohokam village site with interpretive boards, on a rise with the full sweep of the Catalinas behind it. Its own car park on Catalina State Park Road.

trails.name: Romero Canyon Trail to Romero Pools
trails.distance: 7.2 mi for the full Romero Canyon Trail (Arizona State Parks); 6.2 mi round trip to the pools
trails.time: approx. 3 h 10 min to the pools
trails.difficulty: Difficult (Arizona State Parks, for the full trail); moderately challenging to the pools
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities and the biggest day of the stay. NO DOG — the park states dogs and bicycles are not allowed beyond the Forest Service gate, which is well below the pools, so this is a walk that has to happen without her. 5,803 reviews is the second-highest count on this whole leg.

trails.name: Bridle Trail
trails.note: Easy, bike-legal per the park, dog-legal, and inside the park boundary the whole way — the connector between the equestrian centre and the main trailhead. Length, grade and permitted uses are Arizona State Parks; no AllTrails listing surfaced, so no trail link.

trails.name: 50 Year Trail
trails.note: The park's long multiuse line, described by Arizona State Parks as popular with equestrians and mountain bikers. Bike-legal and dog-legal, but no surface description could be sourced, so nothing is claimed about whether it would ride as a gravel cruise. Figures are Arizona State Parks.

offroad.name: Charouleau Gap Road #736
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF: "This scenic route is for 4-wheel drive vehicles only. The road up and over Samaniego Ridge is rough and rocky and requires good ground clearance as well as excellent traction."
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists it as available year-round. High point about 5,400 ft — the top can hold snow after a February storm, though no gate is published.
offroad.note: This is the stop's own road. FR 736 leaves the dirt near Lago del Oro, minutes from the park gate, and climbs over Samaniego Ridge into the upper Cañada del Oro — the same canyon the park's trails walk up from below. No published mileage. A number of primitive spurs branch off it.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Charouleau Gap Road #736 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Control Road #38 (Old Mt Lemmon Road)
offroad.difficulty: "This rough, winding road that snakes up the northeastern slopes of the Santa Catalinas" — no vehicle requirement published
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. Coronado NF: "Seasonal gate closure is in effect yearly from December 15th to February 28th." The stop runs 14-18 Feb 2028, inside the closure; the gate does not lift until 29 Feb 2028.
offroad.note: The Oracle end of this road is close to the park, which is what makes the closure worth stating rather than omitting. Shut for this whole stay and the Tucson stay before it.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Control Road #38 Scenic Drive

catalina-state-park.area_browse_finding: AllTrails has no park page for Catalina State Park, so the trail-box heading falls back to Arizona. Searched and confirmed absent rather than left unchecked — the trails themselves all carry their own listings.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Catalina Highway (Sky Island Parkway) to Mount Lemmon
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 27 miles, climbing to about 9,000 ft. The Forest Service's own Mt Lemmon recreation guide gives the figure as "This paved, 24-mile route ... climbs nearly 6,000 ft. from Sonoran Desert to pine forest" - the two FS pages disagree by three miles and both are recorded rather than picking one.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No scheduled seasonal gate: the Forest Service lists this drive as year-round. But it is snow-liable in February and the Forest Service says so plainly - "Following snowstorms, the road may be closed temporarily; snow tires, chains, or 4WD may be required." That is a storm-by-storm risk, not a dated closure, so it does not conflict with the 14-18 Feb stay; call the Pima County Sheriff's 24-hour Road Condition Hotline, 520-351-3351, on the morning you go.
scenicDrives_patch.note: ADOT designates F.S. 833 / F.S. 10 / F.S. 11 as the Sky Island Parkway, a state Parkway, dated 17 Aug 2001 - one of only a handful of Parkway designations in Arizona. This is the only paved road to the upper Santa Catalinas, and for this stop it is the way up: the unpaved alternative, Control Road #38 (Old Mt Lemmon Road), is already in the offroad box and is gated 15 Dec - 28 Feb, which covers this entire stay.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Cactus Forest Loop Drive, Saguaro NP East
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 8 miles (12.9 km), paved loop
scenicDrives_patch.season: "Open from 5 am to dusk every day of the year" - no seasonal gate.
scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS Getting Around page. The restriction is stated as a combined length, which matters here: "vehicles in excess of 102 inches (8.5 feet) wide and/or towing a vehicle, trailer, semitrailer, etc. for a combined total length of 40 feet or longer are prohibited". The towed truck on its own is fine; nothing about this drive is available to the coach, and there is no RV parking at the district. Several trailheads, scenic vistas and pullouts along it, and bicycles are permitted on the loop.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Bajada Loop Drive, Saguaro NP West
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 6 miles (9.7 km) on the NPS Getting Around page, 5 miles on the NPS Accessibility page - two Park Service pages disagree by a mile and both are recorded. Unpaved graded dirt.
scenicDrives_patch.season: "Open from dawn to dusk every day of the year" - no seasonal gate.
