scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS says high clearance and 4WD are not required, and the accessibility page calls the route "unpaved but passable for all vehicles" - so this is a graded touring road, not a 4x4 route, which is why it sits here and not in the offroad box. Same 102-inch-wide / 40-ft-combined prohibition as the east district. Pullouts, picnic areas and trailheads throughout, accessible parking at the picnic areas; bicycles permitted.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Gates Pass Road, Tucson Mountain Park
scenicDrives_patch.note: Pima County manages this one and publishes no length for the road, so none is recorded - the 4.8-mile figure that circulates on travel sites has no authority behind it and is left out. What the county does publish: a paved staging area at the Gates Pass Overlook with space for 50 vehicles, gates open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., and - the line that decides the day with the dog - "Dogs are not permitted on trails." The county's campground policy page adds "Weight restrictions apply to Gates Pass Road. RVs longer than 25ft should enter Tucson Mountain Park from Ajo Highway to Kinney Road", which is academic for a truck but confirms the road is not a coach route in any circumstance. Sunset viewpoint over Avra Valley; pairs naturally with the Bajada Loop on the same side of town.

bisbee-tombstone.dogs_note: Three different authorities, three different answers, and none of them is 'yes' by default. The Nature Conservancy bans pets at Ramsey Canyon Preserve outright (service animals excepted), "in consideration of canyon wildlife". NPS Coronado National Memorial: "With the exception of the Crest Trail, pets are not allowed on trails in the park and must be leashed at all times." Arizona State Parks publishes no pet rule on the Kartchner trail pages that loaded, so nothing is recorded for Kartchner. The Crest Trail is the only dog-legal walk found for this stop.

trails.name: Foothills Loop Trail, Kartchner Caverns State Park
trails.distance: approximately 2.5 mi; 3.2 mi for the full loop including the 1.7 mi Ocotillo Trail addition
trails.note: Best-reviewed trail in reach of this stop and it pairs with the Kartchner Caverns tour already in the activities — the trail climbs the limestone hill above the cave and drops into the wash on the fault between the Whetstone and San Pedro blocks. No bicycles or motorised vehicles. Figures Arizona State Parks.

trails.name: Ramsey Canyon Trail
trails.season: The Nature Conservancy preserve is CLOSED TUESDAY AND WEDNESDAY, and from 1 Nov to 28 Feb opens 9 a.m.–4 p.m. The 23–28 Feb stay falls inside the winter hours, so plan round the two closed days. $8 per person, $5 for Cochise County residents. Only 27 parking spaces, first come first served — arrive early.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. World-famous birding canyon. NO DOG: TNC prohibits pets, along with smoking, camping, fires, radios, bicycles and drones.

trails.name: Ramsey Canyon and Hamburg Trail
trails.season: Same preserve closures, hours, fee and 27-space car park as above. The Forest Service notes a permit is required for the Hamburg Trail where it starts at the preserve.
trails.note: The longer version — TNC describes the Hamburg Trail as paralleling Ramsey Creek through the preserve, then climbing 500 ft in a half-mile of steep switchbacks to an overlook in the Coronado National Forest a mile above the headquarters. No dog.

trails.name: Coronado Cave Trail
trails.note: Trailhead about 0.25 mi past the Coronado National Memorial visitor centre. Short steep climb to an undeveloped 600 ft cave with 20 ft ceilings — no lighting and no rangers inside, so it needs proper torches. Figures NPS.

trails.name: Coronado Peak Trail
trails.note: Short paved-and-stepped climb from Montezuma Pass to the interpretive summit looking straight down into Mexico and the San Pedro Valley — the best view-per-effort of the stop, and it fits alongside the Coronado Memorial visit already in the activities. Figures NPS. No AllTrails listing surfaced, so no trail link.

trails.name: Crest Trail, Coronado National Memorial
trails.distance: 4 mi round trip to the park boundary; 5.3 mi one way to Miller Peak
trails.note: THE ONLY DOG-LEGAL TRAIL FOUND FOR THIS STOP — NPS names it as the single exception to the memorial's pet ban, leashed. It is also the hardest thing on the card, so the dog's only option here is a serious climb; going as far as the park boundary and turning round is the realistic version. Figures NPS.

trails.name: Guindani Trail #398
trails.difficulty: Arizona State Parks: the first mile easy, the next two-thirds moderate, the last leg strenuous
trails.note: Starts inside Kartchner Caverns State Park and spends almost all of its length on the east flank of the Whetstone Mountains in the Coronado National Forest. Described by Arizona State Parks as a shared-use, non-motorised trail. No AllTrails listing surfaced; the Forest Service page for it is the source of record.

trails.name: Carr Peak Trail
trails.note: Huachuca Mountains above Sierra Vista, in the Miller Peak Wilderness. AllTrails describes it as well maintained with a steady and challenging climb. Listed last: the grade could not be sourced and the count does not clear the outstanding bar, so it sits below everything rated above.

offroad.name: Middlemarch Road #345
offroad.distance: 20.5 miles one way; Coronado NF gives about an hour between the two Strongholds and 3-4 hours for a 100-mile loop from Benson
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF: "20.5-mile (one-way) dirt road", "High-clearance recommended"
offroad.season: No gate published.
offroad.note: The crossing of the Dragoon Mountains east of Tombstone, over Middlemarch Pass through old mining country to Pearce. The best-specified dirt road of this stop — the Forest publishes both the mileage and the clearance recommendation, which most of these pages do not.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Cochise Stronghold

offroad.name: Carr Canyon Road #368
offroad.distance: approximately 7 miles from the highway to the upper reaches
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF: "The first mile or so is paved; the rest is dirt and rugged", "High-clearance recommended beyond the Clark Spring Trailhead", and "The switchbacks are narrow and steep with no guard rails"
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. Coronado NF: "Road closes seasonally (approximately December 15 to March 15) for snow, flooding, or fire danger." The stop is 23-28 Feb 2028, inside that window — the gate does not lift until mid-March, two weeks after departure. Ranger station (520) 378-0311 to check whether it has opened early.
offroad.note: The switchbacks up the east face of the Huachucas above Sierra Vista to the Reef. Also carries a hard length limit worth knowing: "Vehicles longer than 20 feet and trailers longer than 12 feet are prohibited beyond Carr Canyon Picnic Area" — that is a truck-only road even without the closure.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Carr Canyon Road #368 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Montezuma Pass via FR 48 and Border Road #61
offroad.difficulty: not published — Coronado NF describes the route but gives no surface grade or vehicle requirement for the FR 48 / FR 61 dirt sections
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists the route as available year-round.
offroad.note: Paved AZ-83 south from Sonoita to Parker Canyon Lake, then FR 48 and FR 61 angling toward the Huachucas and up to Montezuma Pass at the south end of the range, above Coronado National Memorial. The plateau it crosses sits at about 5,000 ft. FR 61 is the Border Road and runs along the international line — expect Border Patrol traffic and checkpoints.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Arizona Highway #83 to Montezuma Pass Scenic Drive

scenicDrives_patch.name: Ghost Town Trail - Gleeson, Courtland, Pearce
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 34 miles one way from Tombstone
scenicDrives_patch.note: Arizona Highways gives the turns: east from Tombstone on SR 80 to Camino San Rafael, left for 1 mile, right onto Gleeson Road for about 14 miles to Gleeson, then left at Ghost Town Trail / Gleeson-Pearce Road for Courtland and Pearce, in the shadow of the Dragoons. Dirt for most of its length but a graded county road, not a 4x4 route - which is why it is here and not in the offroad box, even though Trails Offroad also indexes it (as a scout route). No published vehicle restriction. The magazine's standing back-road caution applies: carry plenty of water, do not go alone, tell someone when you expect to be back, and check weather and road condition first. No seasonal closure is published; the hazard is wet weather, not the calendar.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Geronimo Trail to Slaughter Ranch and San Bernardino NWR
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 16 miles east from Douglas, then 0.6 mile on San Bernardino Road
scenicDrives_patch.season: Slaughter Ranch Museum is open 9:30 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. Wednesday to Sunday. The stay arrives Wed 23 Feb and leaves Mon 28 Feb, so Wed 23 through Sun 27 are all open days - there is no day of this stop on which the museum is shut.
scenicDrives_patch.note: From Douglas, east on 15th Street, which becomes the Geronimo Trail; Arizona Highways calls the final San Bernardino Road stretch "a well-maintained dirt road". $5 requested from adults, children free. Next door, San Bernardino National Wildlife Refuge - 2,369 acres established in 1982 on the international border, protecting what is left of the San Bernardino cienega, historically the largest wetland in the region - and FWS says outright that the rare birds are what draw most visitors. FWS publishes no road or auto-route detail for the refuge itself, so none is recorded.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Davis Road and Coffman Road to Whitewater Draw
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Entrance is about 2.5 miles off Davis Road on Coffman Road, past the farmhouse
scenicDrives_patch.season: "December through March" is given as the best window and the stay is inside it - this is the wintering ground for tens of thousands of sandhill cranes, and late February still holds them.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Arizona Game and Fish land, open 24 hours a day year-round, no fee, with restrooms, viewing platforms and short trails. The road caution is the one that matters after a storm: "Coffman Rd. and the dirt paths become quite muddy and slick" once rain has fallen. Nearest gas and food are Tombstone and Elfrida - there is nothing at the draw. Recorded at community tier because azgfd.com answers HTTP 403 from this sandbox; the Arizona Birding Trail page is the one actually read. Closer to this stop than to Willcox, which is why it is filed here rather than with the Sulphur Springs Valley birding roads at Chiricahua.

scenicDrives_patch.name: AZ-82 to Fairbank Historic Townsite, San Pedro Riparian NCA
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Parking area is on the north side of AZ-82, half a mile east of the San Pedro River
scenicDrives_patch.season: The Schoolhouse Museum is staffed by the Friends of the San Pedro River and is open Friday, Saturday and Sunday plus Monday holidays, 9:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. Fri 25, Sat 26 and Sun 27 Feb all fall inside the stay. The parking area itself is open sunrise to sunset every day.
scenicDrives_patch.note: BLM says "a standard vehicle is sufficient" and the trailhead lot is packed gravel with room for cars and trailer vehicles. A self-guided walk round a genuine Wild West boomtown: several historic buildings along Railroad Avenue including the Mercantile, and a 1.25-mile hardened compacted-gravel trail at under 2 percent grade running north to the old mill. Vault toilet, picnic tables, interpretive signs; water is not available on site, bring it. Fairbank sits inside the San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area, which protects 40 miles of the upper San Pedro.

superior-globe.dogs_note: Boyce Thompson Arboretum: "Leashed and well-behaved pets are welcome! Pets must be on a leash no longer than six feet and under the physical control of the owner." So the arboretum trails are the dog's day here — unusual for a botanical garden and worth knowing. No pet rule was found for the Tonto National Forest Picketpost trails, so nothing is recorded for those.

trails.name: Boyce Thompson Arboretum Main Trail
trails.distance: 1.5 mi loop (Southwestern USA Hiking); Hiiker logs 1.2 mi
trails.season: October–March hours are 8 a.m.–5 p.m. daily, last admission one hour before closing. The 2–4 Mar 2028 stay is inside that. Adult admission $24.95.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities and the anchor of a two-night stop. Starts at the visitor centre, crosses the suspension bridge, runs through the cactus gardens, the eucalyptus stand, the Chihuahuan and Australian collections. Dog-legal, leashed. AllTrails lists the trail but published no distance, grade, time or count in the indexed snippet, so the figures come from community sources and are labelled as such.

trails.name: Boyce Arboretum Gentle Route
trails.note: The flat version, for a hot afternoon or a slow one. Figures are AllTrails' own, given in metric in the indexed snippet and recorded as returned.

trails.name: Boyce Thompson Arboretum Main Trail to High Trail Loop
trails.note: Main Trail out over the suspension bridge, High Trail back via the Australian desert garden. AllTrails quotes the arboretum calling the High Trail the strenuous option — the same walk with the climb added. No figures published in the snippet.

trails.name: Picketpost Mountain Trail
trails.difficulty: Strenuous — AllTrails calls it a short, intense scramble demanding exceptional fitness and a high tolerance for exposure
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities, and kept on the card only because 3,501 reviews clears the outstanding bar. READ THE GRADE BEFORE COMMITTING: AllTrails states the final section "is not a hike but a difficult ascent up a steep, exposed chute", and multiple guides warn that people routinely lose the route. On a two-night stop with a dog and a coach to move the next morning, the arboretum is the better use of the day and this is the one to walk away from. Distance and gain from community sources; the trail is in the Tonto National Forest above the arboretum.

trails.name: Picketpost Loop via Arizona Trail and L.O.S.T Trail
trails.season: AllTrails notes stream crossings in spring — the 2–4 Mar date is at the start of that.
trails.note: The sane alternative to the summit: from the Picketpost trailhead along the Arizona Trail and the Legends of Superior Trail, circling the mountain instead of climbing it, with the desert views and none of the chute. No figures surfaced in the indexed snippet.

offroad.name: Apache Trail (SR 88) unpaved section
offroad.distance: the unpaved section runs from Fish Creek Vista (milepost 222) to milepost 227 near Reavis Trailhead Road
offroad.difficulty: not graded. ADOT describes the 1.5-mile section at Fish Creek Vista as "steep and more winding and narrow than other parts of SR 88" and asks drivers to ensure vehicles are "appropriate for unpaved terrain"
offroad.season: Open, and that is not a given — this section was closed from 2019 and reopened in stages; monsoon damage shut it again in 2026 and it was repaired and reopened that July. ADOT: "Although there are currently no vehicle restrictions," the status "can change should severe weather or rockfall affect conditions." Check the ADOT project page before driving out.
offroad.note: Approach it from the Globe end via Roosevelt Dam rather than from Apache Junction — the stop sits at the far end of the Trail from the tourist traffic. Fish Creek Hill is the famous bit and the reason to go. The most-changed road on this whole itinerary; verify status the week before.
offroad.source: Arizona Department of Transportation — SR 88 Apache Trail project page

offroad.name: Pinal Peak via Forest Road 651
offroad.difficulty: described as "washboarded dirt that's deeply rutted in places"; no Forest Service grade found
offroad.season: NOT VERIFIED, and this matters. Pinal Peak tops out near 7,800 ft directly above Globe, and secondary sources describe the road as a May-September proposition. The stop is 2-4 Mar 2028. No Tonto National Forest page publishing a gate date for FR 651 was found — treat access as unverified rather than assured, and phone the Globe Ranger District. Do not assume it is open because the desert below is warm.
offroad.note: Straight up out of Globe into ponderosa — an 8,000 ft climb-out from a Sonoran-desert town in a single afternoon, which is the appeal. Pinal Campground is on the way up. Recorded from Arizona Highways because no Forest Service page describing this road was found; the mileage and any restriction are unsourced.

Broken Arrow 4x4 trail (towed truck).entity: The Sedona 4x4 trail. No article. Sedona, Arizona's only 'Broken Arrow' mention is the 1950 film shot there, not the trail, and Coconino National Forest never mentions it.

Devil's Bridge Trail.entity: The Sedona sandstone arch. Rejected on identity: 'Devils Bridge' redirects to Devil's Bridge, an article about dozens of ancient European masonry arch bridges. It lists the Sedona arch in one line that explicitly excludes it from the subject -- 'this is a naturally formed bridge, not a man-made stone bridge'. Coconino NF does not mention it either.

trails.name: Cathedral Rock Trail
trails.was: Cathedral Rock — no url
trails.note_source: Short but steep slickrock scrambling — the difficulty is in the grade, not the distance.

trails.name: Devil's Bridge Trail via Dry Creek Road
trails.was: Devil's Bridge Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Sedona Airport Loop Trail
trails.note: Circuit right around Airport Mesa with red rock on every side the whole way - the most-reviewed trail in Sedona and the one that works in any March weather.
trails.stats_note: No star surfaced in any snippet for this listing; the 10,192 count is from the result title.

trails.name: Fay Canyon Trail
trails.note: Short flat-floored box canyon off Boynton Pass Road - shade, an arch high on the right-hand wall, and a fraction of the crowd that Devil's Bridge carries.

trails.name: Bell Rock - HT Trail
trails.note: The easy way at Bell Rock - the trail around the base rather than the scramble up it, from the Village of Oak Creek end, which is the Sedona trailhead closest to Camp Verde.
trails.stats_note: Not the same listing as 'Bell Rock Loop Trail' (4,870 reviews, moderately challenging, 47 min), which is a separate and harder route on the same formation.

trails.name: Doe Mountain Loop
trails.note: Short steep switchback up onto a flat mesa top and then a level walk right round the rim - a great deal of view for under three miles, which is the ratio that matters on an eight-night stay.

offroad.name: Broken Arrow Trail
offroad.distance: about 3.5 miles round trip, Sedona, Red Rock Ranger District, Coconino National Forest
offroad.difficulty: sources genuinely disagree and both are recorded. The Forest Service trail page presents it as moderate with spectacular views; the off-road community rates it hard — slickrock, rock ledges and 'the Steps', with high-clearance 4WD, low range, skid plates and a short wheelbase wanted. Treat it as the harder reading and scout the Steps on foot before committing.
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round; spring is the best of it. The stop arrives 4 Mar 2028 — good weather, but also the start of the busy season on a route already saturated with commercial jeep tours. Go early in the day.
offroad.note: No permit is needed to drive the route, but a Red Rock Pass or an equivalent federal lands pass is required to park at the trailhead. Chicken Point, a wide slickrock overlook, is the usual turnaround and the highlight; Submarine Rock is on the way. Short enough to be a half-day from Camp Verde with the drive up.

offroad.name: Dry Creek Road (FR 152)
offroad.distance: roughly 1.1 to 1.3 miles of unpaved road from the paved lot to the upper Devil's Bridge trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not published by the Forest Service. Community reports are consistent: high-clearance 4WD required, several large rocks to clear just to get onto the road, extremely rocky and rough throughout
offroad.season: No seasonal closure found. The stop arrives 4 Mar 2028 — no conflict.
offroad.note: No listing found. Coconino NF publishes nothing specific to FR 152 that a search returned, and the detailed accounts are all on hiking blogs and paywalled offroad databases, so this is recorded with no URL rather than a link to something that is really about the hike. Its value is that it cuts the Devil's Bridge hike to about 2 miles round trip instead of the long approach — the road is a way to shorten a walk, not a destination drive. FR 152 is not recommended for pedestrians because of vehicle traffic and dust.

not_a_route.problem: A hike, not an offroad route — 32,000+ reviews on AllTrails as a trail. It belongs in the trails box. What is offroad about it is the access, Dry Creek Road / FR 152, which is now listed separately above.

camp-verde.authority: USDA Forest Service — Coconino National Forest (Red Rock Ranger District)
camp-verde.dogs: Coconino NF: "Pets are typically allowed in most areas of the Coconino National Forest." "Dogs must be leashed and controlled at all times." "Owners must pick up after their pets" and "Do not leave pet waste (bagged or unbagged) along the trail or trailhead."
camp-verde.dogs_exception: Pets are not permitted at the Red Rock District heritage sites — Palatki, Honanki and Grasshopper Point. Cathedral Rock and Devil's Bridge are not among them.

official_links.label: Safety and Outdoor Ethics — Coconino NF (USFS)

camp-verde.stats_note: Dogs left absent throughout. The Red Rock Ranger District's own pet rule for these trails was not sourced this pass and Coconino NF was not fetched; the card should not imply an answer that was not read off the authority.
camp-verde.dogs_source_quote: Pets are typically allowed in most areas of the Coconino National Forest.
camp-verde.dogs_source_note: All four of our card's quotes verify on this page, including "Do not leave pet waste (bagged or unbagged) along the trail or trailhead." The page adds bans our card omits: pets are prohibited at the Palatki and Honanki Heritage Sites and at Grasshopper Point Swimming/Picnic Area (Red Rock District), and allowed at Elden Pueblo except during scheduled school programs.

Navajo Loop & Queen's Garden combo.entity: Navajo Loop and Queen's Garden trails

Mossy Cave Trail.entity: No article of its own. Bryce Canyon National Park's own text lists it among the park's hikes with its length and access: 'Mossy Cave (one hour, State Route 12 northwest of Tropic)'.

Sunrise Point & Sunset Point.entity: The two main Bryce Amphitheater viewpoints. Neither has an article -- and bare 'Sunrise Point' does not resolve at all. The park article names both in its own text as the trailheads for Queens Garden (Sunrise Point) and Navajo Loop (Sunset Point).

trails.name: Navajo Loop Trail
trails.was: Sunset Point (Navajo Loop trailhead) — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Mossy Cave Trail
trails.was: Mossy Cave Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Fairyland Loop Trail
trails.was: Fairyland Point — a viewpoint, not a trail

trails.name: Queen's Garden Trail
trails.distance: 1.8 mi (2.9 km) round trip from Sunrise Point; 2.9 mi (4.7 km) as the Queen's/Navajo Combination Loop
trails.time: 1-2 hours; 2-3 hours for the combination loop
trails.difficulty: Moderate — NPS: 'less than 1000 feet elevation gain, moderate length', and 'the least difficult of the trails descending from the rim into the Bryce Canyon Amphitheater'. Typical grade 11%, maximum 25%, firm native sediment.
trails.reviews_note: Count read from the AllTrails result title as displayed. The en-gb mirror showed 2,546 the same day. No star rating was visible for this listing.

alltrails.name: Queen Victoria via Queen's Garden Trail
alltrails.note: AllTrails indexes the trail under its destination hoodoo and reads it as 2.1 mi / 456 ft out-and-back. NPS's 1.8 mi / 450 ft is the authority figure and is what is recorded above.

other_links.label: NPS — Queen's Garden Trail
other_links.note: Full stat block: trailhead Sunrise Point, 1.8 mi roundtrip, 1-2 hours, 450 ft, Moderate, Pets not allowed.

trails.season: Open year-round. Late March is shoulder season: the descent is on packed, often icy tread in the shaded upper switchbacks and traction devices are the normal kit at this date. The park does not close it.
trails.note: The omission that mattered. Do it as the combination loop the park recommends — descend Queen's Garden from Sunrise Point, walk the amphitheater floor, climb the Navajo Loop switchbacks to Sunset Point, and close the circle on the paved Rim Trail. Navajo Loop was already on the card; this is the other half, and on its own it is the gentlest way below the rim at Bryce.

trails.name: Rim Trail — Sunset Point to Sunrise Point (paved section)
trails.distance: 1.0 mi (1.6 km) round trip, half a mile one way
trails.time: 1 hour (NPS lists the activity duration as 20-60 minutes)
trails.difficulty: Easy — NPS: 'the easiest walk in the park'. Paved concrete, typical grade 3.3%, typical width 97 in; NPS rates this section accessible.
trails.needs: No review count and no star rating could be read for the AllTrails listing; the result title carried neither. Recorded absent rather than guessed.
trails.dogs_source: NPS Bryce Canyon, Sunset Point to Sunrise Point Hike page, verbatim: 'Pets are allowed on paved surfaces.' and 'Pets are allowed on this trail but must remain on paved surfaces.' This is the ONLY trail in Bryce Canyon National Park where NPS answers Pets: Yes.

alltrails.name: Sunset Point and Sunrise Point via Rim Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Sunset Point to Sunrise Point Hike
NPS — Walk the Rim Trail (full 5.5 mi Bryce Point to Fairyland Point)

trails.season: Year-round; it is plowed and it is the section that stays walkable when everything below the rim is ice. Accessible restrooms at Sunset Point are open year-round.
trails.note: On a four-night stay where every other trail in the park is closed to pets, this is the dog's entire Bryce Canyon — and it happens to be the best mile of rim in the park, straight along the edge of the amphitheater with Thor's Hammer and the Silent City below. Oversized vehicles are not permitted in the Sunrise or Sunset parking areas while the shuttle runs; take the truck, not the coach.

trails.name: Bristlecone Loop Trail
trails.time: 1 hour (NPS lists the activity duration as 30-60 minutes)
trails.difficulty: Easy — NPS: 'elevation gain of 200 feet or less, shorter length'. AllTrails: 92% of reviewers call it easy.
trails.season: NPS lists SEASON: Spring, Summer, Fall — winter is deliberately absent — and warns 'This trail may be inaccessible during mid-winter due to snow depths ranging from 2-15 ft (.7-5 m).' The stop arrives 24 March at the trailhead's 9,100 ft, which is the very start of the listed season and above the depth where 2-15 ft of settled snow is still lying in a normal year. Treat it as a maybe, not a plan: check Current Conditions the morning of, and have the amphitheater as the fallback.
trails.note: Added deliberately as the one hike on this card outside the Bryce Amphitheater, and as the thing the itinerary is at risk of missing rather than something to count on. Rainbow Point at the far south end of the park road, 1,800-year-old bristlecone pines, and a view that reaches into the Four Corners. It is also the reason to drive the full 18 miles of park road, which is worth a morning by itself.

bryce.authority: National Park Service — Bryce Canyon National Park
bryce.dogs: NPS: "Pets are not permitted on trails or unpaved viewpoints (Piracy Point), in public buildings or on public transportation vehicles (shuttle bus)." Pets are "only permitted on paved surfaces in the park". Leash no longer than 6 feet; citations carry a minimum $75 fine.
bryce.dogs_exception: Two paved exceptions the park names explicitly: the Rim Trail between Sunset Point and Sunrise Point, and the paved Shared Use Path between the park entrance and Inspiration Point. Fairyland Loop, Navajo Loop and Mossy Cave are all closed to pets.

offroad.name: Cottonwood Canyons Scenic Backway
offroad.distance: 46 miles from Cannonville south to US-89 — "paved for 9 miles between Cannonville and the turnoff to Kodachrome Basin State Park", dirt for the remaining 37
offroad.difficulty: BLM publishes no vehicle requirement for it
offroad.season: No calendar gate — the surface is the gate. This is bentonite clay: fine when dry, undriveable within minutes of rain, and late March is not a dry month. BLM publishes a road condition report for Grand Staircase-Escalante, "typically updated weekly, more frequently if road conditions warrant", at https://www.blm.gov/documents/utah/public-room/data/road-report — read it the morning of, not the week before.
offroad.note: The big day out from Bryce and one of the best dirt roads in southern Utah, running the length of the Cockscomb through Grand Staircase-Escalante. Cannonville is about 15 miles from the stop, so the road starts almost at the door. Kodachrome Basin State Park is on the paved part.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Cottonwood Canyons Scenic Backway

offroad.name: Skutumpah Road
offroad.difficulty: described as a "rough, washboarded dirt road" whose conditions "can change from day to day depending on weather, maintenance" — that wording is from AllTrails, not from BLM; BLM's own report gives status rather than a grade
offroad.season: Same as Cottonwood Canyon and for the same reason. No calendar closure; BLM's weekly road report is the source that actually answers the question on the day.
offroad.note: The other road out of Cannonville, running southwest across the Skutumpah Terrace toward Johnson Canyon and Kanab, past the Willis Creek and Bull Valley Gorge slot trailheads. Pairs naturally with Cottonwood Canyon Road — one out, one back — but that is a long day and both need to be dry.
offroad.source: BLM Utah — Grand Staircase-Escalante road condition report (description from AllTrails)

bryce.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not permitted on trails or unpaved viewpoints (Piracy Point), in public buildings or on public transportation vehicles (shuttle bus).
bryce.dogs_source_note: $75 figure confirmed: "Pet owners not adhering to regulations may be cited (minimum fine is $75)."
bryce.dates_checked: 24-28 Mar 2028, 4 nights. Rim elevation 8,000-9,100 ft, so late March is still a snow-and-ice question, not a spring one.
bryce.trails_note: The card had Fairyland Loop (8 mi), Navajo Loop and Mossy Cave — and was missing the single hike the park itself recommends first. NPS on the Queen's/Navajo Combination Loop: 'Our most popular hike in the park and the one we most recommend to first-time visitors.' Queen's Garden is the half of it that was absent. Also added: the one walk the DOG is allowed, and the one hike outside the Bryce Amphitheater. Two things worth knowing for 24-28 Mar that apply to trails ALREADY on the card and so are recorded here rather than re-added: the Wall Street side of the Navajo Loop is CLOSED during the winter months (NPS) and typically reopens in spring, so the loop may only be walkable as a Two Bridges out-and-back; and the Fairyland Point spur road closes in winter, which turns Fairyland Loop into a longer walk from the main road if it has not yet been plowed. Check Current Conditions before either day.
bryce.dogs_stop_level: NPS publishes a per-trail Pets Yes/No on every Bryce trail page. It is No on every trail in the park EXCEPT the paved Sunset-to-Sunrise section of the Rim Trail: 'Pets are allowed on this trail but must remain on paved surfaces.' That single mile is the whole of the dog's Bryce.

trails.name: Hickman Bridge Trail
trails.was: Hickman Bridge Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Cassidy Arch Trail
trails.was: Cassidy Arch Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail

trails.name: Fremont River Trail
trails.note: THE DOG WALK AT CAPITOL REEF, and one of only two the park allows. NPS permits pets on the Fremont River Trail only as far as the south end of Hattie's Field - the flat orchard-and-river section out of the Fruita Campground. Past Hattie's Field the trail climbs hard to a bench above the river and the dog may not follow. Hickman Bridge and Cassidy Arch, the two trails already on this card, are both closed to pets outright.
trails.note_source: NPS Capitol Reef pets page, fetched: pets are allowed on 'The trail from the visitor center to Fruita Campground' and the 'Fremont River Trail (from campground to south end of Hattie's Field)', in unfenced orchards, the Chestnut and Doc Inglesby picnic areas, campgrounds, parking areas and 'within 50 feet of road center lines'. 'Pets are not permitted on other hiking trails, in public buildings, or in the backcountry.' Leash 6 ft. Distance, elevation change and difficulty from the NPS Fruita trail-guide table.

trails.name: Grand Wash
trails.note: Flat gravel wash between walls that close to the Narrows - the easiest long walk in the park and the one that suits a warm late-March afternoon. It is a flash-flood route: do not enter it with storms in the forecast.
trails.note_source: NPS Capitol Reef trail-guide table: Grand Wash, 7.2 km round trip, 61 m elevation change, Easy.

other_links.label: NPS — Capitol Reef trail guide
other_links.note: Authority for the figures.

trails.name: Capitol Gorge
trails.note: The old wagon route through the reef, past the pioneer register and up to the Tanks. Almost level, and reached by the dirt end of the Scenic Drive - truck, not coach.
trails.note_source: NPS Capitol Reef trail-guide table: Capitol Gorge, 3.2 km round trip, 24 m elevation change, Easy.

other_links.label: NPS — Capitol Reef trail guide
other_links.note: Authority for the figures.

trails.name: Cohab Canyon
trails.note: Switchbacks up out of Fruita into a hidden slot with honeycombed walls, plus two overlook spurs. It starts across the road from the campground, so it needs no drive at all - which on a four-night stay is worth a lot.
trails.note_source: NPS Capitol Reef trail-guide table: Cohab Canyon, 5.4 km round trip, 134 m elevation change, Moderate.

other_links.label: NPS — Capitol Reef trail guide
other_links.note: Authority for the figures.

trails.name: Sunset Point
trails.note: Ten minutes each way to the rim viewpoint off the Goosenecks spur - the evening walk on a day that has otherwise been spent driving.
trails.note_source: NPS Capitol Reef trail-guide table: Sunset Point, 1.2 km round trip, under 15 m elevation change, Easy.

offroad.name: Cathedral Valley Loop
offroad.distance: 57.6 miles, 6 to 8 hours of slow driving. Most drive it clockwise: Hartnet Road from the Fremont River ford 11.7 miles east of the visitor center, 27.8 miles to Hartnet Junction, then Cathedral Road 29.9 miles back to Highway 24
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS, which says high-clearance vehicles can usually manage it without four-wheel drive. That holds only when it is dry — rain or snow can make it impassable to the best high-clearance 4WD
offroad.season: THE FORD IS THE CONFLICT, NOT A GATE. The south end of Hartnet Road fords the Fremont River with no bridge; normally under a foot of water on a rocky bottom, impassable in high water, and NPS says plainly not to attempt it in flood. The stop arrives 28 Mar 2028 — spring runoff and spring storms, the worst combination for that ford, and winter snow can still leave the high sections muddy. There is no seasonal closure to check, only conditions, so this must be phoned in the day before: Capitol Reef visitor center 435-425-3791 (press #1, then #4).
offroad.note: If the ford is up, the loop is not lost — drive Cathedral Road in from the Caineville end as an out-and-back and skip the crossing entirely. That reaches the Cathedrals themselves, which is what people come for. Cell reception is poor to nonexistent on the whole loop, and there is no water; carry recovery gear and tell someone the plan. Rig advice removed from the name per the settled truck-only policy.

torrey.authority: National Park Service — Capitol Reef National Park
torrey.dogs: NPS: "Pets are not permitted on other hiking trails, in public buildings, or in the backcountry." Leash 6 feet or shorter at all times. Pets are allowed "within 50 feet of center line of roads (paved and dirt) open to public vehicle travel", in parking areas, campgrounds, the Chestnut and Doc Inglesby picnic areas and unfenced orchards.
torrey.dogs_exception: Two walkable exceptions the park names: the trail from the visitor center to the Fruita Campground, and the Fremont River Trail from the campground to the south end of Hattie's Field. Hickman Bridge and Cassidy Arch are both closed to pets.
torrey.stats_note: Every figure here is the National Park Service's own Fruita trail-guide table, which publishes metric round-trip distances and elevation change but no times and no ratings; the mile and foot values are arithmetic on the published metric figures. No AllTrails search was run for these five, so `unlisted` means 'not searched this pass', NOT 'no listing exists' - the negative must not be allowed to harden.
torrey.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not permitted on other hiking trails, in public buildings, or in the backcountry.
torrey.dogs_source_note: Spelling: the page writes "Chesnut" (no first T) in "in the Chesnut and Doc Inglesby picnic areas"; our card writes "Chestnut". The page also permits pets on two trails our card does not name — "on the trail from the visitor center to the Fruita Campground" and "on the Fremont River Trail from the campground to the south end of Hattie's Field" — which is what makes the quoted sentence say "other hiking trails".

trails.was: Delicate Arch Trail — no url

trails.name: Mesa Arch Trail
trails.was: Mesa Arch Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Canyonlands Island in the Sky. Sunrise is the famous frame and the crowd is real — the shot list has this stop covered too.

trails.name: Double Arch Trail
trails.was: Double Arch — Windows Section — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: Arches, Windows Section. Note there is a Double Arch Trail in KENTUCKY with a similar name — this is the Utah listing.

trails.name: Devils Garden Trail
trails.distance: 7.9 mi (12.7 km) whole loop; 4.0 mi (6.4 km) round trip to Double O Arch; 1.8 mi (2.9 km) round trip to Landscape Arch
trails.time: 3-5 hr whole trail; 2-3 hr to Double O Arch; 30-60 min to Landscape Arch
trails.difficulty: Hard — NPS files it under 'Longer, More Strenuous Hikes'. The section AS FAR AS Landscape Arch is a hard-packed easy trail; NPS: 'After Landscape Arch, the Devils Garden Trail becomes difficult, with rock scrambling, narrow ledges, and exposure to heights.'
trails.elevation_gain: 40 ft (12 m) to Landscape Arch (NPS). NPS publishes NO elevation figure for the whole loop and the third-party guides disagree (1,150 ft vs 1,350 ft), so no figure is recorded for the full circuit.

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Arches
other_links.note: Source for both sets of figures. 'Roundtrip just to Double O Arch: 4.0 miles (6.4 km), 2-3 hours. Whole Trail: 7.9 miles (12.7 km), 3-5 hours.' Landscape Arch Trail is listed separately at 1.8 mi, 30-60 min, 40 ft.

trails.season: Open year-round. NPS: 'Avoid when rock is wet or snowy' — early April in Moab is dry and cool, which is the best time of year for this trail; the reason it is normally avoided is summer heat, and 1-8 Apr misses that entirely.
trails.note: The single largest omission on the card. This is the trail that holds Landscape Arch — a 300 ft span, the longest in North America — plus Partition, Navajo, Double O and Dark Angel. The 1.8 mi round trip to Landscape Arch and back is a comfortable morning and is where most people should turn; the full 7.9 mi loop is a real day with exposure. Both are given above so the choice can be made at the trailhead. Bring 3 L of water per person for the full loop (NPS).
trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes the whole loop under the slug 'devils-garden-loop-trail-with-7-arches' but titles the page 'Devil's Garden Trail'. The 16,069 count is the whole-loop listing; the en-gb mirror of the same page showed 15,999 on the same day, which is the usual drift between AllTrails locales and is why the count is only good enough to ORDER this trail, not to quote.

trails.name: Park Avenue Trail
trails.distance: 1.8 mi (3.2 km) round trip; 1 mi one way between Park Avenue Viewpoint and Courthouse Towers Viewpoint
trails.difficulty: Easy to moderate — NPS lists it under 'Short and Moderate Hikes', tagged both easy and moderate. The first stretch from Park Avenue Viewpoint is a paved wheelchair-accessible sidewalk; the trail proper drops a long flight of rock-cut stairs into the canyon floor.
trails.elevation_gain: 322 ft (98 m) — 'or much less if you skip the stairs' (NPS)
trails.reviews_note: Review count read from the AllTrails result title. No star rating was visible in any result read for this trail, so none is recorded.

other_links.label: NPS — Park Avenue and Courthouse Towers
other_links.note: NPS's own place page for Park Avenue Viewpoint states plainly 'Dogs are not allowed on this trail.'

trails.season: Open year-round; the canyon floor is shadeless and this is a summer-avoid trail, so early April is close to ideal.
trails.note: The first thing past the entrance station and the best hour-long walk in the park. A canyon floor between sheer 300 ft fins and monoliths — Courthouse Towers, the Organ, Sheep Rock, the Three Gossips. Walk it one way downhill with a car left at Courthouse Towers, or turn around at the base of the stairs for a much flatter out-and-back. NPS asks round-trip hikers to return along the trail rather than walk the road.

trails.name: The Windows Loop and Turret Arch
trails.difficulty: Easy — NPS tags the listing easy and moderate; 'a gentle climb up a hard-packed trail and stone steps'. First 300 ft of the main trail may be wheelchair-accessible with assistance.
trails.reviews_note: Count read from the AllTrails result title. The en-gb mirror of the same page showed 5,848 the same day; treat as approximate. No star rating was visible.

alltrails.name: Windows Loop and Turret Arch Trail

other_links.label: NPS — The Windows Section
other_links.note: NPS: 'The Windows Section is considered by some to be the beating heart of Arches National Park.' North Window, South Window, Turret Arch and Double Arch inside just over two square miles.

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Arches (distance, time, elevation)

trails.season: Open year-round. Best at sunrise or sunset; the Windows face east and south, so the light through North and South Window is a first-hour subject.
trails.note: Double Arch is already on the card and shares this parking loop, but the Windows are a different trail and the reason most people come to this end of the park. Returning on the primitive route around the back side of the two Windows adds about half a mile and loses the crowd entirely.

moab.authority: National Park Service — Arches NP and Canyonlands NP
moab.dogs: Arches: pets "are not allowed: on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier" — leashed pets may go "along established roads or in parking areas" and "in established campgrounds and picnic areas". Canyonlands is stricter still: pets are prohibited "on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier" and "at any overlooks". Leash 6 feet or less in both parks.
moab.dogs_exception: Mesa Arch is in Canyonlands, where even the overlooks are closed to pets. Arches names Cache Valley Road and Willow Springs Road as places to walk a dog; Delicate Arch, Double Arch and the Windows are not among them.

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

moab.dogs_source_quote: on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier
moab.dogs_source_note: Two authorities on this card. Canyonlands verified separately at https://www.nps.gov/cany/planyourvisit/pets.htm, which carries the same "on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier" plus "at any overlooks" — and two further bans our card omits: "in the visitor center or any building" and "in the backcountry (including vehicles on backcountry roads, and on any river trips)". Both parks state "Leashes must be 6 feet (1.8 meters) long or less."
moab.dates_checked: 1-8 Apr 2028, 7 nights. Depart 8 Apr is a FROZEN anchor — out before Easter Jeep Safari closes seven trails.
moab.trails_note: The card carried THREE trails for a seven-night stay covering both Arches and Canyonlands: Mesa Arch, Double Arch, Delicate Arch. That is two half-days and one morning. The three biggest omissions in Arches are added here. Grand View Point (Canyonlands, Island in the Sky) and Corona Arch (BLM) were the next two candidates and are named in `also_considered` rather than pushed past the six-trail cap.
moab.also_considered: Grand View Point Trail, Canyonlands Island in the Sky — 2 mi round trip, the best rim walk in the district; left off only because Mesa Arch already carries Canyonlands on this card and the six-trail cap binds. Corona Arch — BLM, 3 mi round trip, 'moderately strenuous' with safety cables and a short ladder (blm.gov/visit/corona-arch-trail), AllTrails https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/utah/corona-and-bowtie-arch-trail. It is the obvious candidate for the DOG, because Arches and Canyonlands both ban pets from every trail — but BLM publishes no pet rule for it, so `dogs` could only be recorded null, and cables plus a ladder is a poor dog outing regardless. Worth a call to the Moab Field Office, 435-259-2100, before assuming the dog walks anywhere on this stop.
moab.dogs_stop_level: NPS Arches, Pets page, verbatim: 'Pets are not allowed: on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier; at any overlooks; in the visitor center or any building.' Leashed pets are confined to established roads, parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas. Canyonlands applies the same rule. Every trail on this card is therefore dogs:false, and seven nights in Moab currently contain no researched walk the dog may join.

trails.note: Steep climb straight out of town to the Twin Peaks overlook. 4.7 from 162 reviews is outstanding enough to keep a Challenging route on a card built for easy and moderate.

ouray.authority: USDA Forest Service — Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison NFs (Mount Sneffels Wilderness); the Perimeter Trail is City of Ouray
ouray.dogs: Mount Sneffels Wilderness order: dogs are prohibited if "(i) off leash; (ii) not under the direct verbal control of the dog's owner or handler at all times; or (iii) disturbing or damaging wildlife, other animals, people or property". On leash or under verbal control the dog is legal.
ouray.dogs_exception: The Perimeter Trail is a City of Ouray trail, not Forest Service — no municipal rule was sourced, so it is unknown rather than allowed.
ouray.stats_note: The Ouray Trail Group's own site was fetched: it names Sutton/Neosho, Oak Creek, Bear Creek and Full Moon as well as the Perimeter and Blue Lakes trails, but publishes no lengths, gains or grades - those are in its printed map and guide, which is sold rather than posted. Baby Bathtubs and Cascade Falls, both short and both low enough for April, could not be matched to an AllTrails URL this pass and are recorded here rather than guessed at.

Petroglyph Point Trail.entity: Mesa Verde's below-the-rim loop to its petroglyph panel. Rejected on identity: 'Petroglyph Point' resolves to Petroglyph Point Archeological Site, which is in Lava Beds National Monument, California -- wrong state, wrong park. Mesa Verde National Park's own text does document this one by name: 'Modern Hopi have interpreted the petroglyphs at Mesa Verde's Petroglyph Point as depictions of various clans of people.'

trails.name: Petroglyph Point Trail
trails.was: Petroglyph Point Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: Mesa Verde. Register at the trailhead; the loop passes a large petroglyph panel.

trails.name: Long House Loop
trails.season: CLOSED ON THESE DATES — Wetherill Mesa opens late May and shuts late October (NPS published 22 May-21 Oct for 2026). Arrive 15 Apr 2028, depart ~22 Apr 2028: the road is shut, the trail is unreachable
trails.note: PET-LEGAL BUT OUT OF SEASON. NPS Wetherill Mesa: "Hike any trail with your pet except the trails into Step House and Long House. Please keep your pet on a leash and do not leave them unattended." Leash 6 ft or shorter. The paved 5-6 mile loop itself is open to the dog and to bikes; only the spur descending into the Long House dwelling is not — the two are easy to confuse at the junction, and the sign matters. Kept on the card flagged rather than dropped, because it is the answer to "where can the dog walk at Mesa Verde" and the answer for a mid-April stop is nowhere: Wetherill Mesa does not open until late May.
trails.note_source: NPS Wetherill Mesa page (nps.gov/meve/planyourvisit/wetherill-mesa.htm), fetched: trails listed as Badger House 2.25 mi round trip, Step House 1 mi round trip, Nordenskiold Site #16 0.9 mi one way, Long House Overlook 2 mi round trip, paved loop trail 5-6 mi round trip; pet rule quoted verbatim above; "Wetherill Mesa operates daily from May 22 to October 21, 2026." NPS operating-hours page (nps.gov/meve/planyourvisit/hours.htm) gives the same window. No AllTrails url is attached: AllTrails carries a "Long House Trail" listing, and the trail INTO Long House is precisely the one the dog may not use, so linking it would point at the exclusion rather than the permission.

other_links.label: NPS — Mesa Verde operating hours & seasons

trails.name: Badger House Community Trail
trails.season: CLOSED ON THESE DATES — Wetherill Mesa opens late May (NPS published 22 May-21 Oct for 2026); the 15 Apr 2028 arrival is five weeks early
trails.note: PET-LEGAL BUT OUT OF SEASON. Covered by the same Wetherill Mesa rule — "Hike any trail with your pet except the trails into Step House and Long House" — and Badger House is neither. Leash 6 ft. Listed so the card shows what the April dates cost the dog, not to suggest it can be walked.
trails.note_source: NPS Wetherill Mesa page, fetched: "Badger House: 2.25 miles round-trip" and the pet rule quoted above; season 22 May-21 Oct. No trail-database listing was searched for, because the trail is unreachable on these dates.
