other_links.note: Authority. Length, pet rule and season.

trails.name: Mesa Verde Point Lookout Trail
trails.note: The most-reviewed trail in Mesa Verde and it was not on the card. Switchbacks up the promontory that towers over the park entrance, to views over the Mancos and Montezuma valleys and out to the San Juans and La Platas. It starts from the Morefield campground area near the entrance, which means it is reachable on days when the Chapin Mesa road is busy, and it is open in April when half the park is not. NPS calls it 2.2 mi round trip; guide sites call it a lung-buster at altitude with no shade - in mid-April that is a feature.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Mesa Verde Point Lookout Trail is an out-and-back trail that covers 2.1 mi, with an elevation gain of 524 ft. It takes about 1-1.5 hr to complete.' Star and count from the AllTrails Point Lookout POI page: 4.7 from 985 reviews; the park page gave 4.7 from 1,010 and the trail title 1,013. NPS: 'The Point Lookout Trail climbs up the iconic Point Lookout, the geological formation that towers above the park entrance... The 2.2-mile (3.5 km) roundtrip trail...'
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be leashed (6 feet/1.8 m or shorter leash) and under control at all times. Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point but not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings.
trails.dogs_note: NPS. Pets are barred from every Mesa Verde trail except the Wetherill Mesa paved routes, and Wetherill is shut on these dates. The dog does not walk inside this park in April - see Sand Canyon below.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 985, 1,010, 1,013. Ordering signal only.

trails.name: Spruce Canyon Trail
trails.note: The one Mesa Verde trail that goes DOWN into the canyons instead of along the mesa tops, and it is open in April. It drops out of Spruce Tree Canyon, follows the seasonal stream up the canyon floor for the better part of a mile under Douglas fir, and climbs a side canyon back to the mesa. It shares a trailhead area with Petroglyph Point, which is already on the card, so the two are one day out. Register at the trailhead as the park requires for the canyon trails.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Spruce Canyon Trail is considered a moderate hike that covers 2.5 mi, with an elevation gain of 538 ft. It takes about 1-1.5 hr to complete', count 538 from the trail page title (a second snapshot gave 508). Route description from AllTrails and NPS: 'The Spruce Canyon Trail offers an opportunity to explore the canyon bottoms of Mesa Verde... Parts of this canyon trail offers the shade of Douglas Fir trees and the coolness and humidity of a natural wetland area.' COTREX (Colorado's official trail registry) also has it at ~2.5 mi, moderate.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point but not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings.
trails.stats_note: The review count (538) and the elevation gain in feet (538) are coincidentally identical - both were read this pass, from the title and the body of the same AllTrails page. Not a copy.

trails.name: Sand Canyon Trail
trails.distance: 12.7 mi out and back (6.5 mi one way from the McElmo Canyon trailhead)
trails.time: 6-6.5 hr for the full out and back
trails.note: THIS IS WHERE THE DOG WALKS. Mesa Verde bans pets on every trail it opens in April, and Sand Canyon is 30 minutes away in Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, BLM ground, leashed dogs welcome - with a denser run of Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings and pueblos along the canyon walls than anything you can walk to unguided inside the park. It does not have to be walked whole: the lower trailhead in McElmo Canyon reaches the first ruins within the first mile or two and turning back there is the normal way to do it. The upper section is steep and rugged. Mid-April is the right season - this is slickrock and pinyon at 5,500-6,900 ft, unbearable by July.
trails.season: Open. No seasonal closure applies to these dates - which is the whole point of it at this stop.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Sand Canyon Trail is an out-and-back trail that covers 12.7 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,902 ft. It takes about 6-6.5 hr to complete', count 1,137 from the trail page title (1,171 on a second snapshot). Hiking Project: '6.5 miles (one-way) from the trailhead in McElmo Canyon. The trail is open to hiking, horseback riding, and mountain biking, but the upper section is steep and rugged.' BLM's own Sand Canyon / Rock Creek brochure: 'This trail is over 6 miles (one-way) with an approximately 1,390-ft elevation gain from south to north.' Trailhead elevations (5,472 ft lower, 6,862 ft upper) from The Outbound.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Are dogs allowed in the Monument? Yes. Dogs should be controlled with a leash.
trails.dogs_note: BLM Tres Rios Field Office, the managing authority. Corroborated by COTREX, Colorado's official trail registry, which records the Sand Canyon trail as 'Manager BLM Tres Rios Field Office ... Allows Dogs Leash'. Note the BLM's other rule for this area: 'it is restricted to designated routes (on trail only) in the Sand Canyon/Rock Creek Recreation Management Area' - no cross-country wandering here even though the rest of the monument allows it.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 1,137 and 1,171. No star rating appeared alongside either. The AllTrails and BLM lengths and gains disagree (12.7 mi / 1,902 ft round trip vs 'over 6 miles one-way' / 1,390 ft) - both are recorded rather than reconciled.

other_links.label: BLM - Canyons of the Ancients, Sand Canyon and Rock Creek trails (brochure)
COTREX - Sand Canyon Trail
other_links.note: Colorado's official trail registry. Records the manager and the leashed-dog permission.

mancos.authority: National Park Service — Mesa Verde National Park
mancos.dogs: PARTIAL, and the card previously hid the better half. NPS: "Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point but not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings." But the very next sentence opens a whole mesa: "At Wetherill Mesa, pets are permitted on all trails except for the trails leading into Step House and Long House." Leash 6 ft. THE CATCH IS THE CALENDAR: Wetherill Mesa opens 22 May and closes 21 Oct, and this stop is 15-22 Apr 2028. On these dates the dog's legal ground is pavement — Mesa Top Loop Road, the parking lots, Park Point and the campground.
mancos.dogs_exception: Mesa Verde is one of the few parks that opens real trails to dogs, but not on Chapin Mesa: "At Wetherill Mesa, pets are permitted on all trails except for the trails leading into Step House and Long House." Petroglyph Point is a Chapin Mesa trail and is closed to the dog.
mancos._verdict: Mesa Top Loop is a ROAD, not a trail — it does not go in the trails box. See scenicDrives_patch below. The real dog-legal TRAILS at Mesa Verde are all on Wetherill Mesa, and Wetherill Mesa is shut on this stop's dates.

not_a_trail.problem: A 6-mile paved DRIVING loop, not a hiking trail. NPS's own name for it is the "Mesa Top Loop Road" and its self-guided-tours page describes it as "a 6-mile (10 km) drive that is a tour through time. Along the road, you'll find short, paved trails to view twelve ancestral sites". The pet rule allows the dog on the road, the parking lots and those short paved areas — which is a series of car-park walks, not a walk. Moved to scenicDrives, merged into the Mesa Verde road entry that box already carries so it is not duplicated.

Named in the same pet sentence as Mesa Top Loop, and equally not a trail — it is the park's high point, reached by a spur road, with a short paved path to the fire lookout viewpoint. Leashed dogs are allowed on the paved area. Recorded here so a later pass does not add it to the trails box on the strength of the pet rule naming it.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Mesa Top Loop Road and Cliff Palace Loop Road
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: Mesa Verde's Mesa Top Loop/Cliff Palace Loop park roads to the cliff-dwelling overlooks — NPS explicitly prohibits trailers and towed vehicles beyond Morefield Campground, so the 40ft coach cannot bring the towed truck in; drop the trailer/truck combo at Morefield and do the loops in the truck alone.
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 6 mi (Mesa Top Loop Road)
scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS prohibits trailers and towed vehicles beyond Morefield Campground, so the coach cannot bring the truck in — drop the combo at Morefield and drive the loops in the truck alone. THE DOG CAN COME ON THIS ONE. NPS: "Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point but not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings." Leash 6 ft/1.8 m; pets may not be tethered or left unattended. On a 15-22 Apr 2028 stay this and the paved area at Park Point are the ONLY places at Mesa Verde the dog may set foot outside the campground — the park's real dog-legal trails are all on Wetherill Mesa, which does not open until late May. Twelve archaeological stops along a 6-mile paved loop, each a short paved walk from the car: the dog is legal on those paved stretches but not on any trail leading off them, and not inside any ancestral site.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS self-guided tours page: "The Mesa Top Loop Road is a 6-mile (10 km) drive that is a tour through time. Along the road, you'll find short, paved trails to view twelve ancestral sites, including surface sites and overlooks of cliff dwellings". NPS 'Explore the Mesa Top Loop Road' gives the same 6-mile figure. Pet sentence is the one already quoted in this stop's `dogs` field. Merged onto the entry the scenicDrives box already carried rather than added as a second one — that box's existing entry is the same two roads written as a sentence.
scenicDrives_patch.call: Mesa Verde NP, 970-529-4465 — confirm the Mesa Top Loop Road is open by 15 April. NPS publishes a hard season for Wetherill Mesa (22 May-21 Oct) but no opening date for the Mesa Top Loop Road, and if that road is also still shut in mid-April the dog has nowhere legal at Mesa Verde beyond the campground and the parking lots.

offroad.name: La Plata Canyon Road (FR 124) toward Kennebec Pass
offroad.distance: about 15 miles from Hesperus up the canyon, climbing nearly 3,000 ft toward Kennebec Pass at 11,683 ft
offroad.difficulty: graded gravel low down; 4WD with good clearance for the last section to the pass. The mileage and the 4WD note are from theridrs.com and dangerousroads.org, not from the Forest — San Juan NF publishes the gate status but not a grade.
offroad.season: Partly open, and the distinction is the whole answer. San Juan NF's road table lists FR 124 as "Open", with the gate closing "12/15 or 4 inches standing at the gate" — so the lower canyon should be driveable on the stop's 15-22 Apr 2028 dates. The top will not be: Kennebec Pass is above 11,600 ft and holds snow well into summer. Drive it as far as it goes, not as a pass crossing.
offroad.note: The best dirt within reach of a Mesa Verde base, and it is not at Mesa Verde — the park's own roads are all paved and the park prohibits leaving them. La Plata Canyon is old mining country north of Hesperus, about 45 minutes east of Mancos.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Bolam Pass Road (FR 578)
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. San Juan NF gives FR 578 an opening date of "5/1" and closing dates "9/8-10/13, 11/30". The stop is 15-22 Apr 2028 — the gate opens nine days after departure. This one is simply not available on these dates.
offroad.note: The high crossing between Durango and Rico via Hermosa Park, and the reason it is listed rather than dropped is that it is the obvious thing to want at this stop and it is shut. Recorded so the card says what is being missed and why. Anything at that elevation in the San Juans is a July proposition, not an April one.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Canyons of the Ancients — Lowry Pueblo and Painted Hand Pueblo roads
offroad.difficulty: not graded by BLM. A secondary description of the drive: "trips takes you from a paved road to a dirt road which is sometimes primitive. Most vehicles with good clearance will be fine."
offroad.season: No gate published. Mid-April is a good time for it — low country west of Cortez at around 6,000 ft, clear of snow, and the clay dries fast. Wet-weather caveat applies to the primitive sections.
offroad.note: The low-elevation alternative for a stop whose mountain roads are still gated. Over 6,000 recorded sites; Lowry Pueblo has a stabilised great kiva and Painted Hand is the one that needs the dirt. Roughly 40 minutes northwest of Cortez. Mesa Verde itself contributes nothing here — every road in that park is paved and driving off them is prohibited.
offroad.source: BLM — Canyons of the Ancients National Monument

mancos.dogs_source_quote: At Wetherill Mesa, pets are permitted on all trails except for the trails leading into Step House and Long House.
mancos.dogs_source_note: DRIFT by omission — the card is stricter than the park. The quoted sentence is verbatim, but the very next bullet on the page is one our prose drops entirely: "At Wetherill Mesa, pets are permitted on all trails except for the trails leading into Step House and Long House." As written, the card reads as a blanket trail ban and hides a real dog walk at this stop. Tethering rule confirmed: "Do not leave pets tethered or unattended."
mancos._review: The most mis-set box of the thirteen. Two of its three trails - Long House Loop and Badger House Community - are on Wetherill Mesa, which the NPS does not open until late May; this stop arrives 15 April. So a seven-night stay at Mesa Verde had exactly ONE walkable trail on the card, and no answer at all to where the dog goes, because Wetherill was also the only place in the park that allows pets. Two Chapin Mesa trails that ARE open in April, and the dog's actual walk outside the park, are added below.

Animas River Trail & San Juan Skyway dri.entity: San Juan Skyway Scenic and Historic Byway

Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroa.entity: Durango and Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

links.label: Wikipedia — Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

trails.name: Animas River Trail
trails.was: Animas River Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Paved urban river path through Durango — flat, easy and bike-legal.
trails.cruise_reason: A paved, flat 6.2 mi river path rated Easy — the shape that has produced every confirmed cruise on this trip. Paved rather than gravel, so check it suits the dog carrier, but it is the strongest candidate on leg 6.

trails.name: Horse Gulch Trail System
trails.was: Horse Gulch Trail System — a system, not a trail
trails.note_source: Meadow Loop via Horse Gulch Trail is the listed route inside the system. Durango Trails publishes the wider network at durangotrails.org; Horse Gulch Road itself is a 4.1 mi easy non-motorized access route.

trails.name: Spur Line Trail
trails.season: AllTrails gives the usable window as March through October, so the 22-27 Apr stay is inside it.
trails.note: Old rail alignment turned loop on the north side of town - easy, in town, and bike-legal, which makes it the gravel-cruise candidate at this stop.
trails.stats_note: Result title gives 599 Reviews; the rich snippet's star line reads 4.5/5 (493). The two counts differ - title figure used.

trails.name: Animas Overlook Trail
trails.season: AllTrails gives May through October; late April is a week or two early and the Junction Creek Road up to it can still be soft. Worth a call to the San Juan NF office before driving up.
trails.note: Short accessible loop on the rim above the Animas valley with interpretive signs - the biggest view for the least effort anywhere near Durango.
trails.stats_note: Title gives 155 Reviews; star line reads 4.4/5 (134).

trails.name: Falls Creek Waterfall via Church Camp Trail
trails.season: Listed as open year-round, which at this elevation makes it one of the few certainties in the third week of April.
trails.note: Twenty minutes to a waterfall just north of town. The short walk for an arrival day.

alltrails.name: Falls Creek Waterfall via Church Camp Trail

trails.name: Animas River Trail: South Durango Section
trails.season: March through October per AllTrails - inside the stay.
trails.note: The southern continuation of the river path, away from the busy downtown stretch. Listed separately because it is a different section rather than a second name for the trail already on the card, and it doubles the available flat riverside mileage.

alltrails.name: Animas River Trail: South Durango Section

trails.stats_note: Distinct AllTrails listing from the 'Animas River Trail' (6.2 mi, 1,078 reviews) already on the card - different slug, different length, different section. Kept because it is a genuinely different piece of path, but the two overlap at the north end.

durango.dogs: Leashed on both — the City of Durango says leashed dogs are welcome throughout its parks, open space and trails, and a leash is the law inside city limits; voice control applies only on the federal land outside town, not on Horse Gulch.
durango.dogs_source_quote: Leashed dogs are welcome throughout Durango's parks, open space and trails
durango.stats_note: Late April rules out most of what Durango is known for: Goulding Creek, Missionary Ridge, Silver Mountain and Hermosa Creek all carry May-or-June starts in their AllTrails windows. The four above are the low, in-town or near-town options that are actually walkable in the stay.

Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad day tri.entity: Cumbres and Toltec Scenic Railroad; Chama, NM

Reservoir Hill Trail system.entity: The town trail network above Pagosa Springs. Rejected on identity: bare 'Reservoir Hill' resolves to Reservoir Hill, Baltimore, a Maryland neighbourhood. Pagosa Springs, Colorado never mentions Reservoir Hill.

trails.name: Treasure Falls
trails.was: Treasure Falls Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: San Juan National Forest, off US-160 about 15 miles north-east of Pagosa Springs. AllTrails indexes it as a point of interest rather than a trail listing.

trails.name: Piedra River Trail
trails.was: Piedra River Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: USFS lists the full trail between both trailheads at 11.2 mi, easy to strenuous; the AllTrails figure is the common out-and-back. Official page: fs.usda.gov/r02/sanjuan/recreation/trails/piedra-river-trail

trails.name: Skyrocket, Highline, Wapiti and Terri Smith Loop
trails.note: Reservoir Hill, straight above town - the network you can walk to from the hot springs. Low enough to be open in the last days of April, which most of the San Juan is not.

alltrails.name: Skyrocket, Highline, Wapiti and Terri Smith Loop

trails.name: Observation Deck via Skyrocket Trail
trails.note: The short version of the same Reservoir Hill climb, up to the observation deck over the San Juan valley. Under an hour, and the walk for an afternoon that is mostly about the springs.
trails.stats_note: Surfaced on the plp.alltrails.com mirror; slug copied verbatim, host normalised to www.

trails.name: Festival Meadow via Thunderfoot Trail
trails.note: The easy leg-stretch on Reservoir Hill - half an hour, flat by the standards of this town, and the one to do on an arrival evening.

trails.name: Eightmile Mesa
trails.season: March through August per AllTrails - one of very few trails here whose window is already open on 27-30 Apr. That is why it is on the card ahead of better-known San Juan routes.
trails.note: Long mesa walk south-west of town on the low side of the divide. The full-day option at a stop where almost everything higher is still under snow.

pagosa-springs.authority: USDA Forest Service — San Juan National Forest
pagosa-springs.dogs: San Juan NF: "Keep dogs on a leash 6' or shorter" in campgrounds and recreation areas; on wilderness trails dogs must be "under strict leash or voice control". Store dog food in bear-resistant lockers, pack out waste, and keep the dog in the tent or vehicle at night.

official_links.label: Hiking and Camping with Dogs — San Juan NF (USFS)

pagosa-springs.stats_note: The Pagosa trails with the strongest reviews - Pagosa Peak (11.5 mi, 4.4 from 197), Quartz Lake (9.3 mi, 283 reviews) and Four Mile Creek (13.2 mi) - are all challenging AND all carry May-or-June season starts, so none is usable on a 27-30 Apr stay. Piedra Falls (1.0 mi, easy, 24 min) would fit the stop perfectly but the only source that surfaced for it was a Facebook post quoting the AllTrails text, with no AllTrails URL, so it is recorded here rather than linked.

offroad.name: Piedra Road (FR 631)
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: OPEN, and unusually so for this stop. San Juan NF's road table says FR 631 "Remains open all year, plowed in winter" — it is one of very few roads in the district that is. The stop is 27-30 Apr 2028, when almost everything else at altitude is still behind a 5/1 or 6/1 gate.
offroad.note: The main road north out of Pagosa Springs into the Piedra country and toward the Weminuche — and, on these dates, effectively the only high-country road out of this stop that can be counted on. Williams Creek is off it and is also listed as open all year and plowed.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

offroad.name: Buckles Lake Road
offroad.difficulty: not graded on the Forest's table
offroad.season: UNCERTAIN ON THESE DATES. San Juan NF lists its opening as "Conditional" with a 1/15 closure — meaning there is no fixed spring date and the Forest opens it when the road can take traffic. Late April in the eastern San Juans is early for that. Phone the Pagosa Ranger District rather than driving out on spec.
offroad.note: Southeast of Pagosa toward the Continental Divide and the New Mexico line. Listed with its 'conditional' status stated plainly rather than omitted, because 'conditional' is the actual answer and a card that said nothing would read as 'open'. The broader picture for this stop: most San Juan NF gates open 5/1 or 6/1, one to five weeks after departure.
offroad.source: USFS San Juan National Forest — Current Conditions road table

pagosa-springs.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must always be under strict leash or voice control.
pagosa-springs.dogs_source_note: All four elements of the card verify on this page: "Keep dogs on a leash 6' or shorter." and "Store dog food in bear resistant food lockers." and "Pick up and trash your dog's waste." and "Keep your dog in your tent or vehicle at night." The page splits its advice into a campground/recreation-area list and a wilderness list; the quoted sentence is from the wilderness list.

Walkable historic downtown.entity: Salida's downtown core — the Salida Downtown Historic District, on the National Register since 1984. It has no article of its own; the Salida, Colorado article names and dates the district.

Walk the Colorado Trail out of Angel of.entity: The Colorado Trail where it passes the Angel of Shavano trailhead/campground on the north side of Mount Shavano. 'Angel of Shavano' has no article; the Mount Shavano article documents the Angel of Shavano snow formation the place is named for.

Soak at the Salida Hot Springs Aquatic C.entity: Salida's indoor geothermal pool. The pool itself has no article and the Salida, Colorado article does not mention it (a 'Salida Hot Springs' redirect points there but the text is silent — not used). Its water is piped in from the Poncha Springs hot springs, and the Poncha Springs article documents those springs and the City of Salida's ownership of them.

Pre-runoff wade fishing on the Arkansas.entity: Wading the Arkansas River near Salida before spring runoff. The Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area is the state park that manages the fishing easements on this reach and is headquartered in Salida.

offroad.name: Aspen Ridge Road (FS 185), east boundary of Browns Canyon
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "High clearance 4x4 vehicles recommended"
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: BLM adds a parking rule that is easy to break by accident: vehicles must remain within one vehicle length of the road when parking. Trails Offroad's listing for the same road (official name "185") gives a high point of 10,301 ft and a typical open window of 30 Apr – 1 Dec, which agrees with the gate dates.

offroad.name: CR 240 above Angel of Shavano to North Fork Reservoir
offroad.distance: 3 mi on CR 240 from US 50 to Angel of Shavano, then 6 mi west to the reservoir
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road "is very rough and not recommended for vehicles towing trailers. High clearance vehicles are a requirement"
offroad.season: Campground at the top operates June–September, opening and closing dependent on weather
offroad.note: North Fork is the highest-elevation campground on the Salida Ranger District at 11,000 ft, first come first served, and there is no trash service. Salida Ranger District 719-539-3591 will say how far up CR 240 has melted out.

offroad.name: Fourmile Road / Aspen Ridge
offroad.season: Forest Service: "Seasonal gates are closed December 1 and opened April 30"
offroad.note: The Fourmile Travel Management Area is 100,000 acres of joint Forest Service and BLM land; southern access is from CR 371/375, 304-308, 311, 315, 300-301 and 185. Note the two gate calendars do not match — the Browns Canyon monument roads reopen 15 Apr, the wider Fourmile gates 30 Apr — so an early-May visit is inside both windows but late April is not. The Forest Service publishes no difficulty or vehicle rating for these routes and refers visitors to the Fourmile area map or the Salida Ranger District.

offroad.name: FS Road 1434A, north boundary of Browns Canyon
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Worth checking before driving out there: the Friends of Browns Canyon access page states that 1434 is "an ATV trail for machines with a maximum width of 50 inches", which a full-size pickup exceeds. BLM's own page calls 1434A an ATV route without giving a width. If the 50-inch limit applies to 1434A as well as 1434, this route is not legally driveable in the truck at all — phone the Salida Ranger District (719-539-3591) rather than assume. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/plan-your-visit/access-seasonal-closures/

offroad.name: Old Monarch Pass (FS 237)
offroad.difficulty: onX rates it 3 — Easy
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer and fall
offroad.note: The 52.4 miles is the whole onX route, not the pass crossing — it drops off the west side, crosses Waunita Park and runs north to Pitkin, and onX warns the northern part of that descent is very rocky and rough. The pass itself is 11,375 ft, about 0.6 mi northwest of the US 50 summit, and the graded eastern side is the easy half. Recent status reports on the listing mention downed trees.

offroad.name: Turret Road (FS 184) into Browns Canyon
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "a rugged 4x4 experience into the heart of the Monument"; Friends of Browns Canyon add that "only skilled motorists looking for an extreme 4x4 experience should attempt" it
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Turret Road ends at a small parking area at the Browns Canyon Wilderness Study Area boundary, where it becomes Turret Trail and mechanised travel stops — so this is an out-and-back, not a through route to the river. The corridor is bighorn sheep, mule deer, lynx and Mexican spotted owl habitat, which is what the winter gate protects. Neither BLM nor the Friends group publishes a mileage. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/turret-road/

trails.name: River Bench Trail (#6045A), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 5.5 mi round trip to the river

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Managing authority. States 'Roundtrip to the river via the River Bench Trail (#6045A): 5.5 miles, 3 hours'; describes it as the gentle dead-end river-bench route.

other_links.label: Komoot — Turret Trail and River Bench Trail loop
other_links.note: The combined Turret + River Bench loop: 5.4 mi, 558 ft gain, moderate, 2 h 26 min.

other_links.label: Gaia GPS — Ruby Mountain via Turret 6045 and River Bench 6045A
other_links.note: Same combination recorded as a moderate out-and-back.

trails.stats_note: BLM's 5.5 mi is the round trip to the river and is the figure to plan on. AllTrails has no page for #6045A on its own; the 5.4 mi Komoot figure is the Turret+River Bench loop, not this trail alone.

trails.name: Turret Trail (#6045), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 2.7 mi round trip to the river at Little Cottonwood

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Authority: 'Roundtrip to river at Little Cottonwood via Turret Trail (#6045): 2.7 miles, 2 hours'; a steep but short hike with wide views.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Browns Canyon National Monument area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; source of the 4.5 star / 555 review figure.

trails.stats_note: Distance is BLM's 2.7 mi round trip; the AllTrails rating is for its own 'Turret Trail' listing, which does not publish a matching length in the indexed snippet.

trails.name: Monarch Spur Trail
trails.reviews: 4.4 (115) — AllTrails title count 115; the star line shows 95 ratings. TrailLink separately shows 4/5 from 2
trails.cruise_reason: Paved concrete former rail spur, City of Salida, bike-legal per COTREX, 143 ft of range over its whole length, no walk-your-bike sections and no puncture reports. This is the gravel-cruise-with-the-dog day at this stop, and it starts in town.
trails.dogs_note: COTREX, whose manager field for this trail is the City of Salida, states 'Allows Dogs: Leashed'. Not taken from AllTrails.
trails.season: COTREX and AllTrails both have it open year-round; at 7,056-7,199 ft it is dry on a 30 Apr arrival.
trails.note: Runs from the Arkansas River near Sackett Ave out through town to the Milk Run Trail. Unremarkable as riding, which is the point — it is the flat, paved way to get about Salida on the bike with the dog in the carrier.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser; TrailLink for surface and one-way length; COTREX for manager, dog rule, surface and elevation range

other_links.label: COTREX — Monarch Spur Trail (City of Salida)

trails.name: Salida Riverside Park Trail (Salida Riverwalk, #029)
trails.dogs_note: COTREX lists the managing authority as the City of Salida and the rule as 'Allows Dogs: Leashed'.
trails.season: AllTrails gives January through September; COTREX publishes no seasonal gate. Open on a 30 Apr arrival at 7,035-7,056 ft.
trails.note: The short walk along the Arkansas through Riverside Park in downtown Salida, beside the whitewater park. Reviewers report it is pram-friendly, which is the same thing as saying it is flat and smooth. This is the evening walk, not the day out.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title read in browser (the en-gb mirror of the same page shows 58 — the .com figure of 59 is the one recorded); COTREX for manager, dog rule and elevation

other_links.label: COTREX — Salida Riverwalk Trail #029 (City of Salida)

trails.name: Beasway (Salsa) Trail (#1418)
trails.reviews: 4.5 (140) — AllTrails title count 140; the star line shows 145 ratings
trails.dogs_note: COTREX gives the manager as USFS Salida Ranger District and 'Allows Dogs: Yes' — the same forest as the stop's existing San Isabel sourcing.
trails.season: The Forest Service gates this one: COTREX shows access, hiking, biking and horses all 03/16-12/14. A 30 Apr arrival is inside the open season by six weeks. Elevation 8,653-8,947 ft, low enough to be melted out; AllTrails gives best months as April through October.
trails.note: The named trail at the bottom of the Arkansas Hills system that the card previously referred to only as 'the trail system above Salida'. Renamed in 2017 from Salsa Trail for Brett Beasley, a Salida Ranger District trail builder. Multiuse and popular with mountain bikers — singletrack, so it is a walk rather than a cruise.
trails.cruise_reason: Mountain-bike singletrack in the Arkansas Hills, not a rail grade. Bike-legal, but not the surface the dog carrier wants.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser; COTREX for trail number, manager, seasonal gate, dog rule and elevation; Trailforks for the renaming

salida-co.dogs: Dogs are fine on the Browns Canyon NM trails (BLM) and on San Isabel NF trails under control; no leash policy is published for the monument and the City of Salida publishes nothing readable for Tenderfoot.
salida-co.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome on most BLM-managed trails. Please check the trail website or call the local BLM field office for specific leash policies.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US Highway 50 over Monarch Pass
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Summit 11,312 ft, about 25 miles west of Salida on US-50
scenicDrives_patch.season: Kept open year-round, but "prone to heavy winter snowfall, often resulting in temporary closures during severe winter storms". Colorado State Patrol: winter driving conditions in the high country run "as early as September and as late as May" — the stop arrives 30 Apr 2028, still inside that band.
scenicDrives_patch.note: No CDOT page dedicated to Monarch Pass exists; repeated searching returned only CDOT's general winter-driving and traction-law pages (codot.gov/travel/winter-driving, codot.gov/travel/winter-driving/tractionlaw) plus third-party cameras. This Wikipedia article was a real search result and was fetched to confirm it resolves. It crosses the Continental Divide between the upper Gunnison basin and the South Arkansas; runaway-truck ramps on both sides and much of the highway three-laned for winter maintenance. A late-April crossing can fall under Colorado's tiered traction law with little notice.

salida-co._review: 7 nights, arrive 30 Apr 2028, town at 7,050 ft. The card held four, and two of them do not work on these dates: Waterdog Lakes tops out around 11,500 ft under Monarch Pass and will be snow, and River Bench carries no figures at all. That leaves Turret and Tenderfoot for a week. Salida's real asset in late April is that the valley floor is already dry — so the additions are the three trails that are open on arrival: the town rail-trail, the riverside walk, and the first Arkansas Hills trail above town.

South Main riverwalk.entity: South Main, the new-urbanist riverfront district on the Arkansas in Buena Vista. No article, and the Buena Vista, Colorado article does not mention it. No link.

Cottonwood Hot Springs.entity: Cottonwood Hot Springs Inn & Spa on County Road 306 west of Buena Vista. No article; the Cottonwood Pass article covers the pass road but says nothing about the springs. No link.

Small towns: Nathrop, Granite, Twin Lake.entity: Four settlements up and down the upper Arkansas valley. All four have articles; Twin Lakes needs the Lake County disambiguator, and St. Elmo's article title is spelled 'Saint Elmo'.

links.label: Wikipedia — Twin Lakes, Lake County, Colorado

Soak at Mount Princeton Hot Springs Reso.entity: The resort at the foot of the Chalk Cliffs in Nathrop. It has no article; the Mount Princeton article is about the 14er only and never mentions hot springs, so linking it would send the reader to a peak, not a resort. No link.

Denny Creek trailhead walk.entity: The Denny Creek trailhead on CR 306 into the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness. No article, and the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness article does not name it. No link.

Barbara Whipple trail system straight ou.entity: A town trail network on the east bank of the Arkansas at Buena Vista. No article anywhere. No link.

Ride or walk the Midland Bike Trail.entity: The trail on the old Colorado Midland railroad grade east of Buena Vista. No article; the Colorado Midland Railway article covers the railroad and its grade becoming US 24 but never mentions a rail-trail, so it would not answer the reader's question. No link.

Cottonwood Lake.entity: The small reservoir on Cottonwood Creek south of the CR 306 pass road. No article, and no parent article documents it. No link.

offroad.name: Aspen Ridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Typically open 30 Apr – 1 Dec
offroad.note: Listed under its official road number, 185, and managed by the Salida Ranger District. Rated 4.4 from 47 reviews; high point 10,301 ft. Reviewers report loose rock, washout on the rock climbs and deep ruts, and that the middle section turns to mud after rain or snow — the melt-out date and the driveable date are not the same thing here.

offroad.name: Chinaman Gulch and Carnage Canyon, BLM Fourmile Travel Management Area
offroad.distance: 7.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: May through October
offroad.note: FunTreks puts the round trip at about 4 hours with a high point of 8,900 ft, and names the obstacles — Rock Garden, Whale Rock, Double Whammy — most of which have bypasses on the Chinaman side. Carnage Canyon has none of that forgiveness: minimum 35-inch tires, lockers front and rear, and FunTreks tells drivers to carry and use a spill kit. It is one of the most heavily used motorised areas in Colorado, so expect company.

offroad.name: CR 306 west of Collegiate Peaks Campground toward Cottonwood Pass
offroad.season: County: "From November 1st until June 15th this road is not maintained beyond Denny Creek Trailhead"
offroad.note: The road, not the Forest Service, is Chaffee County's — Road and Bridge, 719-539-4591, is who to phone for the plough line. Their published non-maintenance window ends 15 June, later than the tag's "late May"; they aim to open the pass before Memorial Day but only as snowpack allows, and both the Chaffee and Gunnison sides gate independently. Denny Creek Trailhead is the realistic turnaround in mid-May.

offroad.name: Fourmile Area — Natural Bridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Year round
offroad.note: Rated 4.7 from 42 reviews, high point 9,218 ft. The loop runs FS 373 and part of FS 311; surface is mostly sand and smooth dirt with a few mild climbs and only small rocks, which is why it holds a year-round rating while everything above it is gated. The return leg faces the Collegiate Peaks.

offroad.name: Fourmile Travel Management Area general routes
offroad.season: Forest Service: "Seasonal gates are closed December 1 and opened April 30"
offroad.note: 100,000 acres of joint Forest Service and BLM ground. The Forest Service publishes no per-route difficulty and points visitors at the Fourmile area map or the Salida Ranger District instead; the listed uses are hiking, mountain biking, OHV trail and road riding, and ski/snowshoe. Access from the north is via CR 371/375 and CR 304-308.

offroad.name: Mount Antero road (FS 277), off Chalk Creek
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–September
offroad.note: FunTreks budgets 6 hours and puts the high point at 13,750 ft. The specific warning is about vehicle size rather than capability: "extremely narrow shelf road with tight switchbacks", and oversize vehicles will have a hard time at the switchbacks — a full-size pickup is the wrong shape for the top of this road even in August. Small SUVs with low range get all but the last half mile. The same road accesses Browns Lake for quiet camping.

offroad.name: Tincup Pass (FS 267) from St. Elmo
offroad.distance: 13 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–October
offroad.note: About 2 hours one way, summit 12,154 ft. The blocker is specific and late: one short section of narrow shelf road at 12,000 ft holds snow into early July. Sharp rock near the top is reported to cut tires. Once clear it wants low-range gearing, skid plates and good rubber.

buena-vista-co.dogs: All three are San Isabel NF (Salida Ranger District); the forest permits dogs on its trails and in Collegiate Peaks Wilderness provided they are under control at all times.
buena-vista-co.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be under control at all times. Pets can harass, stress, injure or kill wildlife; introduce disease and disturb fellow hikers. Some wilderness areas require dogs to be leashed at all times.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Mount Princeton Road (CR 162) to Chalk Cliffs
scenicDrives_patch.distance: From Buena Vista, 7 miles south on US-285 then 6 miles west on County Road 162 to the Forest Service information kiosk
scenicDrives_patch.note: Pike-San Isabel NF, Chalk Creek Canyon: "From Buena Vista, Colorado, travel south for about 7 miles on Highway 285. Turn right onto County Road 162, and travel west for 6 miles." The kiosk sits opposite the Colorado Trail (#1776) trailhead. Restriction the authority does publish: "No camping or campfires, except in developed campgrounds" outside the four designated campgrounds, with exceptions near St. Elmo and Hancock. The Forest Service page states no seasonal closure for CR 162 and describes the canyon as "a popular visitor attraction during the summer months". Chaffee County Road & Bridge plows CR 162 through to St. Elmo, so a 7 May arrival should find the graded county road open — the 4x4 passes above St. Elmo are a different question and are not this entry.

buena-vista-co._review: 8 nights, arrive 7 May 2028 at 8,000 ft. The card held three: Agnes Vaille Falls (good), Collegiate Peaks Campground Loop (thin, 49 reviews), and Mount Yale, a 14er that will be under snow. That is not eight days of walking and it has no town-level walk at all. Added the two low-elevation Buena Vista trails that ARE open in early May, plus the area's single best-reviewed hike flagged for snow.

trails.name: Barbara Whipple / Midland and North Broken Boyfriend Loop
trails.reviews: 4.7 — AllTrails publishes no review count in the result title
trails.dogs_note: BLM Royal Gorge Field Office / Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area; BLM permits dogs on most trails. Same authority as the stop's existing BLM sourcing.
trails.season: Low trail at 7,950-8,060 ft on the east side of the Arkansas, the first thing in the valley to melt out. Open and walkable on a 7-15 May arrival.
trails.note: Starts from the Buena Vista River Park footbridge in town — the walk you can do from the coach without driving. AllTrails indexes it under the composite route name, not 'Barbara Whipple'; the trailhead signs say Whipple. 360-degree views to Mt Princeton and the Sawatch.
trails.note_source: AllTrails listing (title 'Midland, 1450.A, and North Broken Boyfriend Loop'); distance and time from Garmin Trails; elevation range from COTREX (Colorado Trail Explorer, BLM Royal Gorge Field Office as manager)

other_links.label: COTREX — Barbara Whipple Trail (BLM Royal Gorge FO)
Visit Buena Vista & Salida — Barbara Whipple Trail
Garmin Trails — Midland-North Broken Boyfriend Loop

trails.name: Midland Railroad Grade (Historic)
trails.dogs_note: BLM Royal Gorge Field Office; the AllTrails listing also states leashed dogs, but the verdict here is taken from BLM.
trails.season: AllTrails gives the window as March through October — the arrival is inside it.
trails.note: Former Colorado Midland railway grade above the Arkansas, so it is graded and near-flat rather than climbing. The obvious rail-grade candidate for a bike day with the dog, but the surface has not been sourced from reviews, so cruise is left unset rather than claimed.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result snippet, read in browser

trails.name: Ptarmigan Lake Trail (#1444)
trails.difficulty: Moderate — climbs on moderate grades (hikingwalking.com); AllTrails' own grade is not published in the result
trails.dogs_note: San Isabel National Forest, Salida Ranger District — same authority as the stop's existing dogs_source; pets permitted under control at all times.
trails.season: CLOSED FOR THIS STOP. The lake sits at 12,147 ft in a north-facing bowl below Jones Mountain and the Cottonwood Pass road (CR 306) that reaches the trailhead is not open that high in early May. Reviewers report snow on the trail and heavy snow near and above the lake well past melt-out at lower elevations. Best July for the wildflowers the Forest Service singles out.
trails.note: By a distance the best-reviewed hike in the Buena Vista area and the reason people come here — listed so the card says plainly what a May stop is missing, not because it can be walked. If the dates ever move to July, this is the day.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title read in browser (2,632 reviews, 4.8/5); distance, time and gain from theoutdoorgems.com quoting the AllTrails stats; elevation and season from US Forest Service and Uncover Colorado

other_links.label: US Forest Service — Ptarmigan Lake Trail #1444

Mineral Belt Trail.entity: The 11.6-mile paved loop around Leadville, which has its own article under its full name, Mineral Belt National Recreation Trail.

links.label: Wikipedia — Mineral Belt National Recreation Trail

Leadville historic district.entity: The Leadville Historic District, a National Historic Landmark district covering the town core and 67 mines east of it.

Twin Lakes and the Interlaken ruins.entity: Two things. Twin Lakes, the glacier-carved pair south of Leadville, has an article. The Interlaken resort ruins on the south shore do not, and the Twin Lakes article does not mention them, so only Twin Lakes is linked.

links.label: Wikipedia — Twin Lakes, Lake County, Colorado

Halfmoon Road in the truck.entity: The Halfmoon Creek road southwest of Leadville that serves the Mount Elbert and Mount Massive trailheads. The road has no article; the Mount Elbert article documents the Halfmoon Creek trailheads it exists to reach.

offroad.name: FS Road 125.B, South Mount Elbert trailhead extension
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: four-wheel drive only, summer season; impassable to vehicles in winter
offroad.season: Summer only
offroad.note: The trail it serves, South Mount Elbert #1481, is 5.8 mi with 4,800 ft of gain from the lower trailhead. The road starts just beyond the lower parking lot; there is a ford about 1.5 mi up, and informal dispersed sites line the first mile if you would rather park and walk. Access is from Leadville: 15 mi south on US 24, west 3.75 mi on CO 82, then right on Lake CR 24 for 1.5 mi.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass (FS 105), 11,925 ft
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: The Forest Service page publishes no open or close dates at all for this pass — the seasonal timing in the tag is not theirs and should be checked with the Leadville Ranger District. The 1880s railroad history is the reason the grade exists; west of the summit it continues through White River National Forest past Ruedi Reservoir to CO 82 at Basalt.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass Road (Road 105)
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: Same road as the Hagerman Pass entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. The Forest Service publishes no seasonal dates for it.

offroad.name: Halfmoon Road (FS 110) to Elbert Creek and the Mount Massive trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not rated by the Forest Service on this page
offroad.note: The authority page confirms the road and what it reaches — FS 110 follows the southern border of the Mount Massive Wilderness and serves several campgrounds plus the Mount Massive and North Elbert trailheads — but publishes no surface, mileage or vehicle guidance. The Forest's own trail pages add that the road is not maintained in winter and that the last half mile to the trailhead needs high clearance and 4WD. Very busy in summer.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass (FS 438)
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: The Forest Service signs and numbers this as County Road 12, not 438 — worth knowing at the junction. The tour starts from Fairplay: north on CO 9 for about 4.2 mi, then left onto CR 12, and the interpretive stops begin almost immediately. The brochure is a download from this page as well as a paper copy at the South Park Ranger District.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass Road
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: Same road as the Mosquito Pass (FS 438) entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. Signed as County Road 12 from the Fairplay side.

leadville-co.dogs: All four are San Isabel NF (Leadville Ranger District); dogs are permitted on forest trails and in Mount Massive Wilderness under control, with a 6-ft leash in developed sites such as the Turquoise Lake campgrounds.
leadville-co.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be under control at all times. Pets can harass, stress, injure or kill wildlife; introduce disease and disturb fellow hikers. Some wilderness areas require dogs to be leashed at all times.
leadville-co._review: 6 nights, arrive 15 May 2028; Leadville sits at 10,152 ft and the day trip goes higher. Three of the four trails on the card cannot be walked on these dates — North Mount Elbert and Mount Massive are 14ers and Hagerman Tunnel is an 11,000 ft cirque that holds snow into July. That left one usable walk for six nights. Added the three Leadville-area trails that ARE open in mid-May, which is a net of three additions for three unusable existing entries rather than padding.

trails.name: Mineral Belt Trail
trails.difficulty: Moderately challenging (AllTrails) — the grade is gentle and the whole loop is ADA-accessible; the difficulty is the 10,000 ft air, not the path
trails.reviews: 4.7 (1,069) — read from the AllTrails /en/ result title; the /en-gb/ mirror of the same page shows 1,090, so treat this as approximate
trails.cruise_reason: 11.6 miles of asphalt on old railroad and mining grades, non-motorized, explicitly designed for bicycles, wheelchairs, strollers and skaters, with shelters after miles 3, 5, 7 and 10. No walk-your-bike sections, no surface hazards. Reviewers do warn that the elevation gain plus 10,200 ft of air makes it real work on an unassisted bike.
trails.dogs_note: NEEDS CHECK. The trail's own site, Visit Leadville Twin Lakes and the Colorado Mountain College route page all describe the trail in detail and none of them publishes a pet rule. A Lake County leash ordinance almost certainly applies, but that is an inference, not a source. Do not assume from AllTrails.
trails.season: The trail is the venue for the Leadville Loppet ski race, so it is under snow through the winter and the melt at 10,200 ft is late. Mid-May is the shoulder: the town-side miles are normally clear, the north and east arcs through the mining district can still hold drifts. Worth a look at the trail's own site before driving up.
trails.note: The single best walk or ride at this stop and it was not on the card. It loops the whole of Leadville through the historic mining district with interpretive signs, so it is the day that explains the town. Class I and II e-bikes are permitted.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result titles and stat line read in browser; mineralbelttrail.com and Visit Leadville Twin Lakes for surface, shelters, ADA access and e-bike rule; TrailLink for endpoints; COTREX featured route 138

other_links.label: Visit Leadville Twin Lakes — Mineral Belt Trail
COTREX — Mineral Belt Loop featured route

trails.name: Boulders and Giddy Up Loop
trails.reviews: 4.4 (122) — AllTrails title count 122; the star line shows 106 ratings
trails.dogs_note: COTREX gives the Giddy Up Trail's manager as Lake County and the rule as 'Allows Dogs: Leashed'. Not taken from AllTrails.
trails.season: AllTrails gives best months as May through October — the 15 May arrival is the first day of that window, so expect soft ground rather than snow. The trails double as the Leadville nordic loops in winter, which is why they are cut gently.
trails.note: The easy loop that actually works in mid-May: 40 ft of range on the Giddy Up section, 10,190-10,230 ft, five miles at an hour and three quarters. Shared with mountain bikers.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser; COTREX for manager, dog rule, length and elevation of the Giddy Up section

trails.name: Leadville Fish Hatchery Nature Trail
trails.reviews: 4.7 (405) — AllTrails title count 405; the star line shows 258 ratings
trails.dogs_note: NEEDS CHECK. The managing authority is the US Fish and Wildlife Service (Leadville National Fish Hatchery, established 1889). Its hiking and trails pages describe the trails and publish no pet rule; Colorado Parks and Wildlife's hatchery page does not either. Recorded as unknown rather than assumed.
trails.season: AllTrails gives best months as June through September, so a 15 May arrival is a few weeks early — at roughly 9,600 ft on hatchery grounds the loop should be walkable but muddy, with snow possible in the shaded spruce-fir. Not a closure, a caveat.
trails.note: A short interpretive wooded loop on the grounds of the second-oldest federal fish hatchery in the country, with a picnic area halfway and benches looking at the Sawatch. Half an hour, right by the road — the useful one for a bad-weather afternoon. The hatchery grounds are also the trailhead for Rock Creek, Highline and Kearney Park into the Mount Massive Wilderness.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser; US Fish and Wildlife Service hatchery hiking page and Visit Leadville Twin Lakes for the trail description and the wilderness trailhead access

Visit Leadville Twin Lakes — Fish Hatchery Nature Loop

Green River Lakes day trip.entity: The two headwater lakes of the Green River at the north end of the Wind River Range. They have no article of their own. The Squaretop Mountain article documents them directly ('the iconic view of Squaretop and Green River Lakes'), and the Green River article documents the river's headwaters in northern Sublette County in the Wind Rivers.

Scout the alpine trailheads.entity: Advice for the stay rather than a named place — no entity to link. No link.

Skyline Drive up to Elkhart Park.entity: The Pinedale road up to the Elkhart Park trailhead. Neither the road nor the park has an article; the Wind River Range article documents the Elkhart Park Trailhead as the main access to Titcomb Basin.

Photographer's Point via the Pole Creek.entity: The overlook about 4.5 miles up the Pole Creek Trail from Elkhart Park. Neither it nor the trail has an article, and neither the Bridger Wilderness nor the Wind River Range article names either. No link.

Green River Lakes and Squaretop Mountain.entity: Squaretop Mountain, the flat-topped peak above the Green River Lakes, has its own article and it documents the pairing with the lakes. The lakes themselves are covered via the Green River's headwaters.

CCC Ponds wildlife walk.entity: The Wyoming Game and Fish ponds just outside Pinedale. No article, and the Pinedale article does not mention them. No link.

Fremont Lake and Half Moon Lake.entity: Two lakes northeast of Pinedale. Fremont Lake — Wyoming's second-largest natural lake, in the Wind River foothills — has an article. Half Moon Lake does not, and the Pinedale article does not mention it, so only Fremont Lake is linked.

Soda Lake Wildlife Habitat Management Ar.entity: A Wyoming Game and Fish WHMA north of Pinedale. No article under that or any nearby title, and no parent article documents it. No link.

offroad.name: Boulder Lake Road (CR 125 to FS 370780)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale, roughly 10 mi of it dirt and gravel
offroad.note: The Forest's own directions match the tag turn for turn, and add that the dirt and gravel section is simply bumpy rather than technical — no 4WD language anywhere on the page, which is what makes this the sane shakedown day. The campground at the end has 15 sites on the east end of the lake near Boulder Creek.

offroad.name: Green River Lakes Road (FS 370650)
offroad.distance: 25 mi paved on WY 352 to the forest boundary, then 18 mi of dirt — about 50 mi from Pinedale
offroad.difficulty: "While the dirt road to the campground is suitable for 2 wheel drive vehicles, weather can make this road impassable to all but 4 wheel drive vehicles"
offroad.note: One thing to check before the trip rather than at the junction: the Bridger-Teton began a major reconstruction of this road in July 2026 — grading, drainage, culverts and new aggregate — with Phase 2 from the Union Pass Y to Green River Lakes scheduled for Aug–Oct 2026 or summer 2027. It should be finished and in better shape by 2028, but the Forest's conditions page is where any carryover work would be posted: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/conditions/green-river-lakes-road-construction-updates . Lower Green River Lake sits at 8,000 ft; drinking water at the campground only 1 Jul – 15 Sep.

offroad.name: New Fork Lake access (FS 370730 / 370735)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale — 6 mi US 191, 14.4 mi WY 352, 3 mi CR 162, then under a mile on FS 370730
offroad.note: Shorter and less committing than the tag implies — the forest road portion is under a mile, with the 3 mi of county road before it. The Forest publishes no road-surface warning, no high-clearance requirement and no seasonal date for this approach; the only figures on the page are the distances above. Third-party sites describe the last stretch as rocky, but that is not the Forest's wording and is not sourced here.

offroad.name: Union Pass Road (FS 370600)
offroad.note: This is the Forest's own road-conditions page and it is the only official page that names NFSR 600 by number: Union Pass Road runs from the forest boundary to the Green River Lakes Road (NFSR 650) junction, the "Union Pass Y". Phase 1 reconstruction covered exactly that segment in July 2026 with 30-minute delays and one full closure day; work may carry into 2027, so check this page before driving it. The Forest publishes no mileage, difficulty or open date for the road — the Pinedale Ranger District (307-367-4326) and the MVUM are the authority for what is open. The 70-plus-mile Dubois-to-Pinedale figure that circulates online is not a Forest Service number and should not be relied on.

trails.name: Sinks Canyon (Popo Agie Falls)

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Popo Agie Falls
other_links.note: Trailhead is Bruce's Parking Area on Shoshone National Forest land, 3 miles up the road from the Sinks Canyon State Park visitor center.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Popo Agie Falls Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the falls-overlook route and its high viewpoint.

trails.name: CCC Ponds Trail
trails.time: about 20 min on foot (8 min riding)
trails.difficulty: Easy — Trailforks grades it green; Pacer rates the walking route easy at about 6.6 ft of gain
trails.reviews: no AllTrails listing — official source only. Tripadvisor shows 4.5 from 17 for the CCC Ponds Recreation Area as a whole; no trail database publishes a review count
trails.dogs_note: BLM Pinedale Field Office land; BLM's recreation guidance is that dogs are welcome on most BLM trails with leash policy set locally, and no local rule is published. Not from AllTrails, which does not list this trail.
trails.season: Open and dry by late May at about 7,430 ft — four miles from town and the obvious first walk of this stop, weeks before the Bridger Wilderness trailheads are reachable.
trails.note: Dirt singletrack loop round the 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps ponds at the foot of the Winds. Birds, water, restrooms at the car park, and short enough to do twice a day.
trails.note_source: BLM Wyoming recreation page (authority); Trailforks for surface, length and grade; Pacer for distance and gain; outdooractive/recreation.gov for elevation

trails.name: Pinedale Pathway (CCC Ponds to town)
trails.distance: about 6 mi round trip (about 1.5 mi each way to the Riverside Drive trailhead)
trails.reviews: no AllTrails listing — official source only; no trail database publishes a review count
trails.cruise_reason: Paved BLM bike path from the CCC Ponds car park into Pinedale, listed for biking by the managing agency, no walk-your-bike sections and no surface hazards reported.
trails.dogs_note: Same BLM Pinedale Field Office sourcing as CCC Ponds; no site-specific leash rule published.
trails.season: Clear by late May; the winter grooming is long gone by then.
trails.note: Pairs with the CCC Ponds loop off the same car park — the ride into town with the dog in the carrier, which is the one thing at this stop that does not depend on the snow line.

trails.name: New Fork Lake Trail
trails.dogs_note: NEEDS CHECK. Bridger-Teton National Forest, Pinedale Ranger District — and per the stop's own existing sourcing, the only dog order Bridger-Teton publishes is a winter leash rule on the Jackson district, which does not reach here. That makes it unstated rather than confirmed, which is how the neighbouring Boulder stop records the same forest.
trails.season: AllTrails gives best months as June through November, so a 21-28 May arrival is at the very edge. New Fork Lake sits around 7,800 ft — a thousand feet lower than Elkhart Park and the first of the Bridger front trailheads to open — so this is the one to try if the weather has been kind, and the one to abandon for CCC Ponds if it has not. Not marked closed, because the road is low enough to be plausible; marked unverified for these dates.
trails.note: Three miles at the mouth of New Fork Canyon, the short walk that gets you into the Winds proper without a wilderness permit or a full day. By far the best-reviewed short trail in the Pinedale index — the rest of what AllTrails holds for this area runs 10 to 44 miles.
trails.note_source: AllTrails result title and stat line read in browser

wind-river-ext.dogs: Dogs are welcome on all three: Sinks Canyon State Park requires a leash of 10 ft or less, and the only dog order Bridger-Teton publishes is a winter leash rule on the Jackson district, which does not touch Pinedale or these late-May dates.
wind-river-ext.dogs_source_quote: The Forest Order requires all dogs to be leashed with a tether no longer than six feet, from Dec. 1 to May 1, on designated trails and parking areas on the Jackson Ranger District of the Bridger‑Teton National Forest.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Green River Lakes Road (FR-091)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 15.6 miles of unpaved road from the Union Pass Road fork to Green River Lake Campground
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASON CONFLICT — the campground at the end of the road opens July 1 and runs to September 15; the stop arrives 21 May 2028, six weeks early.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Bridger-Teton NF, Pinedale Ranger District. Two things worth carrying. First, the road number: the Forest Service calls it Green River Lakes Road / FS-370650 (NFSR 650), reached by following WY-352 out of Cora until it becomes Union Pass Road / FS-370600, then bearing right after about 3 miles. The card's "FR-091" is not the number the authority uses. Second, "The access road to the campground is not paved" and the destination is shut on the stop's dates — at 8,000 ft in late May this is snow and mud, not a drive. Also live: the Forest began major reconstruction of the road on 6 July 2026 — grading, drainage, culverts and aggregate surfacing — "with potential for additional work in 2027", and phase-2 windows allowed work between August 1 and October 14 or during summer 2027. Phone the Pinedale Ranger District, (307) 367-4326, before committing a day to it.

wind-river-ext._review: 7 nights, arrive 21 May 2028 at Pinedale. The card held three and two of them are the high Bridger Wilderness approaches — Elkhart Park at 9,500 ft and Green River Lakes — which are still snow in late May; the third, Popo Agie Falls, is 77 road miles away at Lander. So the box was one real walk plus two aspirations for a week. Added the two BLM trails at Pinedale's own elevation, which are open, plus New Fork Lake as the first of the higher ones to melt out, flagged.

Climb the Lake Minatare lighthouse.entity: The 55-foot WPA-era mock lighthouse on Lake Minatare northeast of Scottsbluff, which has its own article.

offroad.name: Robidoux Pass / Carter Canyon gravel loop
offroad.distance: 23 mi as a loop — out on Carter Canyon Road, back on Robidoux Road
offroad.note: No land-management agency publishes this route: the pass is a National Historic Landmark on private and county ground, and the reconstructed 1851 Robidoux trading post in Carter Canyon is run by the Friends of Robidoux Trading Post, not a park service. That means no road-condition page, no seasonal gate and nobody to phone about surface after rain. Access is two miles south of Gering on Hwy 71 then eight miles west. Pioneer graves and wagon ruts are visible along the route; self-guided, no facilities. The Nebraska State Historical Society publishes the history of the pass but nothing about the road, and its page would not load for verification, so it is not linked here.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing is titled just 'Oregon Trail'; its own text confirms it by describing the covered wagons at the Scotts Bluff NM administrative building as the start of the Oregon Trail Pathway. No star rating or length could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

other_links.label: NPS — Prairie View Trail
other_links.note: Authority: the only trail in Scotts Bluff NM that allows bicycling; best views of Saddle Rock eastbound, Mitchell Pass westbound.
