trails.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets can join you at these locations: All Roads, Parking Lots, and Picnic Areas / Sand Point Beaches / Munising Falls Trail / Miners Falls Trail / Miners Castle - Paved Trails, Overlook Platforms / Miners Beach / Au Sable Access Road to the Light Station / Lake Superior Overlook and Beach / Sable Falls Trail
trails.dogs_note: NPS names Miners Falls Trail explicitly. The same page's photo caption is 'Dog on leash on the Miners Falls trail'. This is as clean as a pet permission gets.
trails.stats_note: No star rating appeared with the count in any snippet read. Difficulty is disputed between community sources - waterfallhikes calls it easy, MyHikes calls it moderate - so no grade is recorded; the 64 steps are the reason for the disagreement.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Miners Falls (point of interest)
other_links.note: 'The falls drops about 40 feet (12 m) over a sandstone outcrop with a 10-foot (3.0 m) crest.'

trails.name: Sand Point Marsh Trail
trails.distance: 0.5 mi loop (NPS); AllTrails maps it as a 1.9 mi out and back
trails.note: A wheelchair-accessible boardwalk loop over wetland and old dune ridges beside the Munising visitor centre, built in 1989 - the flattest, shortest, most bird-heavy half hour at this stop and the obvious evening walk after a day on the cliffs. Pram-friendly per AllTrails reviewers. The Sand Point area also has the beaches, which ARE named in the NPS pet list.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Enjoy this 1.9-mile out-and-back trail near Munising, Michigan. Generally considered an easy route, it takes an average of 39 min to complete', 245 reviews from the page title (237 on a second snapshot). NPS: 'The Sand Point Marsh Trail is a half-mile wheelchair-accessible flat interpretive trail loop that traverses a beautiful wetland area. Most of the trail is a wooden boardwalk that crosses a rich variety of wetland habitats and old dune ridges. The rest of the trail is paved.'
trails.dogs_note: READ THE NPS LIST CAREFULLY HERE. The pet page names 'Sand Point Beaches' - it does NOT name the Sand Point Marsh Trail, while it does name Munising Falls Trail, Miners Falls Trail and Sable Falls Trail individually. On a page that lists trails by name, that omission should be treated as a no until the visitor centre says otherwise; it is fifty yards from the trailhead. Recorded as unknown rather than assumed.
trails.stats_note: The NPS half-mile loop and the AllTrails 1.9 mi out-and-back are not the same measurement - AllTrails' track appears to include the approach. Both recorded.

munising-mi.dogs: Pictured Rocks names its pet trails one by one: Miners Castle is open, Chapel, Mosquito and Log Slide are explicitly closed, and Munising Falls appears on neither list.
munising-mi.dogs_source_quote: Your leashed pet is welcome in these areas: … Miners Castle - Paved Trails, Overlook Platforms … These areas are CLOSED to pets: … Chapel Trails and Chapel Beach … Mosquito Trails and Mosquito Beach … Log Slide and Nearby Dunes

scenicDrives_patch.name: County Road H-58
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open and fully plowed only in the warm season. NPS: in winter "H-58 is only plowed from Munising heading east to Adams Trail", and inside the park "Sand Point Road is the only park road plowed in winter" (roughly December 1 to March 31). The stop arrives 25 Jul 2028 — no conflict.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore: H-58 is "the main road that travels through the national lakeshore", running Munising to Grand Marais, and is "suitable for vehicles of all sizes". The warnings the NPS does publish are about sharing it, not driving it: it is a "curvy road", "long sections of H-58 have very little shoulder or no shoulder at all", and it is "used by large logging trucks and many types of ORVs". No length is published on the NPS page, so none is recorded.

munising-mi._review: Five trails for six nights looks full until you apply the dog rule: Chapel Loop, Mosquito Falls and Log Slide are all pet-prohibited, leaving Miners Castle and the 800-foot Munising Falls path as the only walks the dog can join in six days. Both additions were chosen to fix that specifically, and the first of them is named in the NPS pet list.

Upper Falls and the accessible boardwalk.entity: The Upper Falls, the 48-foot single drop. The Tahquamenon Falls article documents the Upper Falls; the boardwalk itself is not described in any article.

Lower Falls and the rowboat crossing.entity: The Lower Falls and the island in the middle of them. The Tahquamenon Falls article documents both, including that the island is reached by rowboat from the basin below (or the 2022 footbridge).

River Trail between the falls.entity: The four-mile trail linking Upper and Lower Falls. It has no article and is not named in either the Tahquamenon Falls or the state park article, which mention only the North Country Trail. No link.

Tahquamenon Falls Brewery & Pub at Camp.entity: The brewpub at the Upper Falls. No article, and neither 'Camp 33' nor the brewery appears in the state park article. No link.

Paddling the lower Tahquamenon.entity: The Tahquamenon River below the falls. Its article documents canoeing on the river.

Upper Falls.entity: The Upper Falls, documented in the Tahquamenon Falls article.

Lower Falls, four miles downstream.entity: The Lower Falls. The Tahquamenon Falls article gives the same distance — about 4 miles downstream — and the five smaller falls around the island.

Camp at the river mouth.entity: The Rivermouth campground unit at the Tahquamenon's mouth. The unit has no article; the Tahquamenon River article documents the mouth at Whitefish Bay and the state park article documents the park's campgrounds.

Tahquamenon Falls Brewery and Pub.entity: Same brewpub as above, second wording. No article, not documented in any parent. No link.

offroad.name: Crisp Point Light access roads (Luce County / forest roads west of Whitefish Point)
offroad.distance: CR 412 Crisp Point Rd, CR 423 to Singleton's Driveway and CR 502 to Crisp Point — 11.60 miles; approach CR 414 Pike Lake Rd, CR 407 to just west of Pike Lake — 11.27 miles
offroad.season: Luce County Road Commission seasonal roads list, Rev. 03/07/2023: not maintained for public travel from November 1 to April 30. The lighthouse society adds that the last 7 miles of CR 412 are usually open by the end of May, and that snow can make the road impassable even in spring.
offroad.note: This is the road authority's own seasonal-roads list, so it is the harder source than the lighthouse society's directions page the sibling entry links. Worth knowing the winter status: the road becomes Snowmobile Trail 8, and the society's own warning is not to drive it when there is snow. Watch for ATVs on the dirt.

offroad.name: Lake Superior State Forest two-tracks toward the Two-Hearted River mouth
offroad.distance: CR 423, CR 414 to the Mouth of the Two Hearted — 4.34 miles (Luce County Road Commission)
offroad.season: The county-road spine in is not maintained for public travel November 1 to April 30.
offroad.note: Honest limit: the graded county roads that get you in are fully documented, but no authority page describes the individual named two-tracks off them — treat the spine as listed and the two-tracks themselves as unlisted. This Newberry-approach directions page is the distinct source (the sibling entry carries the Paradise approach): roughly 37 miles, about 1 hour 10 minutes, and once off M-123 the roads are all dirt or sand, narrow and curvy. The society's own line is that they cannot guarantee you won't get stuck.

offroad.name: Vermilion Road toward the old Coast Guard station
offroad.distance: roughly 13 miles: from Paradise north on N. Whitefish Rd 5.2 mi, left on Vermilion Rd, 0.6 mi keeping right, then 6.1 mi on the straightest road, then 1.3 mi to the preserve
offroad.note: This is not a drive-through. Motorized vehicles, including ATVs and snowmobiles, are prohibited on the Vermilion Point preserve itself, so you drive the road to the boundary and walk to the old life-saving station — if the card implies driving to the station, that is wrong. Dogs are NOT allowed at the preserve 1 May to 15 August; leashed only the rest of the year. 175 acres, 9,240 ft of Lake Superior frontage, station first built 1876. Vermilion Road is in Chippewa County and is absent from the Luce County seasonal list; whether it carries its own seasonal designation is unknown.

trails.name: Clark Lake Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Authority: 'Clark Lake Loop (5.2 miles)', with a warning that conditions vary, fallen trees and wet areas are likely and cell service is minimal.

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Clark Lake Loop
other_links.note: Open to hiking, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing; begins at the Clark Lake Road parking lot and runs through pine forest.

trails.stats_note: Permitted uses are Michigan.org's — hiking, XC ski and snowshoe, with no mention of bikes. A recent AllTrails review measured the loop at 5.3 mi. Neither AllTrails nor the DNR publishes a difficulty grade for it, and no star rating could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

trails.name: Giant Pines Loop

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Giant Pines Trail
other_links.note: Authority: a 3.8-mile hiking trail through hemlocks and streams, named for two giant white pines on the route.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Giant Pines Loop Trail
other_links.note: Graded intermediate.

trails.stats_note: Michigan.org says 3.8 mi, AllTrails 3.5 mi. Takes about 1-1.5 hr and AllTrails reviewers describe it as good for children and families.

trails.name: Lower Falls island loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map covering the Lower Falls area.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing describes about 0.2 miles paved plus 0.4 miles of gravel road along the river with falls views, and notes loaner wheelchairs at the 'Fact Shack' by the Upper Falls parking lot. The river splits around a wooded midstream island reached by an island bridge or by rented rowboat. No star rating could be sourced; the listing carries 1,600 reviews.

trails.name: Tahquamenon River Trail (Lower Falls to Upper Falls)

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map for the river trail between the two falls.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 3.5-4 hr. The ground around the Lower Falls gets very muddy; accessible toilets at both ends and an off-road track chair is available. AllTrails' park page gives this trail 4.6 stars but the review count was not legible in the snippet, so no rating is recorded.

trails.name: Tahquamenon Falls Wilderness Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: Graded moderately challenging, averaging about 3 hours. Quiet — the listing carries only 46 reviews and no star rating could be sourced.

tahquamenon-falls-mi.dogs: Tahquamenon Falls says it outright — leashed dogs on all trails and viewing platforms; Whitefish Point is a USFWS refuge unit that also allows them on lead, except inside the piping plover nesting closure at the tip.
tahquamenon-falls-mi.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are allowed on all trails, including viewing platforms.

scenicDrives_patch.name: M-123 loop: Rivermouth to Lower Falls to Upper Falls
scenicDrives_patch.distance: The park covers nearly 50,000 acres and stretches 13-plus miles; the byway that strings its three units together is 63 miles end to end
scenicDrives_patch.note: Michigan DNR. The park's own General Management Plan states "M-123 is a federally designated scenic byway, which provides access to the three main areas of the park" — Upper Falls, Lower Falls and Rivermouth are all on M-123, which is what makes this a drive rather than three separate outings. Rivermouth sits where the Tahquamenon River meets Whitefish Bay, south of Paradise; Lower Falls is inland west of Paradise. No official mileage between the individual units is published, so none is recorded. Arrival 31 Jul 2028 is mid-season with no closure in play.

scenicDrives_patch.name: M-123 west to Newberry
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 63 miles
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Tahquamenon Scenic Byway, a Pure Michigan Byway: "a 63-mile journey through Michigan's Eastern Upper Peninsula", following M-123 to "experience the thunder of Tahquamenon Falls and the northern hospitality of villages like Newberry and Paradise, Michigan". Originally designated a Michigan Scenic Heritage Route in 1997 from Galloway Creek to County Road 500; all of M-123 north of M-28 carries the designation. MDOT's own byways index is at michigan.gov/mdot/travel/tourists/byways. The byway site promotes winter recreation but publishes no statement on winter road access, so no season field is claimed.

Castle Rock.entity: The limestone stack and climb-the-stairs tourist stop 3 miles north of St. Ignace on I-75, which has its own article under the Michigan disambiguator.

offroad.name: Emmet County shore roads west of Mackinaw City toward Cross Village
offroad.difficulty: Road Commission's own wording: seasonal roads "are not typical road beds and are often narrow, swampy, and can often be difficult to navigate"
offroad.season: A seasonal road will not be maintained November through April, and will not be open to public traffic during that time — though the Road Commission states plainly that it does not enforce any closure. Grading happens once or twice a year, typically late spring through early fall. No winter plowing.
offroad.note: No listing exists for this as a named 4x4 route; this is the road authority confirming the roads and how they are managed. Live caution as of mid-2026: four separate M-119 segments were closed after April 2026 flooding, plus Lower Shore Dr — the corridor was still under FEMA disaster recovery. Check MDOT's MiDrive before relying on the through-route.

offroad.name: Wilderness State Park two-tracks (Sturgeon Bay / Waugoshance Point)
offroad.season: The plover closure is in state law, not just park signage: Land Use Orders of the Director 5.7(1)(b) closes the posted lands April 15 through August 31, and 5.7(1)(c) separately bars possessing or allowing a dog on them at Waugoshance Point and Sturgeon Bay over the same April 15 to August 31 window. The park page adds that the shoreline outside pet-friendly areas is closed to pets April through August.
offroad.note: DNR names Nebo Trail, South Boundary Trail, Swamp Line Trail and Sturgeon Bay Trail as two-tracks, and notes many visitors ride Waugoshance Point Road. Park is 11 miles west of Mackinaw City, 26 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. The dog is the binding constraint here, not the truck — check the arrival date against April 15 to August 31 before planning this one. Recreation Passport required for vehicle entry.

trails.name: Cut River Gorge Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Cut River Bridge Roadside Park
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; source of the 203 ft elevation-gain figure.

other_links.label: Discover St. Ignace
other_links.note: Local visitor bureau page; confirms the trail descends from the US-2 roadside park to the Cut River and the Lake Michigan shoreline.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes this under the name 'Cut River Nature Trail' at a slug built on 'cut-river-bridge-trail'; neither the search title nor snippet published a distance, so none is recorded.

trails.name: M-185 Lakeshore Loop, Mackinac Island

other_links.label: TrailLink — Mackinac Island Loop (State Highway 185)
other_links.note: Fetched directly: 8.3 mi, asphalt, easy, wheelchair accessible; permitted uses walking, biking, horseback, inline skating, cross-country skiing. Motor vehicles have been banned since 1901 — the only state highway in the country where that is true. It is a paved car-free shared-use loop, not a footpath.

other_links.label: Michigan Trails — Mackinac Island Lake Shore Trail
other_links.note: Gives the loop as 8.2 mi paved on Lake Shore Boulevard.

trails.stats_note: TrailLink says 8.3 mi and mitrails.org says 8.2 mi for the same perimeter loop; the difference is where each starts measuring in the village.

trails.name: Mackinac Island — Arch Rock & Fort Holmes trails

other_links.label: AllTrails — Arch Rock
other_links.note: The Arch Rock half of this entry, listed separately: easy short walk to the viewing platform over the arch, 468 reviews.

trails.stats_note: The card entry names two destinations. AllTrails carries them as two listings — Fort Holmes Loop (3.2 mi, mixed paved and dirt) and Arch Rock (easy stroll) — not as one route.

trails.name: Foley Creek Trail
trails.note: The closest real walk to camp and the one the card was missing entirely: six miles north of St Ignace, from the Foley Creek Campground into the Horseshoe Bay Wilderness, an overlooked 3,800-acre piece of Lake Huron shoreline in the Hiawatha National Forest. Creek crossings, wetland edge and shaded forest, essentially flat. It connects onward into the 6.4-mile Horseshoe Bay Trail loop if the day wants more. Early August is bug-tolerable and the shoreline is the point.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Foley Creek Trail is an out-and-back trail that covers 2.9 mi, with an elevation gain of 36 ft. It takes about 0.5-1 hr to complete', 223 reviews on the trail page title. Star and count from the AllTrails Horseshoe Bay Wilderness park page: 4.0 star rating from 221 reviews (a second snapshot gave 4.2 from 170 and 3.1 mi). Description from Discover St. Ignace: 'a peaceful loop through the woodlands of Hiawatha National Forest, winding past creek crossings, wetland edges, and shaded forest groves.' Wilderness acreage and the 6.4-mile loop figure from dwhike and Michigan Trails; trailhead directions from Superior Hiking: north on I-75 to exit 348, then Mackinac Trail 2.4 miles north to Foley Creek Campground.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 170, 213, 221, 223, with stars of 4.0 and 4.2. This is a thinly and inconsistently indexed trail; treat the rating as approximate.

other_links.label: Discover St. Ignace - Foley Creek Trail

trails.dogs_note: Hiawatha National Forest. No published pet rule was read this pass.

trails.name: Tranquil Bluff Trail
trails.distance: 3.1-3.2 mi (community sources; no AllTrails length was returned)
trails.note: The only genuine hiking trail on Mackinac Island, and the card had the island's carriage roads twice without it. Mackinac Island State Park covers more than 80 percent of the island; this route takes the high line along the interior bluffs above the east shore, past limestone formations and quiet forest glades, well away from the M-185 crowd already on the card. It meets Soldiers Garden Trail near Arch Rock, so it links to what is already listed rather than repeating it. Returning along the shore road makes a full day of roughly nine miles.
trails.note_source: AllTrails trail page: 166 reviews; 'this route offers stunning views of Lake Huron, with a unique rock arch that frames the water... Tranquil Bluff Trail, which is a fitting name because this area is very peaceful as you hike along the b[luff]'. Length and grade from community sources that disagree: SecretFalls 3.2 mi moderate, MyPacer 3.1 mi easy, Trailforks 93 ft gain on part 1. The Outbound: 'the longest and most beautiful hiking trail on the island'. Roam Lab's nine-mile round day is the shore-road return.
trails.stats_note: No AllTrails distance, grade, time or star rating was returned in any result read this pass - only the raw count of 166. The distance recorded is community tier and is flagged as such.
trails.dogs_note: Mackinac Island State Park. No published pet rule was read this pass - and the ferry companies have their own pet rules, which is a separate question worth asking before planning this day.

trails.name: Red Pine Trail, Wilderness State Park
trails.note: The best-rated walk within half an hour of this stop, over the bridge at the top of the Lower Peninsula. Wilderness State Park is 10,500-plus acres of mostly coniferous forest with 26 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline and a designated dark sky preserve - which in early August, on a stop that already has a bridge and an island, is the thing the card had no equivalent of. Flat forest walking.
trails.note_source: AllTrails Wilderness State Park forest-trails page: 'the best forest trail to hike in Wilderness State Park is Red Pine Trail, which has a 4.5 star rating from 379 reviews. This trail is 3.4 mi long with an elevation gain of 52 ft.' Park description from the AllTrails park page: 'a large park, made of mostly coniferous forest. It has 26 miles of shoreline along Lake Michigan and a designated dark sky preserve.' Komoot puts the park at over 10,500 acres.

alltrails.note: No direct Red Pine Trail URL was returned in any result read this pass, so the park's forest-trails page is linked rather than a constructed trail slug.

trails.dogs_note: Michigan DNR state park. No published pet rule was read this pass.

st-ignace-mi.dogs: Mackinac Island State Park allows dogs anywhere on commission land as long as they are under immediate control, so Arch Rock, Fort Holmes and the M-185 shore loop all work; dogs are barred from bathing beaches and from historic building interiors. Nobody publishes a dog rule for the Cut River gorge trails — the roadside park is described as MDOT's by some sources and DNR's by others, and neither agency names the trail.
st-ignace-mi.dogs_source_quote: An individual shall not possess a dog on land under the jurisdiction of the commission unless it is under the individual's immediate control, or have a dog within any area used as a bathing beach.
st-ignace-mi._review: Three entries for six nights, two of them on Mackinac Island, and the third - Cut River Gorge - forty minutes west. Nothing at all within twenty minutes of camp. The additions add the mainland wilderness on the doorstep, the island's only real hiking trail as opposed to its carriage roads, and the big shoreline park over the bridge.

Traverse City's walkable downtown.entity: The city of Traverse City, Michigan.

Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive (pickup onl.entity: The 7.4-mile one-way drive inside Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, which has its own article.

Empire Bluff Trail.entity: The bluff-top trail south of Empire. The trail has no article; the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore article names Empire Bluff as one of its Leelanau County features.

links.label: Wikipedia — Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore

The Dune Climb.entity: The Dune Climb on M-109. No article; named in the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore article.

links.label: Wikipedia — Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore

Leland's Fishtown.entity: The surviving commercial fishing shanties on the Leland River. Fishtown has no standalone article; the Leland Historic District (Leland, Michigan) article documents it explicitly as one of the district's two contiguous areas.

Ride the TART Trail from the campground.entity: The TART Trails network around Traverse City, which has its own article.

other_links.label: NPS — Sleeping Bear Dunes trails
other_links.note: Managing authority. A park pass is required for all trails.

other_links.label: NPS — Sleeping Bear Dunes trails
other_links.note: Managing authority. Distance is a range because of the loop/spur options.

trails.name: Dune Climb / Cottonwood Trail loop

other_links.label: NPS — Sleeping Bear Dunes trails
other_links.note: Managing authority. Lists Cottonwood Trail at 1.5 mi, Moderate.

trails.stats_note: Our card name pairs two things NPS treats differently. NPS lists no 'Dune Climb' as a standalone trail — it is a trailhead, and the trail leaving it is the Dunes Hiking Trail (3.5 mi, Strenuous), which is NOT the Cottonwood Trail. The 1.5 mi / Moderate figures are the Cottonwood Trail alone. Worth splitting this into two entries, or renaming to 'Cottonwood Trail'.

trails.name: Old Mission Point Park / Lighthouse Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Old Mission Peninsula Lighthouse Park
other_links.note: The short lighthouse-and-beach walk rather than the full park loop, 198 reviews — the better option for an hour rather than a morning.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Old Mission Point Park browse
other_links.note: Park-level page for the whole trail network at the north end of the peninsula.

trails.stats_note: The 6.2 mi figure is the full park loop, averaging 2 h. The lighthouse itself is a short walk from the lot — see the second link.

trails.name: Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail
trails.distance: 20 mi point to point (TrailLink 21.2 mi; the park describes about 22 mi)
trails.cruise_reason: Paved, multiuse, and separated from the road for most of its length - a purpose-built recreation path rather than a repurposed one, running through the National Lakeshore between Empire and Bohemian Road and connecting Glen Arbor, the Dune Climb and the historic sites. No walk-your-bike sections are reported, no surface hazards, and it is explicitly on the NPS list of routes open to leashed pets. Twenty miles means picking a segment: Empire to the Dune Climb, or Glen Arbor out and back.
trails.note: The single best fit for this stop that was not on the card. Seven nights, a bike, a dog and a towed truck, and everything listed was a dune scramble the dog is banned from. This is the walk-and-ride that works every day of the week.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail is a point to point trail that covers 20 mi, with an elevation gain of 583 ft', 706 reviews from the page title (681 on a second snapshot). TrailLink: 21.2 mi from M-22 and S Bohemian Road (Maple City) to W Salisbury Dr (Empire). Michigan Trails: 'a scenic, approximately 22-mile multiuse route extending through Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore between the village of Empire and Bohemian Road... connects communities, historic sites, forests and several of the nat[ional lakeshore's sites]'.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be controlled on a 6-foot leash at all times.
trails.dogs_note: Sleeping Bear Dunes publishes pet access as a map rather than a list. The areas open to pets, as reported from that map, are Shauger Hill, Alligator Hill, Bay View, Good Harbor Bay and the Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail. Note the seasonal counter-rule elsewhere in the park: pets are prohibited on the designated cross-country ski trails (Old Indian, Platte Plains system, Windy Moraine, Scenic Drive) from 1 December to 31 March - not these dates.
trails.stats_note: Counts read this pass: 681 and 706, no star alongside either. Lengths differ by source (20 / 21.2 / ~22 mi) because the trail has been extended in stages; all three are recorded.

trails.name: Alligator Hill Easy Loop
trails.note: The forest half of Sleeping Bear, which the card did not have at all, and the dog can come. Beech-maple forest climbing to overlooks on Glen Lake, Lake Michigan and the dunes, and consistently quieter than the Dune Climb side. The loop system is tiered: the Easy loop is 2.7 mi / 364 ft, adding the Intermediate loop makes 4.8 mi / 695 ft in 2-2.5 hr, and all three loops together are 6.2 mi / 882 ft in 2.5-3 hr - so the same trailhead scales to whatever the day is worth.
trails.note_source: AllTrails: 'Alligator Hill Easy Loop is considered an easy hike that covers 2.7 mi, with an elevation gain of 364 ft', 487 reviews from the page title; and for the longer versions, 'Alligator Hill Easy and Intermediate Loop is considered a moderate hike that covers 4.8 mi, with an elevation gain of 695 ft. It takes about 2-2.5 hr' and 'Alligator Hill Easy, Intermediate and Advanced Loop is considered a moderate hike that covers 6.2 mi, with an elevation gain of 882 ft. It takes about 2.5-3 hr'.
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be controlled on a 6-foot leash at all times.
trails.dogs_note: Alligator Hill is one of the named pet-open areas on the Sleeping Bear pet map.
trails.stats_note: No star rating appeared with the count in any snippet read.

other_links.label: AllTrails - Alligator Hill Easy and Intermediate Loop
AllTrails - Alligator Hill Easy, Intermediate and Advanced Loop

traverse-city-mi.dogs: Sleeping Bear Dunes names its pet-open and pet-closed areas trail by trail: Empire Bluff and Pyramid Point are open to leashed pets year round and so is the Cottonwood Trail — but the face of the Dune Climb is closed to pets year round, and that is the only way up to the Cottonwood trailhead, so the Dune Climb/Cottonwood loop is off with the dog. Peninsula Township publishes no pet rule for Old Mission Point Park.
traverse-city-mi.dogs_source_quote: The face of the Dune Climb

offroad.name: Luhr's Trail
offroad.distance: 2.5 mi · about 11 km from the stop — the closest of the set
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "some small dips and sandy patches that could impede two-wheel drive cars"; full width listed
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall. No published gate date
offroad.note: "This trail provides an excellent shortcut between Bass Lake Road and Bass Lake Trail. The trail is a single vehicle wide and meanders through a wooded area with occasional clearings. The surface is sandy - can get dusty quickly. Private property is posted along each side of the trail." Stay on the two-track; the posting on both sides is the point.

offroad.name: Davis Lake seasonal road
offroad.distance: 1.5 mi · about 15 km west of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "a single vehicle wide without any technical sections"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall
offroad.note: "This is a seasonal road connecting South Cedar Creek Valley Road to Lake Ann Road... packed dirt and sand. The trail transverses both state land and private property-keep an eye open for no-trespassing signs. At the west end of the trail there is an access point for Cook Lake, which looks nice for shoreline fishing or launching a canoe/kayak." A short, easy, dog-friendly one on a hot August afternoon.

offroad.name: Strombolis
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi · about 16 km southeast of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "Two vehicles wide with plenty of passing room. All rigs can travel this route"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: "Strombolis is a classic Michigan dirt road that provides great views of the surrounding timbered forest... well maintained. Be aware of other trail riders as this is a busy area." The widest and most relaxed of the Traverse City two-tracks, and the one to use as the spine of a loop with Lake Dubonnet and Ransom Lake.

offroad.name: Lake Dubonnet Trail
offroad.distance: 1.4 mi · about 16 km west of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "a few areas where the trail terrain can be a bit tight with surrounding trees and small obstacles"; obstacles listed as tree roots, washouts and mudholes
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: "A great drive just 15 minutes outside Traverse City" — mostly dirt with some sand, through dense forest, with kayak launch points onto Lake Dubonnet and dispersed campsites along it. Decent cell coverage, unusually for these.

offroad.name: Ransom Lake Trail
offroad.distance: 3 mi · about 18 km west of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "one vehicle wide... occasional sections with significantly exposed roots that would be difficult to cross without 4-wheel drive"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall
offroad.note: "A fun trail crossing state land north of Lake Dubonnet... mostly sandy two tracks easily passable by most vehicles. There are sections, however, with tight turns in wooded areas and some relatively steep climbs with exposed roots. Longer vehicles and those with ground clearance less than a stock 4x4 may have difficulty crossing these sections." Read "longer vehicles" as a warning for a full-size crew-cab pickup on the tight turns.

offroad.name: Rogers Road — Trail 58421
offroad.distance: 2 mi · about 15 km southwest of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy); high clearance and full width only, no narrower categories
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall
offroad.note: "Rogers Road - Trail 58421 starts out as a single-lane trail. Brush line a good portion of the trail. Some of the Trail is also wide enough for vehicles to pass. This trail ends at Long Lake Road. The trail is mostly sand and dirt. This trail is managed by the Traverse City Forest Management Unit." Brush on both sides for most of its length — expect pinstriping.

offroad.name: LP510 / Shore To Shore seasonal road (Perla Road to Hoosier Valley Road)
offroad.distance: 9.4 mi · about 16 km south of the stop, near Mayfield
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "some parts are sandy with small ruts and mud"; high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists Summer only
offroad.note: The longest continuous run near Traverse City at nine and a half miles: "The drive is a seasonal Road... The road is generally 2 lane traffic and will connect with multiple trails... mostly dirt but some parts are sandy and we did run across some ruts and some mud." Two cautions. It shares its corridor with the Shore-to-Shore equestrian route, so expect horses and give way. And the legal check for all seven of these is the Michigan DNR forest road map, which distinguishes roads "Closed to ORVs" from roads "closed to all conventional vehicles and ORVs" — the truck is a conventional licensed vehicle, so it is the second category that would shut a road to it. The DNR publishes both an interactive and a printable map and updates them effective 1 April each year.

traverse-city-mi._review: Four trails for seven nights, all four of them dune-and-bluff viewpoints of the same kind, and - the part that matters here - the National Lakeshore prohibits pets on most of them. The two additions are both on the NPS list of pet-open routes, and one of them is the paved rail-grade this whole trip has been short of.

Cave Point County Park.entity: Cave Point County Park, the limestone-shelf shoreline park on the Lake Michigan side of the Door Peninsula. It has no article of its own; Whitefish Dunes State Park's text documents it as an enclave inside the state park reached by the shoreline trail.

Washington Island ferry from Northport.entity: The car ferry across Death's Door from Northport Pier at the north tip of the Door Peninsula to Washington Island. The ferry operator has no article; the Washington Island article's Transportation section documents this exact route and the Northport Pier terminus.

other_links.note: Managing authority. A 0.6-mile portion is graveled for universal access — the flattest option on this stop.

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Peninsula State Park hiking
other_links.note: Managing authority. Runs below 150-foot cliffs past springs and forested terraces. 'More difficult' is the DNR's own three-step scale (Easiest / Moderate / More difficult), not an AllTrails grade.

trails.name: Cave Point County Park shoreline trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Cave Point County Park browse
other_links.note: Two easy trails in the park, 11–12 m of elevation gain between them.

trails.name: Red Trail, Whitefish Dunes State Park

alltrails.name: Whitefish Dunes Yellow and Red Loop

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Whitefish Dunes hiking
other_links.note: Fetched directly. The authority's own words: 'The Red Trail is a 1.2-mile long out and back trail with connections to other property trails. The trail takes hikers to Old Baldy, the tallest dune in the park, which rises 93 feet above lake level.' Listed as hiking; the DNR publishes no difficulty grade for any trail in this park.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Old Baldy Loop Trail
other_links.note: The best-reviewed way onto Old Baldy, 721 reviews — beaches, forest, Lake Michigan views and boardwalks from the Clark Lake Road lot.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Whitefish Dunes Red, Yellow and Green Loop
other_links.note: Longer combination through the forested beech and sugar-maple dunes.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails has no standalone Red Trail listing — it only indexes combination loops. The 1.2 mi is the DNR's figure for the Red Trail alone; the AllTrails Yellow-and-Red loop linked here is 3.3 mi, easy, about an hour.

trails.name: Hotz Trail and Europe Bay Loop, Newport State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted in most campgrounds, trails, roads and outlying areas of properties. ... Pets are not allowed in ... Beaches, except designated pet swim areas ... Trails marked as closed to pets.
trails.note: Newport is Wisconsin's only wilderness state park and an International Dark Sky Park; nothing else in the county is this quiet. The card had nothing north of Fish Creek before this. The loop runs the shore of Europe Lake and Lake Michigan — the walking is dog-legal but the beaches it touches are not.

alltrails.name: Hotz Trail and Europe Bay Loop

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Newport State Park hiking
other_links.note: The authority's own trail list. It gives the full Europe Bay trail loop as 7.0 miles, hiking and bike, mostly level on old logging roads — the AllTrails 2.8 mi loop is the short Hotz combination, not the whole thing.

trails.name: Tower Trail, Potawatomi State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted in most campgrounds, trails, roads and outlying areas of properties.
trails.note: The Sturgeon Bay end of the peninsula, which nothing on the card covered. Oak and cedar down to the Sturgeon Bay shore, rocky and rooty near the water. The observation tower itself has been closed for rebuilding in recent seasons — worth confirming before driving down for it, but the trail is the point.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Ice Age Trail and Tower Trail
other_links.note: The longer version if the short loop is not enough: 6.0 mi, 331 ft, moderate, 2-2.5 hr, 4.6 from 606 reviews.

door-county-wi.dogs: Leashed dogs are fine on all four: Wisconsin DNR permits pets on state park trails unless a trail is signed closed to pets, and none at Peninsula or Whitefish Dunes are. Door County's own rule for Cave Point is "Dogs must be leashed at all times." Beaches are the exception — Whitefish Dunes bars pets from the beach between the nature center and the third beach access from 1 April to 1 November, which covers this stay.
door-county-wi.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted in most campgrounds, trails, roads and outlying areas of properties.
door-county-wi.offroad_finding: Nothing, and the geography is the reason. Door County is a farmed limestone peninsula — orchards, villages and state parks, with paved park drives at Peninsula, Newport and Whitefish Dunes and no public forest road network anywhere on it. Checked: Wisconsin DNR state park roads for the four parks on this card; the Wisconsin DNR off-highway motorcycle and ATV trail listings; and onX Offroad's index for Sturgeon Bay, which returns nothing at all on the peninsula. The nearest full-width unpaved routes it does return are Cedar River Run in Michigan's Escanaba Forest Management Unit and the Oconto County ATV road routes at Pete de Foure Road and Nauke Road — 54, 73 and 82 km away as the crow flies, but all of them on the far side of Green Bay, which means 150-200 km of driving each way around the head of the bay. That is not a day trip from Egg Harbor and none of it belongs on this card. If a gravel afternoon is wanted here, it is the town roads through the Mink River and Europe Lake side of the northern peninsula, and no authority publishes those as a route.

indiana-dunes-in.dogs: All five work on a six-foot leash. Two catches: the lifeguarded swimming area at West Beach is closed to pets through Labor Day, which covers this stay, and the state park (where the 3 Dune Challenge is) bans dogs from its own beach.

indiana-dunes-in.offroad_finding: Nothing within reach, and Indiana makes this unusually easy to state. The Indiana DNR names exactly two state off-road riding areas in the whole state — Interlake Off-Road State Recreation Area (3,500 acres) at Lynnville and Redbird Off-Road State Recreation Area (1,400+ acres) at Linton — plus three private parks, Badlands at Attica, Haspin Acres at Laurel and Lawrence County Recreation Park at Springville. Every one of them is in southern or west-central Indiana, 250-350 km from the Dunes; the nearest, Badlands at Attica, is still about 190 km. Indiana Dunes National Park and Indiana Dunes State Park have paved park roads only and no unpaved public driving route. onX Offroad's index for Chesterton returns zero trails — not a thin list, zero, which is the clearest negative result of any stop in this pass. This stop is beaches, the 3 Dune Challenge and the Chicago skyline; there is no truck day here and nobody should look again.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Grand Trunk backroads to West Montrose
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 198-foot span across the Grand River
scenicDrives_patch.note: The destination is sourced; the backroads themselves are not. Explore Waterloo Region: "The West Montrose Covered Bridge is Ontario's last remaining covered bridge. Located in Woolwich Township, the bridge has a 198-foot span across the Grand River. Built in 1881." THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS: the bridge carries a legal posted load limit of 3 tonnes and "should not be crossed by trucks, buses, tractors or other heavy vehicles", and the Region of Waterloo has confirmed "The legal posted load limit of 3 tonnes will be maintained after the proposed bridge rehabilitation. The Region and Township do not wish to attract more and heavier vehicles." Three tonnes is about 6,600 lb — a half-ton pickup clears it, a loaded three-quarter-ton diesel may not. Weigh or check the door-jamb GVW before driving across rather than after. No named "Grand Trunk backroads" route is published by any authority; the approach roads are ordinary township roads.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Perth County rural loop to St. Marys
scenicDrives_patch.distance: St. Marys is about a 20-minute drive from Stratford (roughly 17.5 km straight-line)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Destination Stratford's own Road Trips page — "Only a 20-minute drive from Stratford, St. Marys is home to museums". No single named rural loop is published; Perth County's tourism arm covers the countryside generically (perthcounty.ca/discover/travel-inspirations/, "Agritourism is thriving in Perth County"). If a defined route is wanted, the best-mapped option in this county is the collaborative cycling map built by Perth County, Destination Stratford and St. Marys — 13 City, Rural and Gravel Signature Routes from short rides up to 230 km — which is drivable as well as rideable and is indexed at ontariobybike.ca/perth-county-st-marys-stratford/.

stratford-on.offroad_finding: Nothing. Stratford sits in the middle of Perth County, which is among the most completely farmed landscapes in Ontario — the public land is river parkland and conservation tracts, not forest. Checked: the Upper Thames River Conservation Authority, which manages the conservation land around Stratford and states plainly that "All-terrain and off-road vehicles are prohibited from all UTRCA property"; the Avon Trail (a footpath, and its own users' code is written for walkers); the City of Stratford parklands, which are municipal parks; and Ontario's Crown Land Use Policy Atlas, which covers "a large part of central and mid-northern Ontario" and does not extend to Perth County, because there is effectively no Crown land here. There are hundreds of kilometres of gravel concession roads through the surrounding farmland, drivable by anything, but they are field-access roads with no viewpoint, no destination and no publishing authority behind them, and putting one on a card would be padding. Note also that neither onX Offroad nor Trails Offroad covers Canada at all, so the usual community backstop does not exist for any of the three Ontario stops.

elora-on.dogs: Elora Quarry is a flat no — the Grand River Conservation Authority bars dogs from that conservation area entirely, service animals excepted. Elora Gorge and the Trailway are fine on a lead under two metres, provided the dog stays on the marked trail; the Gorge's only closed spot is the splash pad.
elora-on.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are not permitted in the conservation area. Service animals are allowed.
elora-on.offroad_finding: Nothing, and two authorities say so explicitly. The Grand River Conservation Authority holds the land that makes this stop — Elora Gorge, Elora Quarry, the Elora Cataract Trailway — and none of it is open to motor vehicles; the Trailway is a rail-trail. The nearest large public woodland is the Dufferin County Forest, about 45 km northeast, and the county's rule is a flat prohibition: "No motorized vehicles are permitted in the Forest, except snowmobiles on designated Ontario Federation of Snowmobile Clubs trails", carried in the County Forest consolidated by-law. Also checked: Wellington County, whose only relevant instrument is an "Off Road Vehicles on County Roads By-law" governing ORVs on public roads rather than opening any route; Ontario's Crown Land Use Policy Atlas, which does not reach Wellington County; and the fact that onX Offroad and Trails Offroad have no Canadian coverage. Elora and Fergus are a gorge, two mill towns and a quarry. There is no legal unpaved driving route within reach and there is no point looking a fourth time.

trails.cruise_reason: It is a former rail bed and flat enough, but the County permits ATVs and licensed dirt bikes on it outside winter, and users report the surface churned and rutted where they have run. That is the surface risk §4 exists to catch — ride it, but scout the section first rather than trusting the rail-grade.

offroad.name: Point Petre / Ostrander Crown Land Block access roads
offroad.season: Ontario Parks states conservation reserves do not have operating dates.
offroad.note: Material change the existing note predates: this land was re-designated in 2023. Point Petre Provincial Wildlife Area and the Ostrander Point Crown Land Block are now the Monarch Point Conservation Reserve, 1,607 ha, regulated under the Provincial Parks and Conservation Reserves Act, 2006 — so any framing of it as MNRF Crown land is out of date. The regulation notice says vehicle use "will be permitted to continue on trails, or off trail to retrieve game, as long as the values the conservation reserve was created to protect are not adversely impacted," and warns that timing restrictions or trail closures could be added later. No management plan with a road inventory exists yet, so no authority publishes mileage, ratings or gate dates. Sandbanks Provincial Park (613) 393-3319 is the only way to get a current answer.

offroad.name: Limerick Forest main access roads
offroad.distance: roughly 180 km of trails and access roads in the forest; the forest is about 75 km northeast of the stop, near Oxford Mills
offroad.difficulty: not graded by the counties; the network runs "from 'single track' to emergency access roads suitable for full-sized vehicles"
offroad.season: No fixed dates are published. The counties close the whole network to motorized use during spring thaw — the 2026 closure ran from late March with reopening expected mid-May — and the truck's permission is conditional: driving the main access roads is allowed "as long as the trails are open". The stop is 14-18 Sep 2028, comfortably outside thaw
offroad.note: The only place within reach of Gananoque where a land manager has written down that a truck may drive. The United Counties of Leeds and Grenville state that if a visitor wants to drive through Limerick "on one of the main access roads in their car or truck and can do so safely and without causing damage to themselves or the forest, then that is permitted as long as the trails are open." That permission is for the MAIN ACCESS ROADS ONLY — the trails themselves are for ATVs and motorcycles whose riders must belong to the OFATV or OFTR and a local club, and "Mud Trucks" are named as not permitted anywhere. So: the wide roads, gently, and nothing else. Everything nearer was checked and came up empty — Thousand Islands National Park is paved roads and footpaths, Frontenac Provincial Park is non-motorized, and Ontario's Crown Land Use Policy Atlas covers central and mid-northern Ontario, not Leeds and Grenville. Frontenac County north of Kingston does carry a real gravel road network, used by the long-distance gravel cycling routes, but no authority publishes any of it as a driving route.

Separately, and worth knowing at this stop: the RVCA does bar dogs entirely from the Perth Wildlife Reserve.

offroad.name: Lanark Highlands gravel township roads (Perth north toward Lanark, Flower Station and Ompah)
offroad.distance: approximately 350 km of gravel roads in the township, many of them seasonal, across 1,048 km²
offroad.season: Two separate restrictions, and the second is the one that bites. Reduced loads are usually in effect from March 1st to mid-May. Seasonal Roads — Class 6B and Class 6C — are CLOSED between November 15 and April 15. That is an outright closure of the seasonal gravel, not a weight limit.
offroad.note: Manager of Public Works 613-259-2398 ext. 239; road emergency 613-264-7329.

perth-on.dogs: The three trails inside Murphys Point are fine on a two-metre lead — Ontario Parks lists no park-specific restriction there. The Rideau Trail is the open question: the Rideau Trail Association says dogs are barred from many portions and does not say which, so the Perth section cannot be called either way without asking them.
perth-on.dogs_source_quote: In many portions of the trail dogs are not permitted! (dogs are not permitted on official Rideau Trail Association hikes). Where dogs are permitted, keep them on a leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Tay Canal / Perth heritage loop
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Rideau Canal Heritage Tour, central section — a driving loop that starts and ends in Perth, "originally laid out as a military settlement in 1816 to help protect the inland water route connecting Lake Ontario with the Ottawa River". Roads used are County Roads 43, 17, 16, 29 and 14 plus Highways 8, 42 and 15; stops are Smiths Falls (Railway Museum, Detached Lock, Visitor Centre), Kilmarnock Lock, Toledo, Forfar and Narrows Lock, where one of the four blockhouses built by Colonel By in 1830-31 still stands. Two caveats: no total distance is published for the loop, and it does NOT include Merrickville, which sits on a different section of the tour (rideau-info.com/canal/driving/). For the Tay itself, Parks Canada is the authority — "The Tay Canal branch of the Rideau Canal extends from Beveridges Lockstation to the town of Perth. The canal ends in the middle of the town at a large turning basin lined with timber crib wharves" (parks.canada.ca/docs/r/on/rideau/whl-lhm/chap2/chap2a1/chap2a1q). Lockstation operating season is not stated on the driving-tour page; an 18 Sep arrival is near the end of the Rideau navigation season, so boats locking through is a check-first, not a given.

Mirror Lake walk.entity: Mirror Lake, the 124-acre lake in the centre of Lake Placid village — the article confirms the village of Lake Placid, town of North Elba, not another New York Mirror Lake.

High Peaks Wilderness day hikes.entity: The High Peaks Wilderness Area, the largest Forest Preserve wilderness in the Adirondack Park.

Drive the Whiteface Veterans' Memorial H.entity: The Whiteface Veterans Memorial Highway (NY 431) to the summit parking area. No separate article; the Whiteface Mountain article documents the highway by name, its 1929 construction and the summit tunnel and elevator.

Walk the gorge at High Falls Gorge.entity: The privately run gorge walk on the Ausable River. No article of its own; the Wilmington, New York article lists High Falls Gorge as a location on NY 86 south of Wilmington village.

Day-run into Saranac Lake.entity: Saranac Lake, New York, the village west of Lake Placid.

Paddle straight off your campsite at Fis.entity: Fish Creek Pond and its state campground in the Adirondacks. No article contains the phrase 'Fish Creek Pond' at all; the Saranac Lakes Wild Forest and Saint Regis Canoe Area articles, which cover the surrounding land, never mention it, and the only 'Fish Creek Ponds' hit is a one-line gazetteer entry in Harrietstown, New York, which documents nothing about the ponds or the campground.

offroad.name: Upper Works Road (CR 25A)
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — onX rates it 1/10 for smooth, well-maintained gravel and dirt with no significant obstacles
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Neither the Town of Newcomb nor DEC publishes a winter plowing status or gate date for this road.
offroad.note: Ends at a large parking area with a pit toilet, and passes the historic McIntyre Blast Furnace of the Tahawus ghost town — you can drive to the gate, the rest of the ghost town is on foot. The road follows the Hudson close to its source, past marshes and ponds. Naming caveat worth carrying: the Town of Newcomb and DEC call the county route CR 25 (Tahawus Road), not CR 25A, and the Town states the old parking lot at the terminus of Upper Works Road is closed, with parking moved to a 60-car lot by the MacNaughton Cottage and unauthorised vehicles towed. The draw is history and trailhead access rather than the driving.

offroad.name: Deer Pond Road
offroad.distance: 2.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — rated 2/10, mostly easy dirt with minor potholes and muddy puddles after rain
offroad.season: DEC requires parking reservations from Memorial Day weekend until the gates close for winter in late November or early December.
offroad.note: Resolved to the Essex Chain Lakes Complex in Newcomb, where DEC calls it the Cornell/Deer Pond Road — not Moose River Plains. Ends at a large parking area on the edge of the Essex Chain Lakes Primitive Area with a pit toilet and a gate; you continue on foot to the water. Several roadside dispersed camp spots along it. DEC's own wording for the roads here: pickup trucks, SUVs and other high axle vehicles are recommended, four wheel drive will serve even better. Beavers occasionally flood portions of the road.

offroad.name: Otter Brook Road
offroad.distance: 2.9 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — not very difficult, but one vehicle wide and needing some higher clearance toward the end
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. DEC publishes no fixed gate dates for Otter Brook Road itself; the parent access, the Limekiln Lake–Cedar River Road, is a seasonal road that opens mid-May.
offroad.note: DEC-maintained, in the Moose River Plains Complex, and it sees very little traffic. Surface alternates sandy two-track and well-maintained gravel; it ends at a bog where a small snowmobile bridge crosses the South Branch of the Grass River. Live closure to check before going: a bridge failure at Payne Brook has forced all Moose River Plains access to the Limekiln Lake/Inlet entrance, with the Cedar River Headquarters gate closed — approach from the west. DEC Region 5 Northville 518-863-4545.

offroad.name: Lake Glen Road
offroad.distance: 6.6 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — an established forest access road with a stable base, no deep waterholes or large rocks
offroad.season: Best summer and fall; no gate dates published by anyone.
offroad.note: Runs around the southern flank of 3,550 ft Saddleback Mountain through the Adirondack Forest Preserve. Side-trail access at the western end is blocked by a forest products company that owns most of the surrounding land. Honest limit: this is the one Adirondack route no authority confirms — no DEC page, unit management plan or roads-open-to-motor-vehicle-use listing names it, and because it runs between Forest Preserve and private industrial timberland its legal access basis is genuinely unestablished. Recent reports include downed trees needing recovery boards in Dec 2025.

lake-placid-ny.dogs: Cascade and Porter are DEC Forest Preserve and take dogs, but the leash is compulsory the whole way — they sit in the zone where DEC requires a leash at all times, not just above 4,000 ft. Mount Jo is on the Adirondack Mountain Club's Heart Lake property and ADK publishes no pet policy for it; the managing authority for the Owl's Head trail could not be established, so both are blank rather than assumed.
lake-placid-ny.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness

trails.name: Mt. Van Hoevenberg
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness and at trailheads, campsites and above 4,000 feet everywhere else.
trails.season: Late September is the front edge of Adirondack colour; the open summit ledges here look straight at Marcy, Colden and the MacIntyres, so this is the view walk of the stop.
trails.note: The card had Mount Jo, Owl's Head and Cascade-Porter — two very short ones and one Hard 4,000-footer, with nothing moderate in between. This is the gap-filler: a real summit with a real view for half a day's work, on a purpose-built graded trail rather than an Adirondack root ladder. Dog legal but must be leashed — this is inside the Eastern High Peaks zone, where rangers write about ten off-leash tickets a year.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mt. Van Hoevenberg East Trail
other_links.note: The newer, better-liked way up, from the Olympic Sports Complex side: 3.7 mi out-and-back, 974 ft, 4.8 from 3,811 reviews — the highest-rated walk anywhere near Lake Placid. No estimated time or difficulty grade was returned for it in any result read, which is the only reason the older trail carries the entry.

trails.needs: star rating — no result read returned one for this listing, only the 2,388-review count from the page title

trails.name: Baker Mountain Loop Trail
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness and at trailheads, campsites and above 4,000 feet everywhere else.
trails.note: Half an hour's drive for Saranac Lake's steepest half hour on foot — 879 ft in under a mile up, then lookouts over Saranac Lake, Lake Flower and the whole High Peaks skyline. Part of the Saranac 6er. It is in the McKenzie Mountain Wilderness, outside the Eastern High Peaks zone, so the DEC leash rule binds at the trailhead rather than the whole way; leash her anyway on something this busy.

other_links.label: Saranac Lake — Baker Mountain
other_links.note: Local visitor bureau: 1.6 mi round trip, 884 ft of gain, summit 2,452 ft. Slightly shorter than the AllTrails loop, which adds the Moody Pond return.

trails.stats_note: A separate AllTrails listing simply named 'Baker Mountain' shows a review count of 2,454 — identical to the mountain's height in feet, which is exactly the coincidence §2 says to distrust. The loop listing was used instead. No star rating was returned for either.

Cross to Burlington for a proper town da.entity: Burlington, Vermont — the city named in the headline, eleven miles south across the lake.

Drive out to Isle La Motte and Saint Ann.entity: Both named things have their own articles: Isle La Motte, the northernmost Champlain island, and Saint Anne's Shrine — confirmed as the Isle La Motte shrine on Lake Champlain (site of Fort Sainte Anne, 1666), not one of the several other Saint Anne shrines.

Grand Isle–Plattsburgh ferry.entity: The route has no article of its own, but the Lake Champlain Transportation Company article documents it under its own heading 'Grand Isle-Plattsburgh' — an ice-breaking route with 24-hour year-round service between Grand Isle, VT and Cumberland Head, Plattsburgh, NY — which is exactly the claim in this entry.

Run the causeway drive up US Route 2 thr.entity: US Route 2 is the named thing; the Vermont article covers the Grand Isle County section that crosses Lake Champlain 'over several bridges' and lists the South Hero junction. Knight Point State Park, the North Hero day-use park named in the note, is confirmed separately — sand beach, boat rentals and the Campmeeting Point Natural Area with its rare plant species.

Snow Farm Vineyard & Distillery.entity: A working winery and distillery on West Shore Road. No Wikipedia article; the only mention anywhere is a one-line directory row in List of wineries in New England ('Snow Farm Vineyard and Distillery - South Hero'), which documents nothing about it. The card already carries the winery's own site.

Walk the shoreline at Grand Isle State P.entity: Grand Isle State Park in Grand Isle, Vermont — the 226-acre lakeshore park; the article confirms the lean-to and cabin sites, hot showers and trailer sanitary station this entry relies on. Disambiguated from the Louisiana park of the same name.

Watch the sunset from the west shore.entity: A viewing direction, not a place: 'the west shore' of South Hero across the widest part of Lake Champlain to the Adirondack High Peaks. Nothing named, and linking the lake or the High Peaks would point at neither the shore nor the sunset window this entry is about.

south-hero-vt.dogs: Split stop: the two Missisquoi NWR trails take a leashed dog under the refuge's own rule, but Vermont publishes nothing reachable for Mount Philo or Niquette Bay, so treat both state parks as unknown until Vermont State Parks is phoned.
south-hero-vt.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be leashed and under the control of the owner while on the refuge.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sandbar Causeway (US-2, Milton to South Hero)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Vermont State Parks' Sand Bar page — "Sand Bar State Park takes its name from a natural sandbar between South Hero Island" and the town of Milton on the mainland; the park address is 1215 US Route 2, Milton. The causeway carrying US-2 across it was built in the 1950s on top of an 1850s bridge, over a sandbar formed by Lamoille River sediment. Fetching vtstateparks.com returned HTTP 403 (bot detection), so the listing is confirmed from the search result's own title and snippet and no season dates are recorded. Sand Bar is a day-use beach park with a short summer season, so a 28 Sep arrival will likely find the park itself closed while US-2 across the causeway stays open — check the park's season before planning a stop rather than a drive-through.

offroad.name: Big Hollow Road (Class 4 town highway)
offroad.distance: 6.2 mi · about 49 km southeast of the stop, in the Green Mountains behind Starksboro and Fayston
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "Expect a varied road surface from packed gravel to dirt to mud"; high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists Fall and Summer, and warns "best to avoid this trail during the spring sugaring season". The stop is 28 Sep - 1 Oct 2028, which is the right end of the year for it — Vermont's mud season is spring, not autumn
offroad.note: Read the distance before planning on it. The Champlain Islands themselves — South Hero, Grand Isle, North Hero, Isle La Motte — have no unpaved public driving route that any authority or database publishes: the islands are farmland, orchards and lakeshore on paved town roads, and the two state parks and the Missisquoi refuge are walking. This is the nearest thing found, and it is off the island, over the causeway and an hour away in the mountains. What it is: "Starts as a Vermont Farm gravel road, then transitions to a standard class 4 road with some small obstacles. You will pass some abandoned homes and a lot of maple sugaring equipment. At the halfway point, the road will narrow, and you will come to a log landing. Past the log landing is a narrow, much older, and less-used trail that will exit into a field with horses." Class 4 town highways are Vermont's unmaintained public rights of way — legal to drive, but the town has no duty to keep them passable, so condition is whatever the last logging job and the last storm left. On a three-night stop this is a whole day; it is honest to say it may not be worth it.

Stowe village and foliage drives.entity: Stowe, Vermont and the roads around it.

Covered bridges.entity: Stowe's covered bridges, chiefly the 1844 Gold Brook Covered Bridge (Emily's Bridge), the state's only 19th-century covered bridge on wooden Howe trusses carrying a public road.

Drive the Mount Mansfield Toll Road in t.entity: The toll road up Mount Mansfield, Vermont's highest peak.

Climb Camel's Hump.entity: Camel's Hump, the 4,083 ft Green Mountains peak.

Base yourself at Gold Brook and stay put.entity: Gold Brook Campground on VT 100 south of Stowe village. No article. Wikipedia's 'Gold Brook' hit is the Gold Brook Covered Bridge (Emily's Bridge, 1844) — a different thing on the same stream, already linked from the 'Covered bridges' entry on this stop — so it is rejected here on identity.

Time it for peak colour.entity: Foliage timing for the Stowe/Waterbury elevation band, not an entity. The places the note names for dropping elevation — Mount Mansfield and the notch — are already linked from the Mansfield toll road and Smugglers Notch entries on this stop.

offroad.name: Patterson Brook Road (Fire Service 50)
offroad.distance: 5.2 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — easy driving, but care is needed because active logging changes road conditions; a chainsaw for blowdowns helps
offroad.season: Green Mountain National Forest, official: most GMNF roads are closed during the winter months from December 15 to May 1, with some exceptions. FR 50 Patterson Brook, Rochester district, currently listed Open.
offroad.note: The one route in this set with a real land-manager behind it. Borders the Bread Loaf Wilderness, climbing from 1,043 ft near Granville to 1,868 ft. Dispersed off-grid campsites along FR 50, no permit, 14-day limit, and no cell service. Stream crossings are on good bridges.

offroad.name: Symonds Mill Road
offroad.distance: 4.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — "country dirt roads"
offroad.season: Best fall, summer, spring. No town or state mud-season restriction found for this road.
offroad.note: The one Vermont route in this set that is genuinely local to the stop — Wolcott/Elmore, about 20 minutes from Stowe. Mostly packed gravel with some muddy sections; these are working farm roads, so watch for farm equipment and livestock. Pairs with Woodbury Mountain Road if you want a longer day.

offroad.name: Big Hollow Road
offroad.distance: 6.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — varied surface from packed gravel to dirt to mud
offroad.season: Best fall and summer. A status report of 14 Apr 2026 has it Temporarily Closed for a posted seasonal closure, with no stated opening day — consistent with a Vermont Class 4 mud-season closure. Best avoided during spring sugaring season.
offroad.note: Location flag worth resolving before the trip: this listing sits at 44.227, -73.056, which is Starksboro in Addison County — west of the Green Mountain spine and about 35 miles from Stowe, not the Fayston Big Hollow Road. Fayston's town roads page and its 2020 Town Plan both fetch clean with no mention of a Big Hollow Road, so no listing for the Fayston one could be sourced. Starts as farm gravel, becomes a standard Class 4 road with small obstacles, past abandoned homes and maple sugaring equipment; narrows at a log landing halfway, then an older, less-used trail out into a field with horses.

offroad.name: Top of the World
offroad.distance: 3.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — maintained gravel that washes out on the steeper climbs, with water bars that can catch a low bumper
offroad.season: Best time listed as summer only.
offroad.note: Same location flag as Big Hollow: this runs the powerlines on the Vermont side of Moore Reservoir, near Waterford in Caledonia County — roughly 50 miles east of Stowe, a long day trip rather than a local run. No Roxbury or Northfield 'Top of the World Road' could be sourced anywhere. The payoff at the top is a view over Moore Reservoir toward New Hampshire. Many offshoots from mild to wild; the final climb is where 4WD matters if it has washed out. Expect ATV and side-by-side groups on a fine day. Reports through 2026 say a washout has been repaired and the route rebuilt into an easy dirt road.

Aug 2026 pass — tried the rule as LAW rather than as a park page, since the park pages are the part that 403s. The adopted rule is Code of Vermont Rules 12 020 009, 'VISITOR CONDUCT AND FEES AND CHARGES FOR STATE PARK SERVICES AND COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES ON DEPARTMENT LANDS'. Every route to its text failed, listed below.

https://secure.vermont.gov/SOS/rules/ — LOADS (so the Vermont 403 is not domain-wide, it is specific to the parks sites). But it carries PROPOSED rules only, and points to LexisNexis for adopted ones.

http://www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/codeofvtrules/ — the Secretary of State's designated publisher of the Code of Vermont Rules. 301-redirects into advance.lexis.com, a JavaScript container that returns no rule text.
https://sos.vermont.gov/rules/ — 403
https://regulations.justia.com/states/vermont/agency-12/sub-agency-020/chapter-009/section-12-020-009/ — 403. This is the one page a search actually surfaced with the right citation, and it refused.

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/vermont/12-020-009 — loads, but only as an agency index; Cornell LII carries no Vermont rule text at this citation (it does carry North Dakota's, which is how Bismarck was settled).

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=%22Vermont+State+Parks%22+rules+%22pets%22+leash+rabies+certificate+official+PDF — returned Burlington Free Press, Hipcamp and a vtstateparks.com tag page. No official rule text anywhere in the index.
dogs_unpublished.action: Phone Vermont State Parks on 1-888-409-7579 (or parks@vermont.gov) and ask two things: are dogs permitted on Mount Mansfield's Sunset Ridge and the Long Trail over the summit ridge, given the alpine zone, and is there any dog restriction on the Putnam State Forest trails at Stowe Pinnacle and Moss Glen Falls. One call settles all six. Worth doing before arrival — this is a 4-night hard-anchored stop on 1 Oct 2028 and the trails are most of what the stop is for.
