Gettysburg town and the Lincoln connecti.entity: Gettysburg and Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, delivered there in November 1863.

offroad.name: Caledonia to Pine Grove Furnace forest roads
offroad.note: DCNR's Michaux map index carries the two documents that actually answer which of these roads can be driven: the Michaux State Forest Public Use Map and a self-guided 'Auto Tour of Michaux State Forest', both PDFs. The index itself publishes no mileage for the auto tour, and the PDFs were not read here. The separate ATV trail map on the same page is a different system and is not the drivable road network.

offroad.name: Michaux State Forest gravel road network, South Mountain
offroad.note: DCNR's forest page confirms the authority and links a Michaux State Forest Recreation Guide PDF, but publishes nothing about which roads are open, gated or seasonally closed. Pennsylvania does not run an MVUM system like the national forests, so the Public Use Map on the maps page is the only thing that distinguishes drivable forest roads from gated administrative ones.

trails.name: Billy Yank Trail

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Komoot logs the same route at 10.8 mi with 570 ft gain — a different GPS trace of the same walk.

other_links.label: New Birth of Freedom Council — Gettysburg Heritage Trails
other_links.note: The route's origin: Billy Yank and Johnny Reb are the two hiking segments of the Scouting Gettysburg Heritage Trails programme, not NPS-built footpaths.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails 9.7 mi / 748 ft vs Komoot 10.8 mi / 570 ft — both are GPS traces of a self-guided battlefield route, and neither is an official published length. AllTrails average time 3 h 32 min.

trails.name: Johnny Reb Trail

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Same route, second trace.

other_links.label: Garmin Trails
other_links.note: Logs it as a 3.7 mi casual loop, 1.5–2.5 h.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails 4 mi / ~2.5 h and 644 reviews; no star rating in the indexed snippet. Garmin gives 3.7 mi for the same loop. Difficulty 'easy' is described by npplan and Garmin, not published by NPS. No water on the route.

trails.name: Bridle Trail Loop
trails.difficulty: Mainly easy with a few moderate hills on the south side of the park

other_links.label: National Park Planner — Bridle Trail Loop Hike
other_links.note: 7.25-mile loop, 5.5 hours. Calls it the best hike in the park — it links the Bridle Trail with the footpaths around the base of Big and Little Round Top.

other_links.label: National Park Planner — Gettysburg hiking and biking
other_links.note: Context for the whole trail network; notes the battlefield 'trails' are largely walking routes rather than built footpaths.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing found for the Bridle Trail Loop under any wording. Length and difficulty are National Park Planner's, not an NPS publication — treat as approximate. The trail itself is the park's horse trail, so hiking and horse use are both established; bicycle status not sourced.

trails.name: Little Round Top

alltrails.name: Little Round Top (point of interest page only — no trail listing)

other_links.label: NPS — Little Round Top trail map
other_links.note: NPS publishes the formalized trail network built during the Little Round Top rehabilitation project — 'These new formalized trails have replaced many of the old social trails where extreme erosion had occurred.' NPS is the authority for current access; a crowd-sourced AllTrails list still carries a stale 'Little Round Top closed' note from the rehabilitation years.

other_links.label: NPS — Little Round Top
other_links.note: Site overview and rehabilitation project video.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails has a point-of-interest page for Little Round Top and says two trails reach it, but no trail listing carries the name. NPS publishes no single length for the summit paths. Confirmed to exist by the National Park Service; recorded unlisted rather than linked to a route that is not the same walk.

gettysburg-pa.dogs: Gettysburg NMP welcomes leashed dogs everywhere on the battlefield grounds and trails; only park buildings, the visitor center and the National Cemetery are closed to them.
gettysburg-pa.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be restrained on a leash at all times while in the park.

Appalachian Trail access.entity: The Appalachian Trail itself, which runs straight through Harpers Ferry; the AT article's West Virginia section covers this stretch.

Lower Town, the Stone Steps and Jefferso.entity: Harpers Ferry's Lower Town Historic District and the Jefferson Rock outcrop above it. The park article documents the Lower Town district and lists Jefferson Rock; Jefferson Rock has its own article. The Stone Steps (the cut-rock stair up to the rock) have no article and are not named in either.

links.label: Wikipedia — Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

Maryland Heights.entity: The cliff across the Potomac in Maryland, not Maryland Heights, Missouri (which is what the bare title resolves to). The Elk Ridge article states the ridge's southern end, part of Harpers Ferry NHP, is known as Maryland Heights; the park article documents the Maryland Heights section.

links.label: Wikipedia — Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

Appalachian Trail Conservancy headquarte.entity: The ATC, whose headquarters the article places in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.

C&O Canal towpath.entity: The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal towpath opposite Harpers Ferry; the park article covers the towpath trail and its Harpers Ferry section.

links.label: Wikipedia — Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Historical Park

trails.name: Weverton Cliffs (Appalachian Trail)

other_links.label: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
other_links.note: ATC's own hike page, with the trailhead directions: from US 340 take MD 67 North to the first right at Weverton Cliff Rd; large paved lot on the right.

trails.stats_note: 1.7 mi / 570 ft / 4.8 from 5,765 reviews are AllTrails' own figures via its Weverton Cliffs point-of-interest page; the trail listing title showed 5,817 reviews in a later crawl, so the count is still climbing. Average 1–1.5 hr. The slug carries a --3 suffix — it is not derivable from the name.

harpers-ferry-wv.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted throughout Harpers Ferry NHP including the Maryland Heights climb, and on the C&O Canal towpath and the Appalachian Trail up to Weverton Cliffs.
harpers-ferry-wv.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be kept on a six-foot leash at all times while visiting any area of the park.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-340 through the Potomac/Shenandoah Water Gap
scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS: "Harpers Ferry NHP's Visitor Center is located along US Route 340 in West Virginia", 8 miles east of Charles Town, WV and 20 miles southwest of Frederick, MD. The park's own directions run US 340 in from three sides — north from Charles Town, south from Frederick, and north from Front Royal via Shenandoah NP. The directions page carries no description of the gap itself, no distances for the scenic stretch and no seasonal conditions; the park's separate Scenic Vistas page (home.nps.gov/hafe/learn/nature/scenicvistas.htm) is where the water-gap view is described. Nothing published on either page about winter driving, so no season field is claimed.

offroad.name: Frederick Watershed loop (Frederick Municipal Forest)
offroad.distance: 9.4 mi · about 33 km east of the stop — much the closest
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "can be done in just about any vehicle however I recommend an off-road oriented vehicle due to persistent bumps and ruts"
offroad.season: onX lists Fall only. The City of Frederick gates the watershed roads and has closed Fishing Creek Road at its junctions with Gambrill Park Road and Hamburg Road in the past, and runs prescribed burns in the second half of November that close Gambrill Park Road in sections
offroad.note: The one to do from Harpers Ferry: nine and a half miles of unmaintained gravel in the city watershed above Frederick, an easy hour away. "The route is a loop with one spur which is Fishing Creek. There is only one way in and out of the watershed and all other access points are blocked. There are also no other places in the watershed that have 4x4 access. I included a picture of one of the gates because as you approach it looks like a dead end, however the intent is to go to the side." Two things to check before driving out, both because the stop is 21-25 Nov 2028: the City of Frederick posts gate closures and prescribed-burn closures for exactly this window (a burn was scheduled 17-21 November in a recent year, closing Gambrill Park Road between Fishing Creek Road and Gate R6), and there is only one way in, so a closed gate means the day is over.

offroad.name: Rattlesnake Run, Michaux State Forest
offroad.distance: 4.3 mi · about 57 km north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "During the winter months, four-wheel drive is suggested but not required"
offroad.season: onX lists Fall, Summer, Spring. Pennsylvania's firearms deer season opens in the days after Thanksgiving and Michaux is heavily hunted; the stop ends 25 Nov 2028
offroad.note: "One of the first trails you'll hit if you enter Michaux from the south end. It is an unmaintained gravel road with multiple inclines and declines. There are many hiking trail options surrounding this trail, with Appalachian Trail access points." Michaux is the real answer for this stop — a Pennsylvania state forest laced with drivable gravel, an hour north, and DCNR publishes both a Public Use Map and a formal "Auto Tour of Michaux State Forest" on its maps page, which is the thing to download before going.

offroad.name: Wirt Road, Michaux State Forest
offroad.distance: 4.6 mi · about 59 km north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "generally passable in good weather and safe for most 4WD and high-clearance 2WD vehicles. Winter maintenance is not provided"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons, with the winter-maintenance warning above
offroad.note: "Wirt Road is a scenic gravel route running from Staley Road to Old Forge Road, cutting through the quiet woodlands of Michaux State Forest. Along the way, it crosses Biesecker Run and Vineyard Run, which offer peaceful streamside views. The road also passes several trailheads popular with hikers, mountain bikers, and horseback riders." The natural pair with Staley Road (5.3 mi, onX rating 1, "an unmaintained forest road running through Michaux State Forest... A few inclines and declines that get slick with snow or ice present") for a half-day loop off Route 233.

offroad.name: Oak Road, Michaux State Forest
offroad.distance: 2.4 mi · about 57 km north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "generally pretty well maintained"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall
offroad.note: "This forest road in the southwest corner of Michaux State Forest is notable for the Valley View Vista that offers a good view towards the town of Mont Alto to the west... the vista is a worthwhile stop while in the southern part of the forest. Where the pipeline crosses south of the vista offers a bit of a view to the west as well." Short, easy and it has the view — the one to pick if there is only an afternoon.

offroad.name: High Rock Road, Michaux State Forest
offroad.distance: 4.6 mi · about 62 km north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "generally in good condition with some potholes. It is usually passable by any road-legal vehicle"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Summer, Fall
offroad.note: "A largely gravel/shale state forest road that meanders along the west side of the ridge of the South Mountain. It's notable for having three rustic, dispersed camp sites in a forest that does not have that many... Section 5 of the Mid-Atlantic BDR uses this road, so look out for" motorcycles on it. One correction worth carrying: "the Pennsylvania DCNR map shows a vista, but they've not cleared the vegetation there for some time, so there is no clear view down to the valley" as of August 2025. District Road (4.3 mi, onX rating 2, gravel between Route 233 and Newman Road with access to Carbaugh Reservoir) is the fifth Michaux option and the only one onX lists as a winter route.

offroad.name: Auto Tour of Michaux State Forest
offroad.distance: not published on the maps index; the tour is a signed driving route through the forest, about an hour north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: not published
offroad.season: not published — DCNR does not post gate dates on the maps page, and the district office (717-352-2211) is the number that would settle it
offroad.note: Recorded because it is the authority's own answer to "where do I drive here", and because it is the map to have in hand rather than a community track: DCNR's Michaux maps page publishes "Auto Tour of Michaux State Forest (PDF)" alongside the Michaux State Forest Public Use Map. Its length, route and surface could not be read from the sandbox — the DCNR elibrary link returns a document viewer rather than the PDF itself — so nothing about the tour is asserted here beyond its existence. Download both from the maps page before the drive.

Skyline Drive.entity: The 105-mile parkway through Shenandoah National Park in Virginia — verified as the Virginia road, not another Skyline Drive.

Staunton's historic downtown.entity: Downtown Staunton, listed as the Beverley Historic District (131 contributing buildings in downtown Staunton).

Walk the Blue Ridge Tunnel.entity: Claudius Crozet's Blue Ridge (Crozet) Tunnel at Rockfish Gap, reopened in 2020 as a walking trail.

Humpback Rocks.entity: The greenstone outcrop on Humpback Mountain at Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 5.8 in Augusta/Nelson County, Virginia. NOTE: the title 'Humpback Rocks' resolves to rocks off South Georgia in the South Atlantic; the Virginia formation is at 'Humpback Rock'.

Downtown Staunton and the Blackfriars Pl.entity: Downtown Staunton (Beverley Historic District) and the Blackfriars Playhouse, which redirects to its operator, the American Shakespeare Center.

Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and.entity: The Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and Museum in Staunton, which contains the birthplace Manse.

Sherando Lake and Grand Caverns as weath.entity: Grand Caverns at Grottoes, Virginia, and Sherando Lake. Sherando Lake has no article; the Blue Ridge Parkway article documents it by name at milepost 16 as a recreation area in George Washington National Forest 4.5 miles from the parkway.

staunton-va.dogs: Shenandoah permits leashed dogs on most of its 500+ miles of trail — it is one of the most dog-friendly national parks on this trip. Fewer than 20 miles are closed, and BOTH of the trails this card originally carried were on that short list: Stony Man and every Old Rag route. The four added trails are all dog-legal. Leash 6 ft, physical leash.
staunton-va.dogs_note: Two of this stop's trails are on Shenandoah's short prohibited list — Stony Man's blue-blazed summit portion and the Old Rag trails (Ridge Access, Ridge, Saddle). Everything ELSE in the park is open to the dog, which still makes this one of the best stops on the trip for walking together; it is just that both trails currently named here happen to be exceptions. Worth adding dog-legal Shenandoah trails to this card.

offroad.name: George Washington NF gravel roads, North River / Todd Lake district
offroad.season: Todd Lake Recreation Area open mid-May to late October
offroad.note: Forest Service directions run 1.1 miles on SR 718 (Stokesville Road) to the FR 95 / FR 101 junction, then 3.1 miles on FR 95 (North River Road) to Todd Lake. The page does not state whether FR 95 is gravel or paved and publishes no vehicle restriction. FR 95 is also the lower end of the North River Trail, which climbs to FR 85 (Shenandoah Mountain Road) — the same road as the Reddish Knob route below, so the two can be linked.

offroad.name: Reddish Knob road (FR 85 from Briery Branch, west of Harrisonburg)
offroad.difficulty: onX rating 2 (Easy) — "easy dirt and gravel trail with just a few rutted and rocky spots"
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer, fall and winter
offroad.note: onX rates this for high-clearance, full-width vehicles and puts the observation point at 4,397 ft. The adjoining Flagpole Knob route meets it at Briery Branch Gap and has its own onX listing at 12.8 miles, also difficulty 2 — the pair make one long day if the weather holds. Note the two are not equivalent: Flagpole's FR 85 approach is reported as much rougher than the Reddish Knob asphalt spur.

trails.name: Stony Man Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Stony Man
other_links.note: NPS route: from the Stony Man parking area at Skyline Drive mile 41.7, take the Appalachian Trail to the trail post. Second highest peak in Shenandoah.

other_links.label: NPS — Stony Man Trailhead
other_links.note: Trailhead page.

trails.stats_note: Important: AllTrails indexes the Appalachian Trail approach, not the Stony Man Trail itself — its own description says the AT route 'runs parallel to the Stony Man Trail and may become overgrown in the warmer months'. 1.5 mi / 318 ft is AllTrails for the AT route; 1.6 mi round trip is the NPS figure for the walk to the summit. 9,311 reviews on the AllTrails listing; no star rating in the indexed snippet.

trails.name: Lewis Spring Falls Trail
trails.season: Listed as open year-round, but Skyline Drive is the only way to the trailhead and NPS closes it in ice and snow. In the 25 Nov - 2 Dec window, check the Drive's status before setting out.
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL, WHICH NEITHER TRAIL PREVIOUSLY ON THIS CARD IS. Shenandoah allows leashed dogs on most of its 500+ miles of trail and publishes a short, closed list of the exceptions; Lewis Spring Falls is not on it, while Stony Man and every Old Rag route are. A waterfall loop from Big Meadows with an 81-foot fall at the turn.
trails.note_source: NPS Shenandoah pets page, fetched: 'Pets are allowed, if leashed, on most trails', leash 6 ft, with pets prohibited only on Fox Hollow, Stony Man, Limberlost, Post Office Junction to Old Rag Shelter, Old Rag Ridge, Old Rag Saddle, Ridge Access, Dark Hollow Falls, Story of the Forest, Bearfence Mountain and Frazier Discovery - 'fewer than 20 miles of the 500+ miles of trails'. This trail appears on no part of that list.

other_links.label: NPS — Pets in Shenandoah
other_links.note: Authority. Publishes the complete list of pet-prohibited trails, which is what makes a dogs:true here defensible rather than inferred.

trails.name: Blackrock Trail
trails.season: April through October per AllTrails; the stay is outside that window, which for a half-mile talus walk means cold and possible ice rather than closure. Skyline Drive access is again the real question.
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL. Thirteen minutes from the Drive out to the Blackrock talus field and one of the widest views in the southern district for the least effort in the park. Not on Shenandoah's prohibited list.
trails.note_source: NPS Shenandoah pets page, fetched - see Lewis Spring Falls entry for the full quotation and the prohibited list.

trails.name: Appalachian Trail to Tanner Ridge Road
trails.season: April through October per AllTrails.
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL. An easy out-and-back on the AT itself - forty minutes, gentle, and the walk to take when the weather is closing in. The AT through Shenandoah is not on the pet-prohibited list.
trails.note_source: NPS Shenandoah pets page, fetched - see Lewis Spring Falls entry.

alltrails.name: Appalachian Trail to Tanner Ridge Road

trails.name: Hazeltop Summit via Appalachian Trail
trails.season: April through November per AllTrails - of the four here, the window that stretches closest to the stay.
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL. Short AT climb to the third-highest summit in the park through red spruce. Two miles, and the dog comes.
trails.note_source: NPS Shenandoah pets page, fetched - see Lewis Spring Falls entry.

staunton-va.dogs_source_quote: Pets are prohibited on the following trails:
staunton-va.stats_note: This stop's dogs_verdict was 'prohibited' because BOTH trails on the card - Stony Man and Old Rag - happen to be on Shenandoah's short prohibited list, which made a park that is one of the most dog-friendly in the system read as closed to the dog. The four above correct that: all are dog-legal, and the verdict for the stop is better described as partial. Story of the Forest Trail (1.8 mi, easy, 768 reviews) surfaced and was left off precisely because it IS on the prohibited list.

Natural Bridge State Park.entity: Natural Bridge, Virginia — the article covers the arch and states it has been managed as Natural Bridge State Park since 2016.

Historic downtown Lexington.entity: The Lexington Historic District, the NRHP district covering the town's historic core.

Natural Bridge.entity: The 215-ft natural limestone arch in Rockbridge County, Virginia.

Devils Marbleyard.entity: The boulder field on Bluff Mountain. It has no article of its own; the James River Face Wilderness article names 'the Devils Marbleyard' as a rock outcrop within the wilderness.

Lexington's historic core on foot.entity: Same Lexington Historic District, walked rather than driven.

Blue Ridge Parkway from the James River.entity: The Parkway's northern Virginia section and the James River it crosses at milepost 63.8, both documented in the Parkway article.

Buena Vista and the Maury River valley.entity: The city of Buena Vista, Virginia and the Maury River, which the river article traces past Lexington and Buena Vista in Rockbridge County.

lexington-va.authority: National Park Service — Shenandoah / Blue Ridge Parkway
lexington-va.dogs: Natural Bridge State Park is a Virginia state park, and leashed dogs are allowed on all of its trails including Cedar Creek under the arch.

offroad.name: George Washington & Jefferson NF gravel roads, North Mountain west of Lexington
offroad.note: Unlisted. No Forest Service page and no off-road database covers this road network as a named route. The forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to which vehicle class, and GWJNF publishes one forest-wide MVUM rather than per-district ones — so plan from the MVUM, not from a route listing.
offroad.season: GWJNF seasonal roads: "Many seasonal roads are closed during the freeze-thaw of winter to protect roads surfaces from damage, typically closing on January 10 and reopening April 1." The stop arrives 2 Dec 2028 for 4 nights, so it clears the gate date by about five weeks — but only just, and the Forest states opening and closing dates vary by road, with some roads separately gated for wildlife.

offroad.name: George Washington National Forest roads (near Natural Bridge, off Rt. 812)
offroad.note: Unlisted, same situation as North Mountain: the Forest Service publishes district topographic maps and a single forest-wide MVUM, but no page for this road network and no named route in any off-road database. The MVUM carries the vehicle-class and seasonal designations for each road.
offroad.season: Same GWJNF winter policy — seasonal roads typically close January 10 and reopen April 1, dates varying by road. A 2 Dec arrival is ahead of it.

offroad.name: James River Face Wilderness access roads (Belfast Trail / Petites Gap)
offroad.season: Forest Service lists the trail open year round
offroad.note: Forest Service directions take the left fork onto VA 781 (Petites Gap Road) and run about 1.0 mile to the parking area. The page grades the Belfast Trail itself Moderate to Difficult over 2.3 miles — that is the walk to the Devil's Marbleyard boulder field, not the drive. The Forest Service says nothing about the road's surface or its FS 35 designation, so no surface claim is recorded.

trails.name: Cedar Creek Trail

alltrails.name: Lace Falls via Cedar Creek Trail

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Same trail, graded easy.

trails.stats_note: The listing is named for its destination, Lace Falls, not for the trail. The route descends 137 stone steps under the 215 ft Natural Bridge and ends at the falls — the stairs are the reason third-party guides grade it harder than AllTrails' 'easy'. Highest-rated trail in Natural Bridge State Park.

trails.name: Buck Hill Trail

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Grades the same loop 'easy' where AllTrails says moderately challenging. Starts near the Natural Bridge Caverns car park.

other_links.label: Lexington & Rockbridge tourism
other_links.note: Green-blazed and easy to follow; young oak, hickory and poplar forest.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails 2.3 mi loop, average 1 h 5 min, 223 reviews; no star rating in the indexed snippet. Difficulty is disputed between AllTrails (moderately challenging) and Komoot (easy).

trails.name: Skyline Trail

other_links.label: Komoot — Skyline Trail & Jefferson's Point loop
other_links.note: Graded easy. Adds Jefferson's Point to the loop.

other_links.label: Lexington & Rockbridge tourism
other_links.note: Walks the loop clockwise from the kiosk; red Skyline Trail sign marks the start.

trails.stats_note: No distance surfaced from AllTrails in any indexed snippet, and neither Natural Bridge State Park nor the tourism board publishes one — recorded absent rather than guessed. The --2 suffix on the slug means there is more than one Skyline Trail Loop in Virginia; this is the Natural Bridge one, confirmed by the park page that ranks it.

lexington-va.dogs_source_quote: Pets are allowed in all Virginia State Parks. State regulations require pets to be confined or kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet and kept under supervision while in the park.

Canyon Rim Visitor Center overlook.entity: The Canyon Rim Visitor Center, named in the park article as one of two year-round visitor centres and a viewpoint for the bridge. No standalone article.

Fayette Station Road (truck only).entity: Fayette Station Road (CR 82) down into the gorge. No article of its own; the Tunney Hunsaker (Fayette Station) Bridge article states it carries Fayette Station Road over the New River, and the park article names Fayette Station as a park feature.

links.label: Wikipedia — New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

Fayetteville's small downtown.entity: The town of Fayetteville, West Virginia, adjacent to the park.

Long Point Trail.entity: The Long Point trail, named in the park article as a viewpoint for the New River Gorge Bridge. No standalone article.

links.label: Wikipedia — New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

Endless Wall Trail.entity: The Endless Wall climbing cliff and its trail. No Wikipedia article exists, and the park article never names Endless Wall — only climbing in general. Left bare rather than pointed at a park page that does not document it.

Drive Fayette Station Road in the truck.entity: Same Fayette Station Road, driven in the towed pickup.

links.label: Wikipedia — New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

Grandview Rim Trail.entity: The Grandview unit of the park, where the Rim Trail runs. The park article lists Grandview as a major feature with a seasonal visitor centre; the Rim Trail itself is not named anywhere. NOTE: 'Grandview, Raleigh County, West Virginia' is a separate unincorporated-community stub that says nothing about the gorge or its overlooks — rejected.

Kaymoor Miner's Trail.entity: The Kaymoor Miners Trail down to the abandoned Kay Moor mine; the Kay Moor article names the trail and its stairs and switchbacks explicitly.

Nuttallburg.entity: The abandoned coal town of Nuttallburg on the New River, with Henry Ford's conveyor.

links.label: Wikipedia — New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

offroad.name: Cunard river access road
offroad.season: Closed every November through March, from the Brooklyn Mine Trail parking lot down to the river; open April to October. NPS says this pattern continues through 2027.
offroad.note: This is the annual winter closure for road and drainage work, not weather. When open, NPS reports the lower sections are gravel and there are one-lane stretches that cause delays. The closure takes out vehicle, bike and pedestrian access to the Cunard river access, the angler's access and Brooklyn campground together. The park's closures page was last updated 6 Aug 2026 — check it again before the stop.

offroad.name: Fayette Station Road (CR 82)
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published
offroad.note: One-way, and the binding restriction is height not length: NPS states vehicles over 12 ft tall cannot complete the route because of the clearance under a railroad bridge, and does not recommend large vehicles, RVs or trailers on the hairpins. Allow 30–45 minutes without stops. The road passes under the New River Gorge Bridge three times.

offroad.name: Keeneys Creek Road down to Nuttallburg
offroad.distance: about 4 mi — NPS gives ~3.5 mi to the wayside exhibit and 0.5 mi more to the Nuttallburg parking area
offroad.note: NPS calls it narrow, winding and steep, part paved and part gravel, with much of it single lane so drivers have to pull off to let others by. Trailers, RVs and motorhomes are specifically advised against — limited parking and difficult to turn around at the bottom. Separate from the road, the Keeney's Creek Rail Trail is closed above the Conveyor Trail junction for flood damage.

offroad.name: WV 25 to Thurmond
offroad.distance: 7 mi from the Glen Jean exit off US 19
offroad.note: The NPS directions page gives the seven miles but publishes no surface or vehicle guidance for WV 25 — the 'narrow, winding, not recommended for RVs or trailers' description that circulates is not on an NPS page that could be opened here, so it is not recorded as fact. Worth knowing separately: the Rend Trail, which starts at Thurmond, is closed from both trailheads until roughly December 2027 per the park's road and trail closures page.

new-river-gorge-wv.dogs: New River Gorge is one of the most dog-open parks on the whole route — the NPS states plainly that leashed pets are allowed on every trail in the park.
new-river-gorge-wv.dogs_source_quote: Pets are allowed on all trails at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve.

trails.name: Glade Creek Trail to Kates Falls
trails.distance: 5.6 mi one-way (NPS); AllTrails indexes the falls out-and-back separately
trails.note: The flattest long walk in the park and the one thing this card had none of — an abandoned narrow-gauge coal railway grade running level along Glade Creek to Kate's Falls. Everything else on the card is a rim trail or a stair climb. Turn round wherever the light goes; it is out-and-back, so there is no committing to the full distance.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted — the NPS states leashed pets are allowed on every trail in New River Gorge. Already sourced at stop level; not re-derived.

other_links.label: NPS — Glade Creek Trail
other_links.note: Source of the 5.6 mi one-way length, the Moderate grade and the hiking-and-biking use: 'follows an abandoned narrow-gauge railroad along Glade Creek... an enjoyable stroll at a very moderate grade, popular with hikers of all ages and abilities'.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Kate's Falls via Glade Creek Trail
other_links.note: A second listing of the same walk under a reversed name. Its description confirms the rail grade and the 'gentle, flat stroll'.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails' result title for this listing carries the 4.6 star average but published no review count and no completion time on any of the pages that surfaced, so neither is recorded. The 5.6 mi and the Moderate grade are NPS's own figures, not AllTrails'.
needs: review count — AllTrails shows the 4.6 average but no count in any indexed result
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal per NPS and it is a former rail bed, which is the right shape for cruising with the dog in the carrier — but no source read here describes the SURFACE, and a rail grade can be anything from crushed limestone to loose ballast and washouts. Not called a cruise route on an assumption; this is the one to look at on the ground.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Six nights and five existing entries, but four of the five are rim-top viewpoint walks within a few miles of each other and the fifth is the Kaymoor stair descent. Nothing on the card was flat, long or riverside.

trails.name: Sandstone Falls Boardwalk
trails.note: Not a day's walk and not offered as one — it is a quarter-mile of accessible boardwalk over the braided channels of the largest waterfall on the New River, 1,500 ft across and dropping 10-25 ft. It anchors the southern end of the park, which this card ignored entirely: pair it with Grandview and Glade Creek and the drive down River Road makes one full day.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted — NPS states leashed pets are allowed on every trail in New River Gorge.

other_links.label: NPS — Sandstone Falls Boardwalk
other_links.note: 0.2 mi one-way, Easy, 'hiking and accessible'. Confirms the 1,500 ft span and the 10-25 ft drop.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Sandstone Falls Boardwalk and Island Loop Trail
other_links.note: The longer combination if the short boardwalk is not enough — same 4.6 average.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails result title reads '887 Reviews' while the snippet also shows a bracketed (586); the title figure is the one recorded, per the rule that the title string as displayed is the copy. Access is off River Road (WV-26), single lane in places with an unpaved lot — that is a truck drive, not a coach one, and December ice on a one-lane river road is the thing to check before setting out.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

Floyd Country Store Jamboree.entity: The Floyd Country Store's Friday Night Jamboree. The store has no article; the Floyd, Virginia article documents the Jamboree by name in its Arts and culture section.

Blue Ridge Parkway access (truck touring.entity: The Blue Ridge Parkway, which passes just south of Floyd.

Friday Night Jamboree at the Floyd Count.entity: Same Friday Night Jamboree, documented by name in the Floyd, Virginia article.

Rock Castle Gorge at Rocky Knob.entity: Rock Castle Gorge in the Rocky Knob Recreation Area at Parkway mileposts 167–174; the recreation-area article names the gorge and its National Recreation Trail.

Winery run along the Parkway.entity: The Blue Ridge Parkway itself, as the touring route. Linked for the road that is named; the Parkway article does not document wineries, so this is a link to the Parkway, not to the wineries.

Day trip to Roanoke.entity: The city of Roanoke, Virginia, the largest city on the Parkway.

trails.name: Buffalo Mountain Natural Area Preserve

other_links.label: AllTrails — preserve page
other_links.note: Area browse page for the preserve — a candidate for AREA_BROWSE_ALLTRAILS.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Buffalo Mountain Ridge Trail
other_links.note: Second listing, 116 reviews: an out-and-back through forest to the same summit.

other_links.label: The Outbound — Buffalo Mountain Loop
other_links.note: The summit is naturally treeless with 360-degree Blue Ridge views.

trails.stats_note: Our entry is the preserve, not a trail. The walk itself is the Buffalo Mountain Trail, which AllTrails describes as following the Oak and Barrens Loop Trail to the highest point in Floyd County; 409 reviews, no star rating or distance in any indexed snippet. Summit elevation 3,971 ft per third-party guides. No length published by Virginia DCR that could be sourced this pass.

floyd-va.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on all the Blue Ridge Parkway trails here; Buffalo Mountain Natural Area Preserve publishes no pet rule at all, so treat it as unknown until DCR Natural Heritage is phoned.
floyd-va.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are allowed on trails, but must be on a leash.

offroad.name: Buffalo Mountain Natural Area Preserve access road (Moles Road, VA 727)
offroad.distance: 0.9 mi of gravel · about 15 km southwest of the stop, at Willis
offroad.difficulty: "The narrow 0.9-mile gravel road to the parking area has multiple pull-offs to facilitate passing cars"
offroad.season: No closure published by DCR. It climbs to about 1,100 m on an exposed mountain and the stop is 12-17 Dec 2028, so ice is the real question, not a gate
offroad.note: Short, but it is the only unpaved route within half an hour of Floyd and it goes somewhere — up to the trailhead for the Buffalo Mountain summit, which is already on this stop's trails card. Turn onto Moles Road (VA 727) and follow the gravel access road to the parking area. Virginia DCR's own preserve page is the authority for the site but says nothing about the road surface; the surface description above is from Virginia Tourism's listing. DCR publishes no pet rule for the preserve either, which is already recorded on this stop as unknown.

offroad.name: Pond Lick Road
offroad.distance: 2.6 mi · about 52 km northwest of the stop, above Gatewood Reservoir near Pulaski
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "A few holes that might require a careful line and a couple of decent mud holes"; high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists Fall only. The stop is mid-December, which is past the window onX gives it — not a published closure, but the mud holes it warns about are exactly what a wet December makes worse
offroad.note: "This dirt track travels just north of Gatewood Reservoir. At just under 3 miles, it's a great quick run, or you can add to a route that includes some of the other local forest roads... unless there was a lot of rain, it shouldn't be an issue for any moderately four-wheel drive." Worth knowing why this box is thin: Floyd County has almost no public forest land. The Blue Ridge Parkway runs along the top of it and is paved; Rocky Knob is Parkway land; and the nearest Jefferson National Forest tracts are 50-70 km away in Pulaski, Montgomery and Giles counties. What Floyd does have is a dense network of VDOT-maintained unpaved secondary roads through farmland, mapped in VDOT's own Unpaved Roads layer, but no authority publishes any of them as a route.

offroad.name: Bailey Gap and Butt Mountain
offroad.distance: 13.6 mi · about 58 km north of the stop, in Giles County near Mountain Lake
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "Bailey Gap has several mud holes, some of which have soft bottoms. When in doubt, use the bypasses. Butt Mountain is simple and is almost totally gravel and dirt"
offroad.season: onX lists Winter as the best time — the only route found near Floyd for which December is the recommended season
offroad.note: The one real half-day drive from Floyd: thirteen and a half miles of Jefferson National Forest road behind Mountain Lake Lodge. "Both trails are beginner-friendly, with Butt Mountain being the easier of the two... Bailey Gap varies from gravel to rock, with several areas of water and mud. Most water pits have rocky bottoms and can easily be forded by a stock SUV. Some of them are mud though, and the mud is very soft." Take the bypasses rather than the mud. One thing that could not be sourced: the Forest Service publishes no gate dates for these roads anywhere reachable, and many Virginia national forest roads do close over winter — the Eastern Divide Ranger District is the call to make before driving an hour to a locked gate. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

Blowing Rock village.entity: The town of Blowing Rock, North Carolina.

Moses Cone Manor carriage roads — but ch.entity: Flat Top Manor and its carriage trails in Moses H. Cone Memorial Park; the park article names the manor and its 25 miles of carriage trails.

links.label: Wikipedia — Moses H. Cone Memorial Park

Ski at Beech or Sugar Mountain.entity: Beech Mountain (skiing and Beech Mountain Resort documented in the mountain article) and the village of Sugar Mountain, whose article places it next to Sugar Mountain Ski Area. Neither resort has its own article.

Blowing Rock and Tweetsie at Christmas.entity: The town of Blowing Rock and the Tweetsie Railroad theme park, which the town article names as a local attraction.

offroad.name: Brown Mountain OHV Trail System, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: 34 mi of designated trails
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April, along with Curtis Creek Campground, on the Grandfather Ranger District seasonal closure list (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/northcarolina/about-area/faqs/seasonal-closures)
offroad.note: This is a ticketed OHV trail system, not a forest-road drive — passes go through Recreation.gov. Before counting on it: the Forest Service page defines the ATV class here as under 60 inches wide and does not state anywhere that full-size 4WD trucks may use the system. The commonly repeated claim that Jeeps and 4WDs are limited to Trail 8 and part of Trail 1 is not on any Forest Service page that could be opened, so it is unverified. Call the Grandfather Ranger District before driving out.

offroad.name: Pisgah NF gravel roads around Edgemont and Mortimer
offroad.season: Mortimer Campground open 31 March to 31 October; the Grandfather Ranger District closure list gates the Mortimer area 1 November to the first weekend in April
offroad.note: The Forest Service confirms the campground and its position in the Wilson Creek Wild & Scenic corridor south of Grandfather Mountain, but publishes no road numbers, mileage or surface for the Edgemont loop. Neither Roseboro Road (FSR 981) nor Edgemont-Pinola Road (FSR 464) has a Forest Service page, so their condition is unsourced. Note this stop's route and the Wilson Creek entry below share the same road corridor from opposite ends.

offroad.name: Wilson Creek Gorge / Brown Mountain Beach Road, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: not published on the free listing
offroad.note: Trails Offroad classes it a Scout Route and shows 4/5 from 3 reviews; distance, difficulty and waypoints are behind the paywall. The listing places it in Adako, Caldwell County, running through the Wilson Creek Gorge past the Mortimer ghost town. The Forest Service's Wilson Creek Wild and Scenic River Area page confirms the area is open all year but says nothing at all about the road.

trails.name: Grandfather Trail (to Calloway Peak)
trails.official_length: 2.4 mi one-way from the Top Shop parking area

alltrails.name: Grandfather Trail to Calloway Peak (Watauga Viewpoint)

other_links.label: Grandfather Mountain (operator)
other_links.note: 'The route follows the crest of Grandfather Mountain from the Top Shop Parking Area out 2.4 miles to Calloway Peak.' Access is through the paid Grandfather Mountain attraction gate — reviewers confirm you pay to start here.

other_links.label: Grandfather Mountain — Profile Trail
other_links.note: The free alternative: the Profile Trail from the state park side ends at Calloway Gap (5,675 ft) at the Grandfather Trail junction. AllTrails also lists Calloway Peak via Profile Trail separately.

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Graded 'expert'. The Grandfather Trail crest route uses ladders and cables — this is not a stroll, and it is the one trail on this card a dog should not be taken up.

trails.stats_note: 4.4 mi / 1,538 ft is AllTrails' GPS round trip; the operator publishes 2.4 mi one-way. AllTrails does not surface a difficulty grade in the indexed snippet — Komoot grades it expert.

trails.name: Price Lake Loop Trail (Julian Price Park)

other_links.label: NPS — Julian Price Park hiking trails
other_links.note: 'This easy 2.7-mile loop circles the shoreline of 47-acre Price Lake.' Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 297.

other_links.label: Explore Boone
other_links.note: Family hike around the Parkway's largest lake; boat rental at the campground.

trails.stats_note: 2.7 mi is the NPS published length; National Park Planner quotes 2.3 mi for the same loop. AllTrails carries 1,550 reviews and grades it easy but surfaced neither a distance nor a star rating. Slug has a -2 suffix.

trails.name: Boone Fork Trail
trails.season: Trailhead is the Price Park picnic area on the Parkway at about MP 296.5. The Blue Ridge Parkway's winter closures are weather-driven gate closures rather than fixed dates — NPS gates sections when they ice and reopens them when they clear, and its own winter-recreation page states you may walk in behind a closed gate. So this is walkable in the 17-23 Dec window; what is not guaranteed is driving to the trailhead. Check nps.gov/blri/planyourvisit/roadclosures.htm the morning of.
trails.note: The best full-day walk near Blowing Rock and the one shape this card was missing — a real loop with a creek, Hebron Falls, meadow, rhododendron tunnel and a boulder-and-ladder section, rather than another rim viewpoint. Most people walk it counter-clockwise; the first mile to Hebron Falls carries most of the traffic and the middle two miles are empty.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Blue Ridge Parkway rule, the same authority already sourced on this card for Moses Cone, Julian Price and Beacon Heights.

other_links.label: Explore Boone — Boone Fork Trail
other_links.note: The county visitor bureau gives the loop as 5.5 miles against AllTrails' 5.1 — the usual GPS-versus-signed discrepancy, recorded rather than reconciled.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Boone Fork Trail Loop via Tanawha Trail
other_links.note: 4.6 from 239 reviews. A longer user-assembled version that joins the Tanawha Trail already on this card. Its description carries the warning worth having: 'giant boulders, stairways, and ladders... can be slippery or muddy'.

trails.stats_note: Distance, time, grade, rating and count are from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. The ladder-and-boulder section is the part to think about in late December; wet rock and ice are the same hazard on a moderate trail as on a hard one.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Six nights, and of the five entries already on the card two are lake loops on the same estate pair, one is a 0.2 mi viewpoint spur, and the Grandfather Trail to Calloway Peak is the cables-and-ladders route on the ridge — which in the 17-23 Dec window is an ice question, not a fitness one. There was no ordinary all-day walk on it.

trails.name: Erwins View Trail (Linville Falls)
trails.distance: 1.8 mi out-and-back (NPS signs it 1.6 mi round trip)
trails.season: Reached from the Linville Falls Visitor Center at the end of the spur road off the Parkway at MP 316.4, about 35 miles south of Boone. Same weather-driven Parkway gate situation as Boone Fork — the trail does not close, the road to it might. Winter is arguably the better time to see it: bare trees open the gorge views that summer foliage hides.
trails.note: The biggest waterfall on the Blue Ridge Parkway, and the card had no waterfall at all. Four separate overlooks on one short walk — the first is half a mile in, so it pays out even if the weather turns. Gentle grades with stone steps near the last overlook.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Blue Ridge Parkway rule, the authority that manages Linville Falls.

other_links.label: NPS — Linville Falls Hiking Trails
other_links.note: 'A moderate 1.6 mile round-trip walk, offering hikers four overlooks... The first overlook is 0.5 miles from the visitor center.' Also the source for the fact that the Linville Falls trails as a group run moderate to strenuous.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Linville Falls Trail
other_links.note: 4.6 from 1,358 reviews — the shorter north-side line to the Upper Falls observation area. Fewer reviews and a lower average than Erwins View, so Erwins View is the one carried.

other_links.label: National Park Planner — Erwins View Trail (MP 316.4)
other_links.note: Gives 2.25 mi round trip including all the overlook spurs, and 1.5 hours — the realistic figure if every overlook is walked.

trails.stats_note: Three lengths are published for the same walk and all three are recorded rather than averaged: AllTrails 1.8 mi, NPS 1.6 mi signed, National Park Planner 2.25 mi with every spur. AllTrails' gain, time, rating and count are from its result title and snippet as displayed.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

boone-nc.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on the Blue Ridge Parkway trails at Moses Cone, Julian Price and Beacon Heights, and Grandfather Mountain State Park permits them too — though the park itself warns the Grandfather Trail's ladders and cables are not suitable for animals.
boone-nc.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are allowed on trails, but must be on a leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: NC-105 (Boone toward Foscoe/Grandfather Mountain entrance)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 19 miles Boone to the Grandfather Mountain entrance
scenicDrives_patch.note: Grandfather Mountain's own directions page: "Take NC 105 South to Linville. Turn left at the stoplight and take US 221 North 2 miles to the entrance of Grandfather Mountain." Worth carrying: the entrance is on US 221, not on NC 105 — NC 105 is the Boone-Foscoe-Linville leg and you turn off it at Linville. No published winter closure for the approach; the page carries no seasonal statement at all, so ice on the 4,000 ft section is an unsourced unknown rather than a documented closure.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-321 (Boone to Blowing Rock)
scenicDrives_patch.note: High Country Press's scenic-drives roundup lists "Blowing Rock to Boone via US 321 & US 221 — Connecting two of the High Country's most popular towns, this route passes Glen Burney Trail". Listing confirmed from the search result's own title and snippet; the page itself answered HTTP 429 when fetched, so nothing beyond the snippet is recorded. Explore Boone's own five-scenic-drives article does NOT list US-321 or NC-105 — its five are the Blue Ridge Parkway, Doc & Merle Watson Highway (8 mi), Mission Crossing (17 mi), Little Parkway (18 mi), New River Valley Byway (32 mi) and the High Country Road Trip Loop (50 mi), which is the better menu if a designated route is wanted.

Downtown Asheville.entity: Downtown Asheville, listed as the Downtown Asheville Historic District.

Walk out of camp into Bent Creek.entity: Bent Creek and its Lake Powhatan recreation area south of Asheville — the campground the stop uses. Lake Powhatan and Bent Creek Experimental Forest have no articles; the Bent Creek article documents both.

Craggy Gardens and Craggy Pinnacle.entity: Craggy Gardens and the Craggy Pinnacle overlook trail on the Parkway. Neither has a standalone article; the Great Craggy Mountains article documents both by name with the milepost.

Pisgah Ranger District waterfalls on US.entity: The waterfalls along US 276 in the Pisgah Ranger District — Looking Glass Falls being the best known. The ranger district has no article; the forest article has a Waterfalls section and the US 276 article covers the Brevard–Waynesville run through Pisgah.

Downtown Asheville and the Grove Park gi.entity: Downtown Asheville and the Omni Grove Park Inn, whose article documents the National Gingerbread House Competition held there each November–December.

links.label: Wikipedia — The Omni Grove Park Inn

offroad.name: Bent Creek gravel road network, from camp
offroad.note: Worth checking before planning a drive here. The Forest Service research station — this is an experimental forest, roughly 6,000 acres, the oldest federal one east of the Mississippi — permits hiking, biking and horseback riding on designated trails, and describes the gravel roads themselves as open to bicycles, horses and hikers. It nowhere says the road network is open to private motor vehicles, and it asks that research study sites not be disturbed. Treat this as a bike-and-walk network from camp unless the Pisgah Ranger District says otherwise.

offroad.name: Curtis Creek Road (FR 482), Old Fort
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April (Grandfather Ranger District), together with Curtis Creek Campground
offroad.note: The Forest Service closure list writes this road as FR 428, not FR 482 as the card has it. One of the two numbers is wrong and it is worth settling with the Grandfather Ranger District rather than discovering it at a junction. No Forest Service page publishes the road's length or surface. Separately, this whole district was closed after Hurricane Helene and has been reopening in stages, so confirm current status close to the date.

offroad.name: FR 475 past the Davidson River fish hatchery toward Gloucester Gap
offroad.note: The forest's live Helene status page is the right authority here, but FS 475 is not named on it — only Yellow Gap Road is. Forest Service news coverage that could not be opened directly reports FS 475 open from US 276 to Cove Creek Group Campground and closed from there to the Daniel Ridge trailhead for a bridge replacement; that is not recorded as fact. This road is the one that reaches Gloucester Gap at the FS 471 junction, so a closed middle section breaks the through route. Call the Pisgah Ranger District.

offroad.name: Yellow Gap Road (FR 1206), Pisgah Ranger District
offroad.note: Currently not a through route. The Forest Service Helene status page has FR 1206 open from US 276 near the Cradle of Forestry as far as Wolf Ford Horse Camp, and closed from Wolf Ford Horse Camp to North Mills River Campground — so it is an out-and-back from the 276 end, not the Brevard-to-Mills River link. No length is published by the Forest Service.

asheville-nc-v3.dogs: All four are dog-legal on a leash — Triple Falls and Hooker Falls under the NC Forest Service in DuPont, Bearwallow under Conserving Carolina, and Mount Pisgah under the Blue Ridge Parkway.
asheville-nc-v3.dogs_source_quote: Your dog may be friendly, but other dogs may not be. Protect your dog by keeping it on a leash.

trails.name: Catawba Falls River Trail
trails.season: Low elevation at Old Fort, roughly 30 minutes east of Asheville on I-40 — reachable when the Blue Ridge Parkway is gated for ice, which in the 23-30 Dec window is the deciding factor for half this card. Open all year per the Rutherford Outdoor Coalition. Two things to verify nearer the time: the trail was rebuilt with a new stairway to the upper falls, and Hurricane Helene in Sep 2024 hit the Old Fort side of Pisgah hard, so Grandfather Ranger District closures have been rolling.
trails.note: The biggest-name hike within an hour of Asheville that was not on this card — 7,631 reviews, more than any other trail on the stop. A wide gravel path along the Catawba headwaters past the 1920s hydro dam ruins, then a narrower climb in the last half mile to the 100 ft falls.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash. Managing authority is the US Forest Service, National Forests in North Carolina (Grandfather Ranger District). The Forest Service's own Catawba Falls page publishes no trail-specific pet rule, so this rests on the standing national-forest rule that leashed pets are allowed on NF trails, not on a sentence naming this trail. Recorded as true with that caveat stated.

other_links.label: MyHikes — Catawba Falls Trail
other_links.note: Gives 2.9 mi against AllTrails' 2.2, and describes the new stair system to the upper falls.

trails.stats_note: Distance, gain, time, grade and star are from the AllTrails result snippet as displayed; the 7,631 count is from its result title. Published lengths for this walk range 2.2-2.9 mi depending on whether the upper-falls stairs are included — all recorded, none averaged.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Seven nights and only four entries, two of which (Triple Falls, Hooker Falls) are the same afternoon in DuPont State Forest and one of which (Mount Pisgah, 5,721 ft, Parkway MP 407) is the single most gate-prone trailhead on the card in Christmas week.

trails.name: Explorer Loop (Bent Creek)
trails.season: Bent Creek Experimental Forest sits low behind the NC Arboretum, fifteen minutes from downtown Asheville on NC-191, with its own road access that does not depend on the Parkway. Walkable in any weather this stop will produce.
trails.note: The card had no ordinary walk-from-camp — everything on it was a drive to a waterfall or a summit. Bent Creek is Asheville's own forest: gravel roads and old logging grades around Lake Powhatan, easy to shorten or lengthen, and the obvious place to go on a grey Christmas-week afternoon when the Parkway is shut.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — US Forest Service, Pisgah National Forest. Same caveat as Catawba Falls: this is the standing national-forest rule, not a trail-specific statement.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Bent Creek Trail, Bent Creek Gap Rd, and Explorer Loop via NC Arboretum
other_links.note: The 6.8 mi / 462 ft / 2.5-3 hr version starting from the Arboretum, 4.6 from 198 reviews. Useful because it shows how freely this network recombines.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Explorer Loop
other_links.note: Listed as a multi-use trail in the Bent Creek Experimental Forest network — the source for the bike use here.

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed.
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal and much of Bent Creek is gravel road, which is the right surface — but the Explorer Loop specifically is singletrack shared with mountain bikers and Trailforks catalogues it inside an MTB network. The cruise route here is Bent Creek Gap Road itself, not this loop. Recorded as not-a-cruise so the biking view does not inherit a trail that riders treat as MTB.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

Deep Creek trails.entity: The Deep Creek area of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Deep Creek has no article of its own; the park article names it as one of the park's major valleys and most accessible areas.

links.label: Wikipedia — Great Smoky Mountains National Park

Deep Creek waterfalls, two miles from to.entity: The Deep Creek falls (Tom Branch, Indian Creek, Juney Whank) just outside Bryson City. None have articles; the park article covers the Deep Creek valley and its streams and waterfalls, and names Bryson City as an adjacent town.

links.label: Wikipedia — Great Smoky Mountains National Park

Kuwohi road is gated — walk it instead.entity: Kuwohi, the peak formerly named Clingmans Dome, and its paved summit road off Newfound Gap Road (the article documents the road; the winter gate closure is not in it).

The Road to Nowhere.entity: Lakeview Drive, the unfinished North Shore Road out of Bryson City. The article's first line gives 'Road to Nowhere' as its alternative name. NOTE: the bare title 'Road to Nowhere' resolves to the Talking Heads song — rejected.

bryson-city-nc.authority: National Park Service — Great Smoky Mountains
bryson-city-nc.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails, with exactly two exceptions: the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail. Leash 6 ft on those. None of the Deep Creek trails on this card qualify, so the dog stays at camp or walks the Oconaluftee River Trail, which starts on the Cherokee side. NPS actively discourages bringing pets because most trails are off limits to them.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_exception: Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail only.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_note: Oconaluftee is the accessible one from this side — the Bryson City stop already names the Oconaluftee Visitor Center in its highlights, so the dog-legal walk is the one you were going to anyway.

offroad.name: Cove Creek Road / Old NC 284 into Cataloochee
offroad.season: The park's seasonal road schedule lists Cataloochee Road as open year round, two-lane gravel, subject to weather closures. Old NC 284 has no fixed dates — the park closes it in severe weather or heavy rain.
offroad.note: NPS describes Cove Creek as a winding gravel road with steep drop-offs and no guardrails, narrow enough that drivers may have to stop or back up to pass. Old NC 284, the back way in from Big Creek, is also winding gravel. Post-Helene the Cataloochee entrance road was open to vehicles only as far as Beech Grove School with the upper section closed — from the park's reopening release, https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-to-reopen-portions-of-cataloochee-on-april-4.htm. Confirm before the drive.

offroad.name: Heintooga Ridge Road / Heintooga Round Bottom Road
offroad.season: Heintooga Ridge Road 15 May – 31 Oct. Heintooga Round Bottom Road: opening date TBD, as is Straight Fork Road, both still recovering from Hurricane Helene.
offroad.note: Two different roads under one name and only the first half is confirmed. Heintooga Ridge Road is paved and two-way, and motorhomes, buses and vans longer than 25 ft are prohibited — the towed pickup is fine. The Round Bottom (Balsam Mountain) half, the one-way gravel descent toward Cherokee that makes this a through route rather than a dead end, had no published opening date when checked. Do not plan the loop until the park posts a date.

offroad.name: Parson Branch Road
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: 1 May – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way gravel leaving Cades Cove — you exit at US 129 and cannot come back the way you came. NPS recommends high clearance and restricts large vehicles. It reopened in 2022 after a six-year closure for hazard trees, and the park still closes it for high water, so it is the least dependable of the four here.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain Road
offroad.season: 10 Apr – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way out of Cades Cove toward Townsend, with the park's standard restriction on these roads — no motorhomes, buses, or vans longer than 25 ft, and no passenger vehicles towing trailers. The schedule publishes no length. Same one-way trap as Parson Branch: it is a way out of the cove, not a there-and-back.

trails.name: Noland Divide Trail

other_links.label: HikingProject
other_links.note: 'Long and steep, with the greatest net gain in elevation of any trail in the Smokies.'

other_links.label: Smokies 900
other_links.note: Elevation profile and GPX for the full trail.

other_links.label: Explore Bryson City
other_links.note: Trailhead is by the Deep Creek entrance, a short drive from downtown Bryson City.

trails.stats_note: Distance and gain are from third-party trail guides (11.3–11.6 mi one-way, 4,689–4,750 ft), not from AllTrails, which surfaced no figures for the base listing — only for the much longer 18.3 mi and 34.9 mi loops built on top of it. As a one-way ridge climb this is a shuttle or a turnaround, not a loop.

trails.name: Oconaluftee River Trail
trails.official_length: 3 miles (4.8 km) roundtrip (NPS); 1.5 mi one way (TrailLink)
trails.cruise_reason: NPS describes it as "relatively flat, wide, and graveled" and calls it bicycle friendly and wheelchair friendly; TrailLink lists bike and walking as the permitted uses and calls it "mostly flat and easy" with "a few small hills". Rail-flat river-grade gravel, bike-legal per the authority, no walk-your-bike section and no puncture-hazard reports found. The one caveat, in NPS's own words, is "occasional obstacles of roots and rocks" — texture, not dismount zones. At 1.5 mi one way it is a short spin rather than a ride, but it is a legal one with the dog in the carrier, which is rare.
trails.season: Low elevation near the Cherokee entrance and open year-round — the walk that survives a 30 Dec 2028-6 Jan 2029 winter stay
trails.note: ONE OF ONLY TWO TRAILS IN THE ENTIRE GREAT SMOKY MOUNTAINS THAT PERMIT PETS, and the practical one from this stop. NPS: "The Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail are the only two park trails where pets are permitted"; leash no longer than 6 feet at all times, pets also allowed in campgrounds, picnic areas and on roads. THIS IS THE DOG'S WALK FOR THE WHOLE WEEK — every Deep Creek trail on this card is closed to it. It starts on the Cherokee side, which is this side: park at the Oconaluftee Visitor Center and walk past the Mountain Farm Museum to the trailhead. That is the visitor center the stop already names in its highlights, and the Cherokee/Great Smokies KOA is on the same side of the park, so this needs no crossing of the mountain and no dependence on Newfound Gap Road staying open. Follows the Oconaluftee River through elk habitat to the outskirts of Cherokee — expect elk, and keep the leash short around them. Gravel, flat, wide, and NPS lists it as wheelchair and bicycle friendly.
trails.note_source: NPS Great Smoky Mountains pets page (nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/pets.htm), fetched: the two permitted trails are "the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail", pets "must be kept on a leash no longer than 6 feet at all times", "Pets are welcome in campgrounds, picnic areas, and along roads", never left unattended in vehicles or RVs. NPS trail page (nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-the-oconaluftee-river-trail.htm), fetched: "3 miles (4.8 km) roundtrip", "relatively flat, wide, and graveled", "occasional obstacles of roots and rocks", bicycle friendly and wheelchair friendly, "Pets are allowed on this trail but must be on a leash", "Park at the Oconaluftee Visitor Center and walk from the visitor center parking to the Mountain Farm Museum to find the Oconaluftee River Trailhead." TrailLink (traillink.com/trail/oconaluftee-river-trail/), fetched: 1.5 miles, dirt, bike and walking, "one of two in the Smokey Mountains National Park that allows bicycles and dogs", endpoints "Oconaluftee Visitor Center and outskirts of the city of Cherokee, NC", elk and deer. AllTrails result snippet, verbatim: "5.1-km out-and-back trail near Cherokee, North Carolina. Generally considered an easy route, it takes an average of 57 min to complete", 2,917 reviews from the result title; no star and no elevation gain surfaced in any snippet.
trails.stats_note: NPS 3 mi roundtrip, AllTrails 5.1 km (3.2 mi) out-and-back and TrailLink 1.5 mi one way are all the same trail measured from the same visitor-center end. The authority's 3 mi roundtrip is the primary figure.
trails.url_note: Two AllTrails hits, one carrying a ?sh= tracking parameter and one an /en-gb/ locale segment. Only the tracking parameter and the locale segment were removed, to match the form every other url in this db uses; the slug itself is the one the search returned and was not assembled from the trail's name.

trails.name: Gatlinburg Trail
trails.official_length: approximately 4 miles (6.4 km) roundtrip (NPS); 1.9 mi one way
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal per NPS, but the surface is mixed rather than rail-grade — NPS lists "sections of paved road, crushed stone, roots, and uneven dirt" and "a few steep sections plus occasional roots and rocks". That is not gravel cruising with a dog in a carrier. The Oconaluftee, on this side of the mountain, is the one that is.
trails.season: REACHING IT IS THE PROBLEM ON THESE DATES — it is on the Tennessee side and the only way there from Bryson City is Newfound Gap Road (US 441) over the crest of the Smokies. NPS: primary roads including Newfound Gap Road are "open year-round, weather permitting", and weather is exactly what a 30 Dec 2028-6 Jan 2029 stay is betting against; the road is routinely shut for snow and ice in late December and January
trails.note: THE OTHER OF THE PARK'S TWO PET-LEGAL TRAILS — and not a realistic day from this stop. Same rule, same six-foot leash: NPS names only the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail. It runs from behind the Sugarlands Visitor Center to River Road in Gatlinburg, along the Little Pigeon River. THE DISTANCE IS THE POINT: Sugarlands is on the Tennessee side, and NPS's own mileposts put roughly 30 road miles between the two visitor centers (Deep Creek Valley Overlook is "almost 14 miles north from Oconaluftee Visitor Center or almost 16 miles south from Sugarlands Visitor Center") — with the run from Bryson City out to the Oconaluftee entrance on top of that, and the whole of it over Newfound Gap at 5,046 ft. Call it an hour each way in good conditions and a road that may simply be closed in the first week of January. Listed so the card carries both of the park's pet-legal trails and says which is which, not as a suggestion: the Oconaluftee is the walk, this is the one you would do if you were spending the day in Gatlinburg anyway.
trails.note_source: NPS Gatlinburg Trail page (nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-the-gatlinburg-trail.htm), fetched: "Approximately 4 miles (6.4 km) roundtrip", "a leisurely path that is mostly flat and wide" with "a few steep sections plus occasional roots and rocks", surface "sections of paved road, crushed stone, roots, and uneven dirt", "Park at the Sugarlands Visitor Center and walk behind the building, past the restrooms, and past the brick headquarters building to the Gatlinburg Trailhead", and verbatim: "The Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail are the only two park trails where pets are permitted." AllTrails result snippet: 3.9 mi out-and-back, 180 ft gain, 1-1.5 hr, 6,695 reviews from the result title; no star surfaced. Difficulty "Easy" is gatlinburg.com's published grade (which also lists "Dogs on Leash" and "Biking" among the trail's features, 1.9 mi one way, 164 ft gain); NPS publishes no difficulty word. Visitor-center-to-visitor-center mileage derived from the NPS Deep Creek Valley Overlook place page (nps.gov/places/deep-creek-valley-overlook.htm), fetched, verbatim: "Travel almost 14 miles north from Oconaluftee Visitor Center or almost 16 miles south from Sugarlands Visitor Center." Road season from NPS seasonal road closures (nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm), fetched, verbatim: "Primary roads such as Newfound Gap Road (US 441), Little River Road, and the Cades Cove Loop Road are open year-round, weather permitting." Winter closures of that road are frequent and well documented in local reporting (WVLT 2 Dec 2025: Newfound Gap Road slated to close for winter weather; Knox News 23 Jan 2026: most park roads closed in an ice storm) — no specific 2028-29 closure is asserted, only that the risk is real on these dates.
trails.stats_note: AllTrails 3.9 mi and NPS ~4 mi roundtrip are the same walk; gatlinburg.com's 1.9 mi one way is the same figure halved. Gain is published as 180 ft by AllTrails and 164 ft by gatlinburg.com; the AllTrails figure is recorded, the difference is noise.

trails.name: Tsali Mouse Branch Loop and Mouse Overlook
trails.season: The Forest Service states the Tsali Recreation Area itself is open year round (the campground inside it runs 15 Apr - 31 Oct only, which does not affect day use). Low, lakeside and outside the national park, so it is not exposed to the crest-line weather that shuts the Smokies roads. Usable across the whole 30 Dec - 6 Jan window.
trails.note: This is the answer to the problem that defines this stop. Great Smoky permits dogs on exactly two trails in the entire park, and both are already on this card — so for seven nights the dog has two walks. Tsali is twenty minutes away in the Nantahala National Forest, where the dog is legal, and it is a genuinely good place in its own right: rolling smooth singletrack on the ridges above Fontana Lake with an overlook worth the walk.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash. Managing authority is the US Forest Service, Nantahala National Forest (Cheoah Ranger District). The Forest Service's Tsali page publishes no trail-specific pet rule, so this rests on the standing national-forest rule, not a sentence naming these loops. AllTrails' own claim that 'Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash' on the sister listing was NOT used as the source.

other_links.label: Explore Bryson City — Tsali Mouse Branch Loop
other_links.note: Gives the loop as 6.5-9 miles with 700-900 ft of gain depending on which connectors are used — which is why AllTrails' 8.6 mi should be read as one line through the network, not a fixed distance.

other_links.label: MTB Project — Tsali Mouse Branch and Thompson Loops
other_links.note: The alternating-use schedule, which is the thing to know before driving out: bikes get Left and Right Loop on Sun/Mon/Wed/Fri and Mouse Branch and Thompson on Tue/Thu/Sat; horses take the other days. Walkers are not restricted, but sharing with horses is a different day out from sharing with bikes.

trails.stats_note: Distance, gain, star and count from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. No completion time was published. The horse use is from the Forest Service's own description of the area; the bike use from AllTrails, MTB Project and Trailforks together.
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal on the published rotation days, but this is purpose-built mountain-bike singletrack — Bike the Sites and MTB Project both catalogue it as an MTB trail, and 875 ft of rolling climb over 8.6 mi is not cruising with a dog in a carrier. Stays in the trails box with a bike badge and out of the biking view.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. This is the sharpest dog case on the whole east extension: seven nights at a stop whose managing authority permits pets on TWO trails park-wide, both already listed. Everything else on the card — Deep Creek, Juney Whank, Noland Divide — is closed to the dog, and the Gatlinburg Trail is on the far side of the crest.

trails.name: Mingo Falls Trail
trails.difficulty: Easy walk, moderate for the stairs
trails.season: On the Qualla Boundary at Cherokee, roughly 1,900 ft — low enough that the 30 Dec - 6 Jan window is a matter of ice on the wooden steps rather than access. No published seasonal closure found.
trails.note: A 120 ft waterfall, one of the tallest in the southern Appalachians, at the top of about 160 wooden steps and nothing else — fifteen minutes of climbing for a payout most day hikes do not match. It is NOT in the national park: it is on the Cherokee Indian Reservation, which is why it does not carry the park's pet ban, and no permit is needed to visit.
trails.note_source: DOG RULE NOT ESTABLISHED. The managing authority is the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, not the National Park Service, so Great Smoky's two-trail pet ban does not apply here — but no EBCI published rule for Mingo Falls was found, and the point of this entry is that it might be the dog's third walk. Recorded as unknown rather than assumed. Worth a call before relying on it.

other_links.label: NC Tripping — Mingo Falls, Cherokee
other_links.note: 0.4 mi and about 160 stairs; 'Mingo' means 'Big Bear' in Cherokee.

trails.stats_note: 0.3 mi / 114 ft / 0.5-1 hr / 4.7 / 2,630 from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. Secondary guides give 0.4 mi and 98-114 ft — the difference is where the count starts at the car park. AllTrails also indexes this under an /en-gb/ locale path with a slightly different count (2,628); the canonical /trail/ path is the one recorded.

trails.name: Kuwohi (Clingmans Dome) Observation Tower Trail
trails.difficulty: Short but steep — the paving misleads
trails.season: CLOSED FOR THIS STOP. Kuwohi Road (formerly Clingmans Dome Road) is closed to vehicles 1 December through 31 March every year, and this stop is 30 Dec - 6 Jan. The summit and the tower stay open — but with the road shut the walk in is 14 to 16 miles round trip in winter conditions, which is a different proposition entirely and not one for this trip. NPS's seasonal road schedule is at https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm
trails.note: Listed precisely BECAUSE it is shut. It is the highest point in the Smokies at 6,643 ft, the highest in Tennessee, and the single most obvious thing a visitor plans a Bryson City week around — and for these dates it cannot be driven to. Better on the card with the reason than absent and rediscovered at a locked gate. The dog could not go anyway: this is inside the national park, which permits pets on two trails and this is not one of them.
trails.note_source: Dogs PROHIBITED — Great Smoky Mountains National Park permits pets on exactly two trails park-wide, the Oconaluftee River Trail and the Gatlinburg Trail. Already sourced at stop level.

other_links.label: NPS — Seasonal Road Schedule, Great Smoky Mountains
other_links.note: Also the source for the OTHER half of this stop's road question: Newfound Gap Road (US 441) is 'open year-round, weather permitting' — a fixed closure it is not, but high-elevation ice shuts it repeatedly through the winter, and that is the road between camp and the Gatlinburg Trail, which is one of the dog's only two legal walks here.

other_links.label: Explore Bryson City — Kuwohi Road
other_links.note: 'The road to Kuwohi is closed each winter, December 1 thru March 31, although you can still use the road as a hiking trail.'

trails.stats_note: 1.0 mi paved with 337 ft of gain is Tripadvisor's figure, corroborated by every guide read as 'a half-mile each way, steep'. No AllTrails listing surfaced under either Clingmans Dome or Kuwohi, so no trail link is carried and none was constructed.

scenicDrives_patch.note: Tennessee River Valley Geotourism lists this under "Scenic Byways or Routes, Scenic Route" as the Lookout Mountain Scenic Parkway, with directions "take S. Broad Street from downtown Chattanooga to community of St. Elmo, following the signs to Rock City; take Ochs Hwy. up Lookout Mountain". The entry page loaded but rendered only navigation and its category labels, so the route text is recorded from the search result snippet. At the top, Point Park is the NPS unit — admission $10 per adult, ages 16 and over (nps.gov/chch). The NPS page's Directions and Hours & Seasons sections did not populate on fetch, so no winter hours are recorded.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Suck Creek Road / TN-27 along the Tennessee River Gorge
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Prentice Cooper State Forest is 26,945 acres, roughly 10 miles west of Chattanooga
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASON CONFLICT — the forest's interior roads are closed annually Dec. 20 to March 15; the stop arrives 6 Jan 2029, inside that window.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Tennessee Division of Forestry, the managing authority: "State Highway 27 (Suck Creek Road)" divides Prentice Cooper State Forest. TN-27 itself is a state highway and stays open, but the drive-out-to-the-overlooks part does not — "The following roads are closed annually from Dec. 20 to March 15...Tower Drive past Pot Point Gate, All side roads, Haley Road". Separately, during scheduled big game hunts "the area west of State Highway 27 (Suck Creek Road) is closed to all visitors except licensed hunters", with the area east (Edwards Point) staying open. Turkey-nesting closures through July 14 affect Persimmon Road, all roads past Pot Point Gate on Tower Drive, Inman Point, Long Point and Elder Point Roads. On a 6 Jan arrival this is a highway drive along the gorge plus Edwards Point, not a forest-road day.

Sunset Trail.entity: The park's 10-mile Sunset Trail. No Wikipedia article, and the Hot Springs National Park article never uses the word 'Sunset' — it says only that there are 'numerous hiking trails'. Left bare rather than linked to a park page that does not document it.
