trails.name: Falls Branch Trail (Lake Catherine State Park)
trails.distance: 2 mi loop (Hiking Project 1.7 mi, Arklahoma Hiker 1.6 mi semi-loop)
trails.season: The waterfall on Falls Creek is SEASONAL — it runs on rainfall, not all year. The stop is 11-18 Jan 2029, and January is one of Arkansas's wetter months, so these dates fall in the good half of the year for it rather than the bad. No closure; the park and trail are open.
trails.note: The best-reviewed walk within half an hour of Hot Springs by a wide margin — 4,479 reviews against 801 for the park's own Gulpha Gorge — and the card had nothing outside the national park at all. A National Recreation Trail through pine and hardwood, crossing Little Canyon Creek several times to a 10 ft waterfall, then back along the Ouachita River.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks permit pets throughout their parks, the same authority already sourced on the Petit Jean and Mount Magazine cards. Lake Catherine is an Arkansas state park, not part of the national park.

other_links.label: Arkansas.com — Falls Branch Trail (National Recreation Trail)
Arklahoma Hiker — Lake Catherine: Falls Branch Trail + Falls Creek Falls

trails.name: Gulpha Gorge Trail
trails.season: Open year round; no published seasonal restriction. Mid-January in the Ouachitas is walkable — the risk is a wet creek crossing, not snow.
trails.note: The park's other side. Everything already on this card climbs the two hills directly behind Bathhouse Row; Gulpha Gorge runs up the creek from the park's own campground on the east flank and links into the Sunset Trail, so it can be walked as a short out-and-back or used as a way onto the long trail from a different start.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted — Hot Springs National Park states dogs are welcome on all 26 miles of its trails. Already sourced at stop level.
trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. The /en-gb/ locale copy of the same page reports 750 reviews against the US page's 801 — the US figure is recorded.

trails.name: Grand Promenade
trails.season: AllTrails records it as open year-round. This is the walk for a January evening or a wet afternoon — brick underfoot, level, lit, and in town.
trails.note: Not a hike, and included deliberately: a landscaped brick promenade on the terrace above Bathhouse Row, threading the historic springs and their markers. It is the one walk on this card that can be done in an hour after dark with the dog, in a week where the other five all need daylight and a drive. Take care near the springs themselves — the water is hot enough to scald.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted — Hot Springs National Park states dogs are welcome on all 26 miles of its trails; only the federal buildings on Bathhouse Row are closed to them, which matters here because the promenade runs directly behind them.

Seven Hollows Trail.entity: The Seven Hollows Trail at Petit Jean. No article, and the state-park article never uses the word 'Hollows'. Left bare.

Rock House Cave Trail.entity: Rock House Cave, listed in the park article among Petit Jean's geological and archaeological features.

Bear Cave Trail.entity: Bear Cave, listed in the park article alongside Rock House Cave, the Grotto and Turtle Rocks.

Museum of Automobiles.entity: The Museum of Automobiles at Winrock, adjacent to Petit Jean State Park.

Mount Nebo day trip in the truck.entity: Mount Nebo near Dardanelle and the state park atop it, both covered in the mountain article.

trails.name: Cedar Falls Trail
trails.was: Rock House Cave / Bear Cave Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: Arkansas' most photographed place: from Mather Lodge steeply down Cedar Creek Canyon to the 95 ft falls. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Logs it as 2 mi out-and-back starting behind Mather Lodge.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails describes it as one of Arkansas' most photographed places: from Mather Lodge it drops steeply into Cedar Creek Canyon to a 95 ft waterfall. Distance/gain are AllTrails GPS; no AllTrails difficulty grade surfaced, and the descent-then-reclimb makes third-party grades range from moderate to strenuous — do not read 'easy' into the absence.

trails.name: Rock House Cave / Bear Cave Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Petit Jean Rock House Cave Trail
other_links.note: The other half of our entry: a short, easy trail to Rock House Cave, a large rock shelter, and the Turtle Rocks.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Rock House Cave and Lookout Trail
other_links.note: Longer variant taking in the lookout.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Bear Cave Trail
other_links.note: Logs Bear Cave at 0.5 mi. Access from Highway 154.

trails.stats_note: Our entry bundles two separate trails that AllTrails lists apart. The stats given are Bear Cave Trail's (1.2 mi / 127 ft, 0.5–1 hr, 1,110 reviews; no star rating surfaced). Bear Cave is a maze under and between giant sandstone boulders — good with a dog on a lead, awkward with anything wide.

trails.name: Petit Jean Canyon Trail
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Late January in the Arkansas River valley is the wet season, which is when Cedar Creek and its pools look their best — and also when the rock underfoot is at its most slippery.
trails.note: Checked specifically against Cedar Falls Trail, already on this card, because at Petit Jean the two are easy to confuse — and they are NOT the same walk. The Canyon Trail branches LEFT after the bridge on the Cedar Falls Trail, where the falls route goes right, and follows the yellow blazes down Cedar Creek Canyon past the Blue Hole, through small falls, emerald pools and boxcar-sized fallen boulders. The park's own description calls it one of the most beautiful and one of the least walked.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks permit pets throughout the park; only public buildings and swimming areas are closed to them. Already sourced at stop level.

other_links.label: Explore the Ozarks — Petit Jean State Park Trails
other_links.note: The source that settled the duplicate question: 'Beginning after you cross the bridge on Cedar Falls Trail, hikers need to head left instead of right and follow the yellow blazes to Blue Hole.'

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Petit Jean State Park trail map (PDF)

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Five nights, three entries, and all three start within a few hundred yards of Mather Lodge.

trails.name: Mount Nebo Rim Trail
trails.season: No published seasonal closure on the trail. The access is the question: AR-155 climbs Mount Nebo in tight switchbacks, and in a late-January cold snap that road is the thing that decides whether this happens. Truck only regardless — it is not a coach road under any conditions.
trails.note: A different mountain, half an hour west. The Rim Trail runs the entire edge of a flat-topped mesa at about 1,350 ft, so the views are continuous rather than at one overlook, and the loop shape means it does not need retracing. Five times the reviews of anything on the Petit Jean card and the same 4.7 average.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule, the same authority already sourced for Petit Jean itself.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Mount Nebo: Rim Trail
other_links.note: Gives it as 3 mi starting from behind the visitor center.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Rim Trail, Mount Nebo State Park Monument Trails
other_links.note: Mount Nebo also carries a Monument Trails mountain-bike network, which is a separate system from this hiking rim loop.

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. Published lengths elsewhere run 3 to 3.6 mi. One aggregator (Secret Falls) grades it 'Expert' and places it in Benton County, which is the wrong end of the state — that listing was disregarded.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

petit-jean-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks allow leashed pets throughout the park, so all three trails including Cedar Falls are open to the dog; only public buildings and swimming areas are closed.
petit-jean-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or other animals brought into state parks will be appropriately leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical (not verbal) control of the owner.

offroad.name: Wallace Bridge Road
offroad.distance: 10.2 mi · about 21 km southwest of the stop — the closest and the easiest
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "an easy dirt road, gentle grades, and is safe for most 2WD vehicles"
offroad.season: onX lists Fall, Spring, Summer — winter is not listed, and the stop is 18-23 Jan 2029. Nothing is gated; read it as a warning about a wet January rather than a closure
offroad.note: "Wallace Bridge Road is a beautiful gravel road that is woven through the Ouachita National Forest. This is a very well-maintained gravel road that passes through farmland in Deberrie, Arkansas, and runs along the Fourche LaFave River. This road is suitable for most vehicles as there are limited obstacles along the way." The bridge itself "was constructed in 1908 by the Southwestern Bridge Company". Ten miles, twenty minutes from camp, nothing asked of the truck — the default outing for this stop.

offroad.name: Brown Creek Road 805
offroad.distance: 7.9 mi · about 29 km south of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "lots of creek crossings which isn't conducive to low-clearance vehicles. The west end of the trail has a steep gradient with big rocks"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons including Winter
offroad.note: "Brown Creek winds you through the forest with beautiful views, lots of creek crossings, and campsites. This trail will also lead you to the Ouachita National Recreation trail which is a 223-mile trail, there are two entrance points along this route to access this trail... Brown Creek Trail Shelter can be accessed off the first NRT crossing on the east end of this route." A January run means cold water at the crossings but none of the snake and tick warnings that dominate the summer notes.

offroad.name: Lake Sylvia to Lake Winona and Highway 9
offroad.distance: 18.5 mi · about 30 km south of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy); high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Fall and Winter — winter is explicitly in scope
offroad.note: The longest single line in this box and a proper day out. "This trail starts at Lake Sylvia State Park where camping, swimming and water/electric sites are available if needed... After leaving Lake Sylvia this route takes you to LAKE WINONA (you will see the intersection where you can pick up a rule pamphlet and turn right to Winona) but this route goes straight to hwy 9 where you can go back to Lake Sylvia or head elsewhere." Pick up that pamphlet at the intersection.

offroad.name: Winona Auto Tour Scenic Drive (Forest Road 132)
offroad.distance: 26 mi end to end · about 41 km south of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "The entire route is a maintained gravel road"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons including Winter
offroad.note: The set-piece gravel drive of the Ouachitas and the best single day of this stop. "The Winona Auto Tour Scenic Drive is a 26-mile trail located in the Ouachita National Forest. The route travels along with Forest Road #132 between AR Highway 7 north of Jessieville and AR Highway 9 south of Perryville. There are several vistas along the route; Oak Mountain Vista, Forked Mountain Vista, Crystal Mountain, Lake Winona Vista, and North Fork Pinnacle. The route is generally traveled in a west-to-east direction." The spur up Crystal Mountain is rougher, rated 3. Note the Forest Service's own Ouachita scenic-drives page lists Buffalo Gap, Scenic 7 Byway and the Talimena Byway and does NOT mention this drive at all, so the official page is not the place to look for it.

offroad.name: Long Caney 849 to the South Fourche LaFave River
offroad.distance: 2.8 mi · about 23 km southwest of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "The depth of the mudholes is why I chose this rating. Some of them are pretty deep. You might need a rear differential breather"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Fall, Winter
offroad.note: "The Northern entrance into the Ouachita National Forest leads to a beautiful large quiet campsite on the South Fourche LaFave River. The road leading to this location is gravel when coming from the north. Once you turn right on Long Caney, it turns into a mud hole road all the way to camp... The campsite even features a boat ramp to the river." Short and close, but the mud is real — in January this is the one to look at before committing to.

offroad.name: Rock Creek 1319
offroad.distance: 5 mi · about 37 km north of the stop, in the Ozark National Forest
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "an easy gravel road with rolling hills and creek crossings which can overflow their banks during heavy rain"
offroad.season: onX lists Spring, Fall, Winter
offroad.note: The one route here that goes north into the Ozarks rather than south into the Ouachitas, which makes it the change of scenery. "Rock Creek is an easy gravel road with creeks, campsites, and views for miles. It has eight spur trails for SxSs, ATVs, and 4x4 rigs. Griffin Mountain peaks at an elevation of 1004 feet." Tackett Mountain 1337 (2.4 mi, onX rating 1, "primarily well-maintained gravel") loops off it and connects back to Rock Creek Road. TWO ROUTES IN THIS AREA WERE CHECKED AND REJECTED for this rig: North Fork Pinnacle Road 132C, whose own description says "No full-size vehicles, or vehicles with rooftop tents" and "just barely a Tacoma width wide", and Link Mountain Road 210, which onX lists as accessible by single track, 50-inch, 60-inch and high-clearance vehicles with no full-width category at all.

Signal Hill summit trail.entity: Signal Hill, the 2,753-ft summit of Mount Magazine and the highest point in Arkansas, named in the mountain article.

Cameron Bluff overlooks.entity: The Cameron Bluff overlooks and campground, named in the state-park article.

Signal Hill Trail.entity: Same Signal Hill summit, the state highpoint.

North Rim Trail.entity: The North Rim Trail at Mount Magazine. No article, and neither the mountain nor the state-park article names it. Left bare.

Mossback Ridge Trail.entity: Mossback Ridge, the mountain's 2,700-ft second summit, named in both the mountain and state-park articles.

Cameron Bluff Overlook Drive.entity: The Cameron Bluff overlook road; the state-park article names Cameron Bluff and documents the CCC-built mountain road that became the Mount Magazine Scenic Byway.

Cove Lake.entity: Cove Lake below the mountain, created by one of the two CCC dams named in the state-park article; the AR 309 article also places it on the Mount Magazine Scenic Byway. NOTE: 'Cove Lake State Park' is in Tennessee — not linked.

trails.name: Signal Hill Trail
trails.was: Bear Hollow Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: To the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 ft. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mount Magazine State Park
other_links.note: Area browse page — candidate for AREA_BROWSE_ALLTRAILS.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Logs a 1.4-mile loop around the north and east of Signal Hill.

trails.stats_note: Signal Hill is the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 ft. AllTrails 1.8 mi / 252 ft vs Arklahoma Hiker's 1.4 mi loop. The only trail in this block with a complete set of AllTrails figures.

trails.name: Bear Hollow Trail
trails.distance: 5.5 mi out-and-back (Arklahoma Hiker walks it as 5 mi; the trail itself is 2.7 mi one-way)
trails.season: AllTrails records it as open year-round. No published winter closure was found for the park or for Cameron Bluff Overlook Drive — but Mount Magazine tops out at 2,753 ft, the highest ground in Arkansas, and AR-309 climbs the whole way. In the 23-27 Jan window ice on that road is the realistic risk and it is recorded as UNVERIFIED, not as clear.
trails.note: The park's own trail list calls out what is on it: WPA steps, Sunrise Rock, Inspiration Point, Bear Head Bluff and Shoal Creek, along the upper rim of Bear Hollow from the Benefield Picnic Area to AR-309. Named by Arklahoma Hiker as one of the three trails with the park's best views, and it was not on the card.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks permit pets on park trails; the lodge building itself is not open to them. Already sourced at stop level.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Mount Magazine: Bear Hollow Trail
other_links.note: 'A 2.7-mile west-pointing v-shaped trail that follows the rim at the east end of the mountain' — which is why AllTrails' out-and-back figure is roughly double.

trails.stats_note: Distance, grade, star and count from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. No completion time published. AllTrails' own 'Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash' line was NOT used as the dog source; the Arkansas State Parks rule is.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Four nights, and the card carried three entries of which TWO ARE THE SAME TRAIL — 'Signal Hill Trail (Arkansas's highest point)' and 'Signal Hill Trail' are one 1.8 mi loop listed twice. That left two real walks for four nights.

trails.name: North Rim Trail
trails.distance: 5 mi out-and-back (2.5 mi each way); a spur to the west end of Mossback Ridge makes a 4.4 mi loop back to the visitor center
trails.difficulty: Easy to moderate — described by Arklahoma Hiker as 'not difficult' and by Trail Run Project as a relatively easy dirt trail
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. This is the one trail on the card that is arguably BETTER on these dates than in summer — Trail Run Project notes the view along the north rim is at its best in winter, when the hardwoods are bare and the valley opens up. Same AR-309 ice caveat as everything else here.
trails.note: Runs the north rim from just west of the visitor center to Cameron Bluff Overlook Drive and on to the Brown Springs campground, through hardwood, scrub oak and cedar glade, crossing several small creeks. The third of the park's three best-view trails and the flattest of them. It also connects onward to the Cove Lake Trail off the mountain.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Mount Magazine: North Rim Trail
other_links.note: Source of the 5 mi out-and-back and of the ranking alongside Bear Hollow and Benefield East Loop.

other_links.label: Mountain Travel Guide — North Rim Trail
other_links.note: Source of the 4.4 mi loop variant via the Mossback Ridge spur.

trails.stats_note: NO ALLTRAILS LISTING — official source only. Repeated searches under 'North Rim Trail' with and without the park name returned Arkansas.com, Arklahoma Hiker, Secret Falls, Trail Run Project and HikeArizona but no alltrails.com result, so no trail link is carried and no slug was constructed. Length and grade are from the state's own trail page and from Arklahoma Hiker.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest gravel forest roads (Cove Lake / Magazine vicinity)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mt. Magazine Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms the district, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Cove Lake or for the district's forest-road network, and no off-road database carries a named route here. The district's only current road alert is Morgan Mtn Rd, partially closed for road repair. Plan from the Ozark-St. Francis MVUM.
offroad.distance: The Magazine Mountain Ranger District carries 274.9 miles of MVUM-designated motorized routes — 245.5 miles of roads and 29.4 miles of trails

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest roads on the north flank of Magazine
offroad.note: Unlisted, same as the Cove Lake network above — the district page is the only authority that confirms these roads are Forest Service, and nothing publishes their numbers, surface or gate dates. Note this stop carries two offroad entries for what may be the same road network; worth folding into one with `same_as` if the tags agree.
offroad.distance: 37.3 miles of trail in three loops — Huckleberry Mountain Trail 18.8 mi, Apple Loop 12.2 mi, Bell Springs Loop 6.6 mi
offroad.difficulty: Not published by the Forest Service; Trails Offroad and onX both paywall their grades
offroad.season: The Forest publishes no seasonal closure. A third-party MVUM-derived index lists the Huckleberry Mountain route as seasonal June-March, which would put a 23 Jan 2029 arrival inside the open window — worth confirming against the current MVUM, which prints seasons of use per route.

mount-magazine-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks allow leashed pets on park trails, so Signal Hill and Cameron Bluff are both walkable with the dog; the lodge building itself is not.
mount-magazine-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or animals other than service animals for individuals with disabilities will not be permitted in public buildings or at swimming beaches or pools at any time.

not_a_trail.problem: The same trail as "Signal Hill Trail (Arkansas's highest point)", already on this card — same AllTrails listing under a second name.

Boxley Valley elk viewing.entity: Boxley Valley, listed on the NRHP as the Big Buffalo Valley Historic District, and the Buffalo National River elk herd — the park article states the park is home to the state's only elk herd.

Boxley Valley elk.entity: Same Boxley Valley cultural landscape and the same elk herd.

links.label: Wikipedia — Big Buffalo Valley Historic District

Lost Valley Trail.entity: Lost Valley, named in the Buffalo National River article as an access point on Arkansas Highway 43 between AR 21 and Ponca. The trail itself has no article.

Steel Creek and the Roark Bluff river be.entity: Steel Creek access on the Ponca section, named in the Buffalo National River article. Roark Bluff, the bluff above it, is not named in any article and has none of its own.

AR-7 Scenic Byway run.entity: Arkansas Highway 7, designated an Arkansas Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway, running through Jasper.

Erbie and the old homesteads.entity: Erbie, described in the Buffalo National River article as the historic community where the river reaches the Springfield Plateau. It has no article of its own.

trails.name: Whitaker Point Trail (Hawksbill Crag)
trails.was: Buffalo River Trail (Ponca to Steel Creek) — a different trail; Hawksbill Crag is the marquee walk here
trails.note_source: The narrow sandstone overhang 200 ft above the valley — the most photographed spot in the Ozarks.

trails.name: Lost Valley Trail
trails.note_source: Along Clark Creek past natural bridges to Eden Falls and Cobb Cave. Crushed rock to natural surface. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike the Lost Valley Trail
other_links.note: 'Lost Valley Trail is an easy to moderate hike with occasional benches on the first portion for resting.' Buffalo National River is the managing authority.

other_links.label: Buffalo Outdoor Center
other_links.note: Directions: from Ponca, south on Hwy 43 about 1.5 miles to the paved turnoff on the right. Large car park.

trails.stats_note: 2.4 mi / 249 ft are AllTrails GPS; the difficulty grade is the NPS one. Follows Clark Creek past natural bridges to Eden Falls. Most-reviewed trail in this whole block and the most popular running trail in Arkansas.

trails.name: Buffalo River Trail (Ponca to Steel Creek segment)

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Moderate 4.1-mile hike with river views and bluffs. A second Komoot trace of the same segment (e2813520458) grades it easy at 4.5 mi.

other_links.label: Buffalo Outdoor Center — Ponca to Steel Creek
other_links.note: Starts at the Ponca access; cross the Ponca low-water bridge to pick up the trail.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Puts the Ponca low-water bridge to Steel Creek Campground stretch at 2.2 miles one way, 4 miles out-and-back.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing for the HIKING segment. The AllTrails result that matches this name — 'Buffalo River Paddle Route from Ponca to Steel Creek' — is a float trip, not this walk, and has deliberately not been linked. Lengths disagree by source: 2.2 mi one way (Arklahoma Hiker), 4.1 mi (Komoot), 4.5 mi (Komoot alternate), 4.6 mi (secretfalls) — the segment is walked both one-way and out-and-back. Buffalo National River (NPS) is the managing authority.

trails.name: Glory Hole Waterfall Trail
trails.season: The whole point of this walk is water, and it is rain-fed. AllTrails' own description says it is 'always best to hike in the spring or late fall when water' is running; the stop is 27 Jan - 3 Feb 2029, which is inside the wet half of the Ozark year and a reasonable bet — but a dry fortnight before arrival turns it into a hole in a rock. The walk in is ALL DOWNHILL, which means the return is all uphill, and the last section is a narrow path rather than the jeep road it starts on. No parking area: cars pull onto the verge of Highway 16 near the marked red barn.
trails.note: The most distinctive waterfall in the Ozarks and it was not on this card — the creek has bored a round hole through a bluff overhang and the water drops through it rather than over it. 2,903 reviews at 4.7, more than anything currently listed for this stop except Whitaker Point. About half an hour south of Ponca.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted under restraint. Managing authority is the US Forest Service, Ozark National Forest (Big Piney District) — the same land status already sourced on this card for Hawksbill Crag, and NOT Buffalo National River, whose pet ban does not reach here.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Glory Hole Falls Trail (Ozark Forest)
other_links.note: Confirms Newton County, Big Piney District of the Ozark National Forest, much of it on old jeep roads.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Ozark-St. Francis National Forest
other_links.note: Forest-level browse page.

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed; a local tourism page gives the identical 2 mi / 393 ft / moderate / 1-1.5 hr independently. Note a DIFFERENT and much smaller trail exists under a confusable name — 'Little Glory Hole Falls' near Big Flat, 1.1 mi, 249 ft, 4.0 from 41 reviews, at https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arkansas/little-glory-hole-falls--2 — which is not this.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Seven nights, and the card carried FOUR entries of which two are the same trail: 'Whitaker Point Trail (Hawksbill Crag)' and 'Hawksbill Crag (Whitaker Point) Trail' are one 2.7 mi walk listed twice. That left three.

trails.name: Alum Cove Loop
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Winter suits it: the small creek that carved the arch runs in the wet months, the two small waterfalls along the loop need rain, and with the leaves off, the bluff line and the arch itself read properly.
trails.note: A 130 ft sandstone natural bridge, one of the largest in the southeastern United States, standing about 50 ft above the forest floor — and a short easy loop that also passes walk-through caves, a bluff line, a creek crossing and a couple of small falls. This is the low-effort day the card did not have between two clifftop walks and a river trail.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted under restraint — US Forest Service, Ozark National Forest. Not Buffalo National River land, so the pet ban that rules out Lost Valley does not apply.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Alum Cove Natural Bridge Trail (Ozark Forest)
other_links.note: 1.2 miles, with the waterfalls, cave and stream listed.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Alum Cove Natural Bridge Recreation Area
other_links.note: Area page; source of the 272 ft elevation-gain figure, and confirms AllTrails indexes exactly one trail here.

trails.stats_note: Star and count from the AllTrails result title as displayed; AllTrails published no distance or time for the trail itself, so the 1.1-1.2 mi comes from Buffalo Outdoor Center, Arklahoma Hiker and AR Own Backyard, which agree, and the gain from AllTrails' own area page. NOTE THE SLUG: AllTrails displays this as 'Alum Cove Loop' but files it under /alum-cove-national-recreation-trail — not a URL anyone would have built from the displayed name.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

trails.name: Round Top Mountain Trail
trails.distance: About 4 mi as a multi-loop (Arklahoma Hiker); 3.55 mi covering every branch on one GPS track
trails.difficulty: Easy on the base loop; light climbing and rock scrambling with two or three flights of steps on the summit branch
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Winter is the season for the view — the whole reason to go up is the panorama over Jasper and the Arkansas Grand Canyon, and that opens up when the hardwoods are bare.
trails.note: Two and a half miles from the Jasper square on Highway 7, which makes it the walk-from-almost-camp option on a card where everything else is a drive down Boxley Valley or out to Highway 16. A flat loop around the base of the bluffs — with the scattered remains of a 1940s bomber crash — and a branch that climbs to the top for the view.
trails.note_source: DOG RULE NOT ESTABLISHED. Secondary sources place Round Top Mountain in the Ozark National Forest, which would make it dog-legal under restraint, but no official Forest Service or Arkansas Natural Heritage page naming this trail and its manager was found, and the whole point of the stop-level dog work here is that Buffalo National River and Ozark NF land are interleaved in Newton County and the rule flips between them. Recorded as unknown rather than assumed from a guess about who owns it.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Round Top Mountain Trail
other_links.note: 4-mile multi-loop, with an elevation profile.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Round Top Mountain
other_links.note: The split that matters: 'The Loop Trail is easy and is a mostly flat dirt trail. However, the trail leading to the top of the mountain requires some light climbing (2-3 flights of stairs) and rock scrambling.'

other_links.label: Buffalo Outdoor Center — Hike Roundtop Mountain
other_links.note: Directions: Hwy 7 south 0.3 mi to the Jasper square, left to stay on Hwy 7, entrance on the right in 2.4 miles.

trails.stats_note: Star and count from the AllTrails result title as displayed. AllTrails published no distance, gain or time in any indexed result for this trail; the mileages are from Arklahoma Hiker and from a GPS track published by a local hiker, and the difficulty description is Hiking Project's and onX's identical wording.
needs: Who manages Round Top Mountain, and therefore whether the dog can walk it. Ozark NF is the likely answer but was not confirmed from an official page.
elevation gain from a single consistent source

offroad.name: AR-43/74 Ponca-Boxley Valley Loop (truck-only)
offroad.note: These are paved state highways, not forest roads — NPS routes visitors to the Jasper/Ponca upper district via Highway 7 or Highway 43 south from Harrison. The park publishes no loop mileage. One genuine warning from the park: GPS is unreliable in this area and has sent numerous visitors the wrong way onto dirt roads, which matters more here than the pavement does.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain / Fallsville forest roads
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither the National Park Service nor the Forest Service publishes a page naming these roads, and no off-road database carries them as a route. The nearest sourced statement is the park's blanket warning that access roads in this area may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. Fallsville sits on the Ozark NF Big Piney district, so its MVUM is the authority for that half.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain Road (to Hawksbill Crag trailhead)
offroad.note: Unlisted, and this is the weakest-sourced route in this batch. It is a Newton County road running to the Upper Buffalo Wilderness trailhead, so it belongs to neither the park nor the Forest Service, and neither publishes anything on it. Every description of it as rough, rocky and steep, and every 'about four miles to the parking area' figure, is user-generated. The park's general warning about unpaved, extremely rocky access roads needing 4WD or high clearance is the only sourced statement that applies.

offroad.name: Erbie Road
offroad.note: The park has no page for Erbie Road itself; what it does publish is the general rule that access roads here may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. An Erbie campground map PDF exists and resolves at https://www.nps.gov/buff/planyourvisit/upload/Erbie-Campground-Map-Final-Edit-2017.pdf (confirmed 200; contents not readable as text here) and would be the thing to open on a phone.

offroad.name: Kyles Landing entrance road
offroad.note: Same position as Erbie — the only sourced statement is the park's warning that access roads may be unpaved, extremely rocky and may require 4WD and/or high clearance. The widely repeated figures of roughly 2.8 to 3 miles of steep gravel off AR 74 are not on any NPS page that could be opened, so they are not recorded. Both Kyles Landing campground map URLs that surfaced return 404, so there is no PDF to fall back on.

jasper-ponca-ar.dogs: Buffalo National River bans pets on most of its trails — Lost Valley is out — but names the Ponca-to-Steel Creek section of the Buffalo River Trail as one of the few where they are allowed; Hawksbill Crag is Ozark National Forest land, where dogs are permitted under restraint.
jasper-ponca-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not allowed in any government buildings, caves, or on most park trails.

not_a_trail.problem: The same trail as 'Whitaker Point Trail (Hawksbill Crag)', already on this card — same AllTrails listing under a second name.

Ozark Folk Center State Park.entity: The Ozark Folk Center, the Arkansas living-history state park at Mountain View.

Mountain View courthouse square.entity: Courthouse Square at Mountain View and the 1922 Stone County Courthouse on it; the city article describes the impromptu folk jam sessions around the square.

Blanchard Springs Recreation Area.entity: Blanchard Springs, whose caverns article covers the site in Ozark–St. Francis National Forest north of Mountain View. The recreation area as such has no separate article.

Sylamore Scenic Byway.entity: The Sylamore Scenic Byway through the Sylamore Ranger District of the Ozark National Forest in Stone County, Arkansas.

White River winter trout.entity: The White River of Arkansas and Missouri; the article's Angling section documents the trout fishery from the Beaver Lake tailwaters down to Guion.

offroad.name: Push Mountain Road & Sylamore Ranger District forest roads
offroad.season: Alert opened 7 April 2025 after the 2025 storms and stands until further notice
offroad.note: Push Mountain Road itself is a state highway, not a forest road, and the Forest Service publishes nothing on it. What this alert does settle is the district's gravel network after the 2025 floods and tornado: Cole Fork Road is still closed, and the Syllamo mountain-bike system including the Jack's Branch and Bad Branch loops and its trailhead is still closed for tornado damage. Barkshed, Gunner Pool and Blanchard Springs campgrounds and day-use area have all reopened.

offroad.name: Sylamore District forest roads to Gunner Pool and Barkshed
offroad.season: Both sites open all year; water at Gunner Pool is seasonal, April to November
offroad.note: The Forest Service gives the road numbers for both. Gunner Pool is FSR 1102, gravel, and the Forest Service calls the approach a steep, winding dirt road not recommended for large recreation vehicles. Barkshed is AR 14 west from Mountain View 17.3 miles, then FSR 1115 (gravel) 2.1 miles, then FSR 1112 1.4 miles — https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/recreation/barkshed-recreation-area — also not recommended for large trailers or RVs. Both reopened after the 2025 storms.

trails.name: Ozark Folk Center State Park grounds trail

other_links.label: Arkansas State Parks — Ozark Folk Center
other_links.note: Fetched and read: the managing authority's own park page names NO trail and publishes NO trail length for the grounds. The park is open mid-April to mid-November. Guided walks such as the 'Herbs, History & Healing Hike' appear as events, not as a marked trail.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Whitewater Creek Trail
other_links.note: The nearest real listing, 194 reviews: it connects the Ozark Folk Center to the Stone County Amphitheater and City Park in Mountain View. This is the walk that gets you off the grounds and into town — a better use of an afternoon than the grounds paths.

trails.stats_note: Recorded as unlisted, not as a failure: Arkansas State Parks confirms the park but does not publish a named grounds trail, and no trail database indexes one. The grounds paths are craft-village walkways rather than a trail. Nothing invented.

trails.name: White River Bluff Loop
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Reviews warn the path is overgrown in the growing season — which makes the 3-8 Feb window the GOOD time to walk it, with the brush down and the bluff-top river views open. Rocky sections near the overlooks stay slick when wet.
trails.note: The card's only real half-day walk. It is the shortest of the five trails in the Syllamo system and, as Strava puts it, a snapshot of the whole thing — rolling pine, rocky sections, and bluffs above the White River. Trailhead is off Green Mountain Road a mile or two from Highway 5, with a self-pay station and a pit toilet.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash. Managing authority is the US Forest Service, Ozark-St. Francis National Forests — AllTrails' own location field names the forest. No trail-specific pet rule is published, so this rests on the standing national-forest rule.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — White River Bluff Loop
other_links.note: Blazed green; 'doesn't have a lot of elevation gain, but some of the climbs can feel a little tough. Most of the rocky sections are by the river overlooks.'

other_links.label: MTB Project — White River Bluff Loop
other_links.note: The same trail from the riding side: 'the climbs can be tough and technical'. Source of the bike use.

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. Strava gives the loop as 4.1 mi against AllTrails' 4.3.
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal and part of a named MTB system, but MTB Project describes technical rocky sections at the river overlooks. Not a gravel cruise with a dog in a carrier.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Five nights and three entries, one of which is a guided cave tour the dog cannot attend and one of which is a state-park grounds path.

trails.name: Mirror Lake Trail
trails.season: No seasonal closure on the trail itself. The waterfall is rain-fed and reviewers single it out as best after heavy rain — early February in the Ozarks is the wet half of the year, so these dates favour it. Note that the Blanchard Springs RECREATION AREA campground has a winter season of its own; day access to Mirror Lake is separate from that and was not found to be restricted.
trails.note: Paved, flat, boardwalked and stroller-accessible, running from Mirror Lake to the point where Blanchard Springs bursts out of the hillside as a waterfall, past the old grist mill. This is the walk for the afternoon of the cave tour, and the one member of the household who cannot go into the caverns can do this one instead.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — US Forest Service, Ozark-St. Francis National Forests. The Forest Service's Blanchard Springs Recreation Area page publishes no trail-specific pet rule; this rests on the standing national-forest rule. It matters here because the dog is barred from the caverns and their visitor centre, which is already recorded at stop level.

other_links.label: US Forest Service — Blanchard Springs Recreation Area

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

trails.name: Blanchard Springs Caverns — Dripstone Trail
trails._merge_warning: This entry MERGES onto a trail already on the card. build_links.merge_keep() CLEARS every key it owns that the new item omits — name, url, label, difficulty, time, distance, rating, uses, dogs, cruise, cruiseWhy, note — so the url, difficulty, distance, time and dogs values below are copied verbatim from the current card entry in desktop/index.html and must not be dropped from this patch. Only `reviews` and `note` (via `season`) are new.
trails.time: 1-1.5 hrs guided tour; no pets allowed in the cave, plan for a sitter/shift
trails.season: CLOSED FOR THIS STOP — but the sources disagree and this needs a phone call, not a decision. Recreation.gov, which is the Forest Service's own ticketing system for this cavern, states: 'Blanchard Springs Caverns tours are available Thursday - Monday between March - October and Closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The facility Closes completely From November - February and cavern tours are NOT available.' The stop is 3-8 Feb 2029, squarely inside that November-February shutdown. Against that, blanchardsprings.org says flatly 'Dripstone Trail tours are available year-round', and two visitor sites give a reduced winter schedule (Wed-Sun, or closed Mon-Tue, Nov-Mar) rather than a closure. Three different answers. Treat as CLOSED until the caverns confirm otherwise.
needs: Confirmation of the February tour schedule. Blanchard Springs Caverns, 870-757-2211 (the number Recreation.gov publishes for the facility). This is the whole reason the stop is here and the strongest source says it is shut on these dates.

other_links.label: Recreation.gov — Blanchard Springs Caverns
other_links.note: The closure statement, and the 870-757-2211 number.

other_links.label: Blanchard Springs Caverns — Dripstone Trail
other_links.note: The contradicting source: 'Dripstone Trail tours are available year-round.' Also gives the tour as 4/10 of a mile in an hour, a constant 58 F at close to 100% humidity, and accessible to strollers and wheelchairs with strong assistance.

trails.resel: NOT a new trail — a seasonal finding merged onto the entry already on this card. The cave tour is the reason for the stop and the official ticketing system says the facility is shut for the whole of February.

mountain-view-ar.dogs: Dogs are fine on the North Sylamore Creek Trail and on the Ozark Folk Center grounds, but they are barred from Blanchard Springs Caverns and its visitor centre, so the Dripstone tour means leaving the dog in the coach.
mountain-view-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not allowed in the Visitor Center or Caverns: seeing-eye dogs and service dogs are an exception.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Arkansas Scenic 9 (Mountain View to Clinton)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: AR-9 runs 94.41 miles in total; the Clinton-to-Mountain View leg crosses Van Buren and Stone counties
scenicDrives_patch.note: Worth correcting on the card: AR-9 is NOT an Arkansas Scenic Byway. ArDOT's Beautification Section administers the state's scenic byway program and publishes the designated list at ardot.gov/divisions/right-of-way/row_sections/beautification-section/scenic-byways/ (fetch returned HTTP 403; the page was confirmed from its search-result title and a snippet describing the Highway 88 designation of 1998). AR-9 appears on no byway list and holds no independent scenic designation — near Clinton it merely intersects the genuinely designated Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway. What AR-9 does carry: "Pieces of all three routes are designated as Arkansas Heritage Trails for use during the Civil War and the Trail of Tears." The drive itself is real and pretty — it climbs and winds through classic Ozark foothill terrain northeast from Clinton through Shirley into Stone County — it just is not a byway, and the name on the card implies it is.

Beaver Lake day trip.entity: Beaver Lake, the White River reservoir whose dam the article places 9 miles northwest of Eureka Springs.

Walk the historic downtown.entity: The Eureka Springs Historic District, which as listed in 1970 covers the whole city.

The spring circuit.entity: The town's cold-water springs (Basin Spring and the rest) that the resort was built on; documented at length in the city article.

Lake Leatherwood City Park.entity: Lake Leatherwood Park, listed by name under Points of interest in the Eureka Springs article. No article of its own.

Beaver Bridge.entity: The 1949 one-lane suspension bridge at Beaver, Arkansas carrying AR 187 over the White River — the 'Little Golden Gate', the only suspension bridge open to traffic in Arkansas, about 8 miles from Eureka Springs.

Berryville and the Carroll County square.entity: Berryville, the larger of Carroll County's two county seats, and Carroll County itself.

trails.name: Passion Play Trails / Magnetic Mountain
trails.official_length: over 18 miles of trail on a 667-acre property

other_links.label: The Great Passion Play — Trails
other_links.note: The landowner and trail manager: 'We have over 18 miles of world-class mountain biking trails on our 667-acre property for all skill levels.'

other_links.label: The Great Passion Play — Trail descriptions
other_links.note: Splits the network into 'Shared-Use and Mountain-Bike Optimized Trails' — this is the authority statement that hiking is permitted, not just tolerated. Individual trails carry Biblically-inspired names.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Passion Play hiking view
other_links.note: 37 trails mapped. Trailforks warns plainly: 'These trails are built specifically with mountain biking in mind and are therefore graded on mountain biking difficulty' — a blue here is not a hiker's blue.

other_links.label: OZ Trails NWA
other_links.note: Regional trail authority listing; describes over 18 miles of professionally built mountain biking and hiking trails, part of the Marble Flats system.

trails.stats_note: Kept in the trails box rather than reclassified because the landowner explicitly designates shared-use trails, so hiking is legal — but it is a network, not a single trail, and every published difficulty grade on it is a mountain-bike grade. No AllTrails listing exists for it under any wording tried. Blind-corner descents shared with bikes: not a place to walk a dog on a long lead.

trails.name: Historic District Walking Trail

other_links.label: Visit Eureka Springs — Downtown Historic District
other_links.note: The city tourism authority's page for the Downtown Historic District — the district this walk is through. It is a streetscape stroll, not a built path.

other_links.label: Visit Eureka Springs — 8 walking trails
other_links.note: The city's own list of walking loops, e.g. the 1.3 mi Starlite North loop through wooded terrain — the closest thing to a published in-town trail inventory.

other_links.label: EurekaSprings.com — Parks and Trails
other_links.note: Overview of the city's connected park and trail system.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing and no published length from the city for a route by this name. Confirmed only as the Eureka Springs Downtown Historic District walk by the city tourism authority. Third-party sources describe a 3.5-mile 'Historic Loop' past 300+ pre-1910 Victorian homes, but nothing official carries that figure, so it is not recorded as the length.

trails.name: Pigeon Roost Trail and Dry Creek Loop (Hobbs State Park-Conservation Area)
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Mid-February suits it — the short side views toward Beaver Lake that the description mentions are the kind that only open through bare trees.
trails.note: The best-reviewed walk within an hour of Eureka Springs by an order of magnitude, and this card had nothing outside the town. Dry Creek side of the Pigeon Roost network in Arkansas's largest state park: old logging-road grades alternating with narrower dirt, ridge tops and shaded hollows, small stream crossings, sinkholes and karst.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule, Code of Arkansas Rules: pets must be 'leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical (not verbal) control of the owner'. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE ADDITION: all three entries already on this card sit on City of Eureka Springs land or on the privately owned Great Passion Play's land, and neither publishes any dog rule at all, which is why the stop currently carries a dogs_unpublished record and a phone number instead of an answer. A state park is a jurisdiction where the rule is written down.

other_links.label: AllTrails — War Eagle Valley Loop Trail (Hobbs)
other_links.note: 4.3 from 131 reviews — a second Hobbs loop if the first one lands well. NOT the same as the War Eagle Trail at Withrow Springs also listed on this card; two different trails on two different parks sharing a creek's name.

trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. Note the slug is /dry-creek-loop-via-the-pigeon-loop-trail while the page displays as 'Pigeon Roost Trail and Dry Creek Loop' — another one that could not have been built from the name.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Six nights, and the three entries on the card were a city park's trail network described as a whole rather than as trails, a town walking route, and a set of paths on private land — with no distance, time, difficulty or review count between them and no dog rule for any of them.

trails.name: War Eagle Trail (Withrow Springs State Park)
trails.distance: 1.5 mi loop (Arkansas State Parks); an optional half-mile spur adds an overlook and a drop to the creek
trails.difficulty: Easy on the loop, moderate on the spur
trails.season: Arkansas State Parks' own trail page opens with the line 'Our other trails are open', which implies at least one trail at Withrow Springs is shut and does not say which or for how long. Not enough to call anything closed for these dates, and too pointed to ignore — worth confirming with the park (Withrow Springs superintendent, 479-559-2593) before driving out.
trails.note: Half an hour south on AR-23, named for the creek that runs the park boundary. An easy loop with a few creek views, and a short moderate spur down to the water and an overlook. Short enough to be an afternoon rather than a day, which is what a six-night stop in a small town actually needs.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule. Same reasoning as the Hobbs entry: a jurisdiction with a published rule, unlike the three city and private-land entries already on this card.

other_links.label: Arkansas.com — War Eagle Trail
other_links.note: Source of the 1.5 mi loop figure and of the 'Our other trails are open' line.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Withrow Springs: War Eagle Trail
other_links.note: Reads it differently: about a mile officially, two miles out and back, three if the visitor-centre spur is added. Recorded alongside rather than reconciled.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Withrow Springs Forest Trail
other_links.note: The park's other listed trail, 90 reviews. Trailhead 0.75 mi northeast of the park office on Spur 23 West. Park superintendent contact: 479-559-2593, withrowsprings@arkansas.com.

trails.stats_note: Star and count from the AllTrails result title as displayed. AllTrails published no distance, gain or time for this listing in any indexed result, so the length is the state's own and the two published lengths disagree.
needs: which Withrow Springs trail is closed, given the state's 'Our other trails are open' line — 479-559-2593

trails.name: Historic Van Winkle Trail (Hobbs State Park-Conservation Area)
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Forty-two feet of gain over six tenths of a mile makes this the all-weather option on the card.
trails.note: A short interpretive loop through the site of the Van Winkle sawmill and homestead in Hobbs, and the obvious pairing with the Pigeon Roost loop on the same drive — one long walk and one short one, rather than two half-hearted ones. Flat enough for a bad-weather day.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule.
trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. The /en-gb/ copy of the same page reports 339 reviews against the US page's 351.

https://www.eurekaparks.com — Eureka Springs Parks and Recreation home page. The only dog reference is the Bark Park at Harmon Park, a separate fenced facility; nothing about dogs on trails.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Lake+Leatherwood+City+Park+Eureka+Springs+dogs+leash+rules+official+city+park — search returned no eurekaparks.com or City of Eureka Springs page carrying a trail dog rule; every 'dog friendly' claim came from BringFido, DogPack or Zoomies Zone, which are not authorities.
https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=eurekaparks.com+Lake+Leatherwood+park+rules+regulations+dogs+leash+trails — same result: no official park-rules page indexed.

Aug 2026 pass — tried the municipal code rather than the park page: https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Eureka+Springs+Arkansas+municipal+code+ordinance+parks+%22dogs%22+leash+Lake+Leatherwood returned a Facebook hiking post, the STATE enabling statute (Ark. Code 14-54-1102, which only grants municipalities the POWER to prevent dogs running at large — it is not itself a Eureka Springs rule), and a dog-beach aggregator. No City of Eureka Springs ordinance text is indexed.

Then ask the Great Passion Play separately about the Magnetic Mountain trails, since that is private land under a different owner.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Beaver Lake Scenic Loop (AR-187)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 16.57 miles, running from AR-23 north of Eureka Springs to US-62 near Eureka Springs, all within Carroll County
scenicDrives_patch.note: The whole point of this loop is the Beaver Bridge — a one-lane 1949 suspension bridge over the White River, the last of its kind still open to vehicles in Arkansas, 554 ft long and 11 ft wide, on the National Register. The published limit is what to check before driving it: the standing restriction is one-lane traffic with a 20,000 lb (10 ton) weight limit, but recent coverage of the bridge's reopening reports "the structure's weight limit was also reduced from 10 tons to five" and further closures planned. Five tons is 10,000 lb — still above a 4x4 pickup, but it is now a number worth confirming with ArDOT rather than assuming, and the bridge has been closed outright for repairs more than once. Cars take turns; only one direction crosses at a time.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-62 Historic Corridor
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 26 miles Pea Ridge National Military Park to Eureka Springs on US-62
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Eureka Springs CVB's own scenic-drives article, titled "Four Scenic Drives Near Eureka Springs That'll Take Your Breath Away" and describing "a curvaceous road with rolling hills and plenty of dense foliage" with mountain vistas. The page answered HTTP 403 when fetched, so the listing is confirmed from its title and snippet only and the four drives are not enumerated here. The westbound stretch is the historically loaded one: US-62 runs 26 miles from Pea Ridge National Military Park east to Eureka Springs through rolling northwest-Arkansas terrain, past historic White River bridges. No seasonal restriction found for US-62 itself.

offroad.name: Butler Hollow
offroad.distance: 9.4 mi · about 12 km northwest of the stop — the closest unpaved route of any stop in this pass
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy); high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons. "This is an easy-going fun cruise crossing state lines that could prove difficult after heavy rains since the road crosses the creek"
offroad.note: "Butler Hollow connects Beaver, Arkansas, and Seligman, Missouri via a retired Arkansas & Ozarks rail line along Butler Creek. Most of the road is well-graded gravel with scattered potholes and dry water crossings. The north end of the road through the National Forest is packed dirt with scattered potholes in the shadows. This passes through protected Ozark glade bottoms where road runners, prickly pear cacti, and other desert animals can be found." Nine miles on an old rail grade, twelve kilometres from camp, and it crosses into Missouri — the obvious first afternoon.

offroad.name: Mark Twain National Forest Scenic Drive
offroad.distance: 7.3 mi · about 15 km north of the stop, over the Missouri line
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "a well-maintained gravel road that can be traveled by any vehicle"
offroad.season: onX lists Winter first of all four seasons, which for a 8-14 Feb 2029 stop is the answer wanted
offroad.note: Seven miles of graded Mark Twain National Forest gravel, close enough to be an afternoon. One caution carried straight from the source: "There are many spur roads that offer a more technical experience and is almost guaranteed to cause pinstriping" — stay on the main line in a truck that has to look respectable for another month of the trip.

offroad.name: Mary Cole Ridge 1011
offroad.distance: 3.4 mi · about 22 km north of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "well maintained gravel with large pieces of rock and gravel hidden under the leaves. The only difficulty is when it starts to narrow"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons; the overlooks are explicitly a fall and winter thing
offroad.note: "Mary Cole Ridge 1011 is a scenic ridge road in Mark Twain National Forest with distant overlooks through the hardwoods seen in the fall and wintertime." February is exactly when the leaves are off and the views are open. "The road eventually becomes narrower and has one last turn around point intersecting other trails before it becomes even more narrow" — turn at that point; past it the spurs are for side-by-sides and motorcycles. There is a large staging car park at the trailhead off Highway 86.

offroad.name: WMA Road 1245
offroad.distance: 2.5 mi · about 23 km south of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "a gravel road with two small water crossings and minimal obstacles"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: "After the entrance, the road opens into a well-maintained gravel drive with plenty of tree coverage and few obstacles in the first half. Beyond the turnoff for WMA Road 9, the terrain becomes slightly more challenging, featuring two small water crossings and a few steeper grades. Cell service is intermittent... Clearly marked campsites are scattered along the route, and visitors should be aware of active hunting and shooting sports in the area." That last line matters in February with a dog aboard — this is a wildlife management area and it is in use.

offroad.name: WMA Road 9
offroad.distance: 2.2 mi · about 21 km south of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 3 (Easy) — "some steep climbs and narrow sections between trees. In several areas, large ruts can be found along the sides of the main route"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: The steeper branch off WMA Road 1245 and the one with the payoff: "Great views overlooking a valley. Smaller cars would struggle on some portions of this trail, but a stock 4Runner or similar vehicle would have no problem... Pay attention to the property lines, as this trail runs adjacent to private property." Do the two as one outing, easy road first.

Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art.entity: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

Crystal Bridges trails and the Razorback.entity: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

Coler Mountain Bike Preserve and Slaught.entity: Bentonville's two city mountain-bike systems. Neither has a Wikipedia article, and the Bentonville article names neither — it refers only to 'long mountain bike trails' in general. NOTE: the bare title 'Slaughter Pen' resolves to the Gettysburg Battlefield article — rejected. Left bare.

Downtown Rogers.entity: The Rogers Commercial Historic District, whose article opens 'known informally as Historic Downtown Rogers'.

trails.name: Bashore Ridge Loop Trail
trails.note: Hobbs State Park-Conservation Area east of Rogers - the best-reviewed real hike within reach of this stop, and a woodland walk rather than a greenway. February is bare-tree season, which is when the ridge actually has a view.

trails.name: Lake Atalanta Loop
trails.note: Rogers' lake circuit - flat, short, close in, and the easy hour on a cold day.

trails.name: North Bentonville Trail
trails.note: Paved greenway running north out of town, part of the Razorback Regional Greenway. The obvious candidate on this stop for a ride with the dog in the carrier rather than a hike - surface is asphalt, so no puncture question.

trails.name: Rim Rock Nature Loop
trails.note: Short bluff-line nature loop near Rogers - twenty minutes, and the shortest thing on this card.

not_a_trail.problem: A 300-acre mountain-bike preserve, not a trail: 20+ miles across 56 mapped trails, run by the Peel Compton Foundation. Trailforks maps the network at https://www.trailforks.com/region/coler-mountain-bike-preserve/map/ ; the operator's page is https://peelcompton.org/coler-mountain-bike-preserve/ and the city tourism page is https://www.visitbentonville.com/things-to-do/parks-trails-lakes/coler/ . Hiking IS permitted and the operator lists it alongside biking and camping — but AllTrails' own preserve page (https://www.alltrails.com/parks/us/arkansas/coler-mountain-bike-preserve) indexes exactly ONE trail for hiking out of the 56, which is the honest measure of how much of this is a walking destination. Belongs in the biking box or as an activity, not as a hiking trail.

A trail SYSTEM, not a trail — the City of Bentonville calls it 'This 23+ mile mountain bike system' and an IMBA Silver Level Ride Center (https://www.bentonville.ar.gov/1071/Slaughter-Pen-Trails); OZ Trails puts it at 30+ miles (https://www.oztrails.com/trail/slaughter-pen/) and Trailforks maps 150 individual trails (https://www.trailforks.com/region/slaughter-pen-trails/). Multi-use — TripAdvisor lists it as 'Slaughter Pen Hollow Multi-Use Trail System' and Trailforks tags hiking and trail running alongside mountain and e-bike — so walkers are legal, but every trail is built and graded for bikes. The one AllTrails route that covers it, https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arkansas/slaughter-pen-hollow-trail (All American, Seed Tick, Medusa, Tatamagouche), is described by AllTrails itself as 'This mountain bike-focused route'. Reclassify to biking.
