https://crystalbridges.org/visit/ — the main visit page. No mention of dogs, pets, animals or service animals.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Crystal+Bridges+Museum+trails+dogs+leashed+pets+policy+crystalbridges.org — the 'leashed pets are welcome on the museum trails' claim traces only to BringFido and similar aggregators, not to the museum.

Aug 2026 pass — no new sources attempted. The three museum pages above are the museum's complete published policy surface and a private landowner has no code, statute or administrative rule to fall back on, which is the route that settled Bismarck. This one only a phone call can close.
dogs_unpublished.action: Phone Crystal Bridges Guest Services on 479-657-2335 and ask whether leashed dogs are allowed on the Art Trail and the wider museum trail network, and whether the rule differs on the paved North Forest / Orchard sections. One call settles the whole stop, since the Art Trail is the only trail on the card.

bentonville-ar.stats_note: Crystal Bridges Art Trail was the only entry on this card and it is a museum grounds path. The four above are the walking options an in-town base actually has: one state-park ridge, one lake loop, one paved greenway and one short nature loop.

offroad.name: North Old Wire Road (Pea Ridge)
offroad.distance: 2.3 mi · about 21 km northeast of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy) — "easy, well-maintained gravel roads"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: The closest gravel to Bentonville and the one with the history attached: it "travels north to south along the far east side of the Pea Ridge National Military Park and can be driven in either direction. If you are traveling south to north. It begins at N. Old Wire Rd and Alvin Seamster Rd. If you are traveling North to South, it starts at the intersection of N. Old Wire Rd and Limekiln Rd. With heavy rain, you will see multiple creeks through the rolling hills. There is also one small concrete low water crossing towards the north side of the trail." Old Wire Road is the historic Butterfield route past the battlefield — a short drive that pairs with a battlefield afternoon rather than standing alone.

offroad.name: Flag Springs Road
offroad.distance: 10.9 mi · about 31 km north of the stop, over the Missouri line
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 2 (Easy) — "mostly easy-going dirt with a few areas that could become difficult after heavy rains. Several creek crossings may become deep after heavy rains"
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons, and names winter as one of the two best times for the views
offroad.note: The real drive for this stop: nearly eleven miles. "Flag Springs Road is a combination of gravel, dirt, and hard-packed red clay. It passes through Flag Springs Conservation Area and a public shooting range. Meandering along Brush Creek, the road crosses multiple dry creek crossings opening up to private ranches when turning left at County Road SE E60. The road then follows along Mikes Creek with some incredible views in the winter and spring seasons of the crystal-clear creek water below." A public shooting range on the route is worth knowing about before the dog is out of the truck.

offroad.name: Butler Hollow
offroad.distance: 9.4 mi · about 37 km east of the stop
offroad.difficulty: onX technical rating 1 (Easy); high clearance and full width
offroad.season: onX lists all four seasons
offroad.note: Carried here as well as on Eureka Springs because it sits between the two and this stop follows straight on from that one — if it was not driven from Eureka Springs it is still an easy morning from Bentonville. Retired Arkansas & Ozarks rail grade along Butler Creek from Beaver, AR to Seligman, MO, well-graded gravel with the creek crossing being the only thing weather affects. The Mark Twain National Forest Scenic Drive (7.3 mi, onX rating 1, "can be traveled by any vehicle") is the other carry-over, 44 km east of Bentonville. Nothing closer than North Old Wire Road was found on the Arkansas side: Benton County around Bentonville is town, greenway and mountain-bike singletrack, and the mountain-bike trails are not driveable.

Yellow Rock Trail.entity: The 3-mile Yellow Rock Trail to the Yellow Rock Bluff overlook, both named in the state-park article.

Devil's Den's CCC landscape.entity: The Civilian Conservation Corps work that built the park from 1933 — cabins, the dam and lake, the overlooks — documented throughout the park article.

Butterfield Hiking Trail.entity: The Butterfield Hiking Trail, named in the park article (it passes the remnants of the drowned town of Anna near Junction Camp) and taking its name from the Butterfield stage route through the Boston Mountains.

Artist Point.entity: The Artist Point roadside overlook on US 71 north of the park. IMPORTANT: the Wikipedia article 'Artist Point' is an overlook in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming — rejected on identity. The Arkansas viewpoint has no article and the Devil's Den article never names it. Left bare.

offroad.name: Shores Lake / Salt Fork forest roads
offroad.distance: about 10 mi of FSR 1501 under reconstruction
offroad.season: Work began autumn 2025, expected to finish summer 2027; the Forest Service expects the road to stay open to traffic through most of it
offroad.note: FSR 1501 runs from AR 23 on the east to AR 215 on the west near Shores Lake — culverts, reshaping, fresh gravel and overlook parking. Hurricane Road (FSR 1003) work is already complete. This lands squarely in the trip's window, so expect active construction rather than a closure. No Forest Service page names a 'Salt Fork' road, so that half of the entry is unsourced.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Part of FSR 1003 is still out. Per the Forest Service alert last updated 22 May 2026 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/alerts/fsr-1003-white-rock-road-closure-partially-lifted), the stretch between Bliss Ridge Road (FSR 1505-1) and Wood's Gap is repaired and open, but the eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge remains closed with no estimate of when or if it will be repaired. Approach from the west via Hurricane Road or from the north via Boles Gap Road (FSR 1505-2). Summit is 2,289 ft with CCC stone cabins and lodge.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road (Ozark National Forest)
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Duplicate — this is the same road as the 'White Rock Mountain Road' entry on this stop, listed twice under two names. Worth folding into one with `same_as` rather than shipping both. Same caveat applies: FSR 1003's eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge is still closed with no repair estimate, so come in from the west or the north.

trails.name: Butterfield Hiking Trail (Ozark Highlands Trail segment)

other_links.label: Arkansas State Parks — Butterfield Hiking Trail
other_links.note: Managing authority's trail page. Named for the Butterfield Stagecoach, which ran the area 1858–1861.

other_links.label: HikingProject
other_links.note: 'One of the few looped backpacking trails in the state.'

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: 15-mile loop from Devil's Den State Park near West Fork; ten of those miles run through the Ozark National Forest.

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: 'A challenging 15-mile loop that can be completed as an all-day trek or backpacking trip with one or two nights on the trail.'

trails.stats_note: Correction worth carrying: this is NOT an Ozark Highlands Trail segment. It is its own 15-mile loop that begins and ends in Devil's Den State Park, with about 10 miles running through the Ozark National Forest. Length and difficulty are the state park / Arklahoma Hiker figures — AllTrails surfaced no distance or gain in any indexed snippet. It is the most popular trail in Devil's Den State Park at 4.4 from 1,165 reviews, but at 15 miles and 9 hours it is an overnight or a very long day, not an afternoon.

trails.name: Shepherd Springs Loop (Lake Fort Smith State Park)
trails.season: Late February is the right time for this one, twice over. The waterfall near the start is SEASONAL and needs the wet months; and hikers who have walked it note that late fall and winter are when the lake views open up through the bare trees. No closure.
trails.note: This stop is called Devil's Den / Lake Fort Smith and the card had nothing at Lake Fort Smith at all. The loop starts at the north end of the campground, reaches the seasonal falls almost immediately, runs the ridgeline past rock formations and two old homesites where the chimneys are still standing, and comes back on a stretch of the Ozark Highlands Trail past Shepherd Spring itself.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule (Code of Arkansas Rules: pets 'leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical control of the owner'), already sourced at stop level.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lake Fort Smith State Park
other_links.note: Park browse page; names Shepherd Springs Loop as the best hike in the park.

trails.stats_note: Star and count from the AllTrails trail-page result title as displayed (649). AllTrails' own area pages for the same trail report 449, 503 and 639 on the same day — a spread worth knowing about, and the reason counts here are treated as good enough to ORDER trails and not good enough to quote. Distance and gain likewise vary 5.3-5.4 mi and 505-515 ft between AllTrails' park page and its POI page; both ranges are recorded rather than one being picked.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Five nights, three entries, all three inside Devil's Den State Park — and one of those three is flagged [CLOSED] by AllTrails, see below.

trails.name: Fossil Flats Loop
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. It runs along and on the creek bed, so it is a wet-feet trail after rain — which late February will supply.
trails.note: The low, flat, creek-bottom counterweight to Yellow Rock's bluff climb, and it starts from Camp Area A rather than needing a drive. Named for the flat exposed rock in the creek bed, which is full of visible fossils; there is CCC and early-settler evidence along it and an old sawmill site on the longer variant.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Fossil Flats Loop
other_links.note: Files it inside the Devils Den State Park Monument Trails network — this is a shared hike-and-ride trail, which is where the bike use comes from. Gives 241 ft of gain against AllTrails' 209.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Fossil Flats Sawmill Loop
other_links.note: The extended version past the old sawmill, 4.1 from 482 reviews.

trails.stats_note: Distance, gain, time, star and count from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. Pacer gives 2.5 mi and 229.6 ft; Trailforks 241 ft.
trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal and part of a Monument Trails network, but it is purpose-built singletrack along a rocky creek bed, not a graded surface. Keeps the bike badge, stays out of the biking view.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

trails.name: Devil's Den Trail
trails._merge_warning: This entry MERGES onto a trail already on the card. build_links.merge_keep() CLEARS every owned key the new item omits, so url, difficulty, distance, time and dogs below are copied verbatim from the current card entry in desktop/index.html. Only `reviews` (now sourced, 4.7 from 2,739, against the card's unsourced 4.6) and `note` (via `season`) are new.
trails.time: 1.5-2.5 hrs; crevices, caves (bat-closed), and Lee Creek bluffs
trails.season: STATUS CONTESTED — check before walking. AllTrails titles this listing 'Devil's Den Trail [CLOSED]' (4.7 from 2,739 reviews). What is definitely shut is the CAVES: the park's sandstone crevice caves, including Devil's Den Cave and the Devil's Ice Box, have been closed to the public since 16 April 2010 to stop humans spreading White-Nose Syndrome to the Ozark big-eared, Indiana and gray bats, and there is no reopening date. What is unclear is the trail itself — secondary guides published in 2026 still recommend walking it 'to see the rugged rock formations and locked cave entrances', which reads as an open trail past sealed caves rather than a closed trail. AllTrails' [CLOSED] tag and those guides cannot both be current.
needs: Whether the Devil's Den Trail itself is walkable, as distinct from the caves on it being sealed. Devil's Den State Park, Arkansas State Parks. This decides whether the card's headline trail exists for this stop or not.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Devil's Den Trail [CLOSED]
other_links.note: The [CLOSED] flag is in AllTrails' own page title. Its description still lists Devil's Den Cave, Devil's Ice Box, Twin Falls and Cold Springs as highlights and adds 'The caves are closed to protect bats and their habitat from White-Nose Syndrome.'

other_links.label: Wikipedia — Devil's Den State Park
other_links.note: Source of the 16 April 2010 cave-closure date and the three endangered Arkansas bat species it protects.

trails.resel: NOT a new trail — a status finding merged onto the entry already on this card. Worth surfacing because it is the trail the park is named for and the largest sandstone crevice cave system in the United States sits on it.

devils-den-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks permit leashed pets on park trails, and the Butterfield's national-forest miles are dog-legal too, so all three work with the dog.
devils-den-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or other animals brought into state parks will be appropriately leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical (not verbal) control of the owner.

Talimena Scenic Byway.entity: The Talimena Scenic Drive, the 54-mile National Scenic Byway from Talihina, Oklahoma to Mena, Arkansas.

Talimena National Scenic Byway.entity: The same Talimena Scenic Drive — the article confirms the National Scenic Byway designation.

Queen Wilhelmina Lodge.entity: The 'Castle in the Sky' lodge on Rich Mountain; the state-park article documents the lodge, its 40 guest rooms and its 1898 origin. The lodge has no separate article.

Lovers' Leap Trail.entity: The Lovers' Leap Trail at Queen Wilhelmina State Park. No article, and the park article never mentions it. NOTE: 'Lovers Leap' resolves to a general article on the folklore place-name — rejected. Left bare.

Spring Trail.entity: The Spring Trail at Queen Wilhelmina State Park. No article, and the park article does not name it. Left bare.

offroad.name: Caney Creek Wilderness access roads (Shady Lake / Forest Service network)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mena-Oden Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms it, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Shady Lake, for Caney Creek Wilderness access, or for the surrounding road network, and no off-road database lists a named route. The Ouachita MVUM is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to what vehicle class.
offroad.distance: Forest Road 38 runs 6 miles north off AR-246 to the east trailhead

offroad.name: Cossatot Falls access road
offroad.note: Arkansas State Parks is the managing authority and its park page is the right link, but it publishes nothing about the access road — no surface, no mileage, no clearance requirement and no flood closure policy, despite the falls area being the part of the park most likely to be cut off by high water. Everything about the road's condition is currently unsourced; the park visitor centre is the place to settle it.

offroad.name: Ouachita National Forest roads (FR 106, FR 25 and others)
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither FR 106 nor FR 25 has a Forest Service page on the Mena-Oden district, and no off-road database lists them. Be careful with the numbers: FR 106 is also a road number on the Grandfather district in North Carolina (Dobson Knob), so a search on the bare number returns the wrong state. The Ouachita MVUM is the authority.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain fire-tower spur
offroad.distance: the byway itself is 54 mi
offroad.season: Byway open year round
offroad.note: The Forest Service page covers the byway that runs the spine of Rich Mountain and Winding Stair Mountain, but says nothing about a fire tower or about any spur road off it — so the spur itself is effectively unlisted and only the parent byway is sourced. The byway is paved; whatever spur the card means is not described anywhere the Forest Service publishes.

offroad.name: Wolf Pen Gap OHV Trail System
offroad.note: A permitted OHV trail system on the Mena-Oden district, not a forest-road drive. The Forest Service lists Mena-Oden among its OHV districts but publishes no mileage, fee, permitted vehicle class or season for Wolf Pen Gap specifically. The same page carries a notice dated 1 June 2026 that USDA and the Forest Service are reviewing OHV policy, so the permit rules may not be what they are now by the time of the stop — confirm with the district before buying anything.

trails.name: Ouachita National Recreation Trail (Rich Mountain segment)

other_links.label: USFS — Ouachita National Forest, Rich Mountain
other_links.note: Managing authority. Rich Mountain is the highest point in the Ouachita National Forest at 2,681 ft.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Rich Mountain point of interest
other_links.note: Confirms the mapping: 'This route follows Section 3 of the Ouachita National Recreation Trail, a long-distance route through the rugged mountains of western Arkansas.'

other_links.label: HikingProject — Rich Mountain Trail
other_links.note: The separate Rich Mountain Trail joins the Ouachita Trail at mile 8.5. Trailforks grades this one black-diamond singletrack, 8 miles — a different and harder line than the OT section.

other_links.label: AllTrails — full Ouachita Trail
other_links.note: The whole east-to-west through-route, for context on where Section 3 sits.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails surfaced no distance, gain, difficulty or rating for Section 3 in any indexed snippet — recorded absent. What it does say: no permits are required for the segment, and overnight use is supported by three-sided shelters and established dispersed campsites. Section 3 is the segment that covers Rich Mountain, confirmed by AllTrails' own Rich Mountain point-of-interest page.

trails.name: Janssen Park Trails (Mena)

other_links.label: City of Mena — Janssen Park
other_links.note: The City of Mena owns and manages the park and confirms it exists, but publishes no trail name or length.

other_links.label: Visit Mena — city parks
other_links.note: City tourism listing for the Mena parks, including a walking/biking trail in the city park system.

other_links.label: Wikipedia — Janssen Park
other_links.note: 'A large grassy expanse with occasional mature trees, and features walkways radiating from a central drive, which circles around Mena's oldest building, the c. 1850s Shelton log cabin.'

trails.stats_note: Confirmed to exist by the City of Mena; no trail database lists it and no authority publishes a length. Realistically a municipal park with radiating walkways and a log cabin, not a hiking trail — a twenty-minute leg-stretch with the dog rather than a walk to plan a morning around. AllTrails has only an empty 'explore/parks' stub for Janssen Park, which is not a listing and has not been linked.

trails.name: Harris Creek Trail (Cossatot River State Park-Natural Area)
trails.season: No published seasonal closure. Late February is the wet season in the Ouachitas and the Cossatot runs hard then — good for the look of it, and the reason not to be casual near the water.
trails.note: The card had two trails on Rich Mountain and a city park. This is the other direction — about three quarters of an hour south into the Cossatot, on a loop that AllTrails' own text says passes through six distinct habitats from a dry open shale pit to mature shortleaf pine and hardwood, with an overlook halfway round. The trailhead is roughly a mile before the state park visitor centre.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule. Cossatot River State Park-Natural Area is a state park, so the Ouachita National Forest verbal-restraint rule already sourced for Rich Mountain does not apply here; the stricter state-park leash rule does.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Cossatot River State Park-Natural Area
other_links.note: Park browse page. Also names the River Corridor Trail, the long linear route through the corridor at 4.6 from 140 reviews with 1,653 ft of total ascent — a backpacking line rather than a day walk, so not carried here.

trails.stats_note: Distance, gain, time and count from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. The star average differs between AllTrails' own pages for the same trail — 4.6 on the trail page, 4.7 on the Harris Creek Overlook area page — and 4.6 is recorded as the trail page's own figure.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection. Five nights and three entries, two of which are the same ridge (Lover's Leap and the Ouachita NRT segment both run Rich Mountain) and one of which is a small municipal park in Mena.

trails.name: Cossatot River Falls
trails.season: AllTrails records it as open year-round. Late February puts the river near its annual high — the falls here are a genuine Class IV-V whitewater drop, not a scenic cascade, and high water is what makes them worth the walk and also what makes the rock beside them the wrong place to be casual with a dog off the lead.
trails.note: Short, easy, and the single most photographed thing in the Ouachitas — the Cossatot dropping through a staircase of ledges. Pairs with Harris Creek to make one full day out of Mena rather than two half ones. The access is down the gravel river road to the Cossatot Falls area: truck, not coach, and worth checking after heavy rain.
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted on a leash — Arkansas State Parks rule.
trails.stats_note: All figures from the AllTrails result title and snippet as displayed. The title gives 98 reviews and the snippet a bracketed (75); the title figure is recorded.
trails.resel: ADDED in re-selection.

mena-ar.dogs: The Ouachita National Forest allows dogs under restraint on its trails and Queen Wilhelmina is an Arkansas state park, so Rich Mountain works both ways; the City of Mena publishes no rule for Janssen Park, so that one is unknown.
mena-ar.dogs_source_quote: On trails, dogs must be under verbal or physical restraint at all times.

Museum of Western Film History.entity: Museum of Western Film History, Lone Pine

offroad.name: Movie Road (Alabama Hills)
offroad.distance: about 6 miles of graded gravel looping off US-395 through the rock formations and back
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded dirt, no low range needed in dry conditions; the spurs off it get rougher
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round at about 4,500 ft. The stop arrives 27 Dec 2027 — snow is uncommon this low, but a winter storm turns the graded dirt greasy and the spurs soft, so pick the day.
offroad.note: Renamed from a vague plural to the one named route. BLM restricts vehicle and mountain-bike use to existing roads and trails — no cross-country driving in the Scenic Area, and the boulder fields are exactly where people are tempted. A free permit is needed to camp, not to drive; get it online, at the Eastern Sierra Interagency Visitor Center on US-395, or at the kiosks on Movie Road itself. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film locations, which is the point of the drive.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Movie Road, Alabama Hills
scenicDrives_patch.note: From the centre of Lone Pine, 2.7 mi west on Whitney Portal Road, then right onto Movie Road where the pavement ends. Graded gravel, about 6 mi through the rock maze past the western film locations before rejoining US-395; sources also describe a fuller 12 mi loop. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film sites. Congress designated the Alabama Hills a National Scenic Area in March 2019. Camping at designated sites needs the free Alabama Hills permit.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; usable year-round. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — cold, low sun, which is the good light here. Graded gravel can wash after storms.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Alabama Hills pages; BLM Alabama Hills National Scenic Area program page

other_links.label: BLM — Alabama Hills National Scenic Area

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-395 north through the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: US-395 north toward the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.note: The run up the middle of the Owens Valley with the Sierra crest on the left and the Inyo and White Mountains on the right. Caltrans has officially designated US-395 a state scenic highway from Fort Independence to Fort Springs Road in Inyo County, and again from the Inyo–Mono county line to south of Walker — the whole 200 mi is not uniformly designated. No single official byway page exists, so the Bishop visitor bureau's scenic-drives itinerary is the best available link.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open year-round as a primary route. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — winter storms bring chain controls and closures on 395; check Caltrans before a long day north.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Caltrans scenic-highway designation as reported on Wikipedia's US Route 395 in California; bishopvisitor.com

not_a_trail.problem: A graded gravel ROAD, not a trail — and a duplicate of the scenicDrives entry 'Movie Road, Alabama Hills' on this same stop. AllTrails does index it as 'Movie Road Trail' (251 reviews), but LINKS_STRATEGY §3 rejects roads from the trails box and §6 says to deduplicate across boxes before adding. Drop it here; the drive already carries the BLM link.

lone-pine.dogs: BLM Bishop Field Office publishes no pet rule for the Alabama Hills at all — not on the scenic-area page, not on the Mobius Arch trail page, not in the 2022 brochure or the map and guide — so this is unknown, not permitted.

not_a_route.entry: The coach is appropriate for the main Alaska Highway.
not_a_route.problem: A statement about the coach on a paved highway. Not an offroad route by any reading — it belongs in the leg notes, if anywhere.

dawson-creek.dogs: On leash in every City of Dawson Creek park (Animal Responsibility Bylaw 4420 — Barbaree Park is the only off-leash area), which covers Chamberlain Nature Park and Leoppky Park; Radar Lake, the Rim Rocks wind-park paths and McQueen Slough are all outside the city and none of their managers publishes a dog rule.
dawson-creek.dogs_source_quote: No owner will permit the owner's animal to be at large in the City.

offroad.name: 223 Road / Bear Mountain Wind Park Road
offroad.distance: 4 km up the 223 Road to the trailhead
offroad.season: no seasonal dates published
offroad.note: Recreation Sites and Trails BC records the Bear Mtn Community Forest site as "The trailhead is located 4km up the 223 Road / Bear Mountain Wind Park Road", with Radar Lake and the Interpretive Trails used for day-use picnicking, hiking and wildlife viewing. This is the only gravel route near Dawson Creek that any managing authority publishes - the RST BC page is a JavaScript app that returns an empty document to a plain fetch, so this text is the indexed record of the authority's own page rather than a page that could be read directly. Surface and vehicle requirements are not published.

Liberty Falls State Recreation Site shor.entity: Liberty Falls SRA — redirects to Edgerton Highway, whose article documents the site at mile 23

4x4 explore O'Brien Creek Road.entity: The 4x4 spur out of Chitina toward the Copper River. No article; the Chitina, Alaska article's full text never mentions O'Brien Creek Road, so there is no parent that documents it.

offroad.name: McCarthy Road
offroad.was_name: Drive the McCarthy Road to McCarthy & Kennecott (in the towed 4x4, not the motorhome)
offroad.distance: 59.4 miles one way, Chitina State Wayside to the McCarthy footbridge over the Kennicott River
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. Usually driveable in 2WD, but soft shoulders, limited visibility and poor surface mean it is a slow, attentive drive rather than an easy one
offroad.season: Best late June through early September, when the road is clear of ice and snow. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027 — squarely inside the good window, no conflict.
offroad.note: Pack-dirt and gravel on an old railbed. The state has spent heavily on it in recent years and it is well maintained in summer, but potholes and washboard hold you to 35 mph or below. NPS suggests two hours; allow three each way, and remember there is no vehicle bridge at the far end — you park at the Kennicott River and walk the footbridge into McCarthy. This is the entry the box was really about; the rig advice in the old name is now settled policy and has moved to the note.

offroad.name: O'Brien Creek Road
offroad.distance: about 3 miles from Chitina to the O'Brien Creek parking area — and that is where driveable road ends
offroad.difficulty: not a technical route. The short spur is ordinary rough gravel
offroad.season: The road is there year-round, but its whole character depends on the Copper River personal-use dipnet fishery, which runs periodically between about 7 June and 30 September. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027, inside that window — expect the parking area busy with dipnetters and charter operators.
offroad.note: Worth correcting an expectation: this is not a 4x4 route, it is a three-mile spur. Beyond O'Brien Creek the old roadbed through Wood Canyon is extremely rough and undriveable — the bridge over the creek takes ATVs only, and the trail past it is an ATV route and a dangerous one. The DOT road project beyond O'Brien Creek has stalled. Also worth knowing before going: the local tribe has petitioned to close the road, which overlies a burial ground, so treat the area as sensitive.

offroad.name: O'Brien Creek Road (4x4)
offroad.distance: About 2.8 miles from Chitina to the parking area on the gravel fan at the Copper River
offroad.difficulty: AWD or high-clearance recommended for the full length; "The final descent to the creek is harrowing and very steep"
offroad.season: Accessible year-round but busiest during dipnetting season, June through early August. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027, just after the crowd.
offroad.note: One-lane road hugging a cliff down to where O'Brien Creek meets the Copper River. The line that matters: it "is no longer maintained by the state" and may have landslides and stray boulders. Drivers in ordinary cars are told to park in a turnaround after Mile 2 and walk the rest — in the truck that is not the constraint, but the unmaintained status and the rockfall are. The Chitina Dipnetters Association pages (chitinadipnetters.com/access-issues.html, dipnetter.com) carry the most current road reports but both refused connection from this sandbox, so nothing from them is recorded.

not_a_route.problem: Duplicate — the same road is listed twice in this box, once as a verb phrase and once as 'O'Brien Creek Road (4x4)'. Folded into a single entry.

not_a_route.entry: Stop at the Wrangell-St. Elias NPS ranger station in Chitina
not_a_route.problem: A building, and a good idea, but not a route. Belongs in activities or points of interest. It is also where you would ask about McCarthy Road conditions, so it is worth keeping somewhere on the card.

chitina.authority: National Park Service, Wrangell-St. Elias National Park & Preserve (907-822-5234; Chitina Ranger Station 907-823-2242); BLM Glennallen Field Office (Liberty Falls, 907-822-3217)
chitina.dogs: Wrangell-St. Elias is one of the very few national parks where the dog can walk the trails. NPS: 'Dogs are allowed on trails within the park and in the backcountry' — leashed, six feet maximum, and not inside visitor centres or ranger stations. Dogs must also be leashed inside the Kennecott Mines National Historic Landmark. NPS additionally warns that trapping is legal in Alaska from fall through spring and that unleashed pets get caught in snares.
chitina.trails_note: Chitina is a two-night stop at the mouth of the McCarthy Road and the next stop is McCarthy/Kennecott for six nights. Root Glacier, Bonanza Mine and Jumbo Mine are Kennecott trails and are deliberately filed there, not here. What is left is genuinely local: three trails within ten road miles of Chitina, plus Crystalline Hills, which is the one worthwhile stop on the McCarthy Road drive. Note that the Chitina Ranger Station is only open Fridays and Saturdays from 24 May to 31 Aug, staffing dependent — 15-17 Aug is inside that window, but the days are not.

trails.name: Liberty Falls Trail
trails.difficulty: Moderate, some steep areas and rock scrambling

other_links.label: NPS Wrangell-St. Elias — Trails Near the Visitor Center (PDF, includes Liberty Falls)
other_links.note: 'This is a Bureau of Land Management maintained trail. It is not managed by the National Park Service.' Access: Mile 23.3 Edgerton Hwy, east of Kenny Lake, on the south side of the road 100 yards before the Liberty Falls State Recreation Site campground; a trail register marks the start. 'This trail ventures up through spruce forest to a rocky ridge with spectacular views of mountains and the Copper River.' Hazards: 'Bears are frequently seen in this area.'

trails.stats_note: The trail does NOT go to the waterfall — NPS is explicit: 'This is not the trail to the waterfall. To view the falls, go to the Liberty Falls campground.' The stop's activity list already carries 'Liberty Falls State Recreation Site short walk', which is the falls, not this ridge climb. Two different outings from the same pullout.
trails.needs: No AllTrails listing found. Reviews unknown. BLM Glennallen Field Office (907-822-3217) holds the map and trail details per NPS.
trails.tag: Ten road miles west of Chitina on the Edgerton — an hour up to a Copper River overlook, and the shortest real hike of the stop.

trails.name: O'Brien to Haley Creek Trail
trails.distance: approximately 10 mi round trip from O'Brien Creek to Haley Creek
trails.difficulty: Easy to moderate, with easy stream crossings

other_links.label: NPS Wrangell-St. Elias — Chitina Area Trails (PDF)
other_links.note: 'This is a privately maintained trail. It is not managed by the National Park Service.' Trailhead: drive through Chitina, take the O'Brien Creek road about 2.5 miles to parking at O'Brien Creek. 'This trail follows the old right of way of the historic Copper River and Northwestern Railway which operated from 1911 to 1938... The majority of the trail is flat with a few hills and easy stream crossings. Old railroad trestles are visible in some places. The trail passes through a historic railroad tunnel.' NPS: 'This is also a nice route for mountain biking.'

trails.cruise_reason: Bike-legal and rail-grade, which is the shape of a cruise, but NPS records it as 'heavily used by ATVs', the access road past mile 1 carries a DOT 'Road Closed' sign with maintenance withdrawn, and private property borders the trail in many places. No published surface description, and no reviews describing riding it. Not enough to call it a dog-in-the-carrier gravel cruise.
trails.stats_note: The trailhead is the same O'Brien Creek Road already in this stop's offroad box — the 4x4 drive and this walk start from the same parking area, so they are one day out, not two.
trails.needs: No AllTrails listing found; no reviews. Surface (packed rail bed vs loose) is not published anywhere sourceable and decides whether this is bikeable with the dog.

trails.name: 5 Mile Trail
trails.time: allow 4-5 hours to reach the top and more time for exploring

other_links.label: NPS Wrangell-St. Elias — Chitina Area Trails (PDF)
other_links.note: 'This is a privately maintained trail. It is not managed by the National Park Service.' Trailhead five miles from Chitina at Mile 27.8 Edgerton Highway, near the Chitina airport. 'This is an ATV trail that is very easy to walk. The first four miles are through trees with some nice views of the Copper River below. Once above treeline there are endless opportunities for venturing off the trail.' Hazards: 'Bears are frequently sighted in this area.'

trails.season: NPS: 'This trail is closed to ATVs and pack animals from July 26th through September 30th, due to the hunting season.'
trails.season_note: The stop is 15-17 Aug, inside that closure — which means the ATV trail is quiet and walkable. NPS also records that in late summer and early fall 'the berries are abundant along the trail. Blueberries are a bonus for making it above tree line.' The dates are the good ones for this trail, not a problem for it.
trails.stats_note: Sixteen miles round trip with 3,500 ft of gain is a full day and does not fit a two-night stop with a travel day either side. It is here because the first four miles to treeline are a real and much shorter outing, and because the card should say what the trail actually is rather than imply the whole thing.
trails.needs: No AllTrails listing found; no reviews.

trails.name: Crystalline Hills Trail

other_links.label: NPS Wrangell-St. Elias — McCarthy Road & Kennecott Trails
other_links.note: Inside the park, and the only maintained day hike on the McCarthy Road itself. 'Crystalline Hills Trailhead is located along the north side of the McCarthy Road, at Mile 34.8. Distance: 2.5 mile loop. Time: 2-3 hours. Difficulty: Easy to Moderate. Highlights: Road access, beautiful views.' Route: 'After hiking 1/2 mile, a short side trail leads to a nice view. The main trail continues to climb gradually through the dense forest, loops back along the base of the steep Crystalline Hills.' NPS note: 'The trail passes through shady forest and bug spray is highly recommended in summer.'

trails.stats_note: Mile 34.8 of the McCarthy Road, about 35 miles from Chitina — too far to be a Chitina day out on its own, but it is directly on the transfer to McCarthy on 17 Aug. Listed here because it is the one thing on that drive worth stopping the truck for; the Kennecott trails belong to the McCarthy stop.
trails.needs: No AllTrails listing found; no reviews.

links.label: Wikipedia — Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument
Wikipedia — Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument

Ranger star party.entity: A scheduled ranger programme, not an entity. The Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument article has no star-party or dark-sky content.

Victoria Mine Trail.entity: Trail to the monument's old Victoria Mine. No article; the monument article never mentions it, and the NRHP listings for Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument do not include it either.

organ-pipe-ajo.dogs_note: NPS Organ Pipe opens with "Pets are always welcome at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument!" and then names exactly three trails: the Palo Verde Trail, the Campground Perimeter Trail and the Visitor Center Nature Trail, plus all roads and paved campground areas. Everything else is closed to pets — the monument cites cholla, venomous animals, coyotes and sharp rock. Leash 6 ft or shorter. Eight nights, and those three trails are the dog's entire itinerary; all three start at or beside the Twin Peaks campground, so they are walkable from the coach.

trails.name: Estes Canyon–Bull Pasture Loop
trails.distance: 3.6 mi round trip including the Bull Pasture spur
trails.difficulty: Moderate loop; NPS calls the Bull Pasture spur itself strenuous with steep switchbacks
trails.season: Winter, spring and autumn are the stated seasons; NPS warns summer and autumn reach 110°F. The 27 Jan–4 Feb stay is the best window of the year.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities and the best hike in the monument. Climbs off Ajo Mountain Drive into the Ajo Range for a 20-mile view. Distance, time, grade and gain are all NPS.

trails.name: Victoria Mine Trail
trails.season: Year-round; NPS notes summer and autumn temperatures to 110°F, which does not touch this stay.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. Leaves from the far side of the campground — no drive needed — and runs out to the monument's oldest gold and silver workings. Not signposted from the highway. All figures NPS.

trails.name: Alamo Canyon Trail
trails.note: NPS lists it as a birding trail; historic ranch and canyon views. Trailhead is at the east end of Alamo Campground off Highway 85 between mile markers 66 and 67, so it is a short drive north of Twin Peaks rather than a walk from camp. Uneven, rocky, some steep sections. All figures NPS.

trails.name: Desert View Trail
trails.note: Loop with benches climbing to a low ridge from the Twin Peaks campground — the sunset walk of the stay, and it starts at the coach. Distance and grade are NPS; NPS publishes no estimated time for it.

trails.name: Arch Canyon Trail
trails.note: Off Ajo Mountain Drive, which the stop already plans to drive — a double natural arch high on the canyon wall. AllTrails' snippet says the best view of the arch is in the first 0.3 mi, including from the car park, so the walk in is optional. Distance and grade are NPS.

trails.name: Palo Verde Trail
trails.distance: 2.6 mi (NPS trail list); the pet page gives it as 1.3 mi one way
trails.note: THE DOG'S BEST WALK AT ORGAN PIPE — the longest of the three trails NPS names as pet-friendly, and by some distance. Runs between the visitor centre and the campground, so it is walkable from the coach in either direction. No AllTrails listing surfaced in search; it is carried on NPS authority alone.

trails.name: Campground Perimeter Trail
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL, and it literally circles Twin Peaks campground — the first-light and last-light walk for eight mornings. Partially ADA accessible. NPS authority only; no trail database lists it.

trails.name: Visitor Center Nature Trail
trails.note: DOG-LEGAL and ADA accessible. A ten-minute interpretive loop at the Kris Eggle visitor centre — worth knowing about only because it is one of three places in the monument the dog may set foot on a trail.

trails.name: Red Tanks Tinaja
trails.note: Off Ajo Mountain Drive to a set of tinajas — the natural rock basins that hold the desert's only standing water. Distance and grade are NPS; no AllTrails listing surfaced, so no trail link.

offroad.name: Ajo Mountain Drive
offroad.distance: 21 miles (34 km)
offroad.difficulty: graded gravel and asphalt, one-way; NPS states "vehicles over 25 feet are prohibited"
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published. The stop's 27 Jan - 4 Feb 2028 dates are the best time of year for it; NPS gives it 1-2 hours.
offroad.note: The signature drive of the monument and the reason the stop is eight nights — a one-way loop under the west face of the Ajo Range through the densest organ pipe stands in the US. The 25 ft limit is the coach's problem, not the truck's.
offroad.source: NPS Organ Pipe Cactus NM — Driving and Biking

offroad.name: North and South Puerto Blanco Drive (full loop)
offroad.distance: 41 miles (66 km)
offroad.difficulty: all vehicles as far as Pinkley Peak; beyond that NPS requires high clearance and four-wheel drive
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published. NPS budgets 4-5 hours for the loop.
offroad.note: The committing one. NPS is explicit: "Vehicles cannot proceed past Pinkley Peak and turn around; they must finish the entire loop." Past Pinkley the road runs the border fence line. The 10-mile round trip out to Pinkley Peak picnic area and back is the low-commitment version and needs no 4WD.
offroad.source: NPS Organ Pipe Cactus NM — Driving and Biking

offroad.name: Bates Well Road
offroad.distance: 23 miles
offroad.difficulty: two-way; NPS strongly recommends high clearance
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published.
offroad.note: Runs west off AZ-85 to the Cabeza Prieta NWR boundary, past the Bates Well ranch buildings. Two-way, so it can be turned around on — unlike the Puerto Blanco loop.
offroad.source: NPS Organ Pipe Cactus NM — Driving and Biking

offroad.name: Pozo Nuevo Road
offroad.distance: 14 miles
offroad.difficulty: two-way; NPS says high clearance and four-wheel drive are highly recommended
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published.
offroad.note: The quietest of the four. Camino de Dos Republicas branches off it for 2 miles, also 4WD — but NPS states "The road beyond Gachado line camp to Dos Lomitas is closed to the public," so that spur dead-ends.
offroad.source: NPS Organ Pipe Cactus NM — Driving and Biking

chiricahua-willcox.dogs_note: NPS Chiricahua permits leashed pets in the campground, on paved car parks, and on the "Lower trails between the Campground and Entrance (Bonita Creek, Silver Spur Meadow, Faraway Ranch area)" — and bans them "on any trails above 5,500 feet (including Massai Point Nature, Echo Canyon, Heart of the Rocks, Natural Bridge, and Sugarloaf Trails)". Carrying a pet on a closed trail is also prohibited. Every hoodoo trail is therefore dog-free; the two lower trails below are the entire dog itinerary and they both start at the campground.

trails.name: Echo Canyon Loop (Echo Canyon–Hailstone–Ed Riggs)
trails.time: 2 hours possible, but NPS says most people prefer 3 or 4
trails.difficulty: Moderate — NPS notes steep drop-offs and loose, rocky, uneven surfaces, 1–25% grade with cross-slope to 50%
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities as the Echo Canyon Grottoes Loop, and the best short hike in the monument — CCC-built trail through the densest hoodoos. All figures NPS. The AllTrails listing that matches is the shorter Grottoes out-and-back below, not this full loop, so the loop carries no trail link.

trails.name: Echo Canyon Grottoes
trails.distance: about 0.5 mi each way from the Echo Canyon car park (the full loop it sits on is 3.3 mi)
trails.note: The short version: down into the grottoes and back, when there is not a whole morning for the loop. NPS states it is not wheelchair or stroller friendly, is steep and rocky, and has sections that are poor for anyone uneasy with height. Figures NPS.

trails.name: The Big Loop
trails.distance: 8+ mi (NPS); AllTrails lists 8.2 mi and reviewers report logging more
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. The full circuit of the Wonderland of Rocks — Echo Canyon, Upper Rhyolite, Sarah Deming, Big Balanced Rock, Mushroom Rock, Ed Riggs, with the Heart of Rocks and Inspiration Point spurs. Kept on the card despite being difficult because 2,166 reviews clears the outstanding bar comfortably. One reviewer measured 11.2 mi without leaving the trail, so budget the whole day and use the hiker shuttle rather than doubling back.

trails.name: Heart of Rocks from Massai Point
trails.note: The Heart of Rocks balanced-rock cluster taken from the Massai Point end instead of round the Big Loop. NPS gives the Heart of Rocks Loop as 8+ miles from the visitor centre; no figures were published for this shorter variant, so none are recorded.

alltrails.listed_as: Heart of Rocks from Massai Point

trails.name: Natural Bridge Trail
trails.note: Its own small pull-out about 1.4 mi past the visitor centre on the Massai Point road, room for roughly five vehicles. Crosses the usually dry Bonita Creek bed then climbs to the rock span. The quietest of the monument's named trails. No length or grade was published by NPS on any page that loaded, so none is recorded.

trails.name: Silver Spur Meadow Trail
trails.note: ONE OF ONLY TWO DOG-LEGAL TRAILS AT CHIRICAHUA. Leaves from across the road from the visitor centre and runs to Faraway Ranch through the settlement history of Bonita Canyon — and it is below 5,500 ft, which is the line the pet closure is drawn on. NPS's own trail description page for it was still marked in progress when checked, so no length or grade could be sourced; recorded as absent rather than guessed.

trails.name: Bonita Creek Trail
trails.note: THE OTHER DOG-LEGAL TRAIL. At the west end of the monument, through grassy meadow and creekside woodland at the mouth of Bonita Canyon, connecting to the Silver Spur Meadow Trail at Faraway Ranch — so the two chain into one longer dog walk from the campground. Grade from HikeArizona; NPS publishes no figures on any page that loaded.

offroad.name: Pinery Canyon Road #42
offroad.distance: 12 miles from near the Chiricahua NM entrance up to Onion Saddle — about an hour one way
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF: "High clearance vehicles are strongly recommended. 4WD also beneficial, if available."
offroad.season: Watch this one. Coronado NF: "Western portion, from East Turkey Creek Road to Forest Boundary can be closed due to snow in the winter." The stop is 18-23 Feb 2028 and the road tops out at 7,600 ft — no published gate date, but a February snow could shut exactly the section that starts at the monument. Douglas Ranger District, (520) 364-3468, for current conditions.
offroad.note: The road out the back of Chiricahua NM and over the crest of the range to Portal — the single best day's driving of this stop when it is open. Continues from Onion Saddle to Rustler Park or drops to Portal on the New Mexico side.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Pinery Canyon #42 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Cave Creek Road #42/42B loop via Paradise
offroad.distance: 17-mile loop
offroad.difficulty: not published by Coronado NF
offroad.season: No gate published. High point about 6,000 ft, lower than the Pinery Canyon crest, so it is the more likely of the two to be open in February.
offroad.note: From Portal up Cave Creek Canyon, around Silver Peak and back through the old mining town of Paradise. Coronado NF's warning is worth repeating: "There are no gas stations in Portal or Paradise, Arizona or Rodeo, NM, so be sure to fill up before you arrive." Best birding in the range.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Cave Creek Road #42/42B Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Cochise Stronghold approach roads (Ironwood Road / FR 84)
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF says only that "Dirt roads surround the Dragoon Mountains and are required to drive on to visit any of the sites" — it publishes no grade or vehicle requirement for the East Stronghold approach itself
offroad.season: No gate published.
offroad.note: West of Willcox in the Dragoons — the granite maze where Cochise held out and is buried. Ironwood Road becomes FR 84 at the forest boundary. The Forest's own page is careful to say the roads are dirt and unavoidable but stops short of grading them, so treat the surface as unknown until seen.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Cochise Stronghold

scenicDrives_patch.name: Bonita Canyon Scenic Drive to Massai Point
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 8 miles, paved, park entrance to Massai Point
scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS states two separate limits and they are not the same number: "no vehicles over 29 feet or day use trailers beyond Faraway Ranch", and "Only standard size vehicles beyond the campground (24 foot maximum)". The truck clears both; nothing longer does. The road narrows and starts winding just past the campground, half a mile in. Stops along it: Erickson Cemetery, Bonita Creek (NPS calls it "often the best place for birding"), the Faraway Ranch Historic District, the visitor centre museum, the Organ Pipe Formation, and Natural Bridge Trailhead - which has only three small parking spaces for a 4.8-mile hike. No entrance fee; the booth is often unmanned, so read the window.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sulphur Springs Valley birding roads - Kansas Settlement, Arzberger, Kimzey
scenicDrives_patch.distance: No mileage published for the loop; the site says the valley is large enough that "at least a half-day should be allotted for a visit"
scenicDrives_patch.season: "Winter (November-March) is best" - the 18-23 Feb stay sits inside the good window, which is also when the wintering cranes are still in the valley.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Agricultural fields, ponds and desert scrub running from north of Willcox all the way to the Mexican border. Access from the Willcox exits off I-10, or from the south via Douglas (SR 191) or Tombstone (Davis Road). The named eBird hotspots are Kansas Settlement Road, Arzberger Road and Kimzey Road; the driving is on dirt farm roads and the warning is explicit - they "can be very slippery after rain or snow has fallen". Park on the road edge so farm vehicles can pass. No fee, open 24 hours. Recorded at community tier: the managing authority here is Arizona Game and Fish, whose own site answers HTTP 403 from this sandbox, so the Arizona Birding Trail page is what was actually read.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Apache Pass Road to the Fort Bowie trailhead
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 13 miles south from the town of Bowie, the last mile unpaved; Bowie is 23 miles east of Willcox on I-10
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Park Service publishes only this one approach: I-10 to the first Bowie exit, through the town, south on Apache Pass Road, 13 miles to the Fort Bowie Trailhead. It is a drive to a trailhead, not to the ruins - NPS is clear that reaching the visitor centre and the fort is a 3-mile round-trip walk from where the car stops. The continuation west from the trailhead on graded gravel for 9 miles to SR 186, which would make this a loop back toward Chiricahua, is described by Visit Arizona and not by NPS, so it is recorded here as unverified rather than as a route. Different road from the offroad box's Pinery Canyon Road #42 and Cave Creek Road #42/42B.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Swift Trail Parkway (SR 366), Mount Graham
scenicDrives_patch.distance: ADOT designates SR 366 milepost 116.0 to 142.0 as the Swift Trail Parkway - 26 miles - dated 15 Jan 1993. The gate sits well below the top.
scenicDrives_patch.season: CLOSED FOR THIS STOP. The upper Swift Trail is gated every year from 15 November to 15 April "approximately one-half mile beyond Shannon Campground at the end of the pavement", and the Forest Service notes the reopening can be pushed later if weather holds. The 18-23 Feb window is four months deep inside that closure. The paved miles below the gate stay open; the high country, Riggs Lake and the top do not, and non-motorized use is the only thing permitted past the locked gate.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Kept on the card rather than dropped, because it is the one designated Parkway within reach of this stop and it is worth knowing why it is not available: this is a summer road, and a summer road that is also a long day - roughly 80 miles from Willcox north on US-191 to the SR 366 junction about five miles south of Safford. Nothing to phone about; the closure is annual and published.

Paton Center for Hummingbirds.entity: Tucson Audubon's hummingbird site in Patagonia. No article, and Tucson Audubon Society has no article to serve as a parent.

patagonia-sonoita.dogs_note: AllTrails states dogs are not allowed on the Patagonia-Sonoita Creek Nature Trail, which is consistent with The Nature Conservancy's practice at its other Arizona preserve. No pet rule was found on the Arizona State Parks pages for Patagonia Lake or the Sonoita Creek State Natural Area that loaded, so nothing is recorded for those — absence, not permission.
patagonia-sonoita.box_note: Three nights and the stop is built around birding rather than mileage. The preserve and the two state units between them publish very little in the way of trail figures — twenty miles of trail at Sonoita Creek and one published length among them.

trails.name: Patagonia-Sonoita Creek Nature Trail
trails.season: Open year-round.
trails.note: Named in the stop's activities. The loop through The Nature Conservancy's preserve along the first two miles of Sonoita Creek's permanent flow — one of the last perennial streams in southern Arizona and the reason the birding here is what it is. AllTrails notes it is unlikely to be busy. Small entrance fee collected at the visitor centre.

trails.name: Sonoita Creek Trail, Patagonia Lake State Park
trails.difficulty: Easy — AllTrails records 88% of reviewers calling it easy
trails.note: The lake park's own creek-side birding walk. Two Arizona State Parks pages give conflicting lengths — the Patagonia Lake page describes a half-mile trail to the creek, the Sonoita Creek natural-area page says the shortest round trip to the creek is three miles on the Sonoita Creek Trail — so no distance is recorded rather than picking one. Worth settling at the entrance station.

trails.name: Overlook Trail, Sonoita Creek State Natural Area
trails.note: Arizona State Parks calls it "a great way to see 360 degrees of spectacular scenery" and it is the only trail in the natural area for which they publish a length. Close to Patagonia Lake State Park. No AllTrails listing surfaced, so no trail link.

trails.name: Sonoita Creek State Natural Area trail system
trails.distance: twenty miles of trail in total, eight of them shared with horses
trails.note: Recorded as a system, not a trail, because that is all the authority publishes. Arizona State Parks names Vista, Sonoita Creek, New Mexico and Arizona Railroad, Overlook, Horse Corral, Foothills, Cat Cave and Blackhawk trails and gives a length for exactly one of them. If more than the Overlook is wanted, the figures have to come from the entrance station — the natural area is day-use and gated, so it is a conversation that happens anyway.

offroad.name: Box Canyon Road #62
offroad.difficulty: Coronado NF describes an "all-weather gravel road" that "turns to dirt"; no vehicle requirement published
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists it as available year-round.
offroad.note: East off the Madera Canyon road, through Box Canyon under the west face of the Santa Ritas, and out to AZ-83 a few miles north of Sonoita — so it can be driven as the way in or the way out of this stop rather than as a there-and-back. The all-weather designation on the first part is the useful bit: this is the route that still works after rain.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Box Canyon Road (FR 62) Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Ruby Road #289/39
offroad.difficulty: not published by Coronado NF — the page gives no mileage, surface or vehicle requirement, only the route
offroad.season: No gate published.
offroad.note: West off I-19 north of Nogales at the Ruby interchange, paved to Peña Blanca Lake where it becomes FR 39, then dirt through grass savanna and past the Ruby ghost town toward Arivaca. Sycamore Canyon and Arivaca Lake are on it. Furthest afield of this stop's three and the one to give a full day.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Ruby Road #289/39 Scenic Drive

offroad.name: Canelo Hills Loops #799/58/49
offroad.difficulty: not published — Coronado NF gives the route and the country but no length, surface or vehicle requirement
offroad.season: Coronado NF lists the route status as open; no gate published.
offroad.note: Off AZ-83 south of Sonoita onto FR 5799 and through the Canelo Hills — "historic ranching and mining country with broad grasslands and distant buttes" — ending in Patagonia. Loops back to the stop itself, which is what makes it the easy pick of the three. Neither restrooms nor water anywhere on it.
offroad.source: USFS Coronado National Forest — Canelo Hills Loops #799/58/49 Scenic Drive

scenicDrives_patch.name: Patagonia-Sonoita Scenic Road (SR 82 and SR 83)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: ADOT's designation covers SR 82 milepost 4.5 to 32.0 and SR 83 milepost 33.0 to 58.0 - 52.5 miles of designated road. The byway programme quotes 57 miles end to end; both figures are recorded rather than choosing between them.
scenicDrives_patch.note: A state-designated Scenic Road, dated 20 Sep 1985 in ADOT's own parkways, historic and scenic roads list - one of nineteen scenic roads in Arizona and the only designated route this stop actually sits on. Paved throughout, running Nogales north through Patagonia and Sonoita, then north on SR 83 toward I-10, through the semi-arid valleys and narrow canyons of the Santa Cruz River Basin. The byway programme names Patagonia Lake State Park, Kentucky Camp Historic Site, the Patagonia-Sonoita Creek Preserve visitor centre and Las Cienegas NCA as the things strung along it - three of which have their own entries elsewhere on this card. On a three-night stop this is the spine, and the other three drives hang off it.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sonoita/Elgin Wine Loop - Elgin Road, Upper Elgin Road, Lower Elgin Road
scenicDrives_patch.distance: No mileage is published for the loop. The Sky Islands Tourism Association's own map gives only drive times off it - Patagonia 20 minutes, Tucson 50 minutes.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Read off the association's own loop map rather than a blog: 21 numbered stops, 19 wineries plus Copper Brothel Brewery and Copper Hop Ranch, strung along Highway 82 and Highway 83 with the dense cluster on Elgin Road, Upper Elgin Road and Lower Elgin Road, which close the loop between the two highways. The Sonoita-Elgin AVA is Arizona's original wine region. The two highways are paved; the association publishes no surface for the Elgin roads, so none is recorded.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Empire Ranch Road (LC 900) into Las Cienegas NCA
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 3 miles east off AZ-83 to the ranch house; the turn is signed between mileposts 39 and 40, which BLM puts 6.6 miles north of the AZ-82 junction coming up from Sonoita
scenicDrives_patch.note: BLM: open daily sunrise to sunset, free, no permit unless you are running a commercial event. The ranch house is a 22-room adobe and wood-frame building dating to 1870, still surrounded by a working cattle operation of 140-plus years, and there is a half-mile packed-gravel Heritage Discovery Trail loop past the Hired Man's House and the New Ranch House with accessible parking. BLM does not publish a surface for LC 900 itself, so none is recorded here. Roughly ten minutes off the Patagonia-Sonoita Scenic Road, so this is an add-on to that drive rather than a separate day.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Gardner Canyon Road (FR 92) and FR 163 to Kentucky Camp
scenicDrives_patch.distance: From AZ-83, a quarter of a mile west on Gardner Canyon Road to FR 163, then about 5 miles to the Kentucky Camp entrance. The Forest Service gives Gardner Canyon Road itself as 8.7 miles one way, but only the first quarter mile is used to reach FR 163.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Forest Service lists Kentucky Camp as operating year-round.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Five adobe buildings left from a 1902-1906 hydraulic gold operation and the cattle ranch that followed, on the eastern flank of the Santa Ritas. The Forest Service describes access as being by dirt roads and standard vehicles reaching the site; separately, its page for Gardner Canyon Road (FR 92) says "High-clearance required to reach trailheads" - that applies to the far western end of FR 92, not to the quarter mile used here, and both statements are recorded rather than reconciled. Graded forest road rather than a 4x4 route, which is why it sits here; note the Forest Service bars OHV riding inside the Kentucky Camp boundary itself. The cabin sleeps five at $75 a night and the headquarters building is a day-use rental, so expect the site to be occupied at times.

offroad.name: Sage Creek Rim Road
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: NPS allows 1–2 hours to drive it and publishes no mileage. It connects SD 44 near Scenic with the Badlands Loop Road (SD 240) north of Pinnacles Overlook, so it can be run as a leg rather than an out-and-back. Along it: Hay Butte and Badlands Wilderness overlooks, Roberts Prairie Dog Town, Sage Creek Basin and Sage Creek Campground. Road status by phone: 605-433-5361.

offroad.name: Sage Creek Rim Road (SD-590)
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: Same road as the entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. NPS confirms the SD 590 designation and gives no mileage. Phone 605-433-5361 for status.

trails.name: Castle Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Badlands
other_links.note: Authority: 10.2 mi / 16.45 km round trip, moderate; longest established trail in the park, Door and Window lot to Fossil Exhibit Trail.

other_links.label: NPS — Castle Trailhead
other_links.note: Five miles one way, relatively level.

trails.stats_note: NPS says 10.2 mi round trip, AllTrails 10.3 mi — the same trail, measured twice. No shade the whole way. About 3.5-4 hr.

trails.name: Cliff Shelf Nature Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in Badlands
other_links.note: Authority: 0.86 mi / 1.38 km round trip, graded moderate; boardwalks, stairs and natural path through junipers.

other_links.label: NPS — Cliff Shelf Trailhead
other_links.note: One of the few shaded spots in the park — a juniper grove.

trails.stats_note: NPS calls it 0.86 mi and moderate; AllTrails 0.5 mi and easy. The stairs are the reason for the harder official grade. AllTrails records dogs as not allowed on this trail.

trails.name: Window Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Window Trailhead
other_links.note: Authority: short accessible boardwalk to a natural window in the Badlands Wall. NPS lists 0.26 mi / 0.41 km round trip, easy, ~20 minutes.

trails.stats_note: Accessible boardwalk the whole way — the one Badlands trail that needs no ability at all.

badlands-sd.dogs: No dog walks any trail here — Badlands NP bars pets from every hiking trail, the nature trails and all backcountry; they are confined to roads, parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
badlands-sd.dogs_source_quote: Pets are prohibited from hiking trails, public buildings (i.e. visitor centers), and backcountry areas, including the Badlands Wilderness Area, and areas with prairie dog colonies.

Badlands Loop Road.entity: The park's main scenic road, which is South Dakota Highway 240 — its article opens by noting it is 'also signed as the Badlands Loop'.

Notch Trail / Door Trail.entity: Two short trails off the Door/Window parking area. Neither has an article; the Badlands National Park article lists both by name among its established hiking trails.

Badlands Loop Road (SD-240) end to end i.entity: Same road, named with its route number.

Notch Trail.entity: The ladder-and-ledge trail to the Notch. No article of its own; named in the Badlands National Park article's trail list.

Door and Window trails.entity: Two short boardwalk trails at the Door/Window area. Neither has an article; the Badlands National Park article names Door Trail and Window Trail.

Castle Trail and Medicine Root Loop.entity: The park's two longest maintained trails. Neither has an article and neither is named anywhere in the Badlands National Park article's text. No link.

Sage Creek Rim Road wildlife run.entity: The gravel rim road along the Badlands Wilderness on the park's west side. It has no article, and the Badlands National Park article mentions only Sage Creek Campground, not the road. No link.

Fossil Exhibit Trail and Wall Drug.entity: Two things. Wall Drug, the roadside store in Wall, has its own article. The Fossil Exhibit Trail does not, and the Badlands National Park article does not name it, so only Wall Drug is linked.

austin-home-v3.offroad_finding: Not researched, and deliberately so: Austin, TX — home is the base, arrive and depart both 1 Mar 2029, a single-day turnaround at the end of the East Extension rather than a touring stop. There is no day to spend on a road, and the truck is being unhitched at home, not driven out. Nothing was checked and nothing should be; if this stop ever grows nights, the Texas options to look at first are the LCRA and Balcones Canyonlands roads west of the city, none of which has been researched here.

_dogs_verdict: Per stop: 'allowed' | 'prohibited' | 'partial' | absent. Absent means NOT RESEARCHED and renders no icon at all — a missing dog rule must never look like a green light. 'partial' means the authority names some trails and not others, so the verdict lives on the trail, not the stop.
_activities: Per-stop overrides for the highlights list. Each entry maps an activity's name to a verified entity: its real Wikipedia article, its direct AllTrails listing where it IS a trail, and the official page. Activities with an entry render real links and pills; activities without one keep the generic name-derived search links, which is the honest fallback until they are researched. `drop: true` removes a duplicate restatement of another activity.
_url_provenance: EVERY url here must be COPIED from a search result that returned it. Never construct a slug from a trail's name — alltrails slugs are unpredictable (--2, --3 suffixes, reworded titles) and a fabricated one looks exactly like a real one until it 404s in front of you at a trailhead. This rule exists because four urls were built from names in this file; three happened to be right and one was not, which is luck, not verification.
_auto: Entries marked auto:true were resolved by resolve_highlights.py — the headline reduced to candidate entity names and checked against Wikipedia's real article index. Exact hits only; a fuzzy match is treated as no match. Hand-written entries are richer and are never overwritten.
_search_note: Searching with allowed_domains=alltrails.com returns FEWER alltrails results than an open web search does. Warner Point, Horse Gulch and Piedra River were all recorded as 'no listing found' from a restricted search and all three have listings — found by searching the open web instead. Search open, then take the alltrails url from the results.
_verification_incident: 32 Wikipedia links were written from a batch verifier that reported non-existent articles as valid. MediaWiki numbers every missing title -1, -2, -3...; the script tested only for '-1', so all but the first missing title in each 40-title chunk passed. The identical bug had already been found and fixed in resolve_highlights.py and was never ported to wiki_batch.py — one fix, two copies. Both now test the `missing` key, and wiki_batch.py also rejects disambiguation pages. Controls proved it: 'Qqxzptl Museum of Nonexistence' passed as valid before the fix. | Third residue, found by sweeping the BUILT page rather than the db: six wikipedia links were live on the page. Four titles did not exist (Alberta Falls, Canyon Road (Santa Fe), Fremont Lake (Wyoming), Green River Lakes) and two were DISAMBIGUATION pages (Salmon River, Sprague Lake) — a class the earlier sweeps did not test for at all. Three had a correct target confirmed by coordinates; three had none and were dropped. Sweep the built page, not the db: the db still holds stripped urls by design.
_dead_links: URLs proven NOT to exist. build_links.py strips any of these from a highlight's links on every run, so a bad link cannot survive in the built page just because it was written there once. Removing an entry from this db is not enough — the page is merged into, not rebuilt.
_offroad: Offroad routes researched per stop. Every url was copied from a search result and re-verified to resolve before merging. rig is truck everywhere by standing decision. `not_a_route` records entries that were never routes: rig constraints filed as list items, road-status links, non-motorised areas, and duplicates of the scenic-drives box.
_dogs_unpublished: Stops carrying `dogs_unpublished` were researched and the managing authority publishes NO dog rule at all. They deliberately have no dogs_verdict: a 'partial' badge with every trail null renders as a green light on the card, which is the one thing this field exists to prevent. The record names every page already checked so a later pass does not re-spend on them, and names the phone call that would actually settle it.
